facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on choosing a commercially viable construct without promising terms or routes that authoritative guidance has not confirmed.
keyTalkingPoints: Partner-transacted shaping applies only where the partner owns the transaction; otherwise use the applicable direct route.
Current execution: Use authoritative agreement, licensing, pricing, policy, and transaction guidance plus opportunity context.
Fallback: If a required source or owner is unavailable, carry the item as an explicit assumption and stop customer commitment on that point.
System of record: Authoritative commercial systems and approved guidance; MSX retains opportunity context and agreed commercial milestones.
Optional AI boundary: Deal Agent may help organize supported scenarios, and Cowork may compare supplied options. Both are optional and maturity/access bounded.
discussionQuestions: Which commercial option fits the confirmed customer constraints?
What assumption requires authoritative confirmation?
Who can approve the route or terms?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate decide, recommend, and partner-owned elements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Make the chosen construct explainable', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Transactable constructs need authoritative agreement mechanics and transaction ownership. Plausible options are not executable offers. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one engaged deal, approved agreement/economic context, candidate constructs, known constraints and the requested commercial decision. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which construct can this customer and transaction route actually execute? Which elements can CE decide, recommend or only route to a partner? How would a peer compare the trade-offs without presenting an unapproved option as available?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a two-construct comparison: transaction route, customer intent, CE versus partner decision rights, authoritative mechanics gap and trade-off. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which option depended on an unresolved agreement mechanic or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could compare a proposed construct with an authorized alternative and route its deciding agreement or policy question to the authoritative owner. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized construct assumption corrected and whether it prevented an unapproved or unworkable option. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Choose between two evidence-backed value angles
activities.description: Connects recruitment messaging to a real business priority while preserving the boundary between capability evidence and desired outcomes.
activities.prompt: For the recruit/priority identified in [approved recruit notes], compare two Microsoft platform or AI positioning angles using the approved recruit notes and up to three supplied current credible capability sources. Extract the verified priority and list assumptions separately. Check the capability claims with dated citations and applicability limits; do not infer technical readiness or guaranteed ROI. Return a two-row positioning table containing recruit relevance, cited capability, uncertainty, and one discovery question per angle, followed by a provisional recommendation. Ask the PDM-R owner to select the conversation angle and the technical owner to validate any fit-dependent claim. Stop when evidence is insufficient or review is required. Do not contact the recruit, promise funding, or publish the brief.
activities.expectedOutput: Two-row positioning comparison with citations, limits, uncertainty, discovery questions, and a provisional preferred angle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R approves positioning and the technical owner verifies fit-dependent claims. Unavailable evidence remains an open question, not a capability or outcome promise.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit and verified priority; approved notes; up to three current Microsoft capability sources; PDM-R and technical reviewer. No sensitive recruit details in public search queries.
activitySteps: 1. Select one documented recruit priority (1 min).
2. Check cited capability evidence (3 min).
3. Compare two positioning angles (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects an angle and assigns validation (2 min); stop before outreach.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Connects recruitment messaging to a real business priority while preserving the boundary between capability evidence and desired outcomes.

activities.name: Turn a supplied value brief into a recruit agenda
activities.description: Turns verified positioning into a useful recruitment conversation without disguising assumptions as stakeholder knowledge.
activities.prompt: Prepare one internal engagement agenda for the stakeholder/role identified in [the approved recruit profile, cited value brief and meeting objective]. Complete the draft. Identify verified stakeholder priorities and mark unconfirmed interests as hypotheses. Select no more than three relevant points from the supplied brief, preserving evidence references and qualifying technical or commercial assumptions. Return a fifteen-minute meeting agenda with opening question, two discussion blocks, proof points, and one proposed next decision; include a short do-not-claim list for unsupported benefits. Pause for the PDM-R owner to approve personalization and assign validation of any sensitive or fit-dependent statement. Stop before inviting attendees, sending material, or promising commitments. If priority evidence is missing, draft discovery questions instead of invented personalization.
activities.expectedOutput: One fifteen-minute internal agenda, referenced proof points, a do-not-claim list, and one proposed next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R reviews relevance, sensitivity, and personalization; technical/commercial claims need their accountable owners. No invitation, sharing, or commitment is made by the practice.
activities.requiredContext: Approved profile, cited value brief, stakeholder context, meeting objective, and PDM-R reviewer. Cowork access/spending policy confirmed; supplied inputs only; no outreach permission implied.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one stakeholder and objective (1 min).
2. Draft an agenda from supplied evidence (3 min).
3. Inspect personalization and do-not-claim list (2 min).
4. PDM-R approves or requests corrections (2 min); stop before sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Turns verified positioning into a useful recruitment conversation without disguising assumptions as stakeholder knowledge.

activities.name: Pressure-test one competitive or AI objection
activities.description: Builds trust by answering the real objection with evidence rather than unsupported competitive or AI claims.
activities.prompt: Examine the objection identified in [approved recruit objection notes and proposed Microsoft response], and up to three supplied credible Microsoft and competitor sources. Limit the work to one evidence check. Restate the objection neutrally and distinguish the recruit's reported concern from verified facts. Verify only the disputed capabilities or constraints with dated citations; record mismatched versions and missing evidence explicitly. Return a three-part response card: what we can substantiate, what needs technical validation, and one discovery question that tests the recruit's actual requirement. Ask the PDM-R owner to approve the response and PTS or PSA reviewer to validate technical applicability. Stop before claiming superiority, guaranteeing results, or contacting the recruit. If sources conflict, preserve the conflict instead of choosing a convenient claim.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited response card with substantiated statements, unresolved technical questions, and a neutral discovery question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R owns the response; PTS/PSA validates technical applicability. Conflicting versions or missing sources block confident comparative claims, not the discovery conversation.
activities.requiredContext: One objection; approved notes and proposed response; up to three current credible sources representing both sides; named PDM-R and technical reviewer. Authorized sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Scope one objection and response (1 min).
2. Verify disputed claims with sources (3 min).
3. Review the three-part response card (2 min).
4. PDM-R approves wording and routes technical checks (2 min); stop before outreach.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.

activities.description: Offers a credible next conversation for a recruit with real incumbent dependencies instead of assuming a greenfield platform choice.
activities.prompt: For the recruit identified in [the approved architecture and switching-constraint notes], use the approved architecture summary, the documented switching constraints, and the supplied cited Microsoft value brief to outline a limited discovery experiment, not a migration commitment. Separate verified incumbent dependencies from assumptions and flag unavailable architecture detail. Identify one recruit-valued question that a bounded experiment could test without promising interoperability, credits, or migration support. Return an internal experiment card with hypothesis, proposed scope exclusions, evidence to collect, success questions requiring owner agreement, and one fallback if dependencies are unresolved. Ask the PDM-R owner and the technical owner to review relevance, feasibility, and any proposed evaluation criteria. Stop before scheduling work, allocating resources, or presenting the experiment as technically approved or commercially funded.
activities.expectedOutput: One internal experiment card with hypothesis, exclusions, evidence needs, owner-reviewed evaluation questions, and a dependency fallback.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R validates recruit relevance and the technical owner validates feasibility/criteria. No automatic migration plan, support promise, funding approval, or resource booking.
activities.requiredContext: One incumbent-platform recruit; approved architecture and switching constraints; cited supplied value brief; PDM-R and technical owner. Supplied inputs only; no inferred connector or resource access.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm incumbent constraints and one question (1 min).
2. Draft a bounded discovery experiment (3 min).
3. Inspect exclusions and unknown dependencies (2 min).
4. PDM-R and technical owner review the proposal (2 min); stop before mobilization.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What would this recruit gain that it actually values? Start with one supplied recruit priority and compare an evidence-backed capability statement with an unsupported AI promise.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate verified recruit needs, public claims, and our value hypotheses. Cite current Microsoft capability evidence and equally credible competitor sources. PDM-R approves positioning; technical owners validate fit. Internal preparation is not permission to send, promise support, or make commercial commitments.
discussionQuestions: Which recruit priority can we substantiate? What capability or outcome claim would be unsafe to repeat today? Which question would test whether our preferred angle resonates?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Choose between two evidence-backed value angles'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose the single weakest part of the planned conversation: evidence, personalization, or objection handling. Use its Featured practice, then inspect one claim before accepting the brief. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Position a bounded experiment for an incumbent-platform recruit', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Have PDM-R approve one positioning hypothesis and name its evidence and technical-validation owner. Keep unvalidated claims in the question list, not the talking track. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved recruit profile, current priority notes, two or three capability/competitor sources, and the stakeholder context. Confirm authorized Researcher or Cowork access; Cowork also needs an applicable spending policy. Keep sensitive recruit details in approved work sources, not public searches. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; no automated outreach or public reuse.
facilitatorQuestions: Can we distinguish a capability from a promised outcome? Which positioning angle has the strongest recruit-specific evidence? Who will validate technical relevance before reuse?
listenFor: Concrete recruit priorities, cited capabilities with applicability limits, honest unknowns, and a clear discovery question. Challenge invented ROI, competitive disparagement, and assertions that an architecture is already approved.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without live research, use approved source excerpts and mark freshness unverified. Without a documented recruit priority, draft a discovery question rather than a personalized claim; do not fill missing context with a generic success promise. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which statement became more credible when we replaced a promise with a question?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore a recruit priority or capability claim and adapt an internal conversation agenda. Any actual approval stays with its authorized owner; no recruit conversation or dated owner response is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized positioning promise replaced by evidence or a question and whether it improved credibility or the recruit agenda. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Build the renewal and growth readiness view
activities.description: Connect health, consumption, adoption, value and stakeholder signals into a renewal readiness view.
activities.prompt: Build a renewal and growth readiness view for [Customer/Account] using authorized records you can access, plus [approved context for any gaps]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue. Include consumption or usage trajectory, commitment risk where relevant, adoption gaps, proven versus planned value, health and stakeholder signals, expansion hypotheses and the next team decision. Use six, twelve and eighteen months as optional starting points for looking ahead, adapting them to the customer; no pre-agreed horizon is needed to explore. Cite available evidence and flag missing coverage rather than inventing it.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal and growth readiness view separating proven value, planned value, supported risks and expansion hypotheses, with a suggested next team decision and an optional longer-term view.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Check the value and risk evidence, agree customer messaging with the account/delivery team and confirm commercial terms with the accountable commercial owner.
activities.requiredContext: Customer/account and the renewal or growth question. Use the selected tool's supported authorized records; supply approved renewal, usage, value or health context only where coverage is missing. Planning horizons can be explored and adjusted.
activities.whyThisMatters: Renewal risk is easier to change when it is seen through health and value before the renewal date.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

Flag missing evidence; do not share, commit renewal actions or update records.

activities.humanCheckpoint: Validate value, adoption and delivery evidence with the AE and team. Confirm commercial terms and negotiation messaging with the CE or accountable commercial owner.
activities.requiredContext: Customer/account; renewal readiness view, v-team roles and next review context.

activities.name: Stress-test the expansion hypothesis
activities.description: Test an expansion hypothesis against usage, stakeholder and timing evidence, and name the likely objections.
activities.prompt: In [Report Name], for [customer scope] during [period], test [expansion hypothesis] against available usage, outcome and timing measures. Cite the relevant visual, filters and comparison basis. Separate observations from the hypothesis; flag stakeholder, intent and commercial questions the report cannot answer.
activities.expectedOutput: Evidence review of the supplied expansion hypothesis, with sourced usage/outcome/timing observations, comparison gaps and objection questions. Stakeholder intent and commercial readiness need separate evidence and CSAM/account-owner judgment; unavailable report access yields a named gap.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM and AE decide this together. Pursuing an expansion the customer is not ready for damages the renewal it was meant to support, and neither role can see the whole picture alone.
activities.requiredContext: Report name; permitted customer scope and filters; reporting period and comparison baseline; expansion hypothesis; available adoption, usage or outcome measures; approved customer priorities and stakeholder context.
activitySteps: 1. Check the right report/view, permitted scope, period, relevant visual and measure definitions, including any comparison baseline.
2. In the available report Copilot Pane, ask the concise business question using the visual's titles and report terms.
3. Compare the answer with the report metrics. Inspect missing measures or unsupported conclusions, and refine the question if needed; optional book prompts can help.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expansion tied to realized value is stronger than expansion tied only to whitespace.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal readiness starts before the renewal motion. Focus on seeing risk and growth conditions early.
keyTalkingPoints: Consumption, MACC or usage trajectory, adoption gaps, value evidence, support health and stakeholder signals all shape renewal confidence.

For the optional MSXI hypothesis test, check the relevant visual, permitted customer scope, period and usage/outcome measures; stakeholder intent and commercial readiness still need separate evidence.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal are you least confident about, and what specifically drives that?
What consumption signal would you want to see six months before a renewal conversation?
Where is growth genuinely available versus where are you hoping?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the renewal and growth readiness view'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the forecast to the one early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align it with. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test the expansion hypothesis', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Consumption trajectory, evidenced value and readiness shape renewal and growth hypotheses. Early signals help inspection; they are not forecast or expansion commitments. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: What is your forecast based on, and how far ahead does the signal reach?
Which growth opportunity is supported by consumption evidence?
What would you need to know now to avoid a surprise at renewal?
How does a peer distinguish customer growth intent from consumption headroom?
listenFor: Forecasts driven by relationship confidence rather than consumption evidence, growth assumed from headroom rather than intent, renewal risk surfacing late because nobody looked early, and commercial ownership blurring between CSAM and CE. Also note consumption trends read without seasonality.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the available MSXI Pane cannot resolve the chosen report question, optionally use a role starter or the current report's book of prompts, or ask for a narrower question aligned to the visual. If access, routing or measures remain unavailable, stop the data claim and use an approved sanitized excerpt or a clearly labeled fictional case to rehearse a renewal/growth row with dated usage signal, intent uncertainty, value evidence and account-owner question. Keep evidence, assumptions and gaps separate; fictional practice establishes no live result, commitment or approval, and requires no additional Team Member prework.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an early consumption signal and what it might help the account owner understand; starting a tracker or sending a handoff is not required. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized early signal checked and whether it changed an evidence request or renewal action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A renewal discussion assumes growth from a consumption signal alone. Compare usage, value and readiness evidence before treating the signal as a bounded growth hypothesis.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Renewal and growth readiness brings consumption and value evidence into an account conversation without assuming customer intent. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the facilitator-arranged expansion hypothesis example. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check customer filters, period, supplied hypothesis and available usage/outcome measures in the relevant report/view and available Copilot Pane; the home link alone confirms neither access nor the report route. Use the report's visual labels for a focused question. Keep missing fields or comparisons visible; no new Team Member artifact is required.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A signal can support a growth hypothesis but not a customer commitment. Look for a bounded risk or growth question linked to accountable account roles.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a signal can support a growth hypothesis but not a customer commitment. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

WF-X-RENEW-01.keyTakeaway: Use customer outcomes and verified timing to distinguish a supported expansion hypothesis from an assumption.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a signal can support a growth hypothesis but not a customer commitment. Manager support can help the team engage the account owner without forecasting unvalidated expansion.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help the facilitator keep a growth hypothesis bounded and route customer-facing renewal messaging through the accountable account roles. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, help the facilitator check customer filters, period, supplied hypothesis and available usage/outcome measures; keep a missing report, route or measure as a gap rather than a participant access test.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations without scoring individuals. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check the report/view, relevant visual, scope, period and source basis before one focused question: Which observation supports the hypothesis, and what stakeholder or value evidence could overturn it? Narrow a broad query using the visual's terminology; keep consequential judgment with its accountable human owner and do not turn the practice into a commitment or readiness test.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help the team engage the account owner without forecasting unvalidated expansion? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)
roles.description: Advances Enterprise solution-area opportunities through prospecting, discovery, proof, objection handling, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: PDM
roles.description: Leads partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executive stakeholders and governance around growth priorities. Coordinates partner growth and co-sell efforts, drives course correction through business reviews, and brings technical, sales, and marketing owners together while reserving investment and commercial commitments for authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.name: PMM
roles.description: Shapes partner marketing plans and campaigns around market needs, partner maturity, and joint business priorities. Recommends investments, coordinates approved claims, localization, activation, and qualified sales handoffs, and optimizes performance with attribution limits and reusable learning in view, leaving funding approvals with program owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS partner marketing plans, campaigns, approved claims, and qualified sales handoffs.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

activities.name: Turn one intake requirement into an accept, return or reroute card
activities.description: Prevents a broad partner request from becoming an unapproved PSA delivery obligation.
activities.prompt: Use only the conversation and approved materials already supplied. Use only the approved intake excerpt, stated CSA, single requirement and owner list I paste below. Draft a six-field triage card: requirement, technical uncertainty, evidence available, missing evidence, proposed disposition and accountable reviewer. Separate PSA architecture work from PTS cross-solution strategy and partner engineering build work. Recommend accept, return or reroute for this question only; explain the recommendation using exact input references, not assumed system access. Mark unclear ownership as unresolved. Do not retrieve partner records, contact anyone, promise delivery or allocate resources. Pause for the PSA technical authority to confirm scope and routing. Stop once the card and one next evidence request are ready, even if the broader intake remains incomplete.
activities.expectedOutput: One six-field triage card plus one draft evidence request, with unknowns visible.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA technical authority confirms scope and disposition. PTS confirms a strategic reroute; partner engineering accepts build handback. Stop if the accountable reviewer is unknown.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved intake excerpt with source/date; stated CSA; one requirement; known PSA, PTS and partner engineering owners. No full account export or inferred owners.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Paste one sanitized intake requirement, CSA and owner list.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for the six-field card with input references.
3. (2 min) Have the PSA technical authority challenge scope and routing.
4. (2 min) Record accept/return/reroute and one evidence request; stop without sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Prevents a broad partner request from becoming an unapproved PSA delivery obligation.

activities.name: Check one intake dependency against dated authoritative guidance
activities.description: Separates authoritative constraints from optimistic intake assumptions before architecture work expands.
activities.prompt: Investigate only the single technical dependency in my supplied intake sentence. Use the product/version and approved official source URLs I provide; if permitted, follow their official documentation links, not unrelated partner material. Produce a compact dependency note with the relevant published condition, citation, publication or update date when available, and today's access date. Distinguish what the guidance states from your inference about this requirement. If the source is unavailable, undated or version-mismatched, mark that limitation rather than substituting a confident answer. Do not claim that documentation proves our environment works or certifies compliance. Ask the PSA technical authority to confirm applicability. Stop after one supported dependency finding and one unresolved question, with no system changes.
activities.expectedOutput: One dependency note: condition, citation/date, version fit, inference boundary and unanswered question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA technical authority inspects the citation and applicability. Stop with a gap when authoritative guidance cannot be inspected; search snippets are not approval.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved dependency sentence, product/version, one or two permitted official documentation URLs and execution date. No private portal access implied.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one dependency, product/version and official URL.
2. (3 min) Ask Researcher for one cited, dated finding.
3. (2 min) Inspect the passage and version applicability with PSA.
4. (2 min) Record supported/unclear guidance and one gap; stop research.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Separates authoritative constraints from optimistic intake assumptions before architecture work expands.

activities.name: Reconcile two conflicting intake claims without inventing a third
activities.description: Turns conflicting assertions into a reviewable evidence task instead of a speculative architecture.
activities.prompt: Compare only the two approved statements and their evidence references that I provide about one technical risk. Create a contradiction ledger with claim A, claim B, what each source actually supports, the decision affected and one discriminating evidence request. Keep dates and product versions attached to each claim. Do not average conflicting claims into a new fact or assume the newest statement is correct. Classify the risk as evidenced, contradicted or unresolved and explain why. Identify whether the next check belongs to the PSA technical authority or partner engineering owner, without assigning work on their behalf. Pause for that authority to review the ledger. Stop at one unresolved risk and its next check; do not design the whole solution.
activities.expectedOutput: One contradiction ledger with a discriminating evidence request and proposed reviewer.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA validates reasoning; partner engineering confirms feasibility of a proposed technical check. If neither claim is supported, retain unresolved status and stop.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: two approved claim excerpts with source/date/version about the same requirement or risk; named technical reviewer. Missing evidence is not invented.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Paste two authorized claims about one risk with source/date.
2. (3 min) Generate the ledger and one discriminating question.
3. (2 min) Have PSA assess whether that question resolves the conflict.
4. (2 min) Record status and proposed owner; stop without assigning or sending work.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Turns conflicting assertions into a reviewable evidence task instead of a speculative architecture.

activities.name: Adapt intake triage for an SI reference or ISV tenant boundary
activities.description: Fits the technical question to the partner model without changing the PSA role or inventing delivery scope.
activities.prompt: Treat this as an optional intake variant, not an additional role or required step. Using only my approved intake requirement, partner model and interface notes, produce one model-specific triage card. If the partner is an SI, focus on a single integration boundary in a reference implementation and who owns site-specific adaptation. If the partner is an ISV, focus on one tenant-isolation assumption and who owns product implementation. Do not claim either model is inherently safer or already validated. Separate reusable assumptions from local unknowns and request one piece of evidence. Keep PSA technical authority, PTS strategy and partner engineering build ownership distinct. Pause for the PSA reviewer, then stop after the card without expanding to a portfolio assessment.
activities.expectedOutput: One SI adaptation-boundary or ISV tenant-boundary triage card and evidence request.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA and partner architect confirm model and boundary; only partner engineering accepts build work. Stop if the model or tenancy assumptions are unknown.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one sanitized requirement, explicit SI/ISV model, one interface/deployment note and owner list. Optional 15-minute follow-on; no prerequisite or extra role path.
activitySteps: 1. Select SI reference or ISV product and supply one approved requirement.
2. Ask Cowork for one model-specific boundary card and evidence gap.
3. Review the boundary with PSA and partner architect.
4. Keep or revise routing; stop at one boundary without implementation commitment.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Intake can mix partner ambition, cross-solution positioning and implementation requests. Separate those before solving anything. Today we decide whether one question is ready for PSA attention; a strategic customer-deal exception needs explicit sponsorship and must not redefine this baseline.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. One intake requirement, not the entire opportunity. 2. A claimed capability is not verified evidence. 3. PSA resolves CSA architecture questions; PTS steers cross-solution choices; partner engineers build. 4. Return and reroute are legitimate outcomes.
discussionQuestions: Which sentence is a technical requirement rather than a commercial aspiration? What evidence would change the routing decision? Who can accept the architecture question and provide the missing input?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Turn one intake requirement into an accept, return or reroute card'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At minute two, freeze one uncertainty. By minute six, review the artifact against supplied evidence. Use the last two minutes to accept, return or reroute; do not run the other practices as a sequence. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Adapt intake triage for an SI reference or ISV tenant boundary', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the disposition and evidence gap aloud. Confirm no one has silently accepted build delivery, resource allocation or customer commitments. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved, sanitized intake excerpt, the stated solution area, one requirement and known technical owners. Remove customer identifiers and secrets. Use authorized EPS research excerpts and date current technical guidance. Record any unconfirmed coverage, prioritization or regional assumption for SME review; do not treat an authored exercise as a policy mandate.
facilitatorQuestions: What single question are we accepting? What would make this a PTS decision or partner engineering task instead? Which missing input prevents a defensible recommendation?
listenFor: Bounded CSA scope, explicit evidence status and a named technical owner. Challenge invented access, automatic Partner Center/PMX retrieval, full-solution commitments and customer-deal motions presented as the baseline.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without approved intake or agent access, use a labeled synthetic requirement on paper. Produce a gap-and-owner card, not an inferred architecture or hidden search across partner systems.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where did we nearly confuse a plausible technical idea with an intake ready for action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a missing PSA intake input and draft a local clarification question. PSA approval is required before a human sends a request; no request or review date needs to be arranged for the huddle. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized intake gap clarified and whether it improved PSA disposition without implying build or capacity acceptance. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Track commercial policy and licensing changes that affect your accounts
activities.description: Set up a monitored, source-locked watch on the commercial policy and licensing guidance you rely on, so changes reach you before a customer raises them. In-huddle practice is one reviewed read-only result; recurrence is optional after approval.
activities.prompt: Check only [confirmed authoritative commercial-policy/licensing source list] for changes affecting [account/portfolio scope]. Quote and cite each change, show possible account impact and flag questions for the authoritative owner—don’t turn changes into commercial advice. Compare with [previous verified result, if available]; otherwise establish a baseline. Report access gaps. Run once, read-only; don’t schedule or send anything.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated first-run baseline or change digest quoting and citing each change, with plausible account impact and the named owner for anything requiring a ruling. Recurrence is a proposed configuration, or a manual repeat plan if unsupported; a scheduled result exists only after separate human approval and an actual later run.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE confirms the source list before the watch is enabled, and routes every interpretation to the accountable policy owner rather than acting on the summary.
activities.requiredContext: The authoritative policy and licensing sources your team treats as canonical; your account list; your escalation owners. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the small named scope and sources this tool can actually access, or supply permitted extracts.
2. Run the prompt once, read-only; on the first run create a dated baseline.
3. Review actual source coverage and findings before any scheduling.
4. Agree the fixed list of authoritative policy and licensing sources with your team before you enable anything.
5. Check the first digest quotes and cites each change rather than paraphrasing it.
6. Route every interpretation to the accountable policy owner rather than acting on the summary.
7. If recurrence is useful, approve its exact scope, reachable sources, cadence, output location and reviewer before enabling it where supported; otherwise use a manual repeat review.
8. Later, verify the first actual recurring or manually repeated result before relying on it. Any message, record correction or commitment is a separate human-reviewed action.
activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial policy changes are only a problem when the customer knows before you do. A locked source list is what separates a reliable watch from confident invention.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Policy questions found at approval cost weeks. Focus on finding the question early and routing it to the authoritative owner.
keyTalkingPoints: AI can assemble the context and possible questions. It cannot interpret policy, approve exceptions, or invent authority. The useful output is a routed question with evidence, not a guessed answer.
discussionQuestions: Which policy or licensing question most often causes rework? Where did an approval path surprise you? Which interpretation must come from an authoritative source?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the investment path against policy and approval requirements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from policy categories to one live deal question and the owner who can answer it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test policy and licensing assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Policy checks distinguish verified positions from unresolved interpretations. Use current authoritative guidance and route rulings beyond your authority instead of letting AI fill the gap. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: Which policy or licensing question changes this deal's next decision? What current authoritative source would settle it? How does another CE frame a self-contained question when the guidance is unavailable or ambiguous?
listenFor: Policy interpreted from memory; uncertainty left unflagged; approval paths discovered late; and questions that need an authoritative owner rather than a generated answer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one policy-question card: precise question, relevant deal fact, current guidance/version gap, authoritative owner and dependent commitment to hold. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which policy or commercial boundary is verified, which is still uncertain, and who can authorize the next step?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could take one open policy or licensing question to its authoritative owner rather than answering it yourself. Keep unresolved rulings pending; only the authoritative owner can confirm the position. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share the type of policy question and whether review clarified, changed or held the next step; omit restricted ruling text. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A licensing interpretation is plausible but not supported by the authoritative source. Frame the precise question and route it rather than treating a generated answer as policy.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A licensing or policy question needs a current authoritative reference and a clearly bounded interpretation route. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the precise question and current reference in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A model's interpretation cannot replace the policy owner. Look for a scoped question with a source and an authoritative decision route.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a model's interpretation cannot replace the policy owner. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

Review the supplied authorized messages and meetings from the relevant time range for technical questions answered more than once. Group by underlying problem, use authorized aggregate counts of distinct askers or customers, and compare the supplied prior report to return only new groups or groups with more distinct askers. Do not draft answers or repeat unchanged groups.
activities.expectedOutput: A technical-question delta table with dates, new/changed themes, authorized aggregate counts, missing history and one DSE-owned reuse question; an optional monitoring proposal stays unactivated.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSE decides whether a newly recurring question reflects a genuine change or a coincidence of timing, and whether it warrants an asset.

activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on reducing repeat work without applying one customer's answer to another customer's constraints.
keyTalkingPoints: Reuse is internal unless the content owner and data-sharing rules explicitly permit external or partner use.
Current execution: Use the approved team repository and current information-protection rules.
Fallback: Create a local team entry and named maintainer if no formal repository exists; do not share customer-specific content.
System of record: Approved technical asset repository and its owner/review record.
Optional AI boundary: AI may help sanitize and describe an asset, but DSE must review customer specificity, technical assumptions, and current validity.
discussionQuestions: What is genuinely reusable here?
Which customer-specific assumption must be removed?
Who can permit reuse and maintain the asset?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Sanitize and state assumptions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Catch the question that has started arriving', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Reuse assets carry source, permission, prerequisite and validation limits. Findable does not mean approved for publication or universal reuse. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one completed technical decision and approved artifact, validation/provenance notes, reuse permission and a proposed maintainer. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What assumption, permission or validation limit must travel with this technical asset? Who owns its maintenance? Which recurring question would a peer use to decide whether it is worth packaging?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one reusable technical-asset entry: sanitization, assumptions, rights gap, maintainer and evidence needed before reuse. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep reuse/publication on hold until rights, sanitization and actual validation are reviewed; no repository access is required for the draft.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What limitation would a new user miss without provenance or review status?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review a small reuse candidate for provenance, permission and validation limits; keep draft status until sharing is authorized. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized reuse boundary clarified and whether it reduced setup ambiguity or exposed a permission gap. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Assemble a one-request investment decision packet
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes for one investment line.
activities.prompt: Assemble a draft decision packet for the single supplied campaign investment request using only the authorized cost line, current requirement excerpts and approver list. Use five fields: purpose/PBP link, amount/currency/cost status, applicable cited requirement and effective date, evidence gaps, and authorized decision owner. Distinguish proposed, approved, committed and actual spend exactly as documented. Recommend hold, revise or seek authorized review, explaining the one gap that could change the recommendation. Do not infer eligibility, promise funding or reimbursement, fabricate approvals or claim ROI from campaign response. Ask the PMM to confirm the recommendation and evidence owner. Stop at the draft packet if a rule, amount or authority is unclear; do not submit requests, commit funds or send communications.
activities.expectedOutput: Five-field packet, one prioritized gap and PMM recommendation separate from funding approval.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM validates recommendation; authorized program/finance approvers decide eligibility/funding. Stop on unclear rules, costs or authority; no commitment/submission.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one authorized request, dated cost line with currency/state, current requirement excerpts with effective dates and actual approver list. No funding-system access assumed; undocumented approval/eligibility stays unknown.
activitySteps: 1. identify request, amount and state.
2. assemble five fields with dated references.
3. inspect gap and authority.
4. PMM chooses hold/revise/seek-review; stop before submission.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Reconcile one campaign investment variance without ROI claims
activities.description: Featured alternative: one cost line/window.
activities.prompt: Reconcile the supplied single-campaign budget line and authorized ledger extract for the stated reporting window and currency. Produce a three-state bridge for approved budget, committed spend and actual spend, keeping the supplied definitions and noting whether actual is included in committed. Calculate only comparable differences using supplied numbers and show the arithmetic; do not sum overlapping states or convert currencies without an approved rate. Mark missing values unknown, not zero. Identify one discrepancy, its evidence owner and the decision it could affect. Do not infer overspend from incomparable periods or calculate ROI from response or referral counts. Ask the PMM to accept the reconciliation or request finance clarification. Stop on unresolved definitions; do not change the ledger or commit funds.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-state cost bridge with comparable arithmetic, one discrepancy and PMM accept/clarify status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM checks governance impact; finance validates definitions. Stop on unresolved currencies/windows/overlap; no ledger change, funds commitment or ROI claim.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one authorized campaign/window ledger extract, approved budget line, cost-state definitions, currency and reconciliation date. No rate, ledger access or attribution model assumed; missing values stay unknown.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm campaign, window, currency and definitions.
2. Build three-state bridge from supplied amounts.
3. Check arithmetic, overlap and one discrepancy.
4. PMM accepts/clarifies; stop without ledger edits.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

agents.whenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
keyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

resources.title: What to Use When
resources.description: Routes a request to the best-fit Copilot agent and reserves Cowork for longer multi-output work. Useful early in a role path when tool choice is still forming.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Choose one investment line and trace amount, purpose, requirement and approver. AI assembles evidence but cannot approve funds or establish eligibility.
keyTalkingPoints: Check rule versions/effective dates and proposed/approved/committed/actual costs. Researcher cites current accessible published requirements; program owners resolve ambiguity. Cowork uses authorized extracts, not PMX/Partner Center/Marketplace/dashboard access. No eligibility, funding, approval or reimbursement promises; no response-based ROI or automatic submissions.
discussionQuestions: Which gap changes the recommendation? What cost state is recorded? Who actually has authority?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Assemble a one-request investment decision packet'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Carry only confirmed investment constraints into localization. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Tailor investment evidence to xPMM L100 or sPMM L200', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Marketing-investment judgment separates requirements, cost state and recommendation from approval or reimbursement. Resolve the material discrepancy with the authorized program or finance owner before any commitment. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Supply one authorized request, dated cost line, current requirements and actual approver list.
facilitatorQuestions: Which current rule, effective date and cost state support this request? Who can decide eligibility or funding? How would another PMM distinguish hold, revise and seek-review without importing historical amounts or implying approval?
listenFor: One request; dated rules; explicit cost state; real authority; unresolved evidence; no invented funding or returns.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, use permitted excerpts to complete one investment packet: request purpose, current rule and effective-date evidence or unknown, cost currency/state, authorized approver or unknown, and a hold, revise or seek-review recommendation. If no excerpts are available, use a labeled synthetic campaign for practice only. Preserve unknowns; do not substitute historical amounts or invented rules. Hold the recommendation for the program owner when current criteria are unverified.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where could a recommendation sound like an approval or reimbursement promise?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore an investment evidence gap and the question for its authorized program/finance owner. Do not submit or commit funds through this practice; no resolved gap or deadline is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized marketing-investment requirement or cost-state mismatch clarified and whether it reduced rework; no packet or funding disclosure is needed. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

WF-ORIENT-01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
WF-ORIENT-01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
WF-ORIENT-01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

primaryAgents.shortDescription: Deep research agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that produces structured, source-cited reports.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Combines work content and web research across multiple steps.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Customer, market, competitor, industry, and strategic research requiring citations. Researcher is also reachable inside Sales Agent, which uses it to answer research questions; call Researcher directly when you want the full sourced report rather than an answer inside a sales conversation.
keyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

resources.description: Official guidance for complex, multistep research across the web and permitted work data, including clarifying questions, structured source-cited reports, and prompting guidance.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for quick summaries or lightweight drafting.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Researcher agent, then state the research question and sources.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion.
