activities.name: Structure value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the Customer Plan
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved value/health evidence, expansion hypotheses and current Customer Plan context], draft feedback for the plan: evidenced outcome/health changes, unresolved risks, supported expansion questions and the next decision. Tie each proposed feedback item to its source and customer priority; distinguish analysis from customer-recognized value or agreed expansion. Preserve recorded owners and identify who must validate or accept the feedback. Do not edit the plan, create pipeline or infer customer intent.
activities.expectedOutput: Customer Plan feedback packet with evidenced value/health changes, expansion hypotheses, validation/acceptance gaps and next decisions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved value/health evidence; expansion hypotheses where supported; current Customer Plan and known decision/owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Use value and health evidence to update customer outcomes, sponsorship, renewal, and expansion actions. ATS: Connect technical progress and remaining constraints to the account strategy.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Closing the value and health loop changes account decisions rather than adding a separate scorecard or turning optimism into expansion. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Monitor value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the Customer Plan
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the customer plan, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Use value and health evidence to update customer outcomes, sponsorship, renewal, and expansion actions. ATS: Connect technical progress and remaining constraints to the account strategy. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Closing the value and health loop changes account decisions rather than adding a separate scorecard or turning optimism into expansion. Governed change review can expose what moved between observations without delegating judgment to unattended work.

activities.name: Structure intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [the approved intake packet, receiving criteria and any recorded receiving-owner response], draft an STU intake review packet. Show the customer decision, required evidence present/missing, receiving role, proposed first action and explicit acceptance, conditional acceptance, return or unknown status only where the response supports it. Identify the questions a receiving owner must settle and preserve recorded dates/ownership gaps. Do not accept the intake, assign ownership or update opportunity records.
activities.expectedOutput: STU intake review packet with evidence gaps, sourced acceptance/return status, receiving-role questions and proposed first action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved intake packet; known receiving criteria; recorded receiving-owner response/acceptance evidence and first-action context where available.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own intake acceptance, solution-area fit, value hypothesis, and pursuit path. SE: Assess technical context, evidence gaps, and discovery or validation needs.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Inspect intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action
activities.description: Ground the team discussion in authorized sales-system context without asking people to paste retrievable records.
activities.prompt: For Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], summarize sales evidence for [intake decision]: customer decision, recorded sender/receiver roles, acceptance evidence and proposed first action. Cite source/date; distinguish assignment or transfer status from accepted ownership. Identify the material evidence gap and the receiving-owner question needed for disposition. Do not infer technical readiness, assign owners, accept intake or change records; unavailable evidence stays unknown.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity ID and relevant authorized sales context, or a permitted dated extract identifying that opportunity.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own intake acceptance, solution-area fit, value hypothesis, and pursuit path. SE: Assess technical context, evidence gaps, and discovery or validation needs. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

activities.name: Rehearse intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action
activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation about intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own intake acceptance, solution-area fit, value hypothesis, and pursuit path. SE: Assess technical context, evidence gaps, and discovery or validation needs.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit. A labeled rehearsal can expose unclear questions before a real interaction without masquerading as customer evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: ATU has routed a Conversation or opportunity, but STU must determine whether the intake is actionable. A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the ATU packet as supplied context, not a reason to require ATU attendance. SSP owns intake acceptance, fit/value and pursuit path; SE examines technical context and evidence gaps. Accept, redirect or return deliberately.
Make acceptance visible in the existing pipeline rhythm; do not reward silent document transfer.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What customer decision is STU being asked to advance?
What evidence is missing for acceptance?
Who owns the next customer action?
suggestedTransitions: Compare peer assessments of the same intake, then record the explicit receiving-side disposition. A return should specify what is missing rather than simply saying the packet is incomplete.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action' (stu-w2-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: To customer Conversation preparation or back to ATU with explicit gaps.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Discovery -> Conversation intake
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare peer assessments of the same intake, then record the explicit receiving-side disposition. A return should specify what is missing rather than simply saying the packet is incomplete. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer decision is STU being asked to advance? Which missing item changes the disposition, and who can provide it?
What does another role or peer notice about one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A single disposition with rationale, sending/receiving owners, first action and next customer interaction; acceptance with no actionable evidence or owner.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If essential intake context is missing, prepare the clarification/return request rather than inferring ATU intent. A simulation cannot accept the intake for SSP/SE. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What made the intake actionable or not, and what would you ask a sender to make clearer next time?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could have the accountable receiving owner confirm one disposition and its first action, or return one precise evidence request to the sender. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one actual intake disposition, its rationale and first action; if blocked, the specific item returned and who must resolve it. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A routed intake contains background material but omits the customer decision and next owner. Compare whether it can be accepted, redirected or returned.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: STU intake makes the customer decision, missing evidence and first receiving action explicit before work is accepted. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the routed intake and open receiving question in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: ATU sending intent does not establish STU acceptance or readiness. Look for an explicit accept, condition or return decision with a first action. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: ATU sending intent does not establish STU acceptance or readiness. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Rehearse customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask
activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation about customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own the solution-specific business value, stakeholders, objections, and decision ask. SE: Own technical discovery questions, grounded responses, criteria, and evidence needs.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A focused Conversation advances a customer decision instead of covering every slide or duplicating role contributions. A labeled rehearsal can expose unclear questions before a real interaction without masquerading as customer evidence.

activities.name: Research customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public sources to inform customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, relevant objections and the decision ask. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates; distinguish public facts, inferred implications and questions to test with the customer. Flag relevant conflicts or staleness. Return a focused brief, not a scripted customer position. Do not invent objections for balance or treat market evidence as this customer's intent or agreement. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated, cited research brief supporting human review of customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own the solution-specific business value, stakeholders, objections, and decision ask. SE: Own technical discovery questions, grounded responses, criteria, and evidence needs.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A focused Conversation advances a customer decision instead of covering every slide or duplicating role contributions. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own the solution-specific business value, stakeholders, objections, and decision ask. SE: Own technical discovery questions, grounded responses, criteria, and evidence needs.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: STU has accepted the intake and must lead a Conversation that advances a specific customer decision. A focused Conversation advances a customer decision instead of covering every slide or duplicating role contributions.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP owns value, stakeholders, objections and the decision ask; SE owns technical discovery, grounded responses and criteria. Rehearse only the turns needed to expose fit and evidence, not a complete presentation.
Rehearse role contributions briefly; optimize for customer decision, not presentation coverage.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What must the customer decide or agree next?
Which questions and evidence will expose real fit?
How will each role contribute without duplicating the others?
suggestedTransitions: Move from decision ask to one consequential question or objection. Compare peer approaches, rehearse a short exchange, then note what the real customer interaction must establish.

A source Featured starting option is 'Rehearse customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask' (stu-w3-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Decision criteria and evidence gaps into solution/value design.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Conversation -> solution definition
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move from decision ask to one consequential question or objection. Compare peer approaches, rehearse a short exchange, then note what the real customer interaction must establish. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which question would expose that the proposed fit is wrong? How does each role's turn advance the same customer decision rather than repeat the other?
What does another role or peer notice about one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A specific decision ask, distinct SSP/SE turns, honest evidence questions and customer criteria; polished responses concealing unknowns or rehearsal reactions treated as customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: When customer facts or access are missing, rehearse structure with clearly labeled unknowns. Do not claim customer agreement or replace the real Conversation with simulated responses. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another role's question reveal about our decision ask or fit assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could refine one Conversation turn or evidence question, have its role owner review it, and use it in the next authorized customer interaction. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one question or decision criterion clarified in the real interaction, or what remained untested; no sensitive transcript is required. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: SSP and SE plan to cover similar material in a customer Conversation. Rehearse complementary turns around one decision ask and an unresolved objection.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A coordinated customer Conversation gives SSP and SE complementary contributions around a shared decision ask. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the decision ask and the example's SSP and SE contributions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Role-play and internal agreement do not confirm customer intent. Look for a coordinated conversation with a clear evidence question and role boundary. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: role-play and internal agreement do not confirm customer intent. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Research technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public technical sources to inform discovery criteria, evidence gaps and the next technical decision. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Use official product guidance for product requirements; cite material claims with source dates and separate facts from proposed criteria or validation questions. Flag relevant conflicts, staleness and applicability gaps. Return a focused evidence brief and questions for the technical decision owner; public research cannot confirm this customer's estate, criteria or technical acceptance. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated, cited research brief supporting human review of technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Clarify the customer outcome, value question, and business decision the technical work must support. SE: Lead technical discovery and define decision criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Clear technical criteria prevent repeated discovery and oversized proofs that do not resolve the customer's next decision. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The Conversation exposed customer questions, but technical criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision remain unresolved. Clear technical criteria prevent repeated discovery and oversized proofs that do not resolve the customer's next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP anchors the business/value question; SE leads technical criteria and discovery. Start with what the Conversation already established and identify the smallest missing evidence instrument, not an automatic PoC.
Do not default to a PoC; choose the smallest evidence instrument that resolves the decision.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What technical decision must the team support?
Which criteria and evidence gaps matter most?
What moves into design or bounded validation?
suggestedTransitions: Compare peers' criteria for the same decision, narrow to the unresolved criterion, then form a design/validation brief with evidence gaps and next technical decision.

A source Featured starting option is 'Research technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision' (stu-w4-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Decision criteria into solution design and bounded validation.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Conversation -> technical discovery -> solution definition
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare peers' criteria for the same decision, narrow to the unresolved criterion, then form a design/validation brief with evidence gaps and next technical decision. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which technical decision remains open? What evidence is sufficient to resolve the most consequential criterion, and which already-completed discovery should we not repeat?
What does another role or peer notice about one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Decision-critical criteria, source gaps and a small next evidence step; feature inventories, repeated discovery or a proof proposed without a decision it resolves.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If technical evidence is inaccessible, map criterion, unknown and responsible verifier. Sales records can supply context but cannot establish technical readiness or substitute for SE judgment. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which criterion changed after peer challenge, and what evidence do you still need before designing a validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify one criterion or evidence gap with the SE and relevant SSP context, or identify the smallest suitable evidence instrument. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one criterion confirmed/revised and the evidence required or checked; state if a proof was unnecessary or not yet authorized. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Conversation raised a technical question without explicit decision criteria. Identify one criterion and the smallest evidence instrument that could resolve its gap.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Technical discovery links a customer criterion to the evidence needed for the next technical decision. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the criterion, existing evidence and remaining uncertainty in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A preferred proof instrument is not automatically necessary. Look for a criterion linked to the smallest useful evidence question. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a preferred proof instrument is not automatically necessary. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Agreed criteria exist, but the preferred design and smallest credible validation path are unresolved. A proof is justified only when it resolves a material uncertainty not already answered by credible evidence; otherwise record a no-proof decision and rationale. When validation is justified, bound it to the smallest safe scope, a named execution owner, and an exit decision.
keyTalkingPoints: Compare solution/value paths against agreed criteria and first ask whether existing credible evidence resolves the uncertainty. SSP defines business success; SE defines technical success, scope, evidence and proof owner. If the evidence is sufficient, document a justified no-proof decision; if not, propose only the smallest safe validation with a named execution owner, success/exit criteria, and required approvals. A partner may execute. A proposed proof is not approval, and a documented no-proof decision is valid.
Name the execution owner, including a partner where appropriate; STU should not imply it runs every proof.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What uncertainty must the proof resolve? First ask whether credible existing evidence already resolves it; no proof is a valid decision.
Who will run it and what is the smallest useful scope? Answer only if validation is justified; the execution owner may be a partner.
What result triggers proceed, revise, or stop?
suggestedTransitions: Move from uncertainty to competing options. First decide whether credible existing evidence answers the question: document a justified no-proof rationale when it does, or propose the smallest bounded validation when it does not. Mark a proposed validation as awaiting approval, not completed evidence.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure solution design and the smallest bounded validation that resolves uncertainty' (stu-w5-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.

Source handoff: The validation proposal, with required human approval - or reviewed evidence when validation is already complete - plus remaining risks and the human-owned proceed, revise, or stop decision into scale planning.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Validation -> technical commitment
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move from uncertainty to competing options. First decide whether credible existing evidence answers the question: document a justified no-proof rationale when it does, or propose the smallest bounded validation when it does not. Mark a proposed validation as awaiting approval, not completed evidence. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What uncertainty must validation resolve, and what result means proceed, revise or stop? Could existing evidence answer the question without a new proof?

What does another role or peer notice about one solution option comparison and minimal validation proposal or explicit no-proof rationale with owner, measures and exit decision that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Small scope, measurable success/exit criteria, named executor and required approvals; STU assuming it runs every proof or a proposal being described as completed evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If execution owner, permissions, safe scope or required approval are unknown, record prerequisites and stop before execution. Do not generate test results or imply authorization. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did peer challenge remove from the proposed proof, and what still determines the human proceed/revise/stop decision?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could have one validation proposal or no-proof rationale reviewed by the authorized owner; execute only when its prerequisites and required approvals are met. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share either a no-proof rationale tied to sufficient existing evidence and the authorized owner’s decision, or the proposed scope/exit criterion plus approvals or prerequisites still open and the authorized owner’s decision; distinguish the two routes. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A proposed design proof may repeat credible existing evidence. Choose an explicit no-proof rationale if the uncertainty is resolved; otherwise identify the smallest safe validation, owner and exit decision.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Solution design asks whether existing evidence resolves the decision before a bounded validation is proposed. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Compare the example's architecture options, credible evidence and residual uncertainty.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Proof is not mandatory when credible existing evidence already resolves the decision. Look for a justified minimal validation or a defensible no-proof decision with a known execution owner. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: proof is not mandatory when credible existing evidence already resolves the decision. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

WF-STU-ARCH-01.keyTakeaway: Decide whether a bounded validation is justified by a material unresolved uncertainty; otherwise document an evidence-based no-proof decision.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when proof is not mandatory when credible existing evidence already resolves the decision. Manager support can support the smallest necessary evidence check without mandating a PoC or assuming who runs it.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Support either a defensible no-proof decision or a minimal validation question with a known execution owner; proof is not the default success condition.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that proof is not mandatory when credible existing evidence already resolves the decision; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. activities.name: Research scale, investment, partner, delivery, and usage-planning dependencies
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public sources on scale, investment, partner, delivery and usage-planning dependencies. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates and distinguish documented requirements, inference and proposed implications; flag relevant conflicts, staleness and access gaps. Return a focused dependency brief and questions for the accountable roles. General program or product guidance cannot confirm this customer's eligibility, funding, delivery capacity, partner acceptance or commitments. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public dependency brief for scale, investment, partner, delivery and usage planning, with accountable-role questions; eligibility, funding, capacity and commitments are not established.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own the solution opportunity, value case, investment ask, and pursuit coordination. SE: Define technical dependencies, scale risks, and the evidence needed for delivery.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one scale/delivery dependency map showing investment/partner need, technical risk, customer commitment evidence and accountable next action; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one scale/delivery dependency map showing investment/partner need, technical risk, customer commitment evidence and accountable next action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A connected scale path exposes investment, partner and delivery dependencies before a milestone is represented as committed. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Validation supports progress, but scale-engine, investment, partner, delivery, and usage-planning dependencies are fragmented. A connected scale path exposes investment, partner and delivery dependencies before a milestone is represented as committed.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP owns pursuit coordination/value/investment ask; SE defines technical dependencies and scale risks. Route investment decisions to authorized owners. Secure and validate customer commitment before marking a milestone committed; do not invent funding, capacity or partner availability.
Use authoritative systems and existing meeting sockets; do not create a local tracker as the product.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: Which scale or delivery path best fits the commitment?
What investment or partner dependency must activate now?
Which milestone is CSU-ready?
suggestedTransitions: Compare options for one blocking dependency, then connect owner, required evidence and next action in the execution map. Keep unapproved resources conditional before the CSU/partner handoff.

A source Featured starting option is 'Inspect scale, investment, partner, delivery, and usage-planning dependencies' (stu-w6-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Committed opportunity and milestone package to CSU/partner.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Technical commitment -> scale/investment/delivery
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare options for one blocking dependency, then connect owner, required evidence and next action in the execution map. Keep unapproved resources conditional before the CSU/partner handoff. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which dependency actually blocks the scale path? What evidence establishes customer commitment, and what remains an investment or delivery request rather than a decision?

What does another role or peer notice about one scale/delivery dependency map showing investment/partner need, technical risk, customer commitment evidence and accountable next action that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Resourced versus proposed actions, accountable dependencies, authoritative records and customer commitment; a local tracker being treated as the product or an investment ask treated as approval.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If resources, approvals or customer commitment are unverified, mark them open. Neither sales-system retrieval nor external research can establish delivery capacity or funding approval. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which dependency changed the path, and what would prevent you from calling the milestone committed today?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify one blocking dependency or customer-commitment fact with its authorized owner; route the investment question rather than resolving it by inference. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one dependency clarified and its status, evidence and owner; distinguish a routed request from an approved/resourced decision. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A scale path assumes investment, partner support and customer commitment are all secured. Review one dependency and distinguish a proposal from an authorized decision or evidenced commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A scale and delivery path connects technical, partner, investment and usage dependencies without assuming they are secured. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the example dependency and its customer and investment conditions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Partner involvement or funding interest does not establish a committed delivery milestone. Look for a dependency map with technical, commercial and receiving-owner boundaries. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: partner involvement or funding interest does not establish a committed delivery milestone. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

WF-STU-ORCH-01.keyTakeaway: Recommend a resourced scale/delivery path and route investment decisions to the authorized owner; secure and validate the customer commitment before marking a milestone committed.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when partner involvement or funding interest does not establish a committed delivery milestone. Manager support can help coordinate the authoritative delivery and investment decisions before a commitment is represented.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help separate proposed support from accepted delivery or funding decisions; do not treat an attractive scale path as a committed milestone.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that partner involvement or funding interest does not establish a committed delivery milestone; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help coordinate the authoritative delivery and investment decisions before a commitment is represented? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Prepare the committed-milestone handoff packet
activities.description: Structure supplied commitment and validation evidence for later CSU review.
activities.prompt: Using [the approved commitment/validation artifacts and receiving criteria], prepare a committed-milestone handoff packet with customer outcome, milestone, evidence, design decisions, dependencies, risks, residual STU obligations, proposed receiving owners, first actions, review point, and return conditions. Mark every owner as proposed until accepted. Do not accept the handoff, assign CSU ownership, or make delivery, technical, commercial, or system decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: A committed-milestone packet ready for CSU review, not an accepted handoff.
activities.humanCheckpoint: STU owners approve the packet; CSU later accepts, conditionally accepts, or returns it.
activities.requiredContext: Approved commitment and validation artifacts plus known receiving criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Transfer customer value, commercial/solution commitments, timing, and specialist ownership. SE: Transfer design evidence, validation results, technical risks, dependencies, and decision records.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one STU committed-milestone packet section with customer commitment evidence, residual obligations, proposed receivers and return conditions; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one STU committed-milestone packet section with customer commitment evidence, residual obligations, proposed receivers and return conditions. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Mark receiving owners as proposed until accepted; STU approves the packet while CSU later chooses its separate disposition.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A usable sending-side milestone packet prevents CSU from reconstructing pursuit history without confusing STU readiness with CSU acceptance. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Monitor handoff evidence readiness before CSU review
activities.description: Track approved handoff evidence within STU without treating monitoring as receiving acceptance.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of handoff evidence readiness before csu review, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Transfer customer value, commercial/solution commitments, timing, and specialist ownership. SE: Transfer design evidence, validation results, technical risks, dependencies, and decision records. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one STU committed-milestone packet section with customer commitment evidence, residual obligations, proposed receivers and return conditions, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one STU committed-milestone packet section with customer commitment evidence, residual obligations, proposed receivers and return conditions. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Track STU evidence readiness only; an evidence change is not CSU acceptance or delivery readiness.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A usable sending-side milestone packet prevents CSU from reconstructing pursuit history without confusing STU readiness with CSU acceptance. Governed change review can expose what moved between observations without delegating judgment to unattended work.

activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one STU committed-milestone packet section with customer commitment evidence, residual obligations, proposed receivers and return conditions; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The opportunity has a committed milestone, but CSU or the delivery partner may not yet have actionable context. A usable sending-side milestone packet prevents CSU from reconstructing pursuit history. The customer commitment that STU records is distinct from CSU acceptance of the milestone; the receiving CSU owner makes that separate disposition after review.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP transfers customer value, the customer commitment and timing; SE transfers design, validation and residual technical risks. A customer commitment does not constitute CSU acceptance. All receiving owners remain proposed until the appropriate CSU owner separately accepts; the huddle stays within STU and CSU disposition happens outside it.
Keep the huddle within STU. Prepare an actionable receiving-owner request, but do not treat preparation as CSU acceptance.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: Is the milestone specific and accepted? Distinguish evidence of the customer's commitment from CSU's separate acceptance, conditional acceptance, or return.
Can CSU and delivery act without reconstructing design history?
Which risk remains with STU after handoff?
suggestedTransitions: Walk through the packet from a receiver's perspective, compare gaps, then approve only the STU sending-side request. Name the separate CSU acceptance/conditional acceptance/return decision still needed.

A source Featured starting option is 'Prepare the committed-milestone handoff packet' (stu-w7-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: STU sends the committed-milestone packet to CSAM and the appropriate CSA domain; CSU accepts, conditionally accepts, or returns it outside this huddle.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Committed opportunity -> adoption/consumption execution
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Walk through the packet from a receiver's perspective, compare gaps, then identify what the STU sending-side request would need for approval; this conversation does not grant it. Name the separate CSU acceptance/conditional acceptance/return decision still needed. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Could CSU act without reconstructing the design history? What customer commitment must STU evidence, which obligations stay with STU, and what separate CSU decision will accept, conditionally accept, or return the proposed handoff?

What does another role or peer notice about one STU committed-milestone packet section with customer commitment evidence, residual obligations, proposed receivers and return conditions that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Specific commitment evidence, residual STU obligations, proposed receiving owners and return conditions; packet approval or monitoring being mislabeled as CSU acceptance.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If receiving criteria or approval are missing, record the gap and proposed owner. A monitor tracks evidence readiness only; it cannot assign CSU ownership or accept a handoff. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did peer review show a receiver would still have to reconstruct, and what must stay STU-owned after transfer?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could close one packet gap or have STU owners review the bounded CSU acceptance request before sending it to the appropriate CSAM/CSA domain; record customer commitments separately from the receiving owner’s later disposition. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one packet improvement and any later actual CSU disposition, clearly separated from STU approval; include any residual obligation still open. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: STU has evidence of a customer commitment, but a receiving CSU owner has not yet reviewed the milestone. Prepare the acceptance request and residual obligations; CSU acceptance, conditional acceptance or return is separate.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A committed-milestone handoff carries customer evidence and residual STU obligations to a separate CSU receiving decision. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the sending-side packet, commitment evidence and proposed receivers in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: STU's evidence of customer commitment is separate from CSU's acceptance, conditional acceptance or return. Look for a specific packet section with residual STU obligations and a separate receiving decision. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: STU's evidence of customer commitment is separate from CSU's acceptance, conditional acceptance or return. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.
