activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation about reusable pursuit learning, limitations, safeguards, and feedback. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for reusable pursuit learning, limitations, safeguards, and feedback.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Capture reusable value, objection, competition, and pursuit patterns with context. SE: Package validated technical assets, evidence, limitations, and safeguards.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one reusable pursuit lesson or retirement recommendation with observed evidence, applicability limits, safeguards and findable context; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one reusable pursuit lesson or retirement recommendation with observed evidence, applicability limits, safeguards and findable context. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A contextual lesson is useful when another pursuit can understand where it worked, where it failed and what safeguards remain—not when upload volume increases. activities.name: Monitor reusable pursuit learning, limitations, safeguards, and feedback
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of reusable pursuit learning, limitations, safeguards, and feedback, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Capture reusable value, objection, competition, and pursuit patterns with context. SE: Package validated technical assets, evidence, limitations, and safeguards. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one reusable pursuit lesson or retirement recommendation with observed evidence, applicability limits, safeguards and findable context, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one reusable pursuit lesson or retirement recommendation with observed evidence, applicability limits, safeguards and findable context. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A contextual lesson is useful when another pursuit can understand where it worked, where it failed and what safeguards remain—not when upload volume increases. Governed change review can expose what moved between observations without delegating judgment to unattended work.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The pursuit produced useful patterns and failure signals, but they may remain trapped in the account team. A contextual lesson is useful when another pursuit can understand where it worked, where it failed and what safeguards remain—not when upload volume increases.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP captures value/objection/competition patterns; SE packages validated technical assets and limitations. Distinguish actual observed learning from an untested pattern, account-specific detail or generated coaching.
Reward contextual reuse, not volume of uploaded artifacts.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What proved reusable and under what conditions?
What failed or changed after delivery?
Where should the asset live so peers can trust it?
suggestedTransitions: Compare one pursuit lesson with a peer's context, then choose reuse, retirement or feedback into discovery/design. Submit or share only the transferable, permission-safe part through an appropriate existing location.

A source Featured starting option is 'Rehearse reusable pursuit learning, limitations, safeguards, and feedback' (stu-w8-p2); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Feedback to ATU discovery, STU design, CSU delivery, and the Topic Library.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Execution -> reuse and feedback loop
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare one pursuit lesson with a peer's context, then choose reuse, retirement or feedback into discovery/design. If you later choose to submit or share, only the transferable, permission-safe part belongs in an appropriate existing location. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What proved reusable, for whom and under what conditions? What failed or changed after delivery, and what would make another team distrust this asset?

What does another role or peer notice about one reusable pursuit lesson or retirement recommendation with observed evidence, applicability limits, safeguards and findable context that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Traceable observations, applicability limits, safeguards, findability and a retire/reuse decision; asset counts, unverified generalizations or confidential customer context.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without evidence, permission or a meaningful applicability boundary, keep the item as an internal question/lesson rather than a validated reusable asset. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did a peer's context reveal about the limits of the lesson you wanted to reuse?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check one lesson's evidence and safeguards, improve an existing asset where appropriate, or retire one misleading pattern; preserve context and review ownership. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one reuse/retire/feedback decision with the evidence and limitation that mattered; do not claim another team used it unless observed. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A pursuit produced a reusable pattern with a failure condition others need to understand. Review whether to reuse, qualify or retire the lesson without requiring an upload.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Reusable pursuit learning includes the conditions, limitations and failures that another team needs to judge applicability. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the permitted lesson, provenance and reuse question in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Findable content is not automatically safe or useful to reuse. Look for a qualified reuse, retirement or feedback recommendation with a maintainer. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: findable content is not automatically safe or useful to reuse. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

WF-STU-ASSET-01.keyTakeaway: Choose what to reuse, retire, or feed back into discovery and design.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when findable content is not automatically safe or useful to reuse. Manager support can support the reviewer or maintenance route without forcing publication of every lesson.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Encourage a qualified reuse, retirement or feedback discussion rather than an upload requirement or an assumption that findable content is safe.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that findable content is not automatically safe or useful to reuse; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support the reviewer or maintenance route without forcing publication of every lesson? keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. activities.name: Structure committed-milestone acceptance, evidence gaps, receiving owners, and review date
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [the approved committed-milestone handoff packet, receiving criteria and acceptance evidence], draft a CSU acceptance review packet. Show outcome/milestone, proof received/missing, dependencies, residual STU obligations, receiving owner and recorded acceptance/conditions/return status or unknown. Identify first-action and review-date proposals separately from confirmed commitments. A committed record or routed packet does not establish CSU acceptance. Do not accept the handoff, transfer ownership or update milestones.
activities.expectedOutput: CSU acceptance review packet with source-backed disposition, missing evidence, residual obligations, receiving-owner gaps and proposed review point.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved committed-milestone packet; known receiving criteria; actual receiving-owner acceptance/conditions/return evidence where available; known review timing.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Accept orchestration accountability, customer stakeholders, success outcome, and review rhythm. CSA: Accept technical work within the appropriate domain and surface readiness or boundary gaps. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Assess engineering execution or acceleration needs; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A receiving-side milestone disposition makes execution responsibility explicit instead of treating an STU customer commitment as automatic CSU acceptance. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

Cite records/dates; distinguish assignment and populated status from confirmed receiver acceptance. Name missing evidence and the question for the accountable receiving role; mark proposed actions or dates unconfirmed. Do not infer technical/delivery readiness, accept the milestone or change records.

activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity ID and relevant authorized sales context, or a permitted dated extract identifying that opportunity.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Accept orchestration accountability, customer stakeholders, success outcome, and review rhythm. CSA: Accept technical work within the appropriate domain and surface readiness or boundary gaps. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Assess engineering execution or acceleration needs; role is not represented in the current app. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A receiving-side milestone disposition makes execution responsibility explicit instead of treating an STU customer commitment as automatic CSU acceptance. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

activities.name: Monitor committed-milestone acceptance, evidence gaps, receiving owners, and review date
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of committed-milestone acceptance, evidence gaps, receiving owners, and review date, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Accept orchestration accountability, customer stakeholders, success outcome, and review rhythm. CSA: Accept technical work within the appropriate domain and surface readiness or boundary gaps. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Assess engineering execution or acceleration needs; role is not represented in the current app. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A receiving-side milestone disposition makes execution responsibility explicit instead of treating an STU customer commitment as automatic CSU acceptance. Governed change review can expose what moved between observations without delegating judgment to unattended work.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A committed opportunity is moving into execution, but the milestone, evidence, and receiving responsibilities need acceptance. A receiving-side milestone disposition makes execution responsibility explicit instead of treating an STU customer commitment as automatic CSU acceptance.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the supplied STU packet within CSU. CSAM accepts orchestration accountability; CSA assesses domain technical work; engineering acceleration is conditional. Choose accept, conditionally accept or return, with first actions and residual STU obligations.
Keep the huddle within CSU. Use the supplied STU handoff packet and route specific gaps back asynchronously; STU roles do not need to attend.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What exactly is committed and how will success be recognized?
Which receiver owns each first action?
What must return to STU before execution starts?
suggestedTransitions: Compare CSAM/CSA assessments of one milestone, then record the actual receiving-side decision and any conditions. Route precise gaps back asynchronously; STU attendance is unnecessary.

facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare CSAM/CSA assessments of one milestone, then distinguish a proposed disposition from any actual receiving-side decision and its conditions. If useful, precise gaps could be taken back through the existing asynchronous route; STU attendance is unnecessary. No acceptance or transfer is required for the huddle. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What exactly is committed and what would completion mean? Which receiving owner can act now, and what must return to STU before execution starts?
What does another role or peer notice about one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A documented disposition, rationale, gaps, receiving owners, first action/review point and return conditions; sales commitment or monitoring output being treated as accepted technical completion.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the packet is incomplete, record conditional acceptance only if the responsible owner actually chooses it; otherwise return specific gaps. Do not infer readiness from sales-system context. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which packet gap most affected acceptance, and did the role boundaries make the first action clearer?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could confirm one disposition/condition with the responsible receiving owner or return one precise missing-evidence request to STU. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one actual accept/conditional accept/return record, its first action, review point and any unresolved residual STU obligation. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A customer-committed milestone arrives from STU, but a receiving responsibility or prerequisite remains unclear. Review acceptance, conditional acceptance or return from the CSU perspective.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: CSU intake tests whether a customer-committed milestone has the evidence, prerequisites and receiving ownership needed to act. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the proposed intake, commitment evidence and receiving-role boundaries in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A customer's commitment does not remove CSU's receiving acceptance decision. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare one milestone's outcome link with a peer, then identify any missing owner/dependency/review decision and the authoritative record. You could propose a plan change if useful; actual updates remain with the accountable owner. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer outcome does this milestone serve? Are owner, dependency and review point executable, and what should remain outside this plan?
What does another role or peer notice about one accepted milestone's Customer Success Plan link to outcome, technical/adoption work, owners, risks and review decision that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Accepted milestones linked to outcomes, owners, dependencies and review decisions; implied new ownership, undifferentiated CSA work or CAIP-specific rhythms generalized to every CSU team.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without an accepted milestone or confirmed owner/outcome link, capture the planning gap rather than call the plan executable. No new cadence or FDE attendance is assumed. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did peer input change about the outcome link or the dependency we thought was clear?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could have CSAM and the relevant CSA owner check one plan link or dependency; keep any required record change with its accountable owner. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one milestone-to-outcome link improved, an owner/dependency clarified or an unresolved planning question, using a permission-safe verbal summary. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.

activities.name: Research consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public sources on consequential health risks, evidence limits, interventions and escalation considerations. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates; separate facts, possible causes and proposed implications, flagging relevant conflicts or stale evidence. Return a focused brief and questions for the appropriate CSAM/CSA or domain owner. Public research cannot diagnose this customer, verify private telemetry or sentiment, assign an intervention owner or infer health from missing evidence. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public health-risk/intervention context brief with evidence limits and questions for the appropriate human/domain owner; not a customer diagnosis or ownership assignment.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.

CSA: Validate technical health, domain-specific risk, evidence, and feasible intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Add engineering execution risk where applicable; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

activities.requiredContext: Permitted access to relevant Sales sources; Account name or TPID, or Opportunity ID for a particular-deal question; one customer-health risk under review; available dated risk/commitment evidence, source coverage and known owner, intervention or escalation context.

CSA: Validate technical health, domain-specific risk, evidence, and feasible intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Add engineering execution risk where applicable; role is not represented in the current app. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Inspecting one consequential risk deeply helps the team act on the threat to the customer outcome rather than chase every visible signal. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

activities.name: Monitor consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Integrate customer, stakeholder, delivery, support, and success-plan signals and own intervention orchestration. CSA: Validate technical health, domain-specific risk, evidence, and feasible intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Add engineering execution risk where applicable; role is not represented in the current app. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.

activities.name: Organize observed usage gaps and competing cause hypotheses
activities.description: Structure supplied usage and milestone evidence without turning correlation into a causal or technical judgment.
activities.prompt: Using [approved usage/milestone evidence and decision criteria], organize observed usage gaps, milestone status, customer-outcome links, and competing cause hypotheses. Separate direct observations from causal hypotheses and identify missing telemetry, support, or customer evidence. Do not infer causes, select the intervention, assign ownership, or make technical judgments; present questions for accountable humans.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-organized usage-gap brief with observations, competing hypotheses, missing evidence, and questions for accountable owners.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved usage and milestone artifacts plus the human-owned criteria for deciding what evidence matters.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Own customer-success planning, customer outcome connection, stakeholder action, and orchestration; align consumption-plan actions with the responsible CSA. CSA: Diagnose technical drivers and blockers within the relevant CSA domain and propose intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Accelerate engineering work where applicable and clarify execution limits; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one observed usage/milestone gap with competing cause hypotheses, missing evidence and the human-owned intervention question; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one observed usage/milestone gap with competing cause hypotheses, missing evidence and the human-owned intervention question. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Organize observations and competing hypotheses only; CSAM/CSA humans diagnose and select the intervention within their responsibilities.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: An intervention is useful when it changes realized usage in service of a customer outcome, not merely a consumption number. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates; separate documented behavior, causal hypotheses and proposed interventions, flagging relevant conflicts or stale guidance. Return a focused brief, alternative explanations and the next evidence question for the human owner. Public research cannot verify private usage figures, customer intent or a diagnosis; missing evidence is unknown. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public usage-gap brief separating documented behavior, competing cause hypotheses and possible interventions, with next evidence questions; no private-data verification or diagnosis.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.

Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Accelerate engineering work where applicable and clarify execution limits; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one observed usage/milestone gap with competing cause hypotheses, missing evidence and the human-owned intervention question; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Deployment or consumption is behind the commitment, and the team needs to distinguish technical, adoption, and nontechnical causes. An intervention is useful when it changes realized usage in service of a customer outcome, not merely a consumption number.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate observed deployment/usage gaps from technical, adoption and nontechnical cause hypotheses. CSAM owns outcome/stakeholder orchestration; the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain and aligns consumption actions; engineering acceleration remains conditional.
Do not flatten CSA variants; name the domain and bring the right specialist.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What explains the gap between commitment and realized usage?
Which intervention changes the trajectory?
How will usage connect to a customer outcome rather than volume alone?
suggestedTransitions: Compare hypotheses for one observed gap, identify discriminating evidence, then let the appropriate human choose an intervention and milestone. Keep the usage plan tied to outcome.

A source Featured starting option is 'Organize observed usage gaps and competing cause hypotheses' (csu-w6-p3); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Usage evidence into value realization and risk feedback.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Deployment -> adoption/consumption -> realized usage
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare hypotheses for one observed gap, identify discriminating evidence, then discuss whether an intervention or milestone change is justified; any actual decision remains with the appropriate human. Keep the usage plan tied to outcome. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which part of the gap is observed and which is a cause hypothesis? What evidence could distinguish the competing explanations before choosing an intervention?
What does another role or peer notice about one observed usage/milestone gap with competing cause hypotheses, missing evidence and the human-owned intervention question that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Actual usage/milestone evidence, domain boundaries, competing hypotheses, owner and outcome link; sales records presented as telemetry or Cowork selecting a technical cause/intervention.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If post-sales evidence is unavailable, structure the gap and evidence request only. Sales Agent supplies bounded sales/commitment context, not usage, health, telemetry, support history or causality. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which hypothesis became less credible after peer challenge, and what must a domain owner verify before action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check one discriminating evidence item with the responsible CSA/CSAM owner or test one authorized intervention; retain the causal uncertainty until evidence supports it. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share observed usage change or a still-open evidence gap, intervention owner/milestone and customer-outcome link; do not imply causality from correlation. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Realized usage trails a commitment, with competing technical and adoption explanations. Test one cause hypothesis without making the CSA owner of every shortfall.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Closing a commitment-to-usage gap starts by separating technical, adoption and nontechnical explanations. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the observed usage gap and competing cause hypotheses in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Technical, adoption and nontechnical causes require different owners. Look for a cause hypothesis with missing evidence and the relevant CSA domain identified. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: technical, adoption and nontechnical causes require different owners. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Structure value evidence, baseline, caveats, and questions for customer validation
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved value evidence, baseline, definitions and caveats], draft a packet for the customer value-validation conversation. Show each observed measure/outcome, source and period, baseline/comparison, attribution limits, unsupported assertions and the question/customer decision still needed. Keep claims awaiting customer validation unless actual customer confirmation is supplied; quote that evidence separately rather than infer recognition from analysis or rehearsal. Preserve recorded evidence owners and mark follow-up proposals unaccepted. Do not declare realized/customer-recognized value, share claims or update records.
activities.expectedOutput: Customer value-validation packet with measures/baseline, source periods, attribution limits, unresolved assertions and customer questions; recognition only where actual customer confirmation is evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved value evidence; baseline, periods/definitions and caveats; known decision criteria; actual customer-confirmation evidence if available.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Own the customer outcome narrative, stakeholder validation, and value review. CSA: Validate technical progress, usage drivers, cost/optimization evidence, and limitations. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Contribute engineering outcome evidence where applicable; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A defensible value narrative shows what changed for the customer against a baseline and what still needs their validation. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Research authoritative benchmarks and methods relevant to value validation
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public benchmarks and measurement methods relevant to a customer value-validation conversation. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates and explain applicability limits, caveats and relevant conflicts or staleness. Separate published findings from proposed value claims and return a focused brief with the next customer-validation questions. Benchmarks are context, not this customer's baseline or realized results; any proposed customer value remains awaiting validation. Research or rehearsal is not customer recognition. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public methods/benchmarks brief with applicability limits, caveats and customer-validation questions; not this customer's baseline, realized value or recognition.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Own the customer outcome narrative, stakeholder validation, and value review. CSA: Validate technical progress, usage drivers, cost/optimization evidence, and limitations. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Contribute engineering outcome evidence where applicable; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Use external methods/benchmarks as context, not as proof of this customer's realized value or baseline.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A defensible value narrative shows what changed for the customer against a baseline and what still needs their validation. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

activities.name: Rehearse the customer value-validation conversation
activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation that tests the evidence package, baseline, caveats, and next customer decision. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement. Label every value claim as awaiting customer validation; do not present analysis, research, or rehearsal as customer recognition.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for customer-recognized value evidence, baseline, caveats, and next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Own the customer outcome narrative, stakeholder validation, and value review. CSA: Validate technical progress, usage drivers, cost/optimization evidence, and limitations. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Contribute engineering outcome evidence where applicable; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A defensible value narrative shows what changed for the customer against a baseline and what still needs their validation. A labeled rehearsal can expose unclear questions before a real interaction without masquerading as customer evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Technical progress and usage exist, but the team has not assembled evidence the customer recognizes as value. A defensible value narrative shows what changed for the customer against a baseline and what still needs their validation.
keyTalkingPoints: CSAM owns the customer-outcome narrative and validation; CSA validates technical progress, usage/cost/optimization evidence and limits; FDE contributes only where applicable. Internal activity, external benchmarks and role-play reactions are not customer-recognized value.
Ask the customer to validate value; internal activity is not itself an outcome.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What changed for the customer and against which baseline?
Which claims are verified, inferred, or still missing?
What customer decision should the evidence enable?
suggestedTransitions: Compare one proposed value claim with its evidence, qualify it where necessary, then prepare a short narrative and explicit customer validation question rather than declare value proved.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure value evidence, baseline, caveats, and questions for customer validation' (csu-w7-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Value evidence to ATU planning, renewal, health, and expansion decisions.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Adoption/consumption -> value realization
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare one proposed value claim with its evidence, qualify it where necessary, then prepare a short narrative and explicit customer validation question rather than declare value proved. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What changed against which baseline? Which claims are verified, inferred or missing, and what should the customer validate before the next decision?
What does another role or peer notice about one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Baseline/source/date, caveats, unresolved claims and a customer decision ask; metrics without outcome meaning, external benchmarks treated as account results or rehearsal treated as validation.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without baseline or customer confirmation, retain the claim as unverified. Research can supply methods/benchmarks only; it cannot establish account-specific value. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did peer review make you remove or qualify in the value claim?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check one value claim with its evidence owner or take one reviewed validation question to the customer through the appropriate owner. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one claim validated, corrected or still unverified; include baseline/caveat and the next ask rather than a sensitive evidence packet. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A value narrative combines observed technical progress with an unverified benefit claim. Compare baseline and caveats and prepare the remaining customer-validation question.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Customer value claims need a baseline, suitable measurement and customer validation beyond deployment or usage alone. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the proposed claim, measurement limits and customer evidence in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Usage or deployment data does not establish every customer outcome. Look for a caveated claim and a specific remaining customer-validation question. The starting prompt or required inputs still need product-owner clarification; do not fill the gap with an invented capability. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: usage or deployment data does not establish every customer outcome. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Rehearse renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback
activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation about renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Synthesize success-plan progress, health, usage, value, and stakeholder readiness. Conditional only where applicable: CSA: Validate technical adoption gaps, platform health, and feasible expansion prerequisites.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Evidence-backed renewal and expansion feedback helps account owners act without turning health optimism into forecast or an unauthorized commercial promise. A labeled rehearsal can expose unclear questions before a real interaction without masquerading as customer evidence.

activities.name: Inspect renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback
activities.description: Ground the team discussion in authorized sales-system context without asking people to paste retrievable records.
activities.prompt: For [Account Name or TPID] or Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], summarize relevant sales-record evidence and proposed Customer Plan feedback for [renewal-risk or earned-expansion question]. Cite source/date; distinguish confirmed customer commitments from inferred potential, and sales signals from missing value, health or delivery evidence. Name the next validation question and accountable role. Propose a correction or next decision for human review, not a renewal/expansion verdict; do not approve, commit or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: Permitted access to relevant Sales sources; Account name or TPID, or Opportunity ID for a particular-deal question; one renewal-risk or earned-expansion question; available dated sales, value/health or delivery evidence and relevant Customer Plan/owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Synthesize success-plan progress, health, usage, value, and stakeholder readiness. Conditional only where applicable: CSA: Validate technical adoption gaps, platform health, and feasible expansion prerequisites. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Evidence-backed renewal and expansion feedback helps account owners act without turning health optimism into forecast or an unauthorized commercial promise. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. activities.name: Structure renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved renewal-risk/expansion evidence, Customer Plan context and decision criteria], draft plan feedback with value/health proof, risks, expansion hypotheses, owner-confirmation questions and next decision. Keep expansion need hypothetical unless customer evidence supports it. Use the actual work object and commitment status: for milestones fitting an open opportunity's Customer Priority and commercial scope, committed work may remain with its CSU owner and uncommitted work goes to STU review; a new unaligned opportunity goes to ATU discovery. Include SAE for Services renewal/pursuit needs. Preserve recorded ownership but do not infer acceptance, create pipeline, set forecast, promise terms, transfer work or edit the plan.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal/expansion Customer Plan feedback with supported value/health evidence, hypothesis/confirmation status, work-object-specific routing questions and next decisions; no assumed acceptance or record action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved renewal-risk/expansion evidence; Customer Plan and known decision criteria; actual opportunity/Customer Priority/commercial scope and milestone commitment status where available; recorded owner/customer-confirmation evidence.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Synthesize success-plan progress, health, usage, value, and stakeholder readiness. Conditional only where applicable: CSA: Validate technical adoption gaps, platform health, and feasible expansion prerequisites.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Evidence-backed renewal and expansion feedback helps account owners act without turning health optimism into forecast or an unauthorized commercial promise. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.
