facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Reuse only works when an asset has enough context for someone else to trust and adapt it.
keyTalkingPoints: Package purpose, prerequisites, steps, parameters, validation checks, limitations, owner, and example use.
Remove sensitive content before reuse.
Use Skill Blueprints for repeatable workflows that are not validated assets yet.
discussionQuestions: What did you build recently that another SE will rebuild?
What context would make someone trust and adapt it?
What should not be reused without review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Package a reusable technical asset with context'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect the selected asset's prerequisites, provenance and actual validation status. A blueprint or workflow walkthrough is specification review, not an installed, executed or tested skill. Name the human implementation/test owner before any promotion or publication. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Sanitize and validate the reusable asset', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical reuse depends on provenance, permissions, prerequisites and validation limits. A workflow outline or Skill Blueprint is a draft, not an implemented or tested capability. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
facilitatorQuestions: Which asset is worth reusing?
What context would make it usable by another SE?
What must be removed, validated, or tested before sharing?
What did another SE need to know before reusing your asset safely?
listenFor: Assets without owner, missing prerequisites, sensitive content, unclear limitations, and reuse patterns that should become blueprints.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one reusable-asset card: purpose, prerequisites, source/provenance, sensitive detail removed, validation status, limit and implementation/test owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep reuse/publication on hold until rights, sanitization and actual validation are reviewed; no repository access is required for the draft.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical lesson is reusable, what needs review before others apply it, and where should it live?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review a small reuse candidate from existing work or draft a workflow outline. Check provenance, permissions, prerequisites and technical limits with its owner; keep draft status until reuse is authorized. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized reuse lesson and whether it reduced explanation or setup effort; no asset upload or distribution is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A reusable script lacks clear validation context and permission limits. Review one representative case and keep draft status until its owner confirms appropriate reuse.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Technical reuse depends on provenance, applicability and known validation limits, not just a useful-looking artifact. SE tests customer technical criteria; plans, hypotheses and rehearsals do not establish an executed test or customer acceptance.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the example artifact's source, intended use and known limits.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A useful example is not universally valid or automatically reusable. Look for a bounded reuse decision with permission, maintenance and applicability stated.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a useful example is not universally valid or automatically reusable. Confirm who can explain the technical discovery, proof and decision evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

SE-ASSET.keyTakeaway: Reuse is safe only when source, limits, and permission are clear.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a useful example is not universally valid or automatically reusable. Manager support can support a maintainer and review route rather than require publication of every artifact.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Encourage an honest reuse, revision or hold decision; do not require an upload or call untested code validated.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a useful example is not universally valid or automatically reusable; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support a maintainer and review route rather than require publication of every artifact? CE-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
CE-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
CE-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Cowork
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
keyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

activities.name: Build the commercial decision brief
activities.description: Prepare commercial talking points, decision needs, and authority boundaries for a live customer or deal review.
activities.prompt: Prepare a read-only commercial decision brief in chat for [Account Name or TPID] or Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID] on [decision or proposed structure; one labeled Enrollment Number or Agreement Number only if contract-specific]. Use existing records and current applicable guidance; do not create, initiate, update or submit a pre-approval, DealBook or other commercial workflow. Cover contract terms, commercial positions, concessions, approval status, authority limits, renewal/consumption risks, customer discussions/questions and the next decision with recorded owner or owner role. Distinguish facts, approved positions, proposed but unapproved positions, risks and unknowns. Cite sources; flag missing, conflicting or stale evidence. Do not infer approval or customer commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Commercial decision brief with authority boundaries, risks, questions, and next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides what commercial position is stated in the room. Authority limits are theirs to hold, and a position offered in a live review is difficult to withdraw once the customer or the account team has heard it.
activities.requiredContext: Account name or TPID, or Opportunity ID for a particular deal; the commercial decision or proposed structure under review; available contract/proposal facts and known approval or authority references. One labeled Enrollment Number or Agreement Number only for a contract-specific question.
activities.whyThisMatters: A commercial review needs an explicit proposed position and authority boundary, not an implied approval hidden in a fluent brief.

activities.description: Prioritize commercial risks from approved evidence, test assumptions, and identify escalation needs; return risk rationale, evidence gaps, and the next decision/handoff.
activities.prompt: In [Report Name], for [account/portfolio scope] during [review period], prioritize material commercial or renewal risk signals using available measures. Separate observed changes from risk interpretations; flag missing measures and the intervention, ownership or escalation questions the report cannot resolve.
activities.expectedOutput: Commercial-risk brief with dated report signals, provisional risk priorities, evidence gaps and escalation questions. A next decision owner is named only from supplied confirmed context; approvals, eligibility and commitments are not inferred. Unavailable report access or comparisons remain gaps.

activities.requiredContext: Report name; permitted account/portfolio scope and filters; review period and comparison baseline; available commercial or renewal measures; approved agreement context and any confirmed decision owners.
activitySteps: 1. Check the right report/view, permitted scope, period, relevant visual and measure definitions, including any comparison baseline.

activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial risk found early is a conversation. The same risk found at approval becomes delay.

activities.name: Set the trigger for each commercial risk
activities.description: Give each prioritized commercial risk an observable trigger, so it is acted on at a defined point rather than watched until it is late.
activities.prompt: For each risk in [the prioritized commercial risks], state the observable condition that means it has to be acted on now rather than watched, who acts when that condition is met, and what they do first. Keep internal steps separate from anything the customer is asked to do. Separate risks within my documented CE authority from those needing a more-authorized role; use supplied authority/owner evidence to identify who can decide and what they need from me. Where a risk has no observable trigger, say so rather than inventing a threshold. Distinguish documented triggers from evidence-supported conditions proposed for CE review; do not present a proposed operational trigger as policy. Preserve confirmed acting owners and mark missing owners unconfirmed rather than inventing a person or implying acceptance. Use the supplied material and flag gaps.
activities.expectedOutput: Each commercial risk with its acting trigger, the person who acts, their first step, and the risks that have no observable trigger named as such.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE owns the escalation route and confirms it before the plan is used. An escalation that arrives through the wrong channel is slower than none, because it must be re-routed after it has already alarmed someone. The CE also decides whether each trigger is one a person would actually act on, since a threshold set where nobody would move produces a register that looks governed and changes nothing.
activities.requiredContext: The validated commercial risk view; the approval owners; the escalation route your team actually uses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A risk everyone agrees is real still waits, because nobody said what would mean now.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Risk you find this week is a conversation. The same risk found by the customer is an escalation. Focus on finding it earlier.
keyTalkingPoints: A health score can tell you something is wrong. It rarely tells you what to do.
Every risk needs an owner and a date or it is an observation.
AI is good at surfacing signal. Prioritizing it is judgment.
For a chosen MSXI practice, inspect the risk visual, permitted scope, dates and defined measures; a report signal is not a policy interpretation, financial approval or confirmed escalation owner.
discussionQuestions: Which account is at risk in a way the reporting does not show?
What stops a known risk from getting an owner?
Which part of this carries policy or precedent risk?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify commercial risk and escalation priorities'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the one deal you just briefed to where commercial risk is concentrated across the book, then back to what you will act on first. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test assumptions behind the commercial risk view', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial risk prioritization needs current authoritative evidence and an accountable intervention owner. Ranking risks does not authorize pricing, exceptions or commitments. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: Which commercial risk is most consequential this week, and what dated evidence supports it? Who can act and by when? How does a colleague distinguish a risk score from a cause that changes the intervention?
listenFor: Risk described without an owner or a date; health reported by score rather than cause; and interventions discussed but never started.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the available MSXI Pane cannot resolve the chosen report question, optionally use a role starter or the current report's book of prompts, or ask for a narrower question aligned to the visual. If access, routing or measures remain unavailable, stop the data claim and use an approved sanitized excerpt or a clearly labeled fictional case to rehearse a commercial-risk row with dated fact, provisional consequence and governed decision-owner question. Keep evidence, assumptions and gaps separate; fictional practice establishes no live result, commitment or approval, and requires no additional Team Member prework.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could compare commercial risks and explore a proposed intervention for the most consequential one, without having to initiate an owner conversation. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized commercial risk verified or routed and whether it made the intervention clearer; keep agreement and pricing details private. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A commercial structure appears workable, but an unresolved policy question could block the next step. Inspect the approved source and identify the governed decision owner.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Commercial risk review connects a structure or timing signal to its consequence and authoritative decision route. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the facilitator-arranged commercial risk example. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check portfolio filters, dated risk measures and authoritative agreement context in the relevant report/view and available Copilot Pane; the home link alone confirms neither access nor the report route. Use the report's visual labels for a focused question. Keep missing fields or comparisons visible; no new Team Member artifact is required.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A commercial trigger is not a policy interpretation or approval. Look for a consequence and intervention question tied to the authoritative source.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a commercial trigger is not a policy interpretation or approval. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CE-HEALTH.keyTakeaway: A health signal is actionable when its evidence, accountable owner, and next decision are clear.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a commercial trigger is not a policy interpretation or approval. Manager support can support access to the commercial decision owner without promising an exception.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Agree which commercial risk question is useful to explore; keep interpretation and escalation within the applicable authority. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, help the facilitator check portfolio filters, dated risk measures and authoritative agreement context; keep a missing report, route or measure as a gap rather than a participant access test.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations without scoring individuals. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check the report/view, relevant visual, scope, period and source basis before one focused question: Which risk is a report observation, and which intervention or approval question needs the commercial decision owner? Narrow a broad query using the visual's terminology; keep consequential judgment with its accountable human owner and do not turn the practice into a commitment or readiness test.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support access to the commercial decision owner without promising an exception? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

activities.name: Compare viable commercial structures
activities.description: Develop commercial strategy options for price and offer, documenting trade-offs and approval dependencies; hand off the options and open questions for CE review.
activities.prompt: Compare up to three candidate commercial structures in chat for Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], using existing deal records, customer-stated priorities and applicable current guidance; do not initiate an offer or approval workflow. Show products/SKUs, term, pricing logic, customer value, Microsoft trade-offs, risks, approval requirements and assumptions. Distinguish confirmed availability from approved positions and proposed but unapproved options; do not invent viability to fill a count. Cite sources, flag missing, conflicting or stale evidence and give neutral questions for unknown preferences. Identify the next decision and recorded owner or owner role; do not submit or approve an offer.
activities.expectedOutput: Commercial structure comparison with evidence-backed availability, customer trade-offs, approval dependencies and options or policy questions still requiring validation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE verifies that each pricing and offer option is available to this customer under current authoritative guidance and keeps unapproved structures distinct from approved terms.
activities.requiredContext: Opportunity ID; available deal facts and customer-stated priorities; candidate structure parameters if already proposed; known applicable guidance and approval references.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparing viable commercial structures surfaces the difference that actually changes the decision.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Map approvals and fastest governed path
activities.description: Identify approval, policy and escalation dependencies.
activities.prompt: Draft an approval map and Deal Desk justification in chat for Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID] and [proposed structure: products, term, pricing and concessions]. Inspect existing deal evidence and applicable current guidance; do not start a pre-approval or other approval workflow. Map known checks, reviewers, dependencies and escalation routes, citing confirmed requirements and distinguishing checks needing validation. Name blockers, missing evidence, owner roles and next actions. State review readiness or its limits; separate facts from assumptions and do not present the structure as approved.
activities.expectedOutput: Approval map and draft justification.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE confirms routing against current policy rather than precedent. Approval paths change, and the fastest route that worked last quarter is the one most likely to be rejected without explanation.
activities.requiredContext: Opportunity identifier/context; proposed structure and approved materials; current applicable approval guidance, with known gaps explicit.
activities.whyThisMatters: A source-checked approval map reveals the evidence and routing that can prevent avoidable Deal Desk rework.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial structure decides whether a deal can move. Focus on comparing options before the structure hardens.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is not to create an offer. The goal is to compare viable structures, surface trade-offs, and name the approval path while options still exist.
discussionQuestions: What option is the deal implicitly assuming? Which approval or exception would surprise the team later? What trade-off should be explicit before negotiation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Compare viable commercial structures'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from possible structures to the smallest options matrix that makes the decision clearer. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial options expose viable trade-offs, customer constraints and approval dependencies before negotiation narrows choice. Recommendation is separate from authority to offer terms. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
facilitatorQuestions: Which commercial option is most plausible? What trade-off would change the decision? Where would this break if an approval requirement appears late?
listenFor: One default structure being treated as the only option; approval path ambiguity; pricing, term, or concession trade-offs not stated; and assumptions that need CE or Deal Desk review.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a two-option commercial matrix: customer intent, known agreement mechanics, trade-off, authoritative source gap and approval dependency. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could build a commercial options matrix for one live deal and identify which option needs approval you do not hold. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized approval dependency or trade-off discovered and whether it prevented an unapproved offer or preserved an alternative. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Two commercial options make different assumptions about an exception. Compare the trade-off and identify which approval is actually needed before negotiation.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Comparing commercial structures means exposing tradeoffs and approval assumptions before negotiation. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the commercial option and explicit approval assumption in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: An AI scenario does not authorize pricing, concessions or contract terms. Look for a tradeoff with the exact decision and approval path visible.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: an AI scenario does not authorize pricing, concessions or contract terms. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CE-DEAL-1.keyTakeaway: Make the next decision and its prerequisites visible before asking customers, partners, or internal teams to act.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when an AI scenario does not authorize pricing, concessions or contract terms. Manager support can help the team reach the relevant approver before treating an option as available.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help distinguish viable options from approved terms; do not let an internal comparison authorize pricing or an exception.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that an AI scenario does not authorize pricing, concessions or contract terms; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help the team reach the relevant approver before treating an option as available? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.description: Ground migration advice in current authoritative sources.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Reviewers do not need more history. They need the recommendation, options, assumptions, risks, and decision requested.
keyTalkingPoints: A commercial decision narrative should separate facts from judgment. It should show why this structure, what alternatives were considered, and who must review it.
discussionQuestions: What would a reviewer need to say yes, no, or not yet? Which assumption is unsupported? What customer impact needs to be explained plainly?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the commercial decision narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from deal facts to the internal recommendation and the decision being requested. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test commercial structure assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial narratives should make assumptions and customer consequences inspectable by the authorized reviewer. Reviewer questions are useful evidence, not failure. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
facilitatorQuestions: Which recommendation would a reviewer understand quickly? What assumption needs evidence? Which reviewer or decision owner is missing?
listenFor: Narratives that bury the ask; options without trade-offs; customer impact omitted; and transition or migration risks stated without a source.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one commercial recommendation outline: decision requested, evidenced facts, options/trade-offs, customer impact, caveat and authorized reviewer. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could write the commercial recommendation for one deal in a form a reviewer could act on without asking you a question. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized assumption challenged or clarified and whether it improved the recommendation; no case or terms are required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A commercial recommendation contains extensive history but hides its unsupported assumption. Prepare a short decision ask with the options, evidence and customer impact.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A commercial recommendation makes the decision ask, customer impact and unsupported assumptions understandable. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the recommendation, alternatives and customer-impact caveat in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A persuasive business narrative is not approval of its terms. Look for a concise decision ask with evidence, assumptions and review boundaries.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a persuasive business narrative is not approval of its terms. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Negotiation is where vague structure becomes expensive. Focus on authority boundaries, give/get logic, and rehearsal before the customer asks.
keyTalkingPoints: The agent can help prepare scenarios and objections. You remain accountable for authority, customer commitments, concession discipline, and escalation triggers.
discussionQuestions: Where is your concession logic unclear? Which customer ask would trigger escalation? What must not be said before review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rehearse the commercial negotiation'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from negotiation principles to one realistic customer objection and the reviewed response. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test negotiation assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Negotiation preparation tests sequenced trades and confirmed authority limits before customer pressure arrives. Rehearsed concessions are not approved concessions. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer ask would test your authority boundary? What give/get logic is clear enough to use? What must be reviewed before customer-facing use?
listenFor: Concession logic that is not tied to value; authority boundaries not explicit; likely objections unrehearsed; and customer commitments that require review.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one negotiation exchange: objective, reviewed give/get or explicitly hypothetical alternative, authority boundary, objection and escalation response. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Rehearse with a peer; if alone, write both sides and mark the exchange untested, not a validated customer or coaching response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could rehearse a negotiation scenario using confirmed concession authority and applicable escalation guidance; ask the authorized owner about unresolved boundaries before offering terms. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized rehearsal lesson about a trade or boundary and whether it improved readiness; a completed negotiation is optional. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A negotiation scenario includes a customer ask outside the approved position. Rehearse the response and escalation boundary without authorizing a concession.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Negotiation preparation tests a position and fallback within the actual concession and escalation boundaries. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the approved position and stated escalation boundary in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Rehearsal cannot authorize a concession or simulate customer agreement. Look for a position, feasible fallback and escalation trigger within actual authority.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: rehearsal cannot authorize a concession or simulate customer agreement. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial execution stalls when owners, evidence, and approval handoffs are implied. Focus on making them explicit.
keyTalkingPoints: Execution is not just follow-up. It is approval routing, evidence readiness, exception handling, ownership, and escalation without overstating authority.
discussionQuestions: Which handoff is implicit today? What evidence is missing for the next approver? Where could ECIF, Deal Desk, finance, policy, or legal review be needed?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Clarify ECIF commercial and approval dependencies'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the full execution path to the single blocker and owner that must be handled next. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test approval and execution assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial execution depends on verified approval state and accepted ownership. Mapping the path matters when it exposes the next governed decision and missing evidence. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
facilitatorQuestions: Which handoff or approval is the deal actually waiting on? What evidence is missing? Who owns the next decision, and what should not be represented as approved?
listenFor: Approval status overstated; handoffs without owners; ECIF, finance, Deal Desk, legal, or policy dependencies hidden; and blockers described without the next governed action.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one approval-path row: required decision, evidence, current status or unknown, authorized owner, sequence dependency and next question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a deal's approval path and identify what the first owner would need to confirm; no outreach is required. Receiving-owner acceptance is required before treating any actual handoff as accepted; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized approval or execution gap checked and whether the owner clarified the next step; a cleared blocker is not required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: An approval request is circulating, but the next approver lacks a source document and no contributor owns the gap. Clarify the handoff and authorized route.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Commercial approval handoffs depend on the evidence the next authorized decision maker needs. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the approval handoff and unresolved evidence need in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Routing a request does not mean a receiving approver accepted it. Look for an exact evidence gap and a known decision or escalation owner.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: routing a request does not mean a receiving approver accepted it. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Watch the renewal portfolio for commercial trigger dates
activities.description: Set up a standing check across your renewal portfolio so commercial trigger dates surface with enough runway to act on them. In-huddle practice is one reviewed read-only result; recurrence is optional after approval.
activities.prompt: For [renewal portfolio/territory], check approaching commercial dates, material consumption/usage shifts and approval dependencies not yet started. Rank by remaining runway, not value, and cite evidence. Compare with [previous verified result, if available]; otherwise establish a baseline. Flag source gaps and route pricing/policy questions to the authoritative owner. Run once, read-only; don’t schedule, send or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated first-run portfolio check ranked by remaining runway, with approval dependencies and the owner for each open question. Recurrence is a proposed configuration, or a manual repeat plan if unsupported; a scheduled result exists only after separate human approval and an actual later run.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE confirms the commercial reading of every flagged item and routes pricing, discount and policy interpretation to the accountable owner rather than acting on the output.
activities.requiredContext: Your renewal portfolio with dates; approved consumption and usage data; the current approval requirements. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Select an authorized renewal scope during the activity or a permitted portfolio excerpt arranged by the facilitator, with dated current approval guidance. Confirm reachable sources or use approved supplied extracts; no new portfolio preparation is required.
2. Run the prompt once, read-only; on the first run create a dated baseline.
3. Review actual source coverage and findings before any scheduling.
4. Check the selected renewals' dates against the supplied current approval requirements; route missing guidance to its authoritative owner.
5. Confirm the runway ranking matches your own read on which renewals are genuinely tight.
6. Route pricing, discount and policy questions to the accountable owner rather than answering them yourself.
7. If recurrence is useful, approve its exact scope, reachable sources, cadence, output location and reviewer before enabling it where supported; otherwise use a manual repeat review.
8. Later, verify the first actual recurring or manually repeated result before relying on it. Any message, record correction or commitment is a separate human-reviewed action.
activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial leverage is a function of how early you saw it coming. A renewal found with three weeks left is a different negotiation from the same renewal found with three months.

activities.name: Map the renewal decision gates and who clears each one
activities.description: Turn the renewal strategy into the decision gates it must pass, with who clears each one and what missing it costs.
activities.prompt: Using only [the validated renewal strategy, renewal date and approval lead times], draft the decision gates in order. For each, show evidenced clearance criteria, internal/customer clearing roles, required evidence and effect of missing the gate on timely completion; do not assume contractual expiry changes. Identify genuine dependencies and parallel gates. For customer-controlled gates, suggest how I can help them clear it. Preserve recorded owners and dates, distinguish accepted responsibilities from proposals and leave unsupported gate timing or ownership open. Do not alter agreements or initiate approvals.
activities.expectedOutput: The renewal decision gates in order with clearing criteria, the person who clears each, the evidence required, the effect of missing it on completing the renewal on time without assuming contractual expiry changes, and which gates can run in parallel.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE confirms timing checkpoints against the actual agreement dates before the plan is used. Renewal mechanics are date-driven, and missing an anniversary or notice window loses options that cannot be recovered. The CE also decides which gates genuinely cannot run in parallel, and confirms that anyone named as clearing a customer-side gate has agreed to that.
activities.requiredContext: The validated renewal strategy; the renewal date and approval lead times; the internal and customer owners.
activities.whyThisMatters: A renewal plan is a list until you know which gate stops it and who holds that gate.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal risk is visible before the renewal date if commercial structure, value evidence, and approval needs are inspected early.
keyTalkingPoints: A renewal is not only a date. It is a commercial strategy with structure, risk, expansion potential, concessions, and approval path.

For a chosen MSXI practice, inspect the renewal visual, permitted portfolio, dates and available commercial measures; missing approval or customer-intent evidence stays outside the report's conclusions.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal risk is already visible? What expansion is supported by evidence? What approval or structure question should not wait?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Watch the renewal portfolio for commercial trigger dates'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from renewal principles to one renewal actually on the horizon. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test renewal strategy assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Renewal strategy uses verified agreement timing, economics and value while preserving commercial options. Expansion needs evidence and authorized decisions, not headroom alone. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal has the least remaining room to change its commercial path? What agreement date, customer evidence or approval dependency changes the priority? How does a peer surface that risk early enough for CE intervention?
listenFor: Renewals treated as administrative; risk noticed inside the last quarter; and expansion pursued without evidence of realized value.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the available MSXI Pane cannot resolve the chosen report question, optionally use a role starter or the current report's book of prompts, or ask for a narrower question aligned to the visual. If access, routing or measures remain unavailable, stop the data claim and use an approved sanitized excerpt or a clearly labeled fictional case to rehearse a renewal workback with event/date, measured signal, remaining options and commercial-owner question. Keep evidence, assumptions and gaps separate; fictional practice establishes no live result, commitment or approval, and requires no additional Team Member prework.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could build a renewal strategy for one account using real agreement and discount data, not recollection. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized renewal assumption confirmed or changed and whether it improved timing or the next review; omit agreement and discount data. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A renewal strategy assumes the current structure still fits despite a new risk signal. Review the value evidence and unresolved structure or approval question.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Commercial renewal planning connects current structure and terms to risk and value evidence. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the facilitator-arranged renewal intervention example. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check renewal filters, agreement dates and available revenue/discount or commitment measures in the relevant report/view and available Copilot Pane; the home link alone confirms neither access nor the report route. Use the report's visual labels for a focused question. Keep missing fields or comparisons visible; no new Team Member artifact is required.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Renewal urgency does not remove current approval or policy requirements. Look for a supported renewal response separated from an unapproved expansion option. Recorded MACC, modeled growth and confirmed customer demand are different evidence. Reading a deal overview does not authorize a MACC change, proposal edit or opportunity claim.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: renewal urgency does not remove current approval or policy requirements. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when renewal urgency does not remove current approval or policy requirements. Manager support can help coordinate commercial and account roles before a customer commitment.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help explore the commercial question without manufacturing urgency; current approval requirements still apply to renewal and expansion options. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, help the facilitator check renewal filters, agreement dates and available revenue/discount or commitment measures; keep a missing report, route or measure as a gap rather than a participant access test.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations without scoring individuals. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check the report/view, relevant visual, scope, period and source basis before one focused question: Which renewal priority is supported by measures, and which depends on missing agreement, approval or customer-intent evidence? Narrow a broad query using the visual's terminology; keep consequential judgment with its accountable human owner and do not turn the practice into a commitment or readiness test.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help coordinate commercial and account roles before a customer commitment? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.whyThisMatters: Reviewing licensing and discount risk is judgment work. The agent proposes; the CE remains accountable.

activities.whyThisMatters: Policy work moves when the question, owner, and evidence are explicit.

activities.name: Check the investment path against policy and approval requirements
activities.description: Surface the commercial and policy dependencies that an investment request will meet.
activities.prompt: Using [a sanitized proposed investment/transaction scope] and current approved guidance, identify the policy, licensing, agreement, exception, or approval questions that a proposed customer investment would raise, the approval path it would follow, and the authoritative owner of each question. Cite the guidance used and flag anything you cannot confirm. Do not infer eligibility, exception, funding, or approval status.
activities.expectedOutput: A cited dependency/approval-question map for the investment, with authoritative owners where evidenced or confirming roles where unresolved; eligibility, exceptions, funding and approval remain unconfirmed unless established.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE confirms every interpretation against an authoritative source and approves no exception here.
activities.requiredContext: Proposed investment, customer agreement context, current approved guidance
activities.whyThisMatters: Clearing the investment path early prevents approval rework without overstating authority.

agents.name: Researcher
agents.shortDescription: Deep research agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that produces structured, source-cited reports.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Combines work content and web research across multiple steps.
agents.whenToUseIt: Customer, market, competitor, industry, and strategic research requiring citations. Researcher is also reachable inside Sales Agent, which uses it to answer research questions; call Researcher directly when you want the full sourced report rather than an answer inside a sales conversation.
keyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

resources.title: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft Copilot
resources.description: Official guidance for complex, multistep research across the web and permitted work data, including clarifying questions, structured source-cited reports, and prompting guidance.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for quick summaries or lightweight drafting.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Researcher agent, then state the research question and sources.

activities.name: Track commercial policy and licensing changes that affect your accounts
activities.description: Set up a monitored, source-locked watch on the commercial policy and licensing guidance you rely on, so changes reach you before a customer raises them. In-huddle practice is one reviewed read-only result; recurrence is optional after approval.
activities.prompt: Check only [confirmed authoritative commercial-policy/licensing source list] for changes affecting [account/portfolio scope]. Quote and cite each change, show possible account impact and flag questions for the authoritative owner—don’t turn changes into commercial advice. Compare with [previous verified result, if available]; otherwise establish a baseline. Report access gaps. Run once, read-only; don’t schedule or send anything.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated first-run baseline or change digest quoting and citing each change, with plausible account impact and the named owner for anything requiring a ruling. Recurrence is a proposed configuration, or a manual repeat plan if unsupported; a scheduled result exists only after separate human approval and an actual later run.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE confirms the source list before the watch is enabled, and routes every interpretation to the accountable policy owner rather than acting on the summary.
activities.requiredContext: The authoritative policy and licensing sources your team treats as canonical; your account list; your escalation owners. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the small named scope and sources this tool can actually access, or supply permitted extracts.
2. Run the prompt once, read-only; on the first run create a dated baseline.
3. Review actual source coverage and findings before any scheduling.
4. Agree the fixed list of authoritative policy and licensing sources with your team before you enable anything.
5. Check the first digest quotes and cites each change rather than paraphrasing it.
6. Route every interpretation to the accountable policy owner rather than acting on the summary.
7. If recurrence is useful, approve its exact scope, reachable sources, cadence, output location and reviewer before enabling it where supported; otherwise use a manual repeat review.
8. Later, verify the first actual recurring or manually repeated result before relying on it. Any message, record correction or commitment is a separate human-reviewed action.
activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial policy changes are only a problem when the customer knows before you do. A locked source list is what separates a reliable watch from confident invention.

agents.name: Scout
agents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Policy questions found at approval cost weeks. Focus on finding the question early and routing it to the authoritative owner.
keyTalkingPoints: AI can assemble the context and possible questions. It cannot interpret policy, approve exceptions, or invent authority. The useful output is a routed question with evidence, not a guessed answer.
discussionQuestions: Which policy or licensing question most often causes rework? Where did an approval path surprise you? Which interpretation must come from an authoritative source?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the investment path against policy and approval requirements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from policy categories to one live deal question and the owner who can answer it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test policy and licensing assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Policy checks distinguish verified positions from unresolved interpretations. Use current authoritative guidance and route rulings beyond your authority instead of letting AI fill the gap. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: Which policy or licensing question changes this deal's next decision? What current authoritative source would settle it? How does another CE frame a self-contained question when the guidance is unavailable or ambiguous?
listenFor: Policy interpreted from memory; uncertainty left unflagged; approval paths discovered late; and questions that need an authoritative owner rather than a generated answer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one policy-question card: precise question, relevant deal fact, current guidance/version gap, authoritative owner and dependent commitment to hold. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which policy or commercial boundary is verified, which is still uncertain, and who can authorize the next step?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could take one open policy or licensing question to its authoritative owner rather than answering it yourself. Keep unresolved rulings pending; only the authoritative owner can confirm the position. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share the type of policy question and whether review clarified, changed or held the next step; omit restricted ruling text. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A licensing interpretation is plausible but not supported by the authoritative source. Frame the precise question and route it rather than treating a generated answer as policy.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A licensing or policy question needs a current authoritative reference and a clearly bounded interpretation route. CE clarifies commercial options and routes; only the designated authority can approve terms, exceptions or funding.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the precise question and current reference in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A model's interpretation cannot replace the policy owner. Look for a scoped question with a source and an authoritative decision route.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a model's interpretation cannot replace the policy owner. Confirm who can explain the commercial judgment and governed approval boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help keep unresolved interpretation with the policy or legal owner rather than asking the huddle to settle it.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals.
