activities.name: Track delivered value against what was promised
activities.description: Keep a running comparison between the outcomes committed in the business case and what consumption and usage data actually show. In-huddle practice is one reviewed read-only result; recurrence is optional after approval.
activities.prompt: Compare [committed business-case outcomes] with current consumption/usage evidence. Show each outcome’s direction, risks to reaching the commitment and what proof the customer’s finance team would need. Distinguish measured from projected results. Use [previous verified result, if available] for changes; otherwise establish a baseline and flag gaps. Run once, read-only; don’t schedule, send or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated first-run value tracker per committed outcome, showing measured versus projected, trajectory against commitment, and the evidence gap. Recurrence is a proposed configuration, or a manual repeat plan if unsupported; a scheduled result exists only after separate human approval and an actual later run.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CSA verifies the measurement basis has not changed and confirms every figure before it is shown to the customer as a delivered result.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed business case and its committed outcomes; current consumption and usage data; the baseline used at commitment. Your delivery context, whether global delivery or field delivery coverage, since it changes which next action is right. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Inspect an existing agreed business case and its commitment baseline using already-authorized context, or a permitted excerpt arranged by the facilitator. Confirm the small scope and reachable sources or use approved supplied extracts; no newly prepared case is required.
2. Run the prompt once, read-only; on the first run create a dated baseline.
3. Review actual source coverage and findings before any scheduling.

4. Check that the selected business case identifies its committed outcomes and the baseline actually used at commitment; if those inputs are missing, discuss the evidence gap rather than calculate unsupported value.
5. Confirm the tracker distinguishes measured results from projected ones on every outcome.
6. Check that the measurement basis has not changed since the commitment was made.
7. Verify any figure yourself before it is shown to the customer as delivered value.
8. If recurrence is useful, approve its exact scope, reachable sources, cadence, output location and reviewer before enabling it where supported; otherwise use a manual repeat review.
9. Later, verify the first actual recurring or manually repeated result before relying on it. Any message, record correction or commitment is a separate human-reviewed action.
activities.whyThisMatters: Value claims lose credibility the moment a customer's finance function finds the number is projected rather than measured. Tracking continuously is what makes the claim survive scrutiny.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Value without evidence tends to read as opinion. Focus on the evidence, and who needs to hear it, inside as well as outside.
keyTalkingPoints: The customer defines value. Our job is to evidence it in their terms.
Causality is easy to claim and hard to support. Say what the data supports.
A value story nobody hears is not value realized.
discussionQuestions: What value story would the customer actually recognize?
Which evidence supports the story, and which part is still only expected?
What next technical action would make the value more real?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the technical progress and value narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from value language to the evidence package and next technical action. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate the evidence behind the customer value story', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical value connects progress to customer-recognized outcomes without overstating attribution. Internal alignment and customer claims need the same evidence and limits. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
facilitatorQuestions: Which technical progress claim can the customer trace to an agreed outcome? What source proves realization rather than deployment or usage alone? How would a peer state the limitation and the next technical action in the review?
listenFor: Progress not connected to agreed outcomes; unsupported realization claims; missing source links; and follow-through that lacks owners.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical-value claim: agreed outcome, observed progress, supporting source/date, realization limit, reviewer and next technical action. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which outcome can you substantiate for this audience, and what claim or next action still needs validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could evidence one technical outcome in terms the customer would use themselves, and name what the account team needs to see internally. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized outcome phrasing or attribution caveat improved and whether it made the value discussion more credible. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A technical milestone is complete, but the value narrative describes a benefit that is still expected. Separate observed progress from claims needing customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A technical value narrative separates observed progress from benefits that still need measurement or customer evidence. CSA works within the relevant technical domain; diagnosis, execution, customer acceptance and commercial approval are separate judgments.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the progress statement, outcome evidence and caveats in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Deployment activity does not establish customer-recognized value. Look for a value narrative with a baseline, measured evidence and unresolved claim.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: deployment activity does not establish customer-recognized value. Confirm who can explain the technical decisions and delivery evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when deployment activity does not establish customer-recognized value. Manager support can help secure customer validation instead of asking for stronger unsupported value language.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Encourage a useful customer-validation question instead of treating deployment activity as proof of value.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. CSAM-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
CSAM-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
CSAM-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

topicResources.title: What we've learned from Microsoft's own AI transformation
topicResources.description: Microsoft Customer Zero evidence for outcome-first transformation, end-to-end workflow redesign, employee-centered change, Capability Add measurement, and continuous human-AI learning. Metrics are bounded to the cited samples and periods.

CSAM-ORIENT.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Introduce the why, reinforce the weekly rhythm, and welcome questions. Help distinguish the future weekly-experience preview from today's Orientation. Support readiness and access questions without inspecting individual tool usage, survey answers, or performance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
Does the team understand the motion and what to expect in the first role-specific huddle in Week 2?
What readiness question or access blocker needs support through our existing channels?

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.title: Sales Agent Capabilities Guide
resources.description: Detailed reference for Sales Agent components, capabilities, and example prompts.

resources.title: Workforce Transformation Hub
resources.description: Always-available hub for role guidance and enablement.

resources.title: Use Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot
resources.description: Official Sales agent overview and example prompts for connected CRM data. Internal sales scenarios and available records can differ.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Cowork
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
keyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

resources.title: Copilot Cowork overview
resources.description: Overview of Cowork tasks, skills and action controls. Optional tool guidance, not a Dynamics 365 Sales skills guide.

resources.title: Workforce Transformation Hub
resources.description: Always-available hub for role guidance and enablement.

resources.title: What to Use When
resources.description: Routes a request to the best-fit Copilot agent and reserves Cowork for longer multi-output work. Useful early in a role path when tool choice is still forming.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.

primaryAgents.name: Researcher
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Deep research agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that produces structured, source-cited reports.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Combines work content and web research across multiple steps.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Customer, market, competitor, industry, and strategic research requiring citations. Researcher is also reachable inside Sales Agent, which uses it to answer research questions; call Researcher directly when you want the full sourced report rather than an answer inside a sales conversation.
keyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

resources.title: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft Copilot
resources.description: Official guidance for complex, multistep research across the web and permitted work data, including clarifying questions, structured source-cited reports, and prompting guidance.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for quick summaries or lightweight drafting.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Researcher agent, then state the research question and sources.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ
resources.description: What Scout is, what it can do across files, browser, shell and Microsoft 365, and how autonomous and scheduled work behaves.

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community
resources.description: Seller community sharing working Scout patterns, including account planning, customer language mining and recurring monitoring.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

activities.name: Draft the outcome-anchored success-plan view
activities.description: Draft the Customer Success Plan around customer-confirmed outcomes, measures, milestones and ownership, keeping proposed changes and any investment linkage explicit for review.
activities.prompt: For [customer/account], draft an outcome-led Customer Success Plan view. Find relevant customer priorities, existing plan or planning notes, recent meeting notes, emails, chats and delivery files. Show outcomes, measures, milestones, recorded owners, dependencies, risks, review points and supporting evidence. Separate customer-confirmed priorities from system entries and proposals; leave unconfirmed items open. Flag sequencing or dates that need a separate maintained tracker. Include investment linkage only where relevant and evidenced. For a Unified plan, use its active scope and parent Customer Priority where established; flag missing linkage rather than requiring a new plan. If the customer or intended planning scope is unclear, ask me to clarify before drafting. Otherwise proceed and flag missing evidence. Draft the view only; do not update the plan or make customer commitments. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Draft Customer Success Plan view with customer-confirmed versus proposed outcomes, measures, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks and review points; applicable investment linkage and evidence gaps are explicit.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides which outcomes and milestones the customer recognizes and confirms plan commitments before treating the plan as final; investment linkage is included only where relevant and evidenced.
activities.requiredContext: Customer/account and the planning scope if it is not clear. Useful existing sources may include the current Success Plan or planning notes, recent customer priorities and delivery updates; not every source type is required. Investment details are optional and only where relevant. No new plan or preceding activity is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most success-plan toil is assembling scattered signals. The CSAM should spend judgment on the outcome and commitment.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Inspect the plan for drift and missing accountability
activities.description: Review Customer Success Plan drift, missed reviews, missing owners, unsupported outcomes, and risk actions; return the smallest update set and owners for CSAM/customer review.
activities.prompt: Review [existing Success Plan name or link] against relevant recent customer and delivery updates. Find relevant meeting notes, emails, chats and files to check for stale milestones, missing owners, unsupported outcomes, risks without mitigation, dependencies without dates and actions no longer tied to the customer priority. Recommend only updates supported by evidence before the next Customer Success Delivery Review (CSDR), naming the recorded owner or an ownership gap for each. Missing evidence is a gap, not proof of missed delivery or drift; say when no update is supported. Include investment-alignment gaps only where relevant evidence establishes them. If the plan or review scope is unclear, ask me to clarify before reviewing. Otherwise proceed and flag missing evidence. Draft findings only; do not change the plan. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Plan-review findings with evidenced stale or missing commitments, investment-alignment gaps only where applicable evidence establishes them, the smallest supported update set, and an evidenced owner or ownership gap for each follow-up.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides what to update or retire and verifies that the customer-facing plan reflects confirmed priorities rather than system-recorded assumptions.
activities.requiredContext: An existing Success Plan identified by name or link; the relevant review period if needed. Recent customer and delivery evidence can be identified in meeting notes, email, chats or files. Extra notes or source links are optional; a Sales Agent response or newly created plan is not required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A stale plan creates false confidence. Drift detection keeps the plan governable.

activities.name: Validate the success-plan evidence
activities.description: Label every statement in the success plan as sourced fact, assumption or recommendation, and flag what is not customer-ready.
activities.prompt: Review [the success-plan update and permitted source material]. Label each statement as sourced fact, assumption, recommendation or missing evidence, citing material factual claims to the record that supports them. Distinguish proposed actions from customer-agreed commitments. Flag material conflicts and anything not ready for customer sharing; a missing source means unverified, not false. Return the evidence validation matrix and the specific claim or evidence correction needed, without rewriting the plan or approving it for use.
activities.expectedOutput: Evidence validation matrix for the success-plan update.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM is accountable for what the customer sees. An unsupported claim in a success plan becomes the thing you are held to at the next review, and removing it now is far cheaper than walking it back later.
activities.requiredContext: Draft success-plan update and source material.
activities.whyThisMatters: Validation prevents the plan from sounding confident where the evidence is thin.

activities.name: Keep success plan commitments visible between check-ins
activities.description: Identify Success Plan commitments that could delay an agreed customer outcome and prepare the next review question or decision.
activities.prompt: Review [Success Plan scope and recent evidence] read-only. Highlight the commitments most at risk of delaying the agreed customer outcome. For each, cite the evidence or gap, show the recorded owner, and draft the question or decision for the next Customer Success Delivery Review. Compare with [previous verified review, if available]; otherwise establish a baseline. Don't schedule, send or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated, outcome-prioritized exceptions view with supporting evidence, recorded owners and questions or decisions for the next customer-success review.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Check the customer outcome and evidence behind each risk. A missing update is not proof of no progress; confirm which question belongs with which owner.
activities.requiredContext: The current success plan with milestones, owners and dates; access to the engagement activity behind it. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Choose an existing Success Plan scope, its agreed customer outcome and permitted recent evidence.
2. Check one flagged commitment against delivery evidence and its effect on that outcome.
3. Discuss the question or decision to take to the next customer-success review.
Repeating or scheduling the check is a separate choice, only where supported.
activities.whyThisMatters: Success plans decay quietly. The milestone that slipped is rarely announced - it is simply never mentioned again until the review.

resources.description: Scout skill that reads mail, calendar and Teams to produce a prioritized brief of what is owed and what is coming.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A success plan connects a customer priority to progress that people can recognize. Focus on whether one milestone still serves the outcome, not whether every field is filled in.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Link the customer outcome to a milestone, an accountable owner and the evidence of progress.
2. An AI draft or complete-looking plan does not establish that the customer agreed the priority.
3. Make the risk or ownership gap visible and keep customer commitment with the appropriate people.
discussionQuestions: When did your success plan last change because the customer's priorities changed?
Which milestone in it would the customer not recognize as theirs?
What is in the plan because it is genuinely the outcome, and what is there because it was easy to measure?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft the outcome-anchored success-plan view'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the plan as it stands to the single outcome you will make observable this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Create the CSDR-ready success-plan narrative', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Governable success plans link confirmed outcomes to observable measures and accountable milestones. Simplify stale detail with the plan owner, not by dropping real obligations. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: Which outcome in your plan is stated in the customer's words rather than ours?
Which milestone has drifted without anyone deciding to move it?
What would you remove from the plan today to make it governable?
How does another CSAM test that the customer recognizes and accepts the stated outcome?
listenFor: Plans built around Microsoft milestones rather than customer outcomes, measures chosen because they are available rather than meaningful, owners who have never agreed to their commitment, and plans so long that nobody governs them. Also note drift being reported rather than decided.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-success-plan row: customer-recognized outcome, measure, milestone, proposed owner, dependency and review point. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed your priority or plan, and which assumption needs checking before the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could make a success-plan outcome more observable and propose simplification if useful. Confirm changes with the plan owner rather than remove obligations to shorten the plan. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized outcome made more observable or plan item clarified and whether it made review easier to govern. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A success-plan milestone remains active after the customer's priority changed. Check the approved plan notes and identify the outcome link or owner that needs clarification.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A success plan connects current customer priorities to milestones, accountable owners and validation of the intended outcome. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the priority, milestone and evidence gap in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A complete-looking success plan can still miss the customer's current outcome. Look for a milestone link qualified by outcome, ownership and customer validation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a complete-looking success plan can still miss the customer's current outcome. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CSAM-SPLAN.keyTakeaway: Make trade-offs explicit: choose what to advance, defer, or route, and name who owns the next decision.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a complete-looking success plan can still miss the customer's current outcome. Manager support can support the next CSAM stakeholder conversation rather than require another plan update.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help the facilitator explore a meaningful outcome link; keep updating or retiring a real plan with the CSAM and relevant customer context.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a complete-looking success plan can still miss the customer's current outcome; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support the next CSAM stakeholder conversation rather than require another plan update? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Rank customer health risks and drivers
activities.description: Review customer health and adoption evidence, prioritize risks, and surface source-backed restart signals; hand off interventions and evidence gaps for owner validation.
activities.prompt: Using the authorized health, usage, support, delivery, sentiment and stakeholder snapshots I supply for [account / portfolio], rank three to five material customer risks. State each source and as-of date, including the cloud/estate areas it covers. Compare conflicting sources without inventing a reconciliation. For each risk give the driver, evidence, possible customer impact, confirmed owner and mitigation/date/threshold only where supplied; mark other items for confirmation. Identify any evidence-backed reason to reopen customer engagement as a question, not a diagnosis or automatic trigger.
activities.expectedOutput: Ranked customer-health risk view with adoption and delivery evidence, intervention owner, and any source-backed signal that may warrant restarting customer engagement; evidence gaps are explicit.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM judges whether the evidence reflects this customer’s current health and whether a restart conversation is appropriate; no threshold or trigger is inferred from an unverified signal.
activities.requiredContext: Permitted, dated extracts from relevant certified reports, health/advisory surfaces, support/delivery records and customer notes for the account or portfolio; source and as-of dates with cloud/estate coverage; known owners, mitigation dates or thresholds where available.
activities.whyThisMatters: Health scores rarely tell you what to do. This turns signals into action.

activities.name: Create the proactive intervention plan
activities.description: Translate the shortlisted risks into customer-safe interventions with owners, vehicles and cadence.
activities.prompt: Using the validated health-risk shortlist and the mitigation options I am supplying, create a proactive intervention plan for the top risks. Name the vehicle that would actually remediate each one, whether that is a success program, a value-based delivery, a support action or a customer-side change, and say which are available to this account today only where the evidence I supplied confirms it, marking anything else unverified and naming who must confirm it. Include customer-facing framing, Microsoft owner, customer owner, required evidence, next meeting, mitigation action, escalation condition and follow-up cadence. Lay it out over the next thirty, sixty and ninety days. Preserve recorded owners and dates, distinguish accepted actions from proposals and mark missing confirmation owners explicitly rather than inventing them. Draft the plan only; do not enroll the account in a program, schedule meetings or make customer commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: A proactive intervention plan across thirty, sixty and ninety days, naming the remediation vehicle for each risk and whether it is available to this account.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM confirms the plan is appropriate for the customer relationship, does not overstate risk, and names a vehicle that actually exists for this account. A remediation the customer cannot be enrolled in is not a plan.
activities.requiredContext: Existing validated health-risk shortlist or permitted shared case; customer/owner context; supported mitigation options and availability evidence where known.
activities.whyThisMatters: Early intervention is where customer health work creates trust.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Rank customer health risks and drivers

activities.name: Update RAID and CSDR follow-through
activities.description: Turn a health risk into RAID and review entries with owner, dependency, decision, due date and evidence source.
activities.prompt: Using only [the validated health-risk evidence and account governance cadence], draft RAID and Customer Success Delivery Review (CSDR) follow-through entries with risk, action, recorded owner, dependency, decision, due date and source. Preserve confirmed commitments; label suggestions proposed and missing ownership, dates or thresholds unresolved. Do not edit the RAID log, success plan or another tracking system.
activities.expectedOutput: Draft RAID/CSDR follow-through entries with source evidence, confirmation status and open owner/date questions; no tracking-system update.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM confirms the record now matches what actually happened. An entry updated from a draft rather than from the outcome makes the next review harder, because everyone downstream treats it as fact.
activities.requiredContext: Validated health risk and account governance cadence.
activitySteps: 1. Select the validated health risk.
2. Draft RAID entries.
3. Confirm owners and dates.
4. Prepare the CSDR follow-up line.
5. Update the system only after review.
activities.whyThisMatters: Health work fails when findings do not become tracked actions.

activities.name: Catch the escalation while it is still a conversation
activities.description: Use satisfaction and support-experience thresholds to find the customer heading for escalation before they get there.
activities.prompt: Across [account list or territory scope], find where the support experience suggests an escalation is building: OSAT below 3.5, ATQ trending worse, RM score declining, or a cluster of negative verbatims about the same theme. For each, tell me what the evidence supports and what would need to be true for this to become a formal escalation. Separate the evidenced signal from the inference. Use 3.5 as a screening input, not an authoritative escalation rule. Do not infer a formal escalation threshold from satisfaction data; identify the question for support/delivery to confirm. Keep CX Vitals and respondent details out of customer-facing drafts.
activities.expectedOutput: A list of accounts with escalation risk building, the evidence behind each, and the condition that would make each a formal escalation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM verifies each signal with delivery and support before raising it with the customer. CX Vitals shows dissatisfaction; it does not know what is already being fixed.
activities.requiredContext: Your portfolio with TPIDs; current known escalations; your delivery and support contacts for each account.
activitySteps: 1. Run the prompt across your portfolio.
2. Treat threshold crossings and trend direction as separate signals; a stable low score is different from a fresh drop.
3. Check each against what delivery and support already know before raising it.
4. Choose one account and open the conversation with the customer proactively.
5. Record the escalation threshold you agreed so the next check is measured against it.
activities.whyThisMatters: An escalation you raise yourself is a conversation about a plan. The same issue raised by the customer is a conversation about your credibility.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving from signal review to intervention. Scores help, but action changes the customer trajectory.
keyTalkingPoints: Health work spans adoption, usage, support, delivery, sentiment and stakeholder change. You must separate noise from the risk that matters most right now.
discussionQuestions: Which customer worries you for reasons the health score does not capture?
What did someone say in a recent conversation that has not made it into any system?
Which risk have you been watching rather than acting on, and why?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rank customer health risks and drivers'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the ranked health view to one intervention with an owner, a due date, and an escalation threshold. If a Team Member rejects or overrides the draft, ask which evidence or workflow condition it missed and compare the correction. Discuss only permitted details; do not assume this review sends anything to a transcript service. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare the customer-safe health message', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Customer health judgment identifies actionable causes rather than collecting scores. Confirm a feasible intervention and established escalation guidance or an agreed review trigger. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the driver behind the score, not the score itself?
Which signal came from a person rather than a system, and did it survive into the record?
Who owns the intervention, and by when does it have to start to matter?
What conversation-based signal did a peer find that the health score missed?
listenFor: Health scores treated as the diagnosis rather than the symptom, risks the team has normalized, interventions without owners, and conversation-based signals that never reached the data. Also note the customer's own view of their health being absent from the discussion.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-health row: score/signal, evidenced driver, customer view, intervention, proposed owner/date and escalation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review the most material actionable risk, verify its driver and ask its owner about a feasible intervention. Use confirmed escalation guidance or agree a review trigger; do not invent a policy threshold or require a minimum-size risk list. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized risk driver checked and whether the owner confirmed an intervention or held it; no risk-list quota is needed. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A health score is stable, while approved conversation context suggests adoption or delivery friction. Compare available signals and explicitly record missing cloud views.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Customer health review combines available signals and their limits to identify a consequential concern. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the health signal and known source limits in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A headline health score does not identify every risk or its cause. Look for a consequential concern with a proportionate evidence check and owner.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a headline health score does not identify every risk or its cause. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CSAM-HEALTH.keyTakeaway: A health signal is actionable when its evidence, accountable owner, and next decision are clear.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a headline health score does not identify every risk or its cause. Manager support can help obtain customer or technical context without treating a score as the answer.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Encourage proportionate questions about risk and missing views; a headline score is not a diagnosis or automatic escalation trigger.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a headline health score does not identify every risk or its cause; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help obtain customer or technical context without treating a score as the answer? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.name: Build the stakeholder and influence map
activities.description: Map stakeholders, decision rights, sponsor health, relationship gaps and next engagement actions.
activities.prompt: For [Account Name or TPID], build a stakeholder/influence map from [customer organizational structure] and available authorized meetings, emails, CRM notes and account context. Place sponsors, BDMs, workload owners, champions and blockers against that structure. Show each person's stated goal, risk and voiced pain point, or 'not yet discussed' when absent. Include last interaction, open asks, relationship risks and next engagement action. Cite source/date; separate recorded roles and customer statements from inferred influence or relationship health.
activities.expectedOutput: Stakeholder and influence map built on the customer's own org structure, showing each person's goal, risk and voiced pain point or a clear not yet discussed, with relationship risks and next actions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM owns the relationship read. Influence inferred from meeting attendance and email traffic looks authoritative and is frequently wrong, and acting on a wrong map wastes the sponsor access you do have.
activities.requiredContext: The customer's organizational structure; approved customer relationship context, recent interactions, CRM notes and known account team inputs.
activities.whyThisMatters: Stakeholder changes can break adoption, value proof and renewal confidence before metrics show it.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Executive alignment is where customer success becomes visible to the people who can sponsor, unblock or redirect it.
keyTalkingPoints: Stakeholder maps should show influence, decision rights, relationship health and the next ask. AI can assemble signals; you decide the message and timing.
discussionQuestions: Who is the most senior person at this customer you have never spoken to directly?
Which stakeholder could stop this work, and do you know what they care about?
When an executive last engaged, what did they actually want from us?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the stakeholder and influence map'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the stakeholder map to the one relationship you will build this month and the reason they would take the meeting. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Rehearse the executive conversation', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Executive alignment rests on observed priorities, relationship coverage and a useful ask. Inferred influence or sponsorship needs confirmation before guiding engagement. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
facilitatorQuestions: Which stakeholder can stop this, and what do they need to believe?
Where is your coverage a title on a map rather than a relationship?
What would you ask the executive for if you had fifteen minutes tomorrow?
What behavior has another CSAM used as evidence that executive sponsorship is real?
listenFor: Stakeholder maps built from org charts rather than observed behavior, executive relationships that exist only through an intermediary, engagement plans with no ask, and blockers identified without a plan to reach them. Also note assuming a quiet stakeholder is a supportive one.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one stakeholder map entry: decision influence, observed behavior, relationship gap, executive ask and engagement owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which priority or sponsorship assumption needs confirmation, and how would that change engagement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate a stakeholder priority or relationship gap with the account owner and draft a useful engagement question. Personally decide whether contact is appropriate; a new executive meeting is not required. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized stakeholder assumption checked and whether it changed the introduction, question or next engagement. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: An executive conversation is planned, but the team is unsure who can decide the next step. Clarify one stakeholder relationship rather than build a full organization map.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Executive alignment depends on real stakeholder influence and decision rights, not only a contact map. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the stakeholder sketch and open executive decision right in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A recorded contact does not demonstrate influence, sponsorship or consent. Look for a relationship assumption and a respectful validation question.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a recorded contact does not demonstrate influence, sponsorship or consent. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a recorded contact does not demonstrate influence, sponsorship or consent. Manager support can support the right executive engagement owner without guessing another person's influence.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help focus on one relationship assumption worth validating; avoid requiring a full organization map or overstating sponsorship.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a recorded contact does not demonstrate influence, sponsorship or consent; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support the right executive engagement owner without guessing another person's influence? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.name: Create the v-team orchestration brief
activities.description: Assemble execution context across workstreams, owners, handoffs, decisions, and blockers; for delivery follow-through, reconcile status and owners against the Customer Success Plan and route blockers for coordination.
activities.prompt: Using only [supplied customer-success sources, current CRM extract and Customer Success Plan] for [account] since [last-review date, or unknown], draft a workstream brief with recorded owners, dependencies, blockers, next steps and plan/review links. Use the extract's as-of and record-modified/activity dates to separate evidenced progress, record-only change, no recorded change and unknown movement. A later record date is not progress; stale records are not proof nothing happened. Missing or imprecise dates mean unknown movement. Flag missing plan links, unaccepted handoffs and specialist/partner work without a recorded CSAM touchpoint. Show source coverage and required confirmations; do not query MSX, update records or accept handoffs.
activities.expectedOutput: V-team execution-context brief listing current workstreams, owners, handoffs, decisions, blockers, delivery status, and the relevant Customer Success Plan/review connection; confirmed and unconfirmed progress are distinguished.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM maintains and checks the currency of execution context and delivery/CSP handoffs; a listed workstream or recorded change is not evidence of completed delivery or customer outcome.
activities.requiredContext: Authorized supplied CRM extract with as-of and record-modified/activity dates where available; current Customer Success Plan; relevant workstream, meeting, delivery/support updates; account and last-review date if known; available handoff-acceptance evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Obtain a permitted CRM snapshot from Sales Agent if enabled for you, or export the authorized records manually from MSX.
2. Preserve its as-of date and the last-modified/last-activity field where available.
3. Supply the snapshot, Customer Success Plan, meeting notes, delivery/support updates and your last-review date to Cowork.
4. Run the prompt and check which sources it actually used.
5. Distinguish confirmed progress, record changed/progress unconfirmed, no recorded change and movement unknown; ask the owner rather than interpreting a missing update as no progress.

activities.whyThisMatters: CSAMs create leverage by making the system visible instead of carrying every detail personally.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Orchestration is making the customer-success system observable enough to run.
keyTalkingPoints: Handoffs need an input, owner and date. Escalation is not a failure when it is used to unblock the system and protect customer outcomes.
discussionQuestions: Where does work currently stop between Microsoft, the partner, and the customer?
Who believes they own something that someone else also believes they own?
Which handoff have you personally been compensating for?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the v-team orchestration brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the coordination map to the one handoff you will make explicit, with both sides named. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the weekly customer-success action plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Customer-success orchestration makes both sides of the handoff explicit and accepted. A date or listed owner is not agreement until the parties confirm it. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
facilitatorQuestions: Where exactly does work stop between the three parties?
Who thinks they own that step, and have you asked them?
What are you personally absorbing because the handoff does not work?
How does a colleague make both sides accept a handoff instead of personally compensating for it?
listenFor: The CSAM compensating for a broken handoff rather than fixing it, ownership assumed across company boundaries, partner commitments with no date, and coordination meetings that report rather than decide. Also note the customer's own team being left out of the orchestration picture.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one three-party handoff row: customer/Microsoft/partner contribution, transfer input, proposed receiver, acceptance gap and date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore where a handoff needs clearer agreement from both sides; no handoff has to be completed for the huddle. Receiving-owner acceptance is required before treating any actual handoff as accepted; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized handoff gap clarified and whether both sides accepted the next step or need a specific input. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A workstream is active across Microsoft, a partner and customer teams, but a handoff has stalled. Expose overlapping ownership assumptions and the acceptance still needed.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Workstream orchestration makes the sending and receiving responsibilities clear when delivery spans several teams. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the example handoff and where ownership or acceptance remains uncertain.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A named recipient is not an accepted handoff. Look for an explicit next action, dependency and receiving-owner confirmation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a named recipient is not an accepted handoff. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a named recipient is not an accepted handoff. Manager support can help settle the cross-team handoff without adding a competing coordination process.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help frame a constructive question about a stalled handoff; do not transfer another role's work to the facilitator or assume a partner accepted it.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a named recipient is not an accepted handoff; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help settle the cross-team handoff without adding a competing coordination process? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

roles.name: Account Executive

Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

activities.name: Identify adoption friction and next activation actions
activities.description: Map usage gaps to customer priorities and build a short activation plan.
activities.prompt: Using the certified usage/adoption extract, verified licensed or committed scope and customer-priority notes I supply for [account / workload], identify underused scope and adoption friction. Do not infer payment, entitlement or rights from usage alone. Mark each possible cause as data-supported, stated by the customer or unresolved. Compare conflicting explanations without treating a customer statement as proof by itself. Propose a four-week activation plan with owner candidates and measurable milestones, flagging unknown data and unconfirmed actions.

A proposed four-week activation plan, with each possible cause marked as shown by the data, stated by the customer, or still unresolved.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CSAM validates whether the adoption action is relevant to the customer priority and achievable with available owners.
activities.requiredContext: Supply an approved dated usage/adoption report extract, verified entitlement/commitment evidence, customer priorities and conversation notes, known rollout scope and available owners. No access to external dashboards or licensing systems is implied.
activities.whyThisMatters: Adoption work matters when it changes customer behavior tied to a business outcome.
