resources.description: CSAM role impact context for customer trust, adoption and outcomes. Use customer evidence to support any account-specific value claim.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Adoption activity does not automatically become customer value. Focus on proving and accelerating value realization.
keyTalkingPoints: Adoption plans should link underused features, customer priorities, behavior-change actions, milestones and value evidence. AI can draft the plan and value narrative; you validate truth and relevance.
discussionQuestions: What value has this customer actually realized that you could prove today?
Where is adoption stalled, and do you know why or are you guessing?
What would the customer say they got, if asked without us in the room?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify adoption friction and next activation actions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the value picture to one claim you will evidence, and one adoption barrier you will actually diagnose. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Draft the sponsor value update', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Adoption and value are different claims: investigate barriers and verify entitlement and usage before acting. Customer statements and measures have limits that must stay visible. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
facilitatorQuestions: What value can you evidence today, and what are you asserting?
Where adoption stalled, do you know the cause or are you inferring it?
Would the customer describe the value the same way you just did?
What evidence would another CSAM require before describing usage as customer value?
listenFor: Value claimed from usage figures alone, adoption barriers guessed rather than investigated, realized value described in Microsoft terms rather than customer outcomes, and proof that would not survive a procurement conversation. Also note value stories that have never been said back to the customer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one adoption/value row: friction hypothesis, distinguishing evidence, customer outcome, claimed value, caveat and activation owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which adoption cause is evidenced rather than guessed, and what supports the customer-recognized value claim?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check a customer-recognized value claim or adoption barrier using permitted data or conversation. Verify unused-entitlement hypotheses with the owner; finding an unused entitlement is not required. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized adoption barrier or value claim checked and whether it improved intervention or avoided an unsupported entitlement claim. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Adoption activity increased, but the reason for the change and customer benefit are uncertain. Review the evidence and keep cause and value assertions qualified.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Adoption and value review connects usage evidence to customer priorities while keeping causes and benefits qualified. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the dated usage signal, customer context and proposed value claim in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Low usage alone does not distinguish adoption friction from a rollout plan. Look for a caveated value or adoption hypothesis with the right next conversation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: low usage alone does not distinguish adoption friction from a rollout plan. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CSAM-VALUE.keyTakeaway: Make the outcome, evidence, contribution, and limitations visible before communicating value.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when low usage alone does not distinguish adoption friction from a rollout plan. Manager support can support customer validation and technical collaboration without blaming delivery.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help distinguish rollout choices from adoption friction; encourage an appropriate next customer conversation rather than a premature success or failure verdict.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that low usage alone does not distinguish adoption friction from a rollout plan; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support customer validation and technical collaboration without blaming delivery? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Build the renewal and growth readiness view
activities.description: Connect health, consumption, adoption, value and stakeholder signals into a renewal readiness view.
activities.prompt: Build a renewal and growth readiness view for [Customer/Account] using authorized records you can access, plus [approved context for any gaps]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue. Include consumption or usage trajectory, commitment risk where relevant, adoption gaps, proven versus planned value, health and stakeholder signals, expansion hypotheses and the next team decision. Use six, twelve and eighteen months as optional starting points for looking ahead, adapting them to the customer; no pre-agreed horizon is needed to explore. Cite available evidence and flag missing coverage rather than inventing it.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal and growth readiness view separating proven value, planned value, supported risks and expansion hypotheses, with a suggested next team decision and an optional longer-term view.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Check the value and risk evidence, agree customer messaging with the account/delivery team and confirm commercial terms with the accountable commercial owner.
activities.requiredContext: Customer/account and the renewal or growth question. Use the selected tool's supported authorized records; supply approved renewal, usage, value or health context only where coverage is missing. Planning horizons can be explored and adjusted.
activities.whyThisMatters: Renewal risk is easier to change when it is seen through health and value before the renewal date.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.description: Create a brief that helps AE, CSA, SSP and CE align on renewal risk and growth actions.

activities.name: Stress-test the expansion hypothesis
activities.description: Test an expansion hypothesis against usage, stakeholder and timing evidence, and name the likely objections.
activities.prompt: In [Report Name], for [customer scope] during [period], test [expansion hypothesis] against available usage, outcome and timing measures. Cite the relevant visual, filters and comparison basis. Separate observations from the hypothesis; flag stakeholder, intent and commercial questions the report cannot answer.
activities.expectedOutput: Evidence review of the supplied expansion hypothesis, with sourced usage/outcome/timing observations, comparison gaps and objection questions. Stakeholder intent and commercial readiness need separate evidence and CSAM/account-owner judgment; unavailable report access yields a named gap.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM and AE decide this together. Pursuing an expansion the customer is not ready for damages the renewal it was meant to support, and neither role can see the whole picture alone.
activities.requiredContext: Report name; permitted customer scope and filters; reporting period and comparison baseline; expansion hypothesis; available adoption, usage or outcome measures; approved customer priorities and stakeholder context.
activitySteps: 1. Check the right report/view, permitted scope, period, relevant visual and measure definitions, including any comparison baseline.
2. In the available report Copilot Pane, ask the concise business question using the visual's titles and report terms.
3. Compare the answer with the report metrics. Inspect missing measures or unsupported conclusions, and refine the question if needed; optional book prompts can help.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expansion tied to realized value is stronger than expansion tied only to whitespace.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal readiness starts before the renewal motion. Focus on seeing risk and growth conditions early.
keyTalkingPoints: Consumption, MACC or usage trajectory, adoption gaps, value evidence, support health and stakeholder signals all shape renewal confidence.

For the optional MSXI hypothesis test, check the relevant visual, permitted customer scope, period and usage/outcome measures; stakeholder intent and commercial readiness still need separate evidence.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal are you least confident about, and what specifically drives that?
What consumption signal would you want to see six months before a renewal conversation?
Where is growth genuinely available versus where are you hoping?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the renewal and growth readiness view'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the forecast to the one early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align it with. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test the expansion hypothesis', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Consumption trajectory, evidenced value and readiness shape renewal and growth hypotheses. Early signals help inspection; they are not forecast or expansion commitments. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: What is your forecast based on, and how far ahead does the signal reach?
Which growth opportunity is supported by consumption evidence?
What would you need to know now to avoid a surprise at renewal?
How does a peer distinguish customer growth intent from consumption headroom?
listenFor: Forecasts driven by relationship confidence rather than consumption evidence, growth assumed from headroom rather than intent, renewal risk surfacing late because nobody looked early, and commercial ownership blurring between CSAM and CE. Also note consumption trends read without seasonality.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the available MSXI Pane cannot resolve the chosen report question, optionally use a role starter or the current report's book of prompts, or ask for a narrower question aligned to the visual. If access, routing or measures remain unavailable, stop the data claim and use an approved sanitized excerpt or a clearly labeled fictional case to rehearse a renewal/growth row with dated usage signal, intent uncertainty, value evidence and account-owner question. Keep evidence, assumptions and gaps separate; fictional practice establishes no live result, commitment or approval, and requires no additional Team Member prework.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an early consumption signal and what it might help the account owner understand; starting a tracker or sending a handoff is not required. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized early signal checked and whether it changed an evidence request or renewal action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A renewal discussion assumes growth from a consumption signal alone. Compare usage, value and readiness evidence before treating the signal as a bounded growth hypothesis.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Renewal and growth readiness brings consumption and value evidence into an account conversation without assuming customer intent. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the facilitator-arranged expansion hypothesis example. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check customer filters, period, supplied hypothesis and available usage/outcome measures in the relevant report/view and available Copilot Pane; the home link alone confirms neither access nor the report route. Use the report's visual labels for a focused question. Keep missing fields or comparisons visible; no new Team Member artifact is required.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A signal can support a growth hypothesis but not a customer commitment. Look for a bounded risk or growth question linked to accountable account roles.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a signal can support a growth hypothesis but not a customer commitment. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CSAM-RENEW.keyTakeaway: Use customer outcomes and verified timing to distinguish a supported expansion hypothesis from an assumption.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a signal can support a growth hypothesis but not a customer commitment. Manager support can help the team engage the account owner without forecasting unvalidated expansion.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help the facilitator keep a growth hypothesis bounded and route customer-facing renewal messaging through the accountable account roles. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, help the facilitator check customer filters, period, supplied hypothesis and available usage/outcome measures; keep a missing report, route or measure as a gap rather than a participant access test.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations without scoring individuals. If the related MSXI practice is chosen, check the report/view, relevant visual, scope, period and source basis before one focused question: Which observation supports the hypothesis, and what stakeholder or value evidence could overturn it? Narrow a broad query using the visual's terminology; keep consequential judgment with its accountable human owner and do not turn the practice into a commitment or readiness test.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help the team engage the account owner without forecasting unvalidated expansion? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

activities.name: Create the escalation and recovery brief
activities.description: Consolidate incident, support, delivery and customer communication context into a grounded brief.
activities.prompt: Create an escalation and recovery brief for the issue identified in the supplied incident and project notes. Include customer impact, current status, timeline, owners, decisions needed, risks, next action, next update cadence and what is unknown. Draw on the project record, the chat threads and what came out of one-to-one conversations with the customer, not only the incident record. For each action, name who does the work; where that is you, say what it displaces this week. Use only approved sources and separate facts from assumptions.
activities.expectedOutput: Escalation and recovery brief where every action names who does the work, and anything the CSAM has taken on names what it displaces.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides what the customer is told and when, and leads the recovery rather than absorbing it. An escalation brief assembled from internal systems holds detail that is accurate internally and damaging externally, and the sequencing of a difficult message is a relationship decision. Work the CSAM takes on personally comes out of the consumption and value work nobody else is doing.
activities.requiredContext: Incident or support notes, delivery updates, customer communications, owners, timelines and current risks; plus the project record, relevant chat threads and what surfaced in one-to-one customer conversations.
activities.whyThisMatters: In escalation moments, clarity protects trust and reduces duplicated status chasing.

activities.name: Draft the customer-safe status update
activities.description: Prepare a concise status update that protects trust and avoids unsupported commitments.
activities.prompt: Using only [the validated escalation brief and approved communication position] for [customer stakeholder and issue], draft a customer-safe status update: what happened, current impact, evidenced Microsoft actions, what is needed from the customer, agreed next-update timing and what remains under investigation. Avoid blame and unsupported commitments. Preserve confirmed owners/timing; mark unknowns for my review rather than promising a new update date. Do not send or post the update.
activities.expectedOutput: Customer-safe escalation update.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM confirms support is aligned and the approval path is cleared before anything goes out. An escalation message that contradicts what support has already told the customer turns one problem into two.
activities.requiredContext: Validated escalation brief, customer stakeholder and approved communication position.
activities.whyThisMatters: The wrong update can create more risk than the issue itself.

activities.name: Build the recovery action register
activities.description: Turn the supplied escalation brief into a recovery action register.
activities.prompt: Using the validated escalation brief and approved owner context I supply, draft a recovery action register with action, owner, customer impact, dependency, due date, escalation threshold and evidence source. Extract confirmed details from the supplied material. Mark absent owners, dates or thresholds unconfirmed and identify who needs to resolve them; do not invent commitments or retrieve incident details from an assumed live connection. Do not update a tracking system or notify anyone.
activities.expectedOutput: Recovery actions with sources, confirmed commitments and open owner/date questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Check that the named owners have accepted their actions and dates.
activities.requiredContext: Existing validated escalation brief; approved owner context; agreed dates and escalation thresholds where available.
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork from the link on this activity.
2. Supply the validated escalation brief from the briefing practice, approved owner context and any agreed dates or escalation thresholds.
3. Run the prompt to draft the recovery action register.
4. Review source evidence and resolve unconfirmed owners, dates and thresholds with the accountable people.
5. Confirm owners accept the actions and approve the register.
6. Record approved actions in the appropriate tracking system through your usual process; no system update or notification is implied by drafting.
activities.whyThisMatters: Escalations repeat when recovery actions do not become governed follow-through.

activities.name: Rehearse the escalation conversation before you have it
activities.description: Practise telling a customer something has gone wrong, before the call.
activities.prompt: Role-play a frustrated customer stakeholder using [fictional or de-identified escalation brief, status and commitment limits]. Press me for a date I cannot yet give. Pause for my response, then coach me on over-commitment, minimizing impact, clarity about unknowns and the next update. Don’t invent incident facts; keep this explicitly fictional.
activities.expectedOutput: A rehearsed escalation conversation, the objections raised, and coaching on where you over-committed or softened the impact.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides what can be said about cause and timing before the facts are settled. Rehearsal makes an answer fluent, and a fluent answer about an unresolved incident is easy to hear as a commitment.
activities.requiredContext: The validated escalation brief; the stakeholder and what they care about; the approved communication position; what you cannot yet commit to.
activities.whyThisMatters: How an escalation is handled shapes the relationship long after the incident closes. Rehearsing it is cheaper than improvising it while they are angry.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Escalations test trust. Focus on moving from scattered status to a grounded recovery plan.
keyTalkingPoints: A useful brief names customer impact, current status, owner, decision needed, next action and update cadence. AI can consolidate threads; you validate tone, accuracy and accountability.
discussionQuestions: What issue are you currently managing that should probably already be escalated?
What is holding you back: evidence, ownership, or the conversation itself?
When an escalation last worked well, what made it work?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the escalation and recovery brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the delivery risk to a recovery plan with an owner, a customer message, and a defined exit condition. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the recovery action register', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Recovery plans need feasible delivery commitments, clear communication and work returned to its accountable owner. Escalation does not make an unaccepted date achievable. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
facilitatorQuestions: What threshold would have told you to escalate this a month ago?
What does the recovery plan commit us to, and can we deliver it?
What will you tell the customer, and when?
What recovery commitment has a peer had to narrow to what delivery could actually support?
listenFor: Escalation delayed to avoid an uncomfortable conversation, recovery plans that promise more than delivery can support, customer communication planned after the internal fix rather than alongside it, and escalations raised without a defined exit. Also note the same issue recurring without anyone treating the pattern.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one recovery brief: risk, escalation trigger needing confirmation, feasible recovery action, customer-safe draft message, owner and exit condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which recovery commitment can delivery support, and which absorbed task should return to its accountable owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review a delivery issue with its owner, confirm feasible recovery and agree escalation or resolution. Humans review customer communication and proposed ownership transfers. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized recovery assumption or ownership gap corrected and whether it made communication or delivery action more realistic. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A delivery issue appears in several status updates, but the recovery owner and escalation trigger are unconfirmed. Use the validated brief to identify the next governed decision.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Recovery orchestration makes the risk, dependencies and escalation boundaries explicit without absorbing every role's work. CSAM connects customer priorities, milestones and stakeholders; technical approval remains with the appropriate technical owner.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the delivery risk, current owner and escalation conditions in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Doing another role's work can hide rather than resolve an accountability gap. Look for an owned recovery action with explicit dependency and escalation boundary.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: doing another role's work can hide rather than resolve an accountability gap. Confirm who can explain the customer-success outcomes and stakeholder orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

CSAM-ESCALATE.keyTakeaway: A health signal is actionable when its evidence, accountable owner, and next decision are clear.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when doing another role's work can hide rather than resolve an accountability gap. Manager support can help remove the delivery or capacity obstacle without turning peers into unofficial owners.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Agree which recovery question is useful to explore; keep cause, timing and customer communications qualified until their owners confirm them.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that doing another role's work can hide rather than resolve an accountability gap; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help remove the delivery or capacity obstacle without turning peers into unofficial owners? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

secondaryAgents.name: Sales Home
secondaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX. It brings relevant alerts, prospecting signals and pipeline context together. Preview is opened across SME&C without separate installation or opt-in; useful data depends on role and assigned records. Managers use separate reporting. Germany and Austria await Works Council approval.
secondaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. For SME&C individual contributors using MSX, preview does not require separate installation or opt-in. Relevant data is currently concentrated in AE, Specialist and CASA workflows involving Sales Accelerator signals or owned opportunities; do not infer that every role has useful records or that CASA means DCSA. If relevant signal data is absent, use Sales Accelerator or the source system that assigned the queue. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. activities.description: Distinguish engagement from plausible customer intent.
activities.prompt: Using only [dated signal record, account/workload extract and interaction notes], propose a short reconciliation plan and pause for my review. activities.expectedOutput: Confirmed facts, evidence gaps, a qualification hypothesis, and the next question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE decides whether evidence is sufficient to contact the customer.
activities.requiredContext: Already-enabled Cowork authorized for these materials; one dated signal selected in DAE-SIGNAL-01, permitted account/workload extracts, recent interaction notes and relationship owner if known. activities.bestFitJob: Distinguish engagement from plausible customer intent.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving one current signal to a customer action or explicit close without treating engagement as buying intent.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies to signals assigned to the DAE; partner-originated demand follows the PSS/partner route and solution-area signals may require DSS qualification.

Current execution: Open Sales Agent, use Sales Home for your relevant assigned prospecting signals. SME&C individual contributors using MSX need no separate installation or opt-in; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. If relevant signals are absent, use Sales Accelerator, MSX TPP, or the source system that assigned them.
Fallback: Export or manually list the assigned queue, confirm the applicable clock from current guidance, and record decisions in the current system.
System of record: The source system that assigned the signal and MSX for resulting account/opportunity action.
Optional AI boundary: Sales Home may assist current prospecting research and drafting. It does not determine qualification, close a signal, or establish future renewal/value capability.
discussionQuestions: What does this signal prove beyond engagement?
Which current action window applies?
What customer action or explicit close can you justify?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Order the queue by verified action window'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Record convert, confirm-first, or close', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Signal triage weighs verified action windows and account evidence. Activity is not intent, and unverified clocks cannot become invented deadlines. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one assigned signal, its source/date, applicable action-window guidance and current account or opportunity context. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which assigned signal has the earliest action window confirmed by current guidance? What account evidence warrants convert, confirm-first or close? How does a colleague triage the queue without turning a proxy into qualification?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one signal triage row: current action-window guidance or unavailable, account evidence, convert/confirm-first/close rationale and record owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal or deadline changed priority after checking evidence and the applicable window?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could inspect an assigned signal, verify any applicable action window and choose an evidenced follow-up, route or hold. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized signal disposition and whether it improved timing or prevented low-value contact. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on producing a defensible coverage position based on real ownership and capacity rather than an account list.
keyTalkingPoints: Use partner-led coverage only where a suitable partner has accepted the account or opportunity; otherwise retain or escalate the coverage gap.
Current execution: Use current territory planning in TPP/Excel and MSX records; verify partner acceptance in Partner Timeline or Partner Center where available.
Fallback: If a partner-status view is unavailable, confirm acceptance directly with the named partner seller and record the source and date.
System of record: MSX for account/opportunity ownership; current territory plan for coverage decisions; Partner Center/Partner Timeline for partner-side status when accessible.
Optional AI boundary: No AI is required. Use an approved assistant only to assemble permitted records; it must not infer partner acceptance or assign coverage.
discussionQuestions: Which account has a real coverage gap?
What confirms partner acceptance and capacity?
What must remain with the current owner until acceptance?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Classify the territory by accepted coverage'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Secure and record owner acceptance', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coverage distinguishes direct attention, accepted partner ownership and genuine gaps. A partner label cannot hide an uncovered priority. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account or territory slice, current ownership, a dated coverage plan and partner acceptance/capacity evidence or an explicit gap. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which priority account is direct-covered, accepted partner-led or still uncovered? What evidence proves the receiving owner accepted it? How does a peer resolve one uncovered account when available DAE capacity changes?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a three-way territory coverage table: direct, accepted partner-led or uncovered; source/date, acceptance evidence or unknown and next coverage decision. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which coverage assumption changed after checking partner acceptance and capacity?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check ownership of an important uncovered or partner-led account and recommend the next action to the territory owner; do not rebuild the full view. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized coverage gap clarified and whether it reduced ownership ambiguity. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

DAE-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
DAE-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
DAE-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE decides who joins and what the conversation is for.
activities.requiredContext: Upcoming conversation, customer objective, active Microsoft roles, partner involvement, and recent interactions. Authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts.
activities.bestFitJob: Avoid making the customer repeat context and choose the right participants.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm this specific task: Establish the outcome and who is already engaged.
2. Supply authorized dated inputs listed in RequiredContext; use clearly labeled synthetic data if permitted real inputs are unavailable.
3. Produce the stated ExpectedOutput using the prompt; verify claims against supplied sources and expose unknowns.
4. DAE decides who joins and what the conversation is for.
5. Keep the output as a draft for the stated human checkpoint; no sending, record update, approval or assignment is authorized by this practice.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. activities.name: Set the primary decision and fallback
activities.description: Convert a meeting objective into two valid customer choices.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For my conversation in [fictional/de-identified customer scenario, desired outcome and authority limits], coach me to turn the desired outcome and the supplied customer constraints, likely objections, and DAE authority into a primary ask with a specific decision and owner plus a genuinely different fallback. Rehearse likely responses and what to say next, and state what the customer must believe for each ask; do not invent facts or decide the asks. Use a fictional or de-identified scenario. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A primary ask, genuinely distinct fallback, decision owner, and evidence needed.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE owns the asks and checks that the fallback is not a disguised concession.
activities.requiredContext: Desired outcome, customer constraints, likely objection, and DAE authority.
activities.bestFitJob: Convert a meeting objective into two valid customer choices.
activitySteps: 1. Open Agent J.ai and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Rehearse the likely objection, not only the version where the customer agrees.
3. Test whether the fallback changes a different axis or merely asks for less.
4. DAE chooses the opening ask and fallback; Agent J.ai does not make the decision.
5. Record only commitments actually accepted in the current system of record.
Access/fallback: Agent J.ai is optional. Use a peer or written de-identified rehearsal; simulated reactions are not evidence or accepted commitments.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving one customer outcome from broad interest to a specific next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: DAE leads broad outcome discovery; DSS deepens solution-area discovery and DSE owns technical decision criteria when those triggers are present.
Current execution: Use current account, interaction, opportunity, and partner records plus direct input from active contributors.
Fallback: If records are incomplete, ask the relationship owner or partner for the missing context and label assumptions before the meeting.
System of record: MSX for account/opportunity decisions and the approved customer follow-up channel for confirmed commitments.

Optional AI boundary: Sales Home within Sales Agent may assemble relevant MSX account research for SME&C individual contributors; Cowork may help structure supplied notes. Neither owns the customer narrative or decision.
discussionQuestions: Which customer outcome needs a decision now?
What prior commitment must be recovered?
What must the relationship owner confirm before the meeting?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Establish the outcome and who is already engaged'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Confirm decisions and route next work', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Outcome conversations connect verified context to useful decisions and the right contributors without specialist commitments. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming customer conversation, approved outcome/commitment notes, known stakeholders and the next decision requested. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer outcome and prior commitment must the conversation preserve? What primary decision and fallback ask are realistic? What did a peer learn from a meeting that needed a clearer role split?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer outcome brief: prior commitment, engaged roles, primary decision, fallback ask and post-meeting handoff question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which question or fallback ask changed when you separated customer outcome from solution assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could prepare or rehearse a customer conversation around its outcome and primary or fallback ask, validating claims with the relevant owner. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized ask improved and whether it focused the conversation or identified the right contributor. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

DAE-RENEW.roleTopicName: Start the Renewal and Expansion Workback
DAE-RENEW.roleTopicDescription: Prioritize the renewal book by risk and commercial optionality, assemble value evidence, involve commercial owners before constructs harden, and test supported same-account expansion hypotheses.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. Leads customer outcome conversations, coordinates partner-led deals and forecasts, routes work to appropriate scale engines, and plans portfolio renewals and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Engages early with the opportunity owner to shape executable commercial constructs across Microsoft and partner transaction routes. Navigates negotiation guardrails, coordinates owner-validated policy and licensing questions, routes approvals and exceptions, and hands off approved terms while addressing renewal commercial risk.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Assesses SME&C handoffs against coverage, sold outcomes, technical decisions, and accepted owners. Supports covered consumption portfolios through milestone readiness, partner and scale-engine handoffs, targeted adoption and technical interventions, attributed value evidence, and expansion hypotheses without assuming blanket customer or partner-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports covered SME&C consumption portfolios with readiness, handoffs, and targeted interventions.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Manages USPSI account priorities, opportunities, forecasts, renewals, and expansion. Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages USPSI accounts and pipeline using certified records and approved, human-verified evidence.

roles.descriptionSummary: Leads USPSI commercial strategy and negotiation within authoritative policy and approval boundaries.

roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates USPSI success plans, adoption, milestones, and delivery risks using approved evidence.

primaryAgents.name: Deal Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Deal Agent is surfaced through Sales Agent. It is not a standalone agent to install or select; it triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Discover agreements and EA/EAS enrollments, generate and reuse renewal Deal Books, explore growth scenarios, and support EA quotes, proposals, amendments and pre-approvals through Sales Agent. Provides integrated MCA-E policy/process/licensing guidance and tools for MCA-E proposal creation or revision, including BYOD and MACC configuration where applicable. Validate returned deal data and recommendations; tool capability does not grant commercial, legal, funding or customer approval.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: For an enterprise EA/EAS renewal, start with an account name, TPID, PCN or Master Agreement when the enrollment is unknown; review returned enrollment details before selecting the intended enrollment. Known agreement/enrollment identifiers remain valid for their specific tasks. For applicable MCA-E work, ask sourced policy/process/licensing questions or use proposal creation and revision tools within your authority. Inspect recorded MACC and growth scenarios where they help the renewal decision; treat recommendations as hypotheses.
keyBenefits: Brings deal facts, renewal context, Deal Books, and proposal work into the Sales Agent conversation instead of gathering them across separate portals. Keeps the capability visible while retaining one entry point and human review of commercial decisions.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Verify complex-deal responses against current data. For general decks, emails or documents beyond deal-making artifacts, use Cowork instead. Review exact proposed record changes and obtain the accountable owner's decision before any creation, edit, claim or submission in an authorized workflow. A confirmation card or tap is not pricing, funding, legal or customer approval.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and use the agent picker to select Sales. Start a new chat with a renewal or deal question, such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically; there is nothing separate to install or select. Lead with a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number, keep one chat thread per deal, and review returned facts and proposed actions before using them.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Prioritize by risk and remaining optionality
activities.description: Choose where early DAE intervention can still change the customer outcome.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Across the renewal agreement extracts I supply, rank where early DAE intervention can still change the customer outcome. For each renewal, include its agreement number, evidence, unknowns, customer sentiment, value or usage signals, unresolved issues, partner ownership, remaining optionality, and workback start date. Preserve CE ownership of commercial optionality and leave final customer prioritization to DAE. Use the supplied agreement evidence; don’t assume a Deal Agent or Sales Home integration.
activities.expectedOutput: A ranked renewal list with evidence, unknowns, and workback start date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE sets customer priority; CE confirms commercial optionality.
activities.requiredContext: Renewal dates, agreement route, customer sentiment, usage/value evidence, unresolved issues, and partner ownership. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Choose where early DAE intervention can still change the customer outcome.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm this specific task: Prioritize by risk and remaining optionality.
2. Supply authorized dated inputs listed in RequiredContext; use clearly labeled synthetic data if permitted real inputs are unavailable.
3. Produce the stated ExpectedOutput using the prompt; verify claims against supplied sources and expose unknowns.
4. DAE sets customer priority; CE confirms commercial optionality.
5. Keep the output as a draft for the stated human checkpoint; no sending, record update, approval or assignment is authorized by this practice.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
