facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on settling the technical doubt without creating an open-ended delivery project.
keyTalkingPoints: A partner may run all or part of the proof only when selected and capable; DSS owns sales progression and normally owns milestone commitment.
Current execution: Use approved reusable assets, current technical environments, and the confirmed program/delivery route.
Fallback: Run a documented manual demo or evidence review when a prototype is unnecessary; stop rather than expand scope without reapproval.
System of record: Technical decision record for criteria/results; route-specific milestone or investment system for funded work.
Optional AI boundary: AI may search permitted repositories or structure the plan; it cannot assert transferability, technical success, or program eligibility.
discussionQuestions: What is the smallest proof that resolves the doubt?
What observed result would change the decision?
What scope or route needs approval before execution?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Decide whether existing evidence transfers'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Capture result and reusable limits', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Useful proof tests remaining decision uncertainty and may reuse existing evidence. Proof plans do not approve resources or execution. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one unresolved criterion, a bounded proof hypothesis, known environment constraints and the applicable approved delivery/program route. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which existing proof transfers to this customer and which does not? What is the smallest additional test that settles the decision? How has a peer avoided turning a demo into an unnecessary PoC?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one minimum-proof card: transferable evidence, applicability limit, remaining doubt, smallest additional test and stop condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. This is a storyboard or proof contract, not an executed demo, successful test or permission to use an environment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What requires new proof, and what could existing validated evidence already settle?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check whether existing evidence settles the criterion; otherwise draft a bounded proof condition and exit rule for technical-owner review. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized reuse or proof-scope decision and whether it avoided unnecessary work or sharpened the next test. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)

roles.name: Solution Engineer

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager

DCSA-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
DCSA-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
DCSA-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

DCSA-ORIENT.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.

primaryAgents.name: Cowork
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
keyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

activities.name: Record acceptance and monitoring signal
activities.description: Compare supplied handoff and milestone evidence to separate actual acceptance, started work, changed risks and missing result evidence.
activities.prompt: Draft a monitoring proposal; don’t activate it. Use only the dated snapshots, baseline and previous report I supply; don’t set up monitoring. Without history, report a baseline—not ‘no change’. Include proposed scope, sources, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and change criteria; flag unknowns. Compare the supplied handoff response, accepted owner, committed start date, milestone evidence, intended result, and escalation route. If two comparable dated snapshots are supplied, return only newly started or still-not-started work, changed ownership, new or resolved risk, changed result evidence, and overdue escalation. Do not assign ownership, judge implementation quality, or update a system.
activities.expectedOutput: A handoff/milestone comparison or baseline-only record with actual acceptance evidence/pending status, start/result gaps, source dates and DCSA review questions; no operational monitor.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DCSA retains milestone governance, not implementation.
activities.requiredContext: Handoff response, baseline, observable signal, check date, and escalation route. Supply approved dated snapshots, comparable definitions, user-maintained baseline/prior report if available, reviewer and actual approved change criteria. Missing scope, source permission, cadence, recipients, expiry/review date or future automation approval remains explicit; no persistent state or tool access is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Know whether work started and whether it is producing the intended result.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.
2. Confirm scope, comparable definitions, evidence permission, access gaps and named human reviewer.
3. Compare only supplied state; missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no progress.
4. Apply the existing HumanCheckpoint to interpret changes; proposed owners, actions and thresholds are not accepted decisions.
5. Keep an unactivated proposal with approval gaps; do not schedule, retain agent memory, send reports or change records.
Access/fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied snapshots manually; no recurring job, retained agent memory or notification is required or authorized.
activities.whyThisMatters: Partner-led scale is structural where selected, but DCSA must not label an unaccepted referral as delivery coverage.

agents.name: Scout
agents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on starting delivery with an owner who can act and a signal that shows whether the handoff landed.
keyTalkingPoints: Use a partner only when selected, capable, and accepted; otherwise use the applicable Factory, FastTrack, customer, or Microsoft route.
Current execution: Use route-specific current handoff and milestone processes; verify partner acceptance directly or in accessible partner status views.
Fallback: Hold a live handoff and record acceptance, baseline, and check date.
System of record: Delivery route system for execution status; committed-milestone/consumption record for DCSA governance.
Optional AI boundary: AI may format DCSA-authored handoff content; it must not disclose unapproved data, assign the implementer, or mark acceptance.
discussionQuestions: Can the selected implementer act from the handoff?
What proves acceptance and readiness?
Which baseline and check date will reveal whether delivery started?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Confirm the selected route and accountable implementer'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Record acceptance and monitoring signal', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Delivery handoffs need route-specific acceptance, a usable baseline and observable milestone. Sending a packet does not transfer accountability. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one accepted technical decision, approved delivery route, handoff packet, recipient acceptance evidence and the agreed baseline/check date. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What selected delivery route and implementer are actually confirmed? Could the receiver act from the technical packet alone? How does another DCSA test acceptance, baseline and the first check date?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical delivery-handoff row: selected route, implementer or unknown, executable input, baseline, acceptance evidence needed and check date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which delivery assumption stayed open until the receiver checked it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check a deciding handoff input or baseline with the receiving owner and seek acceptance of the next milestone or explicit gap. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized handoff clarification and whether it reduced uncertainty or identified an acceptance condition. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

DCSA-PARTNER.keyTakeaway: A handoff is complete when the receiving owner accepts the work and knows the decision, evidence, boundaries, and next step.

roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PDM

roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.descriptionSummary: Recruits EPS partners from qualification to launch, first transactable listings, and early wins.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

Preserve DCSA evidence-quality ownership and renewal-owner decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft internal evidence handoff with supplied acceptance evidence/pending status, proposed next evidence action and owner.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DCSA owns evidence quality; DAE/CE owns renewal use.
activities.requiredContext: Evidence packet, renewal/DAE/CE owner, agreement timing if known, and open questions.
activities.bestFitJob: Transfer the evidence early enough to affect the workback.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm this specific task: Secure renewal-owner acceptance.
2. Supply authorized dated inputs listed in RequiredContext; use clearly labeled synthetic data if permitted real inputs are unavailable.
3. Produce the stated ExpectedOutput using the prompt; verify claims against supplied sources and expose unknowns.
4. DCSA owns evidence quality; DAE/CE owns renewal use.
5. Keep the output as a draft for the stated human checkpoint; no sending, record update, approval or assignment is authorized by this practice.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Usage proves activity, not business value; partner-delivered outcomes must remain attributed to the partner.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use as a substitute for a specialized agent when the work requires a specific system or workflow, for a multi-step task you would rather hand off and review, which is Cowork, or for work that should keep running on a schedule, which is Scout.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on making value usable without claiming outcomes the evidence cannot prove.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies only where DCSA has coverage and accessible evidence; partner/customer evidence remains attributed to its source.
Current execution: Use accessible usage/consumption and milestone evidence plus customer/partner-confirmed outcomes.
Fallback: Create a dated evidence packet that names inaccessible or unproven outcomes.
System of record: Source telemetry/milestone systems for facts; MSX or renewal handoff for the accepted value input.
Optional AI boundary: AI may structure supplied evidence but cannot promote usage into business value or remove source attribution.
discussionQuestions: What outcome does the evidence actually support?
What remains usage rather than business value?
Who must accept the value input for the next review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Classify what the evidence proves'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Secure renewal-owner acceptance', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Adoption, usage proxies, partner reports and confirmed outcomes carry different evidence strength. Attribution must preserve those differences. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one milestone or value-review case, dated source telemetry, customer/partner-confirmed outcomes and an explicit list of unproven claims. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Does the evidence prove deployment, adoption or a customer outcome? Whose contribution does it actually support? How would a peer describe it to the renewal owner without claiming partner-delivered work as Microsoft proof?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one value-evidence strip: deployment/adoption/outcome classification, dated support, contribution attribution and renewal-owner acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which claimed outcome was a usage proxy or partner report, and how did that change the value statement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify a consequential value claim with its evidence owner and revise attribution or caveats before the renewal owner uses it. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized claim qualified and whether it prevented overstated value or improved review. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)

Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Solution Engineer

Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. roles.name: Digital Account Executive

roles.name: Commercial Executive

PSS-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PSS-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PSS-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

PSS-ORIENT.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.

Does the team understand the motion and what to expect in the first role-specific huddle in Week 2?
What readiness question or access blocker needs support through our existing channels?

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on progressing or decline one partner-originated opportunity with its evidence limits visible.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies to partner-originated or partner-shared opportunities; DAE/DSS retain customer and solution decisions when engaged.
Current execution: Use Partner Center/Partner Timeline, MSX, partner report, and current authoritative registration rules.
Fallback: Obtain dated partner confirmation and manually check authoritative conditions when systems are unavailable.
System of record: Partner Center for partner submission/registration; MSX for Microsoft opportunity and owner acceptance.

What evidence justifies progression or decline?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate partner report from Microsoft evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. preparationChecklist: Bring one partner-originated opportunity/referral, its dated evidence, current registration guidance and the owner who can verify customer context. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which demand fact is partner-reported and which is Microsoft-observed? What current registration or co-sell condition needs authoritative confirmation before the window closes? How would a peer secure a clear customer and solution-owner disposition?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.

facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which evidence or registration requirement changed qualify, confirm-first or decline?

bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized gap checked and whether it improved routing or prevented premature qualification. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on creating a negotiation position that survives relay without exposing the floor or exceeding authority.
keyTalkingPoints: Partner briefing applies only when a partner conducts the negotiation; do not imply CE directs the partner's independent commercial decisions.
Current execution: Use current approved concession/authority guidance, account history, procurement context, and the confirmed construct.
Fallback: Use a CE-authored brief and live rehearsal; if partner sharing is restricted, provide only the guardrails needed for the partner's role.
System of record: Approved authority/approval sources for limits; deal decision log for the negotiation position.
Optional AI boundary: Agent J.ai may support rehearsal where available; it does not set authority or concessions.
discussionQuestions: What negotiation outcome is within your authority?
Which concession or objection needs rehearsal?
What may be shared with a partner without exposing restricted positions?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Set the objective and concession sequence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Rehearse escalation triggers', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Negotiation guardrails reflect confirmed authority and sequenced trades. An AI brief or rehearsal cannot authorize concessions. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved construct, current authority/concession boundaries, the customer ask and any partner-sharing constraints. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What outcome, concession sequence and authority limit define this negotiation? Which guardrail does the actual negotiator need? How would a peer handle an objection that crosses the escalation boundary?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one negotiator guardrail brief: objective, hypothetical concession sequence, reviewed authority limit or unknown, objection and escalation trigger. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Rehearse with a peer; if alone, write both sides and mark the exchange untested, not a validated customer or coaching response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which trade exceeds your authority, and what must be escalated before the conversation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could rehearse a consequential trade against confirmed authority and escalation guidance, seeking the owner answer to an unresolved boundary. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized rehearsal correction and whether it improved readiness or exposed an authority gap. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on surfacing one technically credible same-account expansion while respecting customer and commercial timing.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only where the current workload is demonstrably adopted and coverage permits analysis; do not treat product adjacency as customer intent.
Current execution: Use validated adoption/value evidence and current authoritative technical prerequisites.
Fallback: Document the technical hypothesis and ask DAE/DSS to validate customer intent if system access is limited.
System of record: Source systems for adoption facts; MSX/customer plan for the accepted expansion hypothesis.
Optional AI boundary: Researcher may locate current prerequisites; DCSA validates applicability and stops short of commercial timing.
discussionQuestions: What sustained adoption supports this expansion hypothesis?
Which prerequisite could invalidate it?
Who must confirm customer intent and commercial timing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify a workload that is genuinely adopted'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Hand the hypothesis to sales and commercial owners', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Expansion begins with a technical hypothesis and prerequisites, not headroom alone. Customer and commercial decisions remain with their owners. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one adopted workload, approved value evidence, an adjacent-outcome hypothesis and current technical prerequisites; mark intent unconfirmed where needed. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which adopted workload supports the next-workload hypothesis? What prerequisite or customer-intent gap could invalidate it? How would another DCSA hand it to DAE/DSS and CE without making a commercial commitment?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one next-workload hypothesis: adopted starting workload, technical prerequisite, customer-intent gap and DAE/DSS/CE handoff question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which prerequisite or customer need would disprove the workload hypothesis?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check the weakest prerequisite or need assumption and route a discover, defer or stop recommendation to its owner. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized hypothesis tested and whether it improved discovery or justified a hold. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Catch the question that has started arriving
activities.description: Compare two authorized technical-question snapshots to identify new/changed themes, using only permitted aggregate asker counts.
activities.prompt: Draft a monitoring proposal; don’t activate it. Use only the dated snapshots, baseline and previous report I supply; don’t set up monitoring. Without history, report a baseline—not ‘no change’. Include proposed scope, sources, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and change criteria; flag unknowns. Review the supplied authorized messages and meetings from the relevant time range for technical questions answered more than once. Group by underlying problem, use authorized aggregate counts of distinct askers or customers, and compare the supplied prior report to return only new groups or groups with more distinct askers. Do not draft answers or repeat unchanged groups.
activities.expectedOutput: A technical-question delta table with dates, new/changed themes, authorized aggregate counts, missing history and one DSE-owned reuse question; an optional monitoring proposal stays unactivated.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSE decides whether a newly recurring question reflects a genuine change or a coincidence of timing, and whether it warrants an asset.
activities.requiredContext: Permitted messages and meetings, a user-maintained prior report if available, and assets the team has already published. Supply approved dated snapshots, comparable definitions, user-maintained baseline/prior report if available, reviewer and actual approved change criteria. Missing scope, source permission, cadence, recipients, expiry/review date or future automation approval remains explicit; no persistent state or tool access is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Notice what you are answering repeatedly
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.
2. Confirm scope, comparable definitions, evidence permission, access gaps and named human reviewer.

4. Apply the existing HumanCheckpoint to interpret changes; proposed owners, actions and thresholds are not accepted decisions.
5. Keep an unactivated proposal with approval gaps; do not schedule, retain agent memory, send reports or change records.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on reducing repeat work without applying one customer's answer to another customer's constraints.
keyTalkingPoints: Reuse is internal unless the content owner and data-sharing rules explicitly permit external or partner use.
Current execution: Use the approved team repository and current information-protection rules.
Fallback: Create a local team entry and named maintainer if no formal repository exists; do not share customer-specific content.
System of record: Approved technical asset repository and its owner/review record.
Optional AI boundary: AI may help sanitize and describe an asset, but DSE must review customer specificity, technical assumptions, and current validity.
discussionQuestions: What is genuinely reusable here?
Which customer-specific assumption must be removed?
Who can permit reuse and maintain the asset?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Sanitize and state assumptions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Catch the question that has started arriving', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Reuse assets carry source, permission, prerequisite and validation limits. Findable does not mean approved for publication or universal reuse. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one completed technical decision and approved artifact, validation/provenance notes, reuse permission and a proposed maintainer. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What assumption, permission or validation limit must travel with this technical asset? Who owns its maintenance? Which recurring question would a peer use to decide whether it is worth packaging?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one reusable technical-asset entry: sanitization, assumptions, rights gap, maintainer and evidence needed before reuse. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep reuse/publication on hold until rights, sanitization and actual validation are reviewed; no repository access is required for the draft.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What limitation would a new user miss without provenance or review status?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review a small reuse candidate for provenance, permission and validation limits; keep draft status until sharing is authorized. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized reuse boundary clarified and whether it reduced setup ambiguity or exposed a permission gap. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Choose enable, co-deliver, reroute, or escalate
activities.description: Select a treatment proportional to the blocker and customer need.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Using [paste/describe the fictional or de-identified capability gap, evidence, partner relationship, risk, available capacity and alternate routes], coach me to rehearse a non-accusatory partner conversation, likely deflections, evidence-based responses, and a specific partner-owned action and date. Then return a proposed enable, co-deliver, reroute, or escalate treatment for DSE review, with proposed owner, action, date, customer-risk mitigation, evidence, and required acceptances. Do not decide whether the gap is real, assign unaccepted owners, or present the proposed treatment as approved. Use a fictional or de-identified scenario. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A proposed enable/co-deliver/reroute/escalate treatment with evidence, proposed owner/action/date and customer-risk mitigation for DSE and adjacent-owner review.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DSE owns technical recommendation; PSS/PSA/PDM/partner own adjacent decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Gap evidence, customer expectation, partner commitment, DSE capacity, and alternate routes.
activities.bestFitJob: Select a treatment proportional to the blocker and customer need.
activitySteps: 1. Open Agent J.ai and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Rehearse the deflection you expect, not only the version where the partner agrees.
3. Test language that states evidence and customer risk without assigning blame.
4. DSE chooses enable, co-deliver, reroute, or escalate; adjacent owners accept their parts.
5. Close the real conversation with an accepted owner, action, and date, then record it in the current system of record.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on removing one technical blocker without silently absorbing the partner's delivery work.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only for an active partner-led opportunity where a technical capability gap is evidenced; it is not general partner management.
Current execution: Use deal-specific evidence, partner demonstration/history, and input from PSS/PSA/PDM as applicable.
Fallback: Run a bounded technical working session and escalate route/capacity decisions to the correct partner role.
System of record: MSX/partner deal record for the blocker; approved repository for reusable enablement.
Optional AI boundary: AI may structure DSE-authored enablement. It cannot diagnose partner capability from certification or assign business ownership.
discussionQuestions: What technical blocker is evidenced?
Which enablement step could remove it?
Where must partner delivery or capacity ownership remain separate?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Evidence the deal-specific technical gap'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Leave bounded enablement and escalation', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Partner-deal gaps may need enablement, different expertise or a hold; they do not automatically justify assigned delivery work. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one active partner-led opportunity, the agreed technical criterion, evidence of the blocker and the known partner delivery/enablement owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What deal-specific capability gap is evidenced, rather than inferred from a partner label? Should the next step be enablement, co-delivery, rerouting or escalation? How would another DSE bound the support without committing partner capacity?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one deal-specific partner gap card: demonstrated capability, missing evidence, enable/co-deliver/reroute/escalate options and correct capacity decision owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Was the gap capability, capacity or unclear scope, and what changed the treatment?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate the deciding technical gap with its partner or technical owner and agree proportionate treatment or hold without assigning unaccepted work. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized diagnosis and whether it improved routing or prevented an unrealistic commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one proposed partner role on a live opportunity, dated delivery/capability evidence, named people and known capacity or acceptance gaps. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What demonstrated delivery evidence matches this scope? Which named capacity, dates and right to decline are actually confirmed? How does a peer decide ready, conditional or reroute without assuming a partner can absorb more work?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one partner-readiness gate: relevant delivery evidence, named capacity/date or unknown, right to decline, conditional-ready versus reroute rationale. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which claim lacked demonstrated capability or confirmed capacity?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate the deciding readiness claim with the partner and route owner; recommend proceed, treat a gap or hold with a recheck condition. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized readiness claim checked and whether it prevented an unsuitable route. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Find out what the routes actually require
activities.description: Establish from published guidance what each candidate investment route requires, before choosing between them.
activities.prompt: Use only [source extracts and URLs I supply]. Stay within those sources and flag gaps. I am considering customer investment for an opportunity with these characteristics: [paste or attach the approved sanitized deal facts and barrier]. Using approved Microsoft sources and authoritative internal documentation, set out what the published requirements are for each investment route that could apply, what evidence each requires, what each explicitly excludes, and where the documentation is silent. Cite each source and give its date. Do not tell me which route to use and do not assess whether my opportunity qualifies.
activities.expectedOutput: Each candidate route's published requirements, evidence and exclusions, cited and dated, with the silent areas identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS confirms every eligibility reading with the authoritative owner rather than acting on the documentation alone. Published requirements describe the general case and investment decisions turn on specifics the documentation cannot see, so this shortens that conversation instead of replacing it.
activities.requiredContext: Your deal facts and the barrier you named. The routes you are considering.
activities.bestFitJob: Find out what the routes actually require
activitySteps: 1. Open Researcher, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Read current exclusions alongside requirements; flag applicability questions for the authoritative owner.
3. Check the dates. Investment guidance changes between fiscal years and last year's version is still findable.
4. Where the documentation is silent, that is a question for the authoritative owner, not a gap for you to fill.
Access/fallback: Researcher is optional. Inspect supplied extracts or approved official URLs manually; preserve citations/dates and keep unavailable claims open for the authoritative owner.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparing current authoritative requirements and exclusions can reveal a better-fit route or a reason to stop; prior success does not establish current applicability.

activities.expectedOutput: A request answering each published requirement in turn, with unevidenced requirements marked and the observable change stated specifically.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS states what will be observably different if the investment is approved. Separate supplied evidence from proposed effects; do not imply approval likelihood or claim an outcome before it is measured.
activities.requiredContext: Your chosen route and its published requirements. The barrier and the deal facts.
activities.bestFitJob: Draft the evidence-based request for the chosen route
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Look at what it marks as unevidenced. Those are the questions a reviewer will ask first.
3. Make the observable change specific. "Accelerates adoption" is not something anyone can check afterwards.
4. Keep an unsent request draft; only the accountable owner may authorize later submission through the confirmed route process.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A request mapping the customer barrier and supplied evidence to current requirements is easier to assess; completeness does not guarantee approval.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Investment in SME&C is not one thing. Focus on picking the right route before you build anything.
keyTalkingPoints: Choose the investment route before assembling a request. Check current route-specific guidance and the accountable owner for eligibility, thresholds, funding and partner requirements; historical examples are not current policy. Test whether this solution opportunity fits a direct, partner-led or voucher route. AI may organize the evidence but cannot establish eligibility or approval.
discussionQuestions: Which investment route do you reach for by default?
When did an investment request last fail, and at what stage?
Who tells you whether something is eligible?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Establish what the deal actually looks like'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the route to the eligibility question each person will route to an owner. If a participant rejects or overrides the draft, ask which evidence or workflow condition it missed and compare the correction. Discuss only permitted details; do not assume this review sends anything to a transcript service. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Draft the evidence-based request for the chosen route', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Choose the investment vehicle by the barrier it can remove and current authoritative requirements, not program familiarity. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one solution-area opportunity where customer investment might help.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the barrier the investment would actually remove?
Which route fits the size and shape of this deal?
What do you not know about eligibility?
How does another DSS confirm the current route requirements instead of borrowing eligibility from the last deal?
listenFor: One route being used for everything, eligibility being assumed from a previous deal, investment proposed before the barrier is clear, and people who have stopped requesting because a past request failed late.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one route fact base: evidenced customer barrier, scope, transaction facts, candidate route, current-rule gap and authorized eligibility question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which route-fit assumption changed after checking the barrier and current requirement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could compare an opportunity route with its barrier and ask the program owner to verify the deciding eligibility question; keep route fit provisional until confirmed. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized route-fit question and whether checking it prevented the wrong vehicle or clarified a hold. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Check what this partner has already signed up to
activities.description: Establish what program commitments a partner already carries before adding another one.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the partner identified in [paste/attach approved partner/co-sell records], show any co-sell or referral record currently open and the status and date of each, and any record showing a program or campaign this partner has been nominated into. For each, show whether it progressed after it was opened and the date of the last change. Report what is recorded. Do not assess their program eligibility and do not recommend an investment route.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated register of supplied partner commitments, known progress and missing evidence, with capacity questions for PSS and the partner; no inferred program completion or acceptance.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The PSS decides whether this partner can absorb another commitment. Confirm actual capacity and commitment status with the partner; an unfinished or missing record does not establish intent, nonperformance or inability to deliver.
activities.requiredContext: The partner and the opportunity you are considering investment for. Whatever partner program reporting you can reach. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: See what this partner has already been nominated for
activitySteps: 1. Review the supplied partner commitments and program-participation evidence; do not assume Sales Home retrieves these records. The guided-surface fit for this activity needs source-owner confirmation.
2. Flag unprogressed/stale records for partner or source-owner clarification; do not infer intent or capability from missing updates.
3. Check program participation in the partner reporting you have access to - our opportunity record shows nominations, not completions.
4. As PSS, confirm actual capacity and partner acceptance before proposing another commitment; make no offer in this practice.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Dated commitment evidence helps PSS confirm partner obligations and capacity rather than assuming another nomination is accepted.

activities.name: Find out what the route asks of the partner
activities.description: Establish from published guidance what a partner-led route requires the partner to do, not just what it offers.
activities.prompt: Use only [source extracts and URLs I supply]. Stay within those sources and flag gaps. I am considering [partner-led investment route] for a partner opportunity. Using approved Microsoft sources and authoritative internal documentation, set out what the route requires from the PARTNER specifically: what they must nominate, what activity they must complete, what evidence they must produce, over what period, and what they receive in return. Also show what it requires from Microsoft. Cite each source and give its date. Do not assess whether this partner qualifies.
activities.expectedOutput: The route's partner-side obligations, Microsoft-side obligations, timeframe and partner return, cited and dated.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The PSS confirms the partner-side obligations with the authoritative owner before committing a partner to them. Verify current dates, applicable requirements and actual partner agreement; the summary establishes no entitlement or approval.
activities.requiredContext: The route you are considering and the partner it would run through.
activities.bestFitJob: Find out what the route asks of the partner
activitySteps: 1. Open Researcher, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Separate what the partner must do from what we must do, and list each partner obligation on its own line.
3. Note the period. A program requiring activity over two quarters is a different ask from one requiring a single nomination.
4. Take the partner-side obligations into the conversation with them rather than nominating first and explaining later.
Access/fallback: Researcher is optional. Inspect supplied extracts or approved official URLs manually; preserve citations/dates and keep unavailable claims open for the authoritative owner.
activities.whyThisMatters: Confirming published obligations and actual partner agreement reduces the risk of treating nomination as accepted delivery commitment.

activities.name: Get the partner to agree to their half
activities.description: Prepare the conversation where the partner commits to what the route requires of them, rather than simply accepting a nomination.
activities.prompt: Use [fictional or de-identified partner obligations and follow-through history] to help me prepare an investment-route conversation. Explain obligations without making them sound like paperwork, explore objections/constraints, raise unfinished commitments constructively and close on something checkable. Don’t infer intent or future nonperformance, recommend nomination or treat fictional reactions as agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A prepared conversation covering the partner's obligations, the previous record, and a close naming a person and a date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The PSS decides how directly to raise a partner's record of not finishing. Verify actual history and ask neutrally about constraints; do not infer intent or repeated failure from incomplete records, and role-play is not partner commitment.
activities.requiredContext: The route's partner-side obligations. The partner's record of completing what they start.
activities.bestFitJob: Get the partner to agree to their half
activitySteps: 1. Open Agent J.ai, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Rehearse a neutral question about the evidenced unfinished commitment and constraints; do not assume repeated outcomes.
3. Get agreement on a named person on their side, not on the firm. A firm cannot complete an activity.
4. Draft confirmation only after an actual conversation evidences agreement; PSS reviews it and separately authorizes later messaging.
Access/fallback: Agent J.ai is optional. Use a peer or written de-identified rehearsal; simulated reactions are not evidence or accepted commitments.
activities.whyThisMatters: Nomination is not proof of agreed capacity or completed work. A specific action confirmed by the actual partner gives PSS meaningful evidence to review.
