PLC-ENT-CSA-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-ENT-CSA-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-ENT-CSA-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

topicResources.title: Frontier Accelerator App - All Topics and Huddle in a Box
topicResources.description: Open Run a Huddle, choose the relevant view, then switch from Role Path to All Topics. Search and filter by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and AI Tool. For an uncovered team need, select Create your own huddle and download Huddle in a Box.

topicResources.title: Team Member Impact Survey
topicResources.description: Participant survey to complete at the close of the Week 9 transition huddle; allow about five minutes.

PLC-ENT-CSA-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. Be ready to support reflection, the continuing team rhythm, and choosing a Week 10 topic. Confirm the supplied Impact Survey link is available without asking for personal responses.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)
roles.description: Advances Enterprise solution-area opportunities through prospecting, discovery, proof, objection handling, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. Leads customer outcome conversations, coordinates partner-led deals and forecasts, routes work to appropriate scale engines, and plans portfolio renewals and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Engages early with the opportunity owner to shape executable commercial constructs across Microsoft and partner transaction routes. Navigates negotiation guardrails, coordinates owner-validated policy and licensing questions, routes approvals and exceptions, and hands off approved terms while addressing renewal commercial risk.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Assesses SME&C handoffs against coverage, sold outcomes, technical decisions, and accepted owners. Supports covered consumption portfolios through milestone readiness, partner and scale-engine handoffs, targeted adoption and technical interventions, attributed value evidence, and expansion hypotheses without assuming blanket customer or partner-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports covered SME&C consumption portfolios with readiness, handoffs, and targeted interventions.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: PDM
roles.description: Leads partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executive stakeholders and governance around growth priorities. Coordinates partner growth and co-sell efforts, drives course correction through business reviews, and brings technical, sales, and marketing owners together while reserving investment and commercial commitments for authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.name: PDM-R
roles.description: Develops a recruitment portfolio from qualification and partnership development through launch, a first transactable listing, and early wins. Mobilizes technical specialists, coordinates validated readiness, and prepares graduation handoffs accepted by accountable owners, with program approvals and graduation criteria retained by authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Recruits EPS partners from qualification to launch, first transactable listings, and early wins.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: PMM
roles.description: Shapes partner marketing plans and campaigns around market needs, partner maturity, and joint business priorities. Recommends investments, coordinates approved claims, localization, activation, and qualified sales handoffs, and optimizes performance with attribution limits and reusable learning in view, leaving funding approvals with program owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS partner marketing plans, campaigns, approved claims, and qualified sales handoffs.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Manages USPSI account priorities, opportunities, forecasts, renewals, and expansion. Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages USPSI accounts and pipeline using certified records and approved, human-verified evidence.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Sales Professional
roles.description: Advances USPSI solution-area prospecting, discovery, proof, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning using approved evidence and handling information according to organizational requirements. Coordinates account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances USPSI solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and decisions using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads USPSI commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewal planning by assessing commercial risk and structural exposure. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries through authoritative sources and approved handling, coordinating decision narratives, approvals, and execution without assuming policy, exception, legal, or compliance approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads USPSI commercial strategy and negotiation within authoritative policy and approval boundaries.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Provides USPSI technical advice on production architecture, validation, technical health, and cost optimization using approved evidence and organizational handling requirements. Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates USPSI outcome-based success plans, milestones, and accepted owners using approved health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder evidence. Aligns executives and teams, supports adoption and growth planning, and manages delivery risks within organizational requirements while retaining technical architecture approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates USPSI success plans, adoption, milestones, and delivery risks using approved evidence.

roles.name: All ATU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for AE, ATS, and CE roles to explore account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution. Compare account, technical, and commercial perspectives on customer decisions and handoffs while keeping each role's responsibilities clear.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared account team workflows for account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution across AE, ATS, and CE roles.

roles.name: All STU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for SSP and SE roles to explore discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs. Compare customer outcomes, technical criteria, and evidence for the next decision, including what sending and receiving roles need from one another.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared solution team workflows for discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs across SSP and SE roles.

roles.name: All CSU

roles.descriptionSummary: Shared customer success workflows for customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution across CSAM and CSA roles.

roles.description: Co-architect a Services strategy from customer execution and value gaps, with continuity through delivery and value realization. ATU leads account discovery; SAE customer/commercial strategy does not own project delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Execution/value gaps, Services strategy and commercial continuity.

Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

topicResources.title: Frontier Accelerator App - All Topics and Huddle in a Box
topicResources.description: Open Run a Huddle, choose the relevant view, then switch from Role Path to All Topics. Search and filter by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and AI Tool. For an uncovered team need, select Create your own huddle and download Huddle in a Box.

topicResources.title: Team Member Impact Survey
topicResources.description: Participant survey to complete at the close of the Week 9 transition huddle; allow about five minutes.

PLC-SMEC-PSS-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. Be ready to support reflection, the continuing team rhythm, and choosing a Week 10 topic. Confirm the supplied Impact Survey link is available without asking for personal responses.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)
roles.description: Advances Enterprise solution-area opportunities through prospecting, discovery, proof, objection handling, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. Leads customer outcome conversations, coordinates partner-led deals and forecasts, routes work to appropriate scale engines, and plans portfolio renewals and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Engages early with the opportunity owner to shape executable commercial constructs across Microsoft and partner transaction routes. Navigates negotiation guardrails, coordinates owner-validated policy and licensing questions, routes approvals and exceptions, and hands off approved terms while addressing renewal commercial risk.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Assesses SME&C handoffs against coverage, sold outcomes, technical decisions, and accepted owners. Supports covered consumption portfolios through milestone readiness, partner and scale-engine handoffs, targeted adoption and technical interventions, attributed value evidence, and expansion hypotheses without assuming blanket customer or partner-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports covered SME&C consumption portfolios with readiness, handoffs, and targeted interventions.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: PDM
roles.description: Leads partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executive stakeholders and governance around growth priorities. Coordinates partner growth and co-sell efforts, drives course correction through business reviews, and brings technical, sales, and marketing owners together while reserving investment and commercial commitments for authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.name: PDM-R
roles.description: Develops a recruitment portfolio from qualification and partnership development through launch, a first transactable listing, and early wins. Mobilizes technical specialists, coordinates validated readiness, and prepares graduation handoffs accepted by accountable owners, with program approvals and graduation criteria retained by authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Recruits EPS partners from qualification to launch, first transactable listings, and early wins.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: PMM
roles.description: Shapes partner marketing plans and campaigns around market needs, partner maturity, and joint business priorities. Recommends investments, coordinates approved claims, localization, activation, and qualified sales handoffs, and optimizes performance with attribution limits and reusable learning in view, leaving funding approvals with program owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS partner marketing plans, campaigns, approved claims, and qualified sales handoffs.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Manages USPSI account priorities, opportunities, forecasts, renewals, and expansion. Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages USPSI accounts and pipeline using certified records and approved, human-verified evidence.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Sales Professional
roles.description: Advances USPSI solution-area prospecting, discovery, proof, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning using approved evidence and handling information according to organizational requirements. Coordinates account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances USPSI solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and decisions using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads USPSI commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewal planning by assessing commercial risk and structural exposure. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries through authoritative sources and approved handling, coordinating decision narratives, approvals, and execution without assuming policy, exception, legal, or compliance approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads USPSI commercial strategy and negotiation within authoritative policy and approval boundaries.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Provides USPSI technical advice on production architecture, validation, technical health, and cost optimization using approved evidence and organizational handling requirements. Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates USPSI outcome-based success plans, milestones, and accepted owners using approved health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder evidence. Aligns executives and teams, supports adoption and growth planning, and manages delivery risks within organizational requirements while retaining technical architecture approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates USPSI success plans, adoption, milestones, and delivery risks using approved evidence.

roles.name: All ATU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for AE, ATS, and CE roles to explore account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution. Compare account, technical, and commercial perspectives on customer decisions and handoffs while keeping each role's responsibilities clear.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared account team workflows for account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution across AE, ATS, and CE roles.

roles.name: All STU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for SSP and SE roles to explore discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs. Compare customer outcomes, technical criteria, and evidence for the next decision, including what sending and receiving roles need from one another.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared solution team workflows for discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs across SSP and SE roles.

roles.name: All CSU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for CSAM and CSA roles to explore customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution. Connect customer outcomes with delivery, usage, and technical evidence, and clarify decisions and handoffs across the success team.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared customer success workflows for customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution across CSAM and CSA roles.

roles.name: Services Account Executive (SAE)
roles.description: Co-architect a Services strategy from customer execution and value gaps, with continuity through delivery and value realization. ATU leads account discovery; SAE customer/commercial strategy does not own project delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Execution/value gaps, Services strategy and commercial continuity.

PLC-USPSI-AE-W01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PLC-USPSI-AE-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-USPSI-AE-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

topicResources.title: What we've learned from Microsoft's own AI transformation
topicResources.description: Microsoft Customer Zero evidence for outcome-first transformation, end-to-end workflow redesign, employee-centered change, Capability Add measurement, and continuous human-AI learning. Metrics are bounded to the cited samples and periods.

topicResources.title: Becoming a Frontier Firm: Microsoft Frontier Playbook
topicResources.description: Practical Microsoft guide to Persona Acceleration, AI-Powered Process Redesign, and AI-First Possibility, grounded in Customer Zero transformation lessons.

PLC-USPSI-AE-W01.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Introduce the why, reinforce the weekly rhythm, and welcome questions. Help distinguish the future weekly-experience preview from today's Orientation. Support readiness and access questions without inspecting individual tool usage, survey answers, or performance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
Does the team understand the motion and what to expect in the first role-specific huddle in Week 2?
What readiness question or access blocker needs support through our existing channels?

PLC-USPSI-AE-W02.desiredOutcome: Apply an evidence-based account prioritization rhythm that makes trade-offs explicit, revisits weak assumptions, and keeps proposed changes subject to your approval.

activities.name: Build or assess the account plan with approval gates
activities.description: Draft an initial account plan or assess and improve a supplied plan using approved evidence; proposed updates and all subsequent actions require authorized human review.
activities.prompt: For [customer/agency], draft an initial account plan from the approved evidence I supply, or assess and improve my existing plan if included. Cover evidenced priorities, stakeholders, opportunity hypotheses and next actions; distinguish sourced facts from proposed additions. Use only minimum necessary supplied CRM/MSX excerpts; do not retrieve records. If evidence is absent, give a planning structure and a few decision-relevant questions, not invented account facts. Show gaps and items needing human approval; do not present proposals as approved. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Draft initial account plan or assessment with proposed improvements, sourced versus hypothetical content, evidence gaps and pending human approval items; without evidence, a planning structure and questions only.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE approves or rejects each proposed change and confirms nothing is written or committed without review.
activities.requiredContext: Approved tool/use and audience; sanitized, dated evidence for the identified customer. Include an existing account plan only if improving it. Priorities and relevant stakeholder/opportunity evidence where available; missing evidence may yield an unfilled planning structure, not customer claims. Human owners separately approve and apply changes.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the customer and supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this tool/use and audience; sanitize before entry. Include a current plan only when improving it.
2. If Copilot is permitted and available, draft or improve from that supplied evidence; otherwise work manually. No retrieval or record writes are assumed.
3. Where evidence is absent, use a planning structure and confirmation questions, not invented account facts. Fictional practice is not customer evidence.
4. Review facts, assumptions, gaps and proposed additions. Authorized owners approve or reject proposed changes.
5. Any sending, implementation, commitment or record change is a separate authorized human action.
activities.whyThisMatters: Account planning becomes usable when it creates next actions, not just more content.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Account planning fails when it becomes an inventory. Focus on a short operating plan that helps you decide where attention goes this week.
keyTalkingPoints: Prioritization requires saying no. AI can assemble customer, pipeline, renewal, whitespace, partner, and investment signals. You decide which account deserves action and why.
discussionQuestions: Which accounts get your attention by habit rather than evidence? Where is the account plan missing a decision? What signal would change your priority list?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Prioritize account action for this week'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from account list discussion to one AE selecting a top account and naming the next action. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test the account priority list', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Prioritization improves when account signals change where you spend attention, not when the list grows. Separate supported priorities from assumptions before choosing the next account action. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one territory or account list and one account where the next action is unclear. For the account-plan practice, bring its TPID, current account plan, and approved supporting evidence as user-provided inputs, with source, scope, and as-of date. A human verifies the records and decides.
facilitatorQuestions: Which account deserves attention that it is not getting? Which account gets attention mostly by habit? What evidence would change your top three?
How does another AE distinguish evidence-led priority from an account that gets attention by habit?
listenFor: Planning as annual documentation, prioritization by revenue alone, unclear next actions, missing role coverage, and customer priorities not connected to pipeline.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a three-account priority table: dated signal, customer priority, role gap, next action and AE judgment. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed your priority or plan, and which assumption needs checking before the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an account priority view, with or without AI, and consider whether it suggests a worthwhile next action. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share one priority you checked and whether it clarified the next action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: Using only the approved records and excerpts I provide, with source, scope, and as-of date, identify opportunities with material changes, missing next steps, stale customer engagement, or newly surfaced risk. For each item, state the source signal, evidence quality, and one seller action to consider. Flag gaps; do not infer missing facts. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on restoring trust in the pipeline signal before it becomes a forecast argument.
keyTalkingPoints: Bad data creates bad inspection. Stage, close date, next step, customer engagement, and partner attach should reflect reality. AI can flag issues; you verify and decide the correction.
discussionQuestions: Where does your pipeline data most often mislead you? Which field do you trust least? Which opportunity would you hesitate to defend in a review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Ask what the certified business data says'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the individual records the check surfaced to the aggregate gap they add up to, then decide which correction would change the forecast conversation. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Tell the applied fixes apart from the ones waiting on you', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Pipeline trust comes from checking material signals and routing corrections to the record owner. An AI explanation is a hypothesis, not a verified stage or forecast change. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring the scope you normally inspect for pipeline reviews and one opportunity you suspect may be stale or misrepresented.
facilitatorQuestions: Which opportunity would you not want inspected right now? What field, date, or next step might be telling the wrong story? What correction would change the forecast conversation?
What recurring inspection check has a peer used to catch a misleading date or next step before the review?
listenFor: Manual reconciliation, stale dates, close-date optimism, missing customer engagement, and records corrected only right before reviews.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or approved context is unavailable, use a sanitized supplied example or a clearly labeled synthetic case. On paper, complete one pipeline record check: field/date, definition, supporting evidence, discrepancy, correction owner and verification gap. Mark evidence, assumptions and unknowns; the exercise does not establish live pipeline status or authorize a correction. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient. Any later AI run must use project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot and approved supplied inputs.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did inspection reveal about the pipeline or forecast story, and which correction or caveat changes the decision?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could run one pipeline signal-quality check and correct or flag one material issue. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share the type of issue verified, corrected or routed and whether it reduced a misleading pipeline signal. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: Pressure-test the opportunity hypotheses from my whitespace/outreach practice. For each, state the trigger, supporting evidence, and whether customer intent is stated or inferred. Assess duplication only against existing pipeline excerpts I supply; if absent, mark duplication unassessed. Flag unsupported pipeline and name one test that would qualify or kill each hypothesis. activities.requiredContext: Approved tool/use and audience; sanitized, dated opportunity hypotheses from my whitespace/outreach practice and their source evidence. Existing pipeline excerpts only if checking duplication; without them duplication remains unassessed. Missing hypotheses require the upstream output, not a second generation exercise.
activities.whyThisMatters: A documented trigger and disqualifying test keep optimistic signals out of unsupported pipeline.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The next opportunity is often already visible in customer signals. Focus on finding and testing those signals without creating pipeline noise.
keyTalkingPoints: Whitespace is not just a product gap. A qualified opportunity has a trigger, stakeholder, business problem, next action, and evidence. AI can surface signals; you test whether they are real.
discussionQuestions: Where did your last real opportunity come from? What makes a signal qualified rather than hopeful? Which potentially relevant signal is absent from the approved records provided?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Qualify buying signals into opportunity hypotheses'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from signal discovery to one opportunity hypothesis and the first outreach or discovery action. If a participant rejects or overrides the draft, ask which evidence or workflow condition it missed and compare the correction. Discuss only permitted details; do not assume this review sends anything to a transcript service. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test the opportunity hypotheses', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Buying signals become opportunities only when discovery supports a customer need and a sensible next action. Rejecting a weak hypothesis is useful learning, not failed pipeline creation. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account with recent meetings, engagement, or whitespace that might become an opportunity.
facilitatorQuestions: Which signal looks promising but not yet qualified? What evidence would make it real? What customer action would test the hypothesis?
What signal did a colleague initially reject, and what customer evidence changed the qualification?
listenFor: Opportunities created to fill coverage, whitespace treated as product absence, duplicate opportunities, and signals without a named stakeholder or trigger.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one opportunity hypothesis: observed signal, stakeholder/trigger, customer validation question, duplicate check and go/hold rationale. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal warrants a customer action rather than just a new record, and what evidence would disprove the opportunity?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could qualify one opportunity hypothesis and document the trigger, evidence, next action, and uncertainty. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized signal confirmed or rejected and whether discovery prevented wasted pursuit or clarified customer need. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Evaluate customer and competitive evidence from supplied sources
activities.description: Build the sourced research base for the executive conversation, so claims can be traced back to something.
activities.prompt: For [customer/agency/organization], use the supplied dated public-source excerpts and any separately permitted internal excerpts to prepare an evidence brief for an executive conversation: documented priorities, announcements, industry pressures, technology direction and competitor positioning only where evidenced. Cite source keys/links for material claims, separate public/internal material and flag missing or stale coverage. Do not search records or infer work-content access. End with two supported talking points and a confirmation question. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Sourced research brief with citations, separating published sources from internal work content, and naming the gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE verifies each citation actually supports the claim, discards anything unsourced, and decides what is appropriate to reference in front of the customer.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied dated public excerpts and separately permitted sanitized internal excerpts; customer/executive remit, decision and intended audience.
activities.whyThisMatters: An executive notices the difference between a seller who did the research and one who read the account record. Use source material supplied by the seller; verify important claims and retain source citations before using them in the conversation.

activities.name: Rehearse the executive customer conversation
activities.description: Rehearse the executive narrative and asks, then revise the weakest answer before customer use.
activities.prompt: Act as a skeptical executive for the meeting in the supplied conversation plan. Ask one hypothetical question at a time and wait for my response, for three exchanges. Test the outcome, evidence, primary ask and genuinely different fallback ask. Do not invent customer facts. Then give feedback on listening, clarity and evidence, identify unsupported commitments, and propose two changes for AE review. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Role-play output with likely questions, coaching observations, improvement actions, and claims requiring review.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE decides what they will actually say. Rehearsal smooths an answer, and a smoothed answer can acquire confidence and detail the underlying evidence does not support.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Approved conversation plan; meeting type; customer or stakeholder context; role contribution; desired decision or outcome; known boundaries.
activities.whyThisMatters: Rehearsal lets weak claims fail safely before the customer hears them.

activities.name: Decide whether the satisfaction signal changes your ask
activities.description: Test the ask you were planning to make against the customer's current satisfaction and support experience, and change it if the evidence says you should.
activities.prompt: Compare my intended customer ask with the satisfaction/support evidence I supply. Identify supported changes and gaps; do not infer health from missing data or guess metric meanings. Distinguish unresolved issues from those already resolved. Recommend proceeding, acknowledging an issue first or delaying the ask, with supporting evidence and one question to settle the main uncertainty. Do not quote internal metrics or identifiable verbatims in customer-facing wording. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: A judgment on whether the intended ask is well timed, the issues a customer could raise that you are not ready for, and what to resolve or acknowledge before making the ask.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE decides whether to proceed with the ask. A written review may highlight a poorly timed ask, but only the AE knows what the relationship can carry and what has already been discussed offline.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied sanitized satisfaction/support excerpts with metric definitions, source dates and account scope; intended ask, meeting date and known resolved issues.
activitySteps: 1. Write down the ask you intend to make before you run anything. The point is to test it, not to discover it.
2. Supply your case details as inputs to the prompt.
3. Run the prompt with that ask included.
4. Decide whether to proceed with the ask, soften it, or resolve something first.
5. Prepare an answer for anything the customer could reasonably raise.
6. Never quote the internal satisfaction data in the meeting. It shapes your preparation and stays out of the room.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: Preparation usually fails at the ask, not the agenda. Walking a growth ask into a customer whose support experience is deteriorating is how a relationship gets set back a quarter.
