facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Customer conversations are where decisions move. Focus on preparing the position, evidence, objections, and ask before the meeting starts.
keyTalkingPoints: A brief is not a recap. It should state the intended outcome, customer context, evidence, open questions, likely objections, and the ask. You validate tone and relationship nuance.
discussionQuestions: What do you often walk into a meeting still not knowing? What would change if the ask were explicit before the meeting? Which claim would need validation before customer use?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the account and conversation brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from preparation concept to one live meeting brief and the ask the AE will use. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test the executive conversation plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Customer preparation is useful when grounded claims and a primary or fallback ask help the customer decide. Rehearsal does not replace judgment about what to say or promise. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming customer meeting, the desired decision, and any approved source materials you want to use.
facilitatorQuestions: What decision should the meeting move? What claim must be validated? What objection is likely but uncomfortable to prepare for?
What did a peer change after the executive questioned the value claim or meeting ask?
listenFor: Recaps instead of positions, meetings with no intended outcome, generic value language, unsupported claims, and missing fallback asks.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one executive meeting brief: intended decision, supported value claim, caveat, likely objection, primary ask and fallback. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence would make this customer conversation credible, and what decision or question still belongs to a person?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could prepare one customer conversation brief and validate the claims before use. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized claim validated or removed, or an ask sharpened, and whether preparation made the conversation more useful; a meeting result is optional. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Prepare the quote-input checklist and approval questions
activities.description: Translate a reviewed scenario into a text-only input checklist; do not create or submit an EA quote.
activities.prompt: Using the reviewed renewal scenario and supplied agreement/pricing excerpts, draft a quote-input checklist. List products, quantities, terms and price fields supported by the supplied reference, their sources and missing validation. Identify approval questions only from supplied current guidance; mark unknown authority/routing explicitly. Include multi-year or multi-tenant issues only if evidenced. Draft an approval-question note for the accountable owner. Do not create an official quote, populate a system, request approval or submit an artifact. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Text-only quote-input checklist with sourced versus missing fields and draft approval questions; no official artifact created.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE verifies every pricing field before submission, treats the draft as a draft rather than a final quote, and routes discount approval, exceptions, and any material amendment through the accountable owner and the legal approval chain rather than around it.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Reviewed scenario and supplied agreement/product/quantity/pricing excerpts; authority guidance and commercial owner. An enrollment identifier is not evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the reviewed scenario and permitted agreement/product/quantity/pricing excerpts.
2. Draft a text-only checklist manually or in Copilot if permitted.
3. Verify quantities, terms and price basis.
4. Have the commercial owner resolve fields and confirm authority/routing.
5. Keep the approval-question note as a draft.
6. An authorized human separately prepares any official quote or request.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: A sourced checklist exposes missing inputs before the separately authorized quote process begins.

activities.name: Pressure-test the deal inspection
activities.description: Find the blocker, approval or stakeholder gap that the deal plan assumes is handled but nobody owns.
activities.prompt: Review [seller-validated deal inspection and dated agreement/enrollment/renewal excerpts]. Identify the next customer decision, exit criteria, supporting evidence and ownerless blockers. Which assumption would most affect the close date if wrong, and what would confirm it? Don’t infer the customer decision path or team ownership from financial context alone; flag missing evidence. Use supplied material only; don’t search, connect or take actions.
activities.expectedOutput: A deal challenge naming the next customer decision, unowned blockers, and the assumption with the largest close-date impact.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE names the assumption that would most move the close date. A model can list unowned blockers, but which one actually threatens the date depends on customer dynamics that were never written down.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. The seller-validated deal inspection, including the next customer decision, current-stage exit criteria, blockers and known account-team owners, plus the verified agreement, enrollment and renewal context from AE-PUBSEC-DEAL-03. That financial context supplements but does not replace the inspection.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expose unowned blockers and unsupported close-date assumptions while the decision is still movable.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Strategic deals stall when the next decision, blocker, or owner is unnamed. Focus on making the deal inspectable.
keyTalkingPoints: A close date is not a plan. Exit criteria, approvals, commercial dependencies, stakeholder coverage, and customer actions determine whether the deal can move. AI can organize the deal picture; you route decisions to the right owners.
discussionQuestions: What is your deal really waiting on? Which approval, customer action, or role gap is not yet explicit? What should not be decided by AI?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect deal context before customer action'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from deal summary to the next decision and owner map. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test the deal inspection', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Deal inspection should expose the next decision and its accountable owner, not merely produce a blocker list. A routed ask is not accepted or approved work. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one live opportunity, current stage, and a seller-validated inspection naming the next customer decision, exit criteria, blockers, known owners and agreed or unconfirmed dates. If relevant and policy permits, bring approved agreement or enrollment details as a sanitized excerpt with its source and as-of date. Treat this as context only; it supplements the seller-validated inspection and does not establish the customer decision path or team ownership.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the next decision, not the next task? Which blocker has no owner? Which commercial, technical, or partner decision needs another role?
How does another AE secure a decision owner without taking over CE, technical or partner authority?
listenFor: Close date as proxy for plan, approval paths discovered late, role gaps, unsupported deal assumptions, and AI outputs that overstep CE or SME authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one deal decision map: next customer decision, commercial/technical/partner blocker, evidence gap, accountable role and checkpoint. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a strategic deal's next decision or blocker and consider a question for its accountable owner; no blocker needs to be resolved or routed for the huddle. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized decision routed to its owner and whether it clarified the next step; pending acceptance is valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Assemble the renewal and expansion package
activities.description: Pull the renewal position, consumption evidence, value story and expansion options into one package the customer and the account team can both work from.
activities.prompt: From [customer renewal evidence], draft a short customer-facing summary, separate internal risk view and one-page value story. Cover agreement/renewal position, usage/consumption, delivered value, risks and supported expansion options. If evidence is missing, flag it and pause rather than estimate. Show the plan first and check in before each draft so I can redirect it. Use supplied material only; don’t search, connect or take actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal package with a customer-facing summary, an internal risk view, and a one-page value story.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE validates every claim in the customer-facing material, confirms commercial statements with the Commercial Executive, and decides what is shared externally.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Approved renewal, consumption, usage and value evidence for the account, supplied as files or pasted text rather than described; the renewal risk view you reviewed earlier in this session; the expansion hypotheses already tested.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the customer, the renewal date, and the renewal risk view you produced earlier in this session.

2. Provide only the minimum necessary approved fields or excerpts, with source, scope, and as-of date. Do not include restricted customer or personal data unless policy permits. A human verifies every source record and claim, makes all decisions, and performs any authorized updates; this workflow uses only supplied inputs and makes no source-record changes.
3. Supply your case details as inputs to the prompt.
4. Run the prompt.
5. Separate what the package claims as delivered value from what is projected.
6. Flag every pricing or commercial statement for the person who owns it before this goes anywhere near the customer.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: The renewal conversation needs a package, not a chat answer. This work spans several sources and needs checkpoints, so keep source scope, freshness, and human review explicit.

activities.name: Create the renewal follow-through plan
activities.description: Turn the renewal read into the actions and dates that change the outcome while there is still runway.
activities.prompt: Turn the renewal assessment into a follow-through plan. For each at-risk renewal, define the action, the owner, the date it must happen by given the renewal date, the value evidence to assemble, and the point at which CE or commercial support must be engaged. Use the supplied material and flag gaps. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: A renewal follow-through plan with actions, owners, deadline-aware dates, value evidence, and CE engagement triggers.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE decides when CE or commercial support must be engaged, and engages them before the renewal date forces it. Bringing commercial help in late converts a negotiable renewal into an expiring one.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. The reviewed renewal view; the renewal dates and their lead times; the account-team and CE owners.
activities.whyThisMatters: Deadline-aware actions preserve time for the team and commercial owner to change the outcome.

activities.name: Test renewal risk against how the customer actually feels
activities.description: Put the customer's satisfaction signal next to your own renewal risk read, and investigate every account where the two disagree.
activities.prompt: Compare the supplied renewal risk ratings with sanitized satisfaction/support evidence. Use named metrics only with supplied definitions, scales, periods and source dates; prefer aggregate themes over identifiable verbatims. Missing data is unknown, not healthy. Identify disagreements, alternative commercial explanations and evidence needed to resolve them. Satisfaction alone does not establish renewal intent. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: A satisfaction picture per renewing account ordered by deterioration, set against your own risk ratings, and the shortlist where the two disagree.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE owns the renewal risk call. Satisfaction is one input, not a verdict, and a satisfied customer can still leave for commercial reasons no CX metric will show.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied renewal portfolio/risk ratings, sanitized satisfaction/support excerpts, metric definitions and periods, known commercial drivers and resolved issues; only necessary identifiers.
activitySteps: 1. During the activity, select an authorized six-month renewal scope from approved evidence arranged by the facilitator or manager. State an initial human risk judgment before comparing the supplied evidence; no new Team Member renewal view or rating sheet is required.
2. Compare the supplied approved evidence with your current human-assessed risk ratings; identify satisfaction-record gaps rather than assuming access.
3. Put any evidence-based ordering next to your own ratings and focus on disagreements.
4. For each disagreement, decide which evidence is reliable and what additional source would settle it.
5. Raise any renewal you downgrade with the account team before it appears in a review.
6. Discuss a disagreement found in this activity between supplied evidence and the initial human judgment, using only the facilitator- or manager-arranged approved sanitized context.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: Renewal risk assessed on pipeline signals alone misses the customer who is quietly unhappy and has not told you yet.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal risk is usually visible before the renewal conversation. Focus on finding it while there is still time to act.
keyTalkingPoints: Renewal health depends on value evidence, usage or consumption signals, relationship recency, commercial readiness, and expansion logic. AI can surface patterns; you validate intent and next action.
discussionQuestions: Which upcoming renewal has the weakest value evidence? What expansion hypothesis is already visible? Where do you need CSAM, CSA, CE, or SSP input?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Assess renewal risk and expansion readiness'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from renewal principles to one account and the action that changes risk this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test the renewal assessment', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Renewal and expansion choices depend on evidenced value, risk and customer readiness. Available headroom is a hypothesis, not a customer commitment. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account renewing in the next planning window and the evidence you currently use to judge risk.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the largest renewal risk? What value evidence would the customer recognize? Which expansion signal is supported by usage, consumption, or customer priority?
What early evidence has a peer used to separate renewal risk from a supported expansion signal?
listenFor: Renewals treated as admin, value evidence built too late, expansion detached from customer outcomes, and unclear CSAM/CSA/CE ownership.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal-risk card: agreement event, customer value evidence, risk, supported expansion hypothesis, role owner and next check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an upcoming renewal's risk or value-evidence gap and consider a possible response. Any benefit remains unconfirmed until observed. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized renewal assumption checked and whether it changed the next customer or owner action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-USPSI-AE-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-USPSI-AE-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-USPSI-AE-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

topicResources.title: Frontier Accelerator App - All Topics and Huddle in a Box
topicResources.description: Open Run a Huddle, choose the relevant view, then switch from Role Path to All Topics. Search and filter by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and AI Tool. For an uncovered team need, select Create your own huddle and download Huddle in a Box.

topicResources.title: Team Member Impact Survey
topicResources.description: Participant survey to complete at the close of the Week 9 transition huddle; allow about five minutes.

PLC-USPSI-AE-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. Be ready to support reflection, the continuing team rhythm, and choosing a Week 10 topic. Confirm the supplied Impact Survey link is available without asking for personal responses.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)
roles.description: Advances Enterprise solution-area opportunities through prospecting, discovery, proof, objection handling, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. Leads customer outcome conversations, coordinates partner-led deals and forecasts, routes work to appropriate scale engines, and plans portfolio renewals and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Engages early with the opportunity owner to shape executable commercial constructs across Microsoft and partner transaction routes. Navigates negotiation guardrails, coordinates owner-validated policy and licensing questions, routes approvals and exceptions, and hands off approved terms while addressing renewal commercial risk.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Assesses SME&C handoffs against coverage, sold outcomes, technical decisions, and accepted owners. Supports covered consumption portfolios through milestone readiness, partner and scale-engine handoffs, targeted adoption and technical interventions, attributed value evidence, and expansion hypotheses without assuming blanket customer or partner-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports covered SME&C consumption portfolios with readiness, handoffs, and targeted interventions.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: PDM
roles.description: Leads partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executive stakeholders and governance around growth priorities. Coordinates partner growth and co-sell efforts, drives course correction through business reviews, and brings technical, sales, and marketing owners together while reserving investment and commercial commitments for authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.name: PDM-R
roles.description: Develops a recruitment portfolio from qualification and partnership development through launch, a first transactable listing, and early wins. Mobilizes technical specialists, coordinates validated readiness, and prepares graduation handoffs accepted by accountable owners, with program approvals and graduation criteria retained by authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Recruits EPS partners from qualification to launch, first transactable listings, and early wins.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: PMM
roles.description: Shapes partner marketing plans and campaigns around market needs, partner maturity, and joint business priorities. Recommends investments, coordinates approved claims, localization, activation, and qualified sales handoffs, and optimizes performance with attribution limits and reusable learning in view, leaving funding approvals with program owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS partner marketing plans, campaigns, approved claims, and qualified sales handoffs.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

roles.description: Manages USPSI account priorities, opportunities, forecasts, renewals, and expansion. Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages USPSI accounts and pipeline using certified records and approved, human-verified evidence.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Sales Professional
roles.description: Advances USPSI solution-area prospecting, discovery, proof, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning using approved evidence and handling information according to organizational requirements. Coordinates account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances USPSI solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and decisions using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Commercial Executive

Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries through authoritative sources and approved handling, coordinating decision narratives, approvals, and execution without assuming policy, exception, legal, or compliance approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads USPSI commercial strategy and negotiation within authoritative policy and approval boundaries.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect

Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

Aligns executives and teams, supports adoption and growth planning, and manages delivery risks within organizational requirements while retaining technical architecture approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates USPSI success plans, adoption, milestones, and delivery risks using approved evidence.

roles.name: All ATU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for AE, ATS, and CE roles to explore account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution. Compare account, technical, and commercial perspectives on customer decisions and handoffs while keeping each role's responsibilities clear.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared account team workflows for account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution across AE, ATS, and CE roles.

roles.description: Shared huddle content for SSP and SE roles to explore discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs. Compare customer outcomes, technical criteria, and evidence for the next decision, including what sending and receiving roles need from one another.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared solution team workflows for discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs across SSP and SE roles.

roles.name: All CSU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for CSAM and CSA roles to explore customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution. Connect customer outcomes with delivery, usage, and technical evidence, and clarify decisions and handoffs across the success team.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared customer success workflows for customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution across CSAM and CSA roles.

roles.name: Services Account Executive (SAE)
roles.description: Co-architect a Services strategy from customer execution and value gaps, with continuity through delivery and value realization. ATU leads account discovery; SAE customer/commercial strategy does not own project delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Execution/value gaps, Services strategy and commercial continuity.

PLC-USPSI-ATS-W01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PLC-USPSI-ATS-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-USPSI-ATS-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

topicResources.title: What we've learned from Microsoft's own AI transformation
topicResources.description: Microsoft Customer Zero evidence for outcome-first transformation, end-to-end workflow redesign, employee-centered change, Capability Add measurement, and continuous human-AI learning. Metrics are bounded to the cited samples and periods.

topicResources.title: Becoming a Frontier Firm: Microsoft Frontier Playbook
topicResources.description: Practical Microsoft guide to Persona Acceleration, AI-Powered Process Redesign, and AI-First Possibility, grounded in Customer Zero transformation lessons.

PLC-USPSI-ATS-W01.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Introduce the why, reinforce the weekly rhythm, and welcome questions. Help distinguish the future weekly-experience preview from today's Orientation. Support readiness and access questions without inspecting individual tool usage, survey answers, or performance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
Does the team understand the motion and what to expect in the first role-specific huddle in Week 2?
What readiness question or access blocker needs support through our existing channels?

activities.name: Build the account intelligence brief
activities.description: Combine work and public context into a meeting-prep brief. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt: Build an account-intelligence and meeting-prep brief for [customer/agency] from the approved records and excerpts I supply. Summarize business priorities, technical strategy, stakeholders, relevant KPIs, AI/cloud workload signals, open risks, recent commitments and candidate next actions. Separate sourced facts from hypotheses; leave unsupported sections open. Identify sections supported only by my own view and the specific questions v-team counterparts could answer. If no account evidence is supplied, return a brief structure and the key planning questions, not customer facts. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Account intelligence and meeting-prep brief with risks, priorities, and actions, plus a short list of questions to put to the v-team where the brief rests on one person's view. If evidence is insufficient, an unfilled planning structure and material confirmation questions only.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The ATS decides which context is current enough to rely on. A brief assembled from work and public sources mixes material of different ages, and the stakeholder position that changed most recently is the one that matters most. The ATS also decides where one perspective is not enough, because a brief built from one person's sources can read as complete while missing what a teammate already knows.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. User-provided approved account records and excerpts, with source, scope, and as-of date; the minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or excerpts you want reflected; and relevant information already shared by v-team counterparts. Do not include restricted customer or personal data unless policy permits. A human verifies every source record and claim, makes all decisions, and performs any authorized updates; Microsoft 365 Copilot does not make record changes.
activities.whyThisMatters: Account intelligence is useful when it changes the next technical decision, not when it creates a longer dossier.

activities.name: Draft an intelligence-hub structure for human-maintained contributions
activities.description: Turn account intelligence into something the whole v-team feeds, so the picture reflects what each member can see rather than what one person could reach.
activities.prompt: Using only the approved account excerpts and contributor roles I supply, draft a text-only intelligence-hub structure: priorities, opportunity context, stakeholders, estate, interactions and risks. Leave unsupplied contributor sections visibly empty. For supplied contributions record role, source, account scope and date. Keep conflicts separate with a resolution question. Draft contribution requests and a refresh checklist. Do not obtain contributions, retain memory, create a shared hub or publish. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Text-only structure with supplied sourced contributions, empty sections, conflicts, draft requests and human refresh checklist; no shared hub created.
activities.humanCheckpoint: ATS reviews the hub for accuracy before sharing with the v-team, and reviews each contribution before it reaches the shared hub rather than only at first build, confirming that no customer-confidential material sits where it should not. Where two contributors describe the same stakeholder or risk differently, the hub keeps both accounts with their sources and dates, and the ATS records which one the account plan proceeds on and why, or marks it unresolved. A difference between two contributors can be two accurate observations from different vantage points, and collapsing it early loses the signal.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied sanitized account excerpts, contributor roles, intended audience and permitted contributions already received with sources/dates; human-maintained location.
activitySteps: 1. List the approved account-planning records available to provide, and identify missing records. For CRM/MSX-derived information, provide only the minimum necessary approved fields or excerpts, with source, scope, and as-of/freshness date.
2. List the v-team members who can see what you cannot, and what each of them holds.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Review the first hub build against what you already know about the account.
5. Check that nothing customer-confidential sits where the wider v-team should not see it, then send the contribution requests and give people a deadline they can meet.
6. As contributions come back, review each one before it reaches the shared hub and hold anything that should not sit there.
7. Add the approved contributions with their contributor, source and date, and chase the sections still empty.
8. Set the refresh cadence and agree with the v-team who reads the change summary.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: An account picture assembled by one person is bounded by the records and context that person can provide. The hub's value is that the gaps stay visible until somebody who can see them fills them in.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on building an account intelligence and meeting-preparation brief.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is an account intelligence brief with technical risks, workload signals, stakeholder context, and next actions. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: Which account are you least confident you could brief someone on right now?
Where does your current account picture come from, and how old is it?
Which part of your account picture exists only in a teammate's head?
What technical signal would change your priorities this week if you knew it today?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the account intelligence brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the assembled account picture to the single signal that should change this week's priorities. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build a standing account intelligence hub the v-team contributes to', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Account intelligence improves technical priorities when missing context is reconciled with the v-team. The useful change is a decision informed by their answer, not a longer brief. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one account, its approved current plan or context, dated technical signals and the unresolved account question. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What is in your account brief that you could not source if challenged?
Which signal in the brief actually changes what you do next week?
What is missing that you only notice once it is written down?
What source-checking habit has a peer used when a polished brief hid stale stakeholder context?
listenFor: Briefs assembled from memory rather than systems, KPI figures quoted without their definition or date, technical risks with no named owner, and stakeholder context that is a year old. Also note the brief becoming an end in itself rather than driving a decision.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one account-intelligence brief: source/date, customer priority, stakeholder position, KPI definition, technical risk and v-team validation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What intelligence gap changed the technical priority after v-team review, and which assumption remains unsupported?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an account intelligence brief and identify a question your own sources cannot answer; whether to seek v-team input is a separate, optional next step. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a safe description of the intelligence gap, what the counterpart could confirm, and whether it changed the technical priority. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on assembling an executive technical customer narrative.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is an executive-ready technical narrative with sourced claims, proof points, decision questions, and a technical ask. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: When did an executive last stop you to ask what something meant?
Which part of your technical story do you find hardest to say without jargon?
What is this executive personally putting at risk by backing your recommendation?
What decision do you actually need from the executive, and have you ever asked for it directly?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Translate architecture into business value'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the technical story to the one decision you want the executive to make, and the proof they need to make it. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Executive technical narratives translate options into customer consequences and an explicit decision. Preserve the difficult trade-off instead of hiding it behind technical detail. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming executive conversation, the desired decision, approved technical proof points and the claims that need validation. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Read your opening line aloud. Would a CFO know what you meant?
Which claim in your narrative rests on a proof point you do not have?
What are you asking the executive to decide, stated in one sentence?
How would another ATS translate your strongest technical claim without losing its caveat?
listenFor: Architecture described rather than translated, value asserted without evidence, narratives that end without an ask, and jargon that survived because nobody in the room questioned it. Also note a narrative aimed at the technical stakeholder while claiming to target the executive.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one executive technical narrative: business decision, technical option, sourced proof, caveat and one-sentence ask. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical trade-off became clearer in customer terms, and what proof does the executive still need?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could adapt a technical narrative for an executive audience, clarifying the decision, options and trade-offs without needing to present it. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized trade-off made clearer and whether a reviewer better understood the executive decision. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on developing a technical strategy and decision trajectory.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a technical trajectory with priority bets, proof needs, owners, risks, milestones, and open decisions. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What is the next technical decision this customer has to make, and when?
Which of your technical bets is least supported by evidence?
What would have to be true for the customer to commit to the direction you are recommending?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Analyze consumption and technical blockers'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the technical direction to the next decision it requires, with an owner and the evidence that unblocks it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate technical and business assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Technical strategy advances through sequenced, evidence-backed decisions. A proposed owner or date remains a proposal until the person with authority confirms it. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one technical strategy decision, approved customer context, known constraints and the next proof or decision needed. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the next decision in the trajectory, and who makes it?
Which bet would you abandon first if evidence went against it?
What proof does the customer need before they will commit, and do you have a path to producing it?
How does a peer make the next technical decision visible before it becomes a delivery blocker?
listenFor: A strategy that is a destination without a sequence, bets with no falsification condition, proof needs identified after the customer already asked, and milestones with no owner. Also note technical direction set without the customer's own objectives in the room.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical decision path: customer objective, options, next decision, proof gap, decision owner and date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption affects the technical decision sequence, and what proof or owner confirmation would change it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore the next technical decision and the proposed proof or timing questions for its owner. Unconfirmed ownership and timing must remain open. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized technical decision or proof gap clarified and whether owner confirmation improved the next step. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Validate briefing evidence and decisions

activities.whyThisMatters: A briefing plan without evidence and follow-through becomes calendar management.
