facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on designing an executive briefing experience.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is an EBC plan with desired decisions, participants, evidence, preparation milestones, and follow-through ownership. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What is the one thing the customer should leave the briefing believing?
Who in the room can actually approve the next step?
What is on your briefing preparation list that currently has no owner?
What would make this briefing worth their time rather than ours?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Design the executive briefing experience'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the briefing design to the single decision it is meant to produce and who must be present for that. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate briefing evidence and decisions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: A briefing earns executive time by advancing a relevant customer decision with the right evidence and contributors. An invitation is not confirmed attendance or a decision guarantee. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one planned executive briefing, its intended customer decision, proposed participants and known preparation dependencies. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What will the customer do differently after this briefing?
Who in the room can approve that, and are they invited?
Which part of the agenda serves us rather than them?
Which agenda choice did a peer remove to make room for the customer decision?
listenFor: Agendas built around what we want to present, attendee lists without a decision maker, briefings with no ask, and content density that leaves no room for the customer to talk. Also note an experience designed for the meeting rather than for what happens after it.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or approved context is unavailable, use a sanitized supplied example or a clearly labeled synthetic case. On paper, outline the customer decision, required decision-maker role, agenda choice, supporting evidence and follow-through ask. Mark evidence, assumptions and unknowns; proposed attendance or follow-through is not confirmed. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient. Any later AI run must use project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot and approved supplied inputs.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What makes the briefing worth executive time, and which decision or contributor is still missing?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review an executive briefing around a customer decision, check who can make it and draft the reason to attend; report attendance as requested or confirmed, not guaranteed. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized change to the decision, audience or reason to attend and whether it made the briefing more purposeful; pending attendance is acceptable. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: Using supplied current customer signals and the reviewed talk track, rehearse an adaptive technical conversation. Ask one hypothetical stakeholder question at a time and wait for my reply. After three exchanges identify missed signals, overclaimed proof and proposals stated as commitments. Produce a revised opening, two follow-up questions and source-review list; do not reuse unverified claims as facts. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.

activities.humanCheckpoint: The ATS decides which technical claims survive into the conversation. Rehearsal makes an answer fluent, and fluency is easy to mistake for evidence in front of an audience technical enough to test it.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Approved narrative; meeting type; customer context; desired decision.
activities.whyThisMatters: Ten minutes rehearsing the talk track is cheaper than improvising it in the room.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on adjusting the technical talk track from customer signals.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a signal-adjusted talk track with opening language, questions, objections, responses, and human review flags. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What did the customer say recently that should change how you talk about this?
Where is your current talk track still answering last quarter's objection?
What signal are you choosing to ignore because it is inconvenient?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Adjust the talk track from current signals'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the customer signal to the specific line in your talk track that has to change because of it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Find the weak claims before the customer does', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Talk tracks improve when actual customer signals change a specific message. Keep what the customer said separate from your interpretation and validate new claims. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one current talk track, recent approved customer comments or signals, and the objection or assumption those signals challenge. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What specifically did the customer say, and what did you infer from it?
Which part of your talk track is now answering a question they stopped asking?
What would you change if you took their last objection at face value?
What change in a customer's wording caused a colleague to change the substance, not just the phrasing?
listenFor: Signals interpreted to confirm what we already planned, talk tracks updated in wording but not in substance, and customer silence read as agreement. Also note adjustments based on one conversation with one person treated as the account's position.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one talk-track revision: quoted synthetic or sanitized signal, separate inference, changed line, caveat and customer validation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What customer statement changed the message, and where did you separate the signal from interpretation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could revisit a talk-track line against an existing customer statement and consider what you would change; no new customer conversation is needed. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized customer signal and a paraphrase of the line it changed, plus whether the revised message was clearer or still needs testing. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot from the app launcher or copilot.cloud.microsoft and start in Chat.

activities.name: Build the v-team commitment board
activities.description: Lay the v-team's commitments out as a board the team can see and work from. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt: From [commitment and technical evidence], draft a v-team board for its account/portfolio scope, oldest activity first. Show each commitment’s owner, dependency, last evidenced activity and agreed checkpoint, with outcomes, workloads, technical decisions, risks and roles. Mark missing checkpoints unagreed and proposed dates as proposals; only agreed dates can be overdue. Keep my portfolio view separate from each account’s shareable view to prevent cross-account disclosure. Return paste-ready tables. Use supplied material only; don’t search, connect or take actions.
activities.expectedOutput: A v-team commitment board covering your accounts, sorted by last observed activity, oldest first, with an owner and a last-activity date on every row, the agreed next checkpoint where one exists and not agreed where none does, any proposed date labelled as a proposal, passed checkpoints marked, and the shared per-account views kept separate from your own portfolio view.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The ATS confirms each named role has capacity to take the work. Orchestration that assigns without asking produces a plan everyone nods at and nobody starts. The ATS also agrees the human handoff structure and what may be shared, because accounts carry different teams and confidentiality boundaries; a shared record the v-team did not agree to maintain creates avoidable overhead.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. User-provided approved account and technical records for the accounts you carry, with source, scope, and as-of date; role list; decision needs; for each open commitment, the date and nature of the last observed activity and the agreed next checkpoint where one exists; today's date; and the approved source record each v-team uses to track work.
activities.whyThisMatters: Twelve commitments written as prose have to be re-read. The same twelve as rows can be sorted.

activities.name: Review v-team commitments at a human-owned checkpoint
activities.description: Compare supplied commitment snapshots; no recorded activity is an owner question, not proof of a stall.
activities.prompt: Compare the prior/current commitment snapshots I supply using the review date and agreed checkpoints. Show source, last observed activity, agreed versus proposed date and new versus unchanged exception status from the supplied prior review. Distinguish confirmed progress, record change without progress evidence, no recorded change and unknown status. Draft one targeted owner question per exception. Do not scan mail/accounts, schedule checks or remember an unsupplied prior review. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: One-time exceptions with new/unchanged status, agreed-versus-proposed dates and owner questions; no recurring check configured.
activities.humanCheckpoint: ATS decides whether silence actually means a stall, and owns the judgment about which chases are appropriate given the relationships involved.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied prior/current snapshots, source dates, agreed checkpoints/owners, review date and prior exceptions if available.
activitySteps: 1. Supply prior/current approved snapshots, review date and previous exceptions if available.
2. Compare documented activity with agreed checkpoints manually or in Copilot if permitted.
3. Treat absent evidence as unknown until the owner confirms.
4. Review and ask the owner questions yourself.
5. Maintain the tracker separately and agree a human-owned next review.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: Technical commitments can go quiet until the customer has moved on. Keep a named owner and agree human-led follow-up so commitments remain visible between sessions.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on mobilizing the technical v-team around priorities and risks.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a v-team commitment board with owners, dependencies, investment signals, checkpoints, and next actions. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: Who on your technical v-team could not state the current priority if asked today?
Which dependency has gone quiet in the last two weeks?
Where does your v-team actually look to see what is outstanding?
What are you carrying yourself that should belong to someone else?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the v-team commitment board'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the coordination picture to one specific ask, to one named person, with a date. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Keep the v-team commitments moving between huddles', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: V-team mobilization turns a dependency into a bounded, answerable ask. Confirm accepted ownership and capacity rather than treating the board as agreement. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring the accounts you currently carry with their open commitments and review the commitment from the prior huddle.
facilitatorQuestions: If I asked each v-team member the current priority, would I get the same answer?
Which dependency is at risk, and does its owner know?
What are you doing yourself that is really someone else's accountability?
How does another ATS confirm a v-team commitment without absorbing another role's accountability?
listenFor: Priorities that live only in the ATS's head, owners assigned in a document but never agreed in a conversation, dependencies tracked without dates, and the ATS absorbing work because delegating it feels slower. Also note v-team meetings that report status without deciding anything.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one v-team commitment row: technical priority, dependency, proposed accountable role, acceptance needed, date and escalation trigger. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a bounded v-team ask using the existing account board or a small manual note, with the input and proposed date clearly marked. Drafting does not require sending it. Receiving-owner acceptance is required before treating any actual handoff as accepted; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a safe description of a v-team ask and whether it was accepted, clarified or held; note any reduction in handoff ambiguity. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. Be ready to support reflection, the continuing team rhythm, and choosing a Week 10 topic. Confirm the supplied Impact Survey link is available without asking for personal responses.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

PLC-SMEC-SMEC-CE-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-SMEC-SMEC-CE-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-SMEC-SMEC-CE-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Risk you find this week is a conversation. The same risk found by the customer is an escalation. Focus on finding it earlier.
keyTalkingPoints: A health score can tell you something is wrong. It rarely tells you what to do.
Every risk needs an owner and a date or it is an observation.
AI is good at surfacing signal. Prioritizing it is judgment.
discussionQuestions: Which account is at risk in a way the reporting does not show?
What stops a known risk from getting an owner?
Which part of this carries policy or precedent risk?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify commercial risk and escalation priorities'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the one deal you just briefed to where commercial risk is concentrated across the book, then back to what you will act on first. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test assumptions behind the commercial risk view', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Commercial risk prioritization needs current authoritative evidence and an accountable intervention owner. Ranking risks does not authorize pricing, exceptions or commitments. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one real commercial structure and policy example you are working on now, and review the commitment you made last week.
facilitatorQuestions: Which commercial risk is most consequential this week, and what dated evidence supports it? Who can act and by when? How does a colleague distinguish a risk score from a cause that changes the intervention?
listenFor: Risk described without an owner or a date; health reported by score rather than cause; and interventions discussed but never started.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one commercial-risk brief: dated fact, cause versus score, customer consequence, governed action, owner and action date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could compare commercial risks and explore a proposed intervention for the most consequential one, without having to initiate an owner conversation. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized commercial risk verified or routed and whether it made the intervention clearer; keep agreement and pricing details private. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: Review the supplied licensing, discount and agreement structure against dated authoritative guidance. Separate documented exceptions or concerns from questions for the policy/licensing owner. Identify unused paid entitlement only when compatible supplied purchase, licensing and usage evidence supports the claim; missing activity or commercial evidence is unknown, not unused licensing or non-compliance. Cite source sections, units, periods and applicability limits. List approval evidence, renewal implications and gaps without determining compliance, eligibility or discount approval. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Source-linked licensing/discount risk questions, documented versus unconfirmed exception status, evidence-supported entitlement observations only where possible, and authoritative review gaps; no compliance determination.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE validates eligibility against current policy. Licensing rules change between program cycles, and a discount structure that was compliant last year is the kind of thing found during audit rather than during the deal.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied licensing/discount structure, executed terms, dated authoritative guidance and approval evidence; purchase/licensing/usage excerpts with compatible units and periods if unused-entitlement analysis is needed; accountable commercial/policy reviewers.
activities.whyThisMatters: Reviewing licensing and discount risk is judgment work. Any proposed option requires CE review; the CE remains accountable.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Policy questions found at approval cost weeks. Focus on finding the question early and routing it to the authoritative owner.
keyTalkingPoints: AI can assemble the context and possible questions. It cannot interpret policy, approve exceptions, or invent authority. The useful output is a routed question with evidence, not a guessed answer.
discussionQuestions: Which policy or licensing question most often causes rework? Where did an approval path surprise you? Which interpretation must come from an authoritative source?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the investment path against policy and approval requirements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from policy categories to one live deal question and the owner who can answer it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test policy and licensing assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Policy checks distinguish verified positions from unresolved interpretations. Use current authoritative guidance and route rulings beyond your authority instead of letting AI fill the gap. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one real commercial structure or policy example, the approved source you would check, and the decision or approval path currently unclear.
facilitatorQuestions: Which policy or licensing question changes this deal's next decision? What current authoritative source would settle it? How does another CE frame a self-contained question when the guidance is unavailable or ambiguous?
listenFor: Policy interpreted from memory; uncertainty left unflagged; approval paths discovered late; and questions that need an authoritative owner rather than a generated answer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one policy-question card: precise question, relevant deal fact, current guidance/version gap, authoritative owner and dependent commitment to hold. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which policy or commercial boundary is verified, which is still uncertain, and who can authorize the next step?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could take one open policy or licensing question to its authoritative owner rather than answering it yourself. Keep unresolved rulings pending; only the authoritative owner can confirm the position. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share the type of policy question and whether review clarified, changed or held the next step; omit restricted ruling text. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Reviewers do not need more history. They need the recommendation, options, assumptions, risks, and decision requested.
keyTalkingPoints: A commercial decision narrative should separate facts from judgment. It should show why this structure, what alternatives were considered, and who must review it.
discussionQuestions: What would a reviewer need to say yes, no, or not yet? Which assumption is unsupported? What customer impact needs to be explained plainly?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the commercial decision narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from deal facts to the internal recommendation and the decision being requested. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test commercial structure assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Commercial narratives should make assumptions and customer consequences inspectable by the authorized reviewer. Reviewer questions are useful evidence, not failure. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring a reviewed deal option, known assumptions, transition considerations, and the audience for the recommendation.
facilitatorQuestions: Which recommendation would a reviewer understand quickly? What assumption needs evidence? Which reviewer or decision owner is missing?
listenFor: Narratives that bury the ask; options without trade-offs; customer impact omitted; and transition or migration risks stated without a source.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one commercial recommendation outline: decision requested, evidenced facts, options/trade-offs, customer impact, caveat and authorized reviewer. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could write the commercial recommendation for one deal in a form a reviewer could act on without asking you a question. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized assumption challenged or clarified and whether it improved the recommendation; no case or terms are required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.description: Bring your own product data into proposal creation for an MCA-E or EA to MCA-E transition, and resolve what does not map before it reaches the customer.
activities.prompt: Using the product/quantity table I supply for an MCA-E proposal, help me prepare a human-review draft from the data and agreement terms I provide. State any required input format; compare SKUs/products only against supplied agreement or reference data, and list every unmatched product separately. Do not create or update a record. activitySteps: 1. Prepare the minimum necessary approved product and quantity data as a spreadsheet or CSV, with source, scope, and as-of date.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Negotiation is where vague structure becomes expensive. Focus on authority boundaries, give/get logic, and rehearsal before the customer asks.
keyTalkingPoints: Prepare scenarios and objections from approved evidence; the accountable role owner reviews them. You remain accountable for authority, customer commitments, concession discipline, and escalation triggers.
discussionQuestions: Where is your concession logic unclear? Which customer ask would trigger escalation? What must not be said before review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rehearse the commercial negotiation'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from negotiation principles to one realistic customer objection and the reviewed response. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test negotiation assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Negotiation preparation tests sequenced trades and confirmed authority limits before customer pressure arrives. Rehearsed concessions are not approved concessions. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one negotiation scenario, approved position, authority boundaries, and any known customer asks.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer ask would test your authority boundary? What give/get logic is clear enough to use? What must be reviewed before customer-facing use?
listenFor: Concession logic that is not tied to value; authority boundaries not explicit; likely objections unrehearsed; and customer commitments that require review.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one negotiation exchange: objective, reviewed give/get or explicitly hypothetical alternative, authority boundary, objection and escalation response. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Rehearse with a peer; if alone, write both sides and mark the exchange untested, not a validated customer or coaching response. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could rehearse a negotiation scenario using confirmed concession authority and applicable escalation guidance; ask the authorized owner about unresolved boundaries before offering terms. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized rehearsal lesson about a trade or boundary and whether it improved readiness; a completed negotiation is optional. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial execution stalls when owners, evidence, and approval handoffs are implied. Focus on making them explicit.
keyTalkingPoints: Execution is not just follow-up. It is approval routing, evidence readiness, exception handling, ownership, and escalation without overstating authority.
discussionQuestions: Which handoff is implicit today? What evidence is missing for the next approver? Where could ECIF, Deal Desk, finance, policy, or legal review be needed?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Clarify ECIF commercial and approval dependencies'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the full execution path to the single blocker and owner that must be handled next. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test approval and execution assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Commercial execution depends on verified approval state and accepted ownership. Mapping the path matters when it exposes the next governed decision and missing evidence. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one in-flight deal or investment dependency, its known approval stage, and the evidence or owner currently missing.
facilitatorQuestions: Which handoff or approval is the deal actually waiting on? What evidence is missing? Who owns the next decision, and what should not be represented as approved?
listenFor: Approval status overstated; handoffs without owners; ECIF, finance, Deal Desk, legal, or policy dependencies hidden; and blockers described without the next governed action.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one approval-path row: required decision, evidence, current status or unknown, authorized owner, sequence dependency and next question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a deal's approval path and identify what the first owner would need to confirm; no outreach is required. Receiving-owner acceptance is required before treating any actual handoff as accepted; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized approval or execution gap checked and whether the owner clarified the next step; a cleared blocker is not required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test renewal strategy assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Renewal strategy uses verified agreement timing, economics and value while preserving commercial options. Expansion needs evidence and authorized decisions, not headroom alone. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one renewal, approved context, current structure, risk signal, and expansion or approval question.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal has the least remaining room to change its commercial path? What agreement date, customer evidence or approval dependency changes the priority? How does a peer surface that risk early enough for CE intervention?
listenFor: Renewals treated as administrative; risk noticed inside the last quarter; and expansion pursued without evidence of realized value.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal workback: agreement event/date, customer evidence, commercial risk, remaining options, CE/DAE/partner ownership and next check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could build a renewal strategy for one account using real agreement and discount data, not recollection. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized renewal assumption confirmed or changed and whether it improved timing or the next review; omit agreement and discount data. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
