facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A weekly, monthly, quarterly, or event-driven leadership review requires decisions, adjustments, escalation asks, and a clear performance narrative. Focus on one decision and the evidence needed to make it.
keyTalkingPoints: Leadership decision: Confirm the decisions, adjustments, owners, escalation asks, messages to cascade, and next inspection.
Boundary: Use only the cadence and decision rights established for the relevant organization; the leader confirms the forecast, commitments, narrative, and communications.
discussionQuestions: Which review decision changes the plan?
What is evidenced, forecast or assumed in the narrative?
What message, owner and next inspection follow the decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Produce the operating review, decision log, and action register'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Design a change-only signal feed for the next review', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Operating reviews turn governed evidence into human decisions and accepted follow-through. Use established org cadence; the leader validates forecast, commitments, narrative and communication. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted current review decision, governed evidence and the narrative or escalation that needs confirmation. Identify the actual decision authority and next owner. Exclude employee/HR data and AI-generated individual performance judgments.
facilitatorQuestions: Which operating-review decision actually changes the next cycle? What governed evidence, owner and approved message support it? How would another leader communicate it while preserving the organization's actual cadence and decision rights?
listenFor: Activity reporting without a decision, local shadow data, mixed metric definitions, assumed authority, AI-generated employee evaluation, or leader takeover of field execution. Use only the cadence and decision rights established for the relevant organization; the leader confirms the forecast, commitments, narrative, and communications.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one operating-review decision log: governed evidence, decision, owner, adjustment, approved-communication gap and next inspection. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which caveat changed the decision or message, and how will next review test follow-through?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could check a consequential operating-review claim or follow-through gap and personally confirm a bounded decision or communication within authority and org rhythm. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized caveat clarified and whether it improved next review; no full pack, forecast or cascade message is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-LDR-LDR-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-LDR-LDR-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-LDR-LDR-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)
roles.description: Advances Enterprise solution-area opportunities through prospecting, discovery, proof, objection handling, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. Leads customer outcome conversations, coordinates partner-led deals and forecasts, routes work to appropriate scale engines, and plans portfolio renewals and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Engages early with the opportunity owner to shape executable commercial constructs across Microsoft and partner transaction routes. Navigates negotiation guardrails, coordinates owner-validated policy and licensing questions, routes approvals and exceptions, and hands off approved terms while addressing renewal commercial risk.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Assesses SME&C handoffs against coverage, sold outcomes, technical decisions, and accepted owners. Supports covered consumption portfolios through milestone readiness, partner and scale-engine handoffs, targeted adoption and technical interventions, attributed value evidence, and expansion hypotheses without assuming blanket customer or partner-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports covered SME&C consumption portfolios with readiness, handoffs, and targeted interventions.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: PDM
roles.description: Leads partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executive stakeholders and governance around growth priorities. Coordinates partner growth and co-sell efforts, drives course correction through business reviews, and brings technical, sales, and marketing owners together while reserving investment and commercial commitments for authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.name: PDM-R
roles.description: Develops a recruitment portfolio from qualification and partnership development through launch, a first transactable listing, and early wins. Mobilizes technical specialists, coordinates validated readiness, and prepares graduation handoffs accepted by accountable owners, with program approvals and graduation criteria retained by authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Recruits EPS partners from qualification to launch, first transactable listings, and early wins.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: PMM
roles.description: Shapes partner marketing plans and campaigns around market needs, partner maturity, and joint business priorities. Recommends investments, coordinates approved claims, localization, activation, and qualified sales handoffs, and optimizes performance with attribution limits and reusable learning in view, leaving funding approvals with program owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS partner marketing plans, campaigns, approved claims, and qualified sales handoffs.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Manages USPSI account priorities, opportunities, forecasts, renewals, and expansion. Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages USPSI accounts and pipeline using certified records and approved, human-verified evidence.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Sales Professional
roles.description: Advances USPSI solution-area prospecting, discovery, proof, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning using approved evidence and handling information according to organizational requirements. Coordinates account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances USPSI solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and decisions using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads USPSI commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewal planning by assessing commercial risk and structural exposure. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries through authoritative sources and approved handling, coordinating decision narratives, approvals, and execution without assuming policy, exception, legal, or compliance approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads USPSI commercial strategy and negotiation within authoritative policy and approval boundaries.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Provides USPSI technical advice on production architecture, validation, technical health, and cost optimization using approved evidence and organizational handling requirements. Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates USPSI outcome-based success plans, milestones, and accepted owners using approved health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder evidence. Aligns executives and teams, supports adoption and growth planning, and manages delivery risks within organizational requirements while retaining technical architecture approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates USPSI success plans, adoption, milestones, and delivery risks using approved evidence.

roles.name: All ATU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for AE, ATS, and CE roles to explore account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution. Compare account, technical, and commercial perspectives on customer decisions and handoffs while keeping each role's responsibilities clear.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared account team workflows for account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution across AE, ATS, and CE roles.

roles.descriptionSummary: Shared solution team workflows for discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs across SSP and SE roles.

roles.name: All CSU

roles.descriptionSummary: Shared customer success workflows for customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution across CSAM and CSA roles.

roles.description: Co-architect a Services strategy from customer execution and value gaps, with continuity through delivery and value realization. ATU leads account discovery; SAE customer/commercial strategy does not own project delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Execution/value gaps, Services strategy and commercial continuity.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

activities.name: Separate coverage facts from unanswered transition risks
activities.description: Compare the coverage evidence and relevant role guidance to identify continuity risks before an interim ownership decision.
activities.prompt: For one account transition or coverage gap in [ATU/STU/CSU remit], review the permitted coverage snapshot I supply and the authoritative role guidance I identify. Separate customer commitments with accepted owners, unconfirmed coverage and missing evidence. Cite material facts to the snapshot and guidance with publisher, title, date and link; general guidance is not customer proof, and CAIP assignment rules apply only within their documented scope. Return material continuity risks, the evidence needed to settle them and the role that can confirm each; do not invent risks to fill a count. Keep this to business evidence, not employee assessment. Draft only. Flag unavailable sources.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-linked list of material continuity risks, where supported, with confirmed/unconfirmed coverage, evidence gaps and role-specific confirmation questions; no fixed risk count or AI assignment of ownership.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager verifies local remit and asks the named role owner to confirm coverage; research does not assign work or establish interim ownership.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted transition/coverage snapshot, customer commitments, manager remit, named authoritative role-guidance sources and known current owners.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this activity or another Featured option; use an existing relevant business artifact rather than completing every activity in sequence.
2. Confirm your remit and permitted inputs, then run the prompt with the evidence listed here. If the tool/source is unavailable, use a permitted extract or manual review.
3. Check source dates, access gaps and the distinction between evidence, proposal and agreement.
4. Make the stated human decision or confirmation request, with owner-role acceptance and a review point; any real record update or communication follows the separate authorized process.
activities.whyThisMatters: A coverage gap becomes manageable when customer commitments and actual accepted ownership are visible, without assuming another org's assignment rules.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: An account transition, vacancy, or at-risk customer creates a coverage decision. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: AE vacancy and account transition. STU: SSP vacancy and specialist transition. CSU: CSAM continuity; CAIP CSA capacity rules apply only to CAIP.
Boundary: Normal AE, SSP, CSAM, and CSA execution remains with those roles; do not generalize CAIP assignment rules.
discussionQuestions: Which customer outcome is exposed by the coverage gap?
What evidence supports the proposed route in your organization?
Who must accept the assignment?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate coverage facts from unanswered transition risks'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Check authorized account context where access exists', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coverage inspection protects continuity by separating verified assignment from gaps needing manager judgment. Normal account and delivery execution stays with AE, SSP, CSAM and CSA roles. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers. CAIP assignment rules are not universal coverage rules.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-continuity gap is evidenced and what capacity is available in your own team? What interim owner and review point can you authorize or escalate? How does a peer manager keep a proposed assignment distinct from accepted coverage?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Normal AE, SSP, CSAM, and CSA execution remains with those roles; do not generalize CAIP assignment rules.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one coverage decision card: customer continuity risk, permitted capacity evidence, interim owner proposal, authority gap and next check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which continuity risk changed after checking evidence, and what intervention can you authorize here?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could review a consequential coverage question and decide a bounded intervention or evidence request within your authority. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a de-identified coverage assumption clarified and whether it improved continuity or the next check. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified coverage gap exposes a customer outcome, while proposed routes have different capacity assumptions. Check applicable guidance and the role that must accept, without using HR data.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Coverage decisions connect a customer-outcome gap to capacity and accepted ownership within the manager's remit. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the de-identified coverage exception and current capacity evidence in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A coverage discussion is not an employee ranking or a cross-remit assignment. Look for a bounded coverage decision within the documented organizational remit.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a coverage discussion is not an employee ranking or a cross-remit assignment. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Check authorized stage-specific signals and missing evidence
activities.description: Inspect a signal at the correct stage of work and formulate a source-backed question for its owner.
activities.prompt: For [team/portfolio scope] and [commercial pipeline, technical milestone or post-signature consumption stage], inspect the dated authorized record signals actually available and the stated outlook I supply. Return up to three material mismatches, each with source identifier/date, what changed, what is interpretation and the confirmation question for the record owner. Do not mix pipeline, technical proof and realized consumption as interchangeable measures. Recommend one correction request or investigation, not a forecast verdict. If access is missing, use a permitted extract or manual checklist. Keep this to business evidence, not employee assessment. Draft only. Flag unavailable sources.
activities.expectedOutput: A stage-specific mismatch list and one evidence-backed correction/investigation request, with unavailable sources explicit.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager chooses the intervention and the accountable IC verifies and corrects records; no universal sole M1 forecast ownership is assumed.
activities.requiredContext: Named team/portfolio scope, stage of work, stated outlook, authorized dated signals and record-owner roles.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this activity or another Featured option; use an existing relevant business artifact rather than completing every activity in sequence.
2. Confirm your remit and permitted inputs, then run the prompt with the evidence listed here. If the tool/source is unavailable, use a permitted extract or manual review.
3. Check source dates, access gaps and the distinction between evidence, proposal and agreement.
4. Make the stated human decision or confirmation request, with owner-role acceptance and a review point; any real record update or communication follows the separate authorized process.
activities.whyThisMatters: Intervening on the wrong stage measure can miss the real risk while creating a correction that does not improve the customer work.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A pipeline, milestone, or consumption signal no longer matches the team's stated outlook. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: commercial opportunity and renewal evidence. STU: technical close and uncommitted-to-committed progression. CSU: accepted milestones, consumption and delivery health.
Boundary: No source establishes sole Enterprise M1 forecast ownership; IC owners correct records and the manager decides the intervention.
discussionQuestions: What changed since the prior outlook?
Which signal needs correction by the record owner?
What intervention can you decide within your own organization?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check authorized stage-specific signals and missing evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare a concise inspection readout for human review', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Stage inspection distinguishes evidence, assumptions and the right intervention. IC owners correct records; manager review does not establish sole Enterprise M1 forecast ownership. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
facilitatorQuestions: Which stage-specific evidence gap could change the intervention? Who owns the record correction and who decides the manager response? How would a peer challenge the risk without assuming sole forecast ownership?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. No source establishes sole Enterprise M1 forecast ownership; IC owners correct records and the manager decides the intervention.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one stage-specific intervention card: governed signal, missing evidence, IC record owner, manager decision and review date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which stage signal changed your intervention, and what correction belongs to the IC record owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could inspect a consequential stage signal and choose a manager intervention or evidence/correction request to its record owner. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized stage assumption checked and whether it made intervention or correction more precise. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified outlook exception no longer matches dated opportunity or milestone evidence. Ask which record owner can verify it and what intervention is within the manager's remit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A manager's inspection question must fit the stage of work: opportunity, milestone and consumption evidence answer different questions. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the de-identified outlook exception and dated stage-of-work evidence.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Pipeline, milestone and consumption evidence are not interchangeable. Look for an inspection question matched to the actual stage and record owner.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: pipeline, milestone and consumption evidence are not interchangeable. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Draft coaching questions from a de-identified business scenario
activities.description: Prepare evidence-focused coaching questions for a de-identified business decision without taking over the team member's judgment.
activities.prompt: Using only [the fictional or de-identified business plan, handoff or technical decision], write three coaching questions: one testing evidence, one exposing a material tradeoff and one letting the person choose their next action. Explain each decision criterion; propose a team-member-owned follow-up and work evidence to revisit. Do not rewrite the person's answer or assess employee ability, behavior or performance; use business evidence only, not employee profiles or history. Draft only and flag unavailable inputs.
activities.expectedOutput: Three judgment-focused coaching questions with decision criteria and a proposed owner-led follow-up evidence check.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager chooses questions appropriate to the situation; the team member owns the real decision and follow-up. No employee evaluation is generated.
activities.requiredContext: A fictional or de-identified business artifact, its intended customer outcome, known evidence gaps and a review point; no real employee/customer identifiers.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this activity or another Featured option; use an existing relevant business artifact rather than completing every activity in sequence.
2. Confirm your remit and permitted inputs, then run the prompt with the evidence listed here. If the tool/source is unavailable, use a permitted extract or manual review.
3. Check source dates, access gaps and the distinction between evidence, proposal and agreement.
4. Make the stated human decision or confirmation request, with owner-role acceptance and a review point; any real record update or communication follows the separate authorized process.
activities.whyThisMatters: Coaching improves judgment when it probes evidence and trade-offs rather than replacing the person's decision with an AI answer.

activities.name: Rehearse a judgment-focused coaching conversation
activities.description: Rehearse an evidence-focused coaching conversation using a fictional business scenario and clearly simulated reactions.
activities.prompt: Role-play a fictional colleague discussing [paste/describe the fictional or approved de-identified business scenario]. I will open with a coaching question. Pause for my response in each of three exchanges, then coach whether I tested evidence, explored a trade-off and left the next action with the colleague. Label all reactions simulated; do not invent actual customer agreement or make any employee evaluation. End with one revised question and the business evidence to verify in real work. Keep this to business evidence, not employee assessment. Draft only. Flag unavailable sources.
activities.expectedOutput: Three simulated coaching exchanges, feedback on the manager's questions, one revised question and a business-evidence verification point.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager judges the questions before any real conversation and verifies business facts separately; simulated reactions are not evidence about an employee.
activities.requiredContext: A fictional/de-identified business scenario, intended decision, coaching question and evidence boundaries; no real employee or customer data.
activitySteps: 1. Supply a fictional or de-identified business scenario with its evidence and boundaries; no real employee/customer data.
2. Rehearse three exchanges, responding yourself before the coaching.
3. Distinguish simulated reactions from verified facts and choose one question or explanation to improve.
4. The manager verifies any real-work evidence and owns the next conversation; nothing is sent or recorded by this rehearsal.
activities.whyThisMatters: Rehearsal exposes when a coaching question supplies the answer or takes ownership away from the colleague.

activities.prompt: For the de-identified plan and next action I supply, compare the evidence with the applicable decision criteria or role guidance I identify. activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager verifies the criterion fits the local work and leaves the actual decision and evidence gathering with its owner.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A customer decision stalls when its next action rests on an unsupported assumption. Focus on a coaching question that exposes the evidence gap without taking ownership away from the accountable role.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Coach within your remit: account-plan ownership, technical decision criteria and customer-success responsibilities are not interchangeable.
2. Test the customer hypothesis and compare realistic options without turning the discussion into a performance score.
3. A useful question makes the remaining evidence check and its owner clearer; internal rehearsal is not customer agreement.
discussionQuestions: Which weak assumption blocks the next customer action?
What coaching question tests it without rating an employee?
What evidence should return after the decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft coaching questions from a de-identified business scenario'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test whether plan evidence supports the proposed next action', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coaching improves decisions through evidence and questions, not seller scores. People and performance decisions stay with the manager and outside AI evaluation. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
facilitatorQuestions: Which observable business decision needs better reasoning rather than a seller score? What question lets the owner explain their judgment? How would another manager test the reasoning without asking AI to evaluate an employee?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Never rank, score, or evaluate individual employees; keep people and performance decisions with the manager.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one de-identified business-decision coaching card: observed evidence, reasoning question, owner-led action and follow-up test. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Rehearse with a peer; if alone, write both sides and mark the exchange untested, not a validated customer or coaching response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which question helped the team member examine a decision criterion without inferring performance or intent?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could rehearse or use a coaching question from a de-identified business scenario and agree a team-member-owned next check; do not rate people. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a de-identified question or criterion refined and whether it improved the decision discussion; exclude employee and performance details. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified decision depends on a weak assumption. Try a question that reveals the missing evidence without rating the employee or prescribing an unsupported answer.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Judgment-focused coaching tests the evidence behind a decision while leaving ownership with the accountable role. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the de-identified decision and unresolved assumption in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Coaching a decision must not become scoring an employee. Look for an evidence-testing question that leaves ownership with the accountable role.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: coaching a decision must not become scoring an employee. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-MGR-W04.keyTakeaway: Coach the reasoning and next behavior; do not take over the decision or specialist ownership.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when coaching a decision must not become scoring an employee. Manager support can reinforce the useful coaching habit in a 1:1 rather than a performance scorecard.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Agree how peers can compare useful coaching questions without evaluating an employee or presenting simulated reactions as evidence.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that coaching a decision must not become scoring an employee; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to reinforce the useful coaching habit in a 1:1 rather than a performance scorecard? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A transition or committed milestone is ready for another role to review. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: inspect the AE-led integrated account transition. STU: validate customer commitment and send to CSU. CSU: accept or return milestone through its own receiving owner.
Boundary: Each org discusses this in its own huddle; the receiving owner accepts separately. No joint ATU/STU/CSU huddle is assumed.
discussionQuestions: Can the receiving role act from this transfer?
What commitment or evidence is still missing?
Who must accept separately under the applicable organizational process?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the handoff packet against explicit acceptance criteria'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Draft a precise acceptance request or return reason', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Handoff inspection distinguishes sent requests from accepted responsibility. Discuss gaps in your own org huddle and seek receiving-owner acceptance separately. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
facilitatorQuestions: Could the receiver act from the handoff and its explicit criteria? Is acceptance actually recorded or only requested? How does a peer manager resolve a blocker within their own org without claiming the receiving org's decision?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Each org discusses this in its own huddle; the receiving owner accepts separately. No joint ATU/STU/CSU huddle is assumed.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one acceptance checklist: handoff requirement, missing evidence, sender/receiver role, recorded/requested acceptance and bounded blocker. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What showed acceptance rather than assumption, and what remains for the receiver to confirm?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could check a consequential handoff input and request separate receiving-owner confirmation or a precise gap; no joint cross-org huddle is assumed. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized acceptance gap clarified and whether it reduced ambiguity; pending is valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified transition packet is ready to send, but the receiver may not be able to act. Inspect the evidence and keep receiving acceptance a separate decision.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A management handoff review asks whether the receiver can act, with acceptance separate from sending a packet. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the de-identified handoff and known sending and receiving owners.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Sending a packet is not receiving-owner acceptance. Look for a receiving-owner decision with its evidence, conditions and next action.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: sending a packet is not receiving-owner acceptance. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-MGR-W05.keyTakeaway: A handoff is complete when the receiving owner accepts the work and knows the decision, evidence, boundaries, and next step.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when sending a packet is not receiving-owner acceptance. Manager support can help settle acceptance and ownership without reconstructing the entire history.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help distinguish local acceptance criteria from a universal process; do not presume a joint cross-organization huddle or receiving agreement.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that sending a packet is not receiving-owner acceptance; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help settle acceptance and ownership without reconstructing the entire history? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.name: Distinguish source evidence from proposed value claims
activities.description: Challenge a customer-value claim against its baseline, outcome measures and current source evidence.
activities.prompt: Using the proposed value claim, agreed customer outcome and dated evidence I supply, separate measured results, projections, activity completed and unsupported interpretation. Check baseline, measurement period and whether the cited evidence actually supports the claimed outcome or causality. Consult the authoritative measurement guidance I identify only where needed and cite it separately from customer facts. If a material gap is supported, identify the most consequential one, the owner role who can supply proof and the question that would change the claim. Otherwise state that no material gap was found within the inspected scope, or that evidence is insufficient; neither establishes customer-recognized value. Keep this to business evidence, not employee assessment. Draft only. Flag unavailable sources.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-linked value-claim challenge with measured/projected/activity distinctions and, where supported, one material proof gap, owner role and settling question; otherwise explicit no-gap-within-scope or insufficient-evidence findings.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager validates the interpretation with the outcome and measurement owners before requesting an intervention; AI does not confirm customer-recognized value.
activities.requiredContext: Proposed value claim, agreed outcome, baseline/measurement period, actual dated results and any authoritative measurement guidance.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A customer value claim or renewal plan is unsupported by current delivery and usage evidence. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: review renewal/account risk. STU: verify technical commitment and residual obligations. CSU: inspect customer-success, consumption, and delivery signals.
Boundary: CAIP CSU account-health cadence is CAIP-specific; CSAM normally leads customer-facing value reviews, not every M1.
discussionQuestions: Which value claim is supported by actual delivery or usage?
What remains expected rather than realized?
Who owns the customer-facing value or renewal decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Retrieve authorized customer-risk context if accessible'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare a customer-outcome intervention for human approval', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Intervention needs customer value or renewal evidence while CSAM and field owners retain normal customer-facing execution. Do not generalize CAIP-specific cadence. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-outcome or renewal risk warrants intervention, and what source proves it? Who owns the customer-facing review and next action? How does a peer manager avoid treating a CAIP-specific cadence as a universal rule?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. CAIP CSU account-health cadence is CAIP-specific; CSAM normally leads customer-facing value reviews, not every M1.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-outcome intervention card: risk evidence, customer-facing role owner, manager action, authority limit and next signal/date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which value or renewal assumption changed intervention, and what stays with the customer-facing field role?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could check a material value or renewal assumption and agree a manager intervention or evidence request within the existing org rhythm. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized assumption checked and whether it improved field-owner follow-up or manager judgment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified renewal claim relies on expected rather than observed value. Compare approved delivery or usage evidence and identify the accountable customer-facing owner.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A manager's value intervention depends on supported customer outcomes rather than expected benefits or internal activity. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the de-identified value or renewal claim and dated delivery evidence.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Internal progress cannot stand in for customer-recognized value. Look for a supported intervention or explicit unvalidated claim.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: internal progress cannot stand in for customer-recognized value. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.
