facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A coverage, delivery, or approval blocker threatens the next customer outcome. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU/STU: cover transition or specialist vacancies. CAIP CSU: use documented capacity and investment rules. CSAM/CSA: apply only documented delivery-request approval gates.
Boundary: Do not assume universal pricing, discount, delegation, or investment approval authority.
discussionQuestions: Which resource or approval dependency blocks the outcome?
What authority do you actually hold?
What must be recommended or escalated rather than approved here?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Frame a capacity decision with the documented authority boundary'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Design a scoped, human-reviewed exception-monitoring pilot', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Capacity and exceptions need explicit authority and a resolution path. Recommendations cannot authorize staffing, pricing, discounts or investment beyond delegation. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
facilitatorQuestions: What capacity constraint is evidenced rather than assumed? Is the next step within your documented authority or an escalation? How would a peer preserve financial, staffing and investment decision rights while defining a stop condition?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Do not assume universal pricing, discount, delegation, or investment approval authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one capacity/exception decision card: evidenced constraint, options, formal delegation gap, authorized escalation owner and stop condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which capacity trade-off changed your recommendation, and what exception needs another decision owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could frame a material capacity trade-off or exception and decide within delegation or route to the authorized owner. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a de-identified authority or capacity assumption clarified and whether it improved escalation; exclude staffing and personnel details. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified blocker combines a capacity choice with an approval held elsewhere. Separate support within the manager's remit from the decision requiring escalation.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Capacity support within a manager's remit is separate from an exception or approval held elsewhere. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the de-identified capacity question and relevant delegation guidance in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A manager's interest does not extend their formal approval authority. Look for a local resource decision separated from the exception that needs escalation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a manager's interest does not extend their formal approval authority. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Rehearse a manager explanation of what changed and why

activities.prompt: Role-play a skeptical peer using [paste/describe the fictional/de-identified management-workflow experiment]. I will explain what changed and why. Pause for my response for three exchanges, then coach my explanation and draft a short practice note with observed evidence, caveat, owner-role follow-up and review date. Label simulated reactions and do not add results I did not supply. Keep this to business evidence, not employee assessment. Draft only. Flag unavailable sources.
activities.expectedOutput: Three simulated peer exchanges, evidence-focused explanation feedback and a draft practice note with caveat and follow-up.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager verifies every real result separately before sharing a practice note; no simulated response or AI assessment becomes employee evaluation.

4. The manager verifies any real-work evidence and owns the next conversation; nothing is sent or recorded by this rehearsal.
activities.whyThisMatters: Explaining the limits as well as the gain helps peers reuse a management practice without inheriting an unsupported success claim.

2. Confirm your remit and permitted inputs, then run the prompt with the evidence listed here. If the tool/source is unavailable, use a permitted extract or manual review.
3. Check source dates, access gaps and the distinction between evidence, proposal and agreement.
4. Make the stated human decision or confirmation request, with owner-role acceptance and a review point; any real record update or communication follows the separate authorized process.
activities.whyThisMatters: A useful practice earns retention through actual workflow evidence, not fluent explanation or another team's success story.

resources.description: AIT manager-view resource; confirm manager-specific access and current applicability before using it to inform a workflow experiment. Program context and related resources: https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/MCAPSAcademy/SitePages/MCAPS-Manager-Empowerment.aspx

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A team has tried an AI-supported manager workflow and has mixed evidence about its usefulness. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the manager's own ATU, STU, or CSU evidence and team rhythm; do not impose one Enterprise-wide cadence.
Boundary: Never use AI output to rate individual sellers or imply a tool can approve actions or update systems.
discussionQuestions: What changed in the workflow after the experiment?
Which result is evidenced and which is anecdotal?
What will you retain, revise or stop without judging individual performance?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rehearse a manager explanation of what changed and why'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test whether the evidence supports retaining the practice', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Reinforce a practice because evidence shows better work, not a polished AI note. Keep limitations visible and never turn workflow learning into seller ratings. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
facilitatorQuestions: What changed in the work, and what evidence supports keeping the practice? What failure or constraint would make you revise or stop it? How would another manager design the next experiment without rating individual sellers?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Never use AI output to rate individual sellers or imply a tool can approve actions or update systems.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one learning review: before/after workflow evidence, competing explanation, keep/revise/stop rationale and next bounded experiment. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What improved in the work, what supports that, and when should the team not repeat the practice?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: A suitable Featured practice or manual discussion could support your exploration. If relevant, you could review a permission-safe improvement example and identify a recurring habit and caveat; seek permission before broader reuse. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open; do not infer status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized habit lesson and whether it reduced rework, improved clarity or showed no benefit; do not rate individuals. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A de-identified manager-workflow trial has mixed observations. Decide what to retain, revise or stop without turning anecdotal benefit into a performance assessment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Reviewing a manager-workflow trial means judging what changed in the work, including friction and inconclusive observations. Manager authority depends on the organizational remit and formal delegation; the huddle must not rank, score or evaluate employees.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the de-identified trial, baseline and observed friction in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A busy workflow or tool use is not proven improvement. Look for an honest retain, revise or stop judgment grounded in the observed trial.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a busy workflow or tool use is not proven improvement. Confirm who can explain the management decision quality within organizational remit boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-MGR-W08.keyTakeaway: Reuse is safe only when source, limits, and permission are clear.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a busy workflow or tool use is not proven improvement. Manager support can protect the useful management habit and remove the blocker rather than require a success story.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Encourage a retain, revise or stop discussion about the workflow rather than an adoption score, employee measure or new monitoring requirement.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to protect the useful management habit and remove the blocker rather than require a success story? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

PLC-ENT-MGR-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-ENT-MGR-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-ENT-MGR-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.

managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. roles.name: Commercial Executive

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive

roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist

PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

topicResources.description: Microsoft Customer Zero evidence for outcome-first transformation, end-to-end workflow redesign, employee-centered change, Capability Add measurement, and continuous human-AI learning. Metrics are bounded to the cited samples and periods.

PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Introduce the why, reinforce the weekly rhythm, and welcome questions. Help distinguish the future weekly-experience preview from today's Orientation. Support readiness and access questions without inspecting individual tool usage, survey answers, or performance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
Does the team understand the motion and what to expect in the first role-specific huddle in Week 2?
What readiness question or access blocker needs support through our existing channels?

activities.name: Reconcile one partner growth baseline before using it
activities.description: Comparable measures prevent unsupported growth promises.
activities.prompt: Create a working growth-baseline reconciliation for the partner and period identified in [the approved dated growth evidence pack], using only the supplied approved evidence pack available at the cutoff. Compare at most three supplied measures and retain their units, periods, definitions and source references. Separate observed actuals, partner estimates and planning assumptions. Flag incompatible denominators, stale extracts and duplicate pipeline rather than normalizing them silently. Return a compact table of measure, comparable baseline, discrepancy, source and owner question, followed by the single discrepancy most likely to change our growth choice. Flag missing values and ask what matters. Keep this a PDM review draft, not a partner commitment or a forecast submission.
activities.expectedOutput: At most three measure rows with dates, units, discrepancy and source; one prioritized clarification with owner and review date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks comparability; metric owner confirms disputed values. Stop use of a measure if its definition, source or permission is unknown; record the gap instead of endorsing a target.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. No connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. choose one partner, period and three measures; bind inputs.
2. generate from approved excerpts.
3. verify one baseline against its source.
4. select the first discrepancy to resolve.
5. record owner and review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparable measures prevent unsupported growth promises.

activities.name: Test one growth hypothesis against two cited market signals
activities.description: A bounded external check separates partner ambition from actionable demand.
activities.prompt: Test [growth hypothesis] for the partner and market identified in [approved public partner profile or reference] as of today. Start with the approved source URLs and use at most two authoritative, dated sources; prefer official statistics or first-party published evidence. Produce a two-row evidence table with claim, supporting passage summary, publisher, date, URL and relevance limit. Distinguish a market signal from proof that the named partner can capture it. Give one disconfirming interpretation and one question for the partner. If a source is inaccessible, stale or absent, state the limitation and do not invent a citation or conclusion. End with a provisional supported, uncertain or contradicted rating; do not recommend a revenue commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Two cited signal rows, one counterinterpretation and a provisional rating with one partner question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM verifies the citation and rejects leaps from market size to attainable revenue. Stop reliance on the rating if provenance or applicability is unresolved; retain a research question.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. bound one hypothesis and two references.
2. run the bounded cited check.
3. open and verify one citation.
4. decide whether a capacity check is warranted.
5. record question, owner and review date.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: A bounded external check separates partner ambition from actionable demand.

activities.name: Choose a growth bet using evidence and capacity constraints
activities.description: PDM makes trade-offs explicit rather than letting unsupported initiatives consume the partner plan.
activities.prompt: Compare up to three growth bets using only [partner options, evidence and confirmed constraints]. Weigh evidence strength, execution capacity, time to test and the cost of being wrong—without invented scores or financial projections. Draft a growth-choice card with the tradeoffs, one reversible test, what would overturn it, an unresolved dependency and owner question. Leave unsupported options unassessed; this isn’t an approved partner plan.
activities.expectedOutput: One three-option comparison and a reversible test with overturning evidence, dependency, owner and review date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM owns prioritization; the partner must accept plan changes. Stop recommendations exceeding confirmed capacity or implying investment commitment; replace unknown assumptions with an evidence request.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps. Other practices are not prerequisites.
activitySteps: 1. choose one partner and up to three options.
2. generate the constrained comparison.
3. challenge the preferred option's evidence.
4. choose one reversible test or defer.
5. record owner, evidence need and review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: PDM makes trade-offs explicit rather than letting unsupported initiatives consume the partner plan.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Name one partner and planning period. Frame this as partner strategy, not a customer opportunity stage. Outputs are working hypotheses, not approved plans.
keyTalkingPoints: Compare periods, currencies and definitions before discussing growth. Separate observed demand, partner ambition and capacity. Keep partner-reported pipeline distinct from customer-opportunity evidence. Prefer one falsifiable priority over a broad wish list.
discussionQuestions: Which number changes the growth choice if wrong? What proves this partner can execute? Whose capacity confirmation or acceptance is still missing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile one partner growth baseline before using it'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose only one Featured practice. Move from the artifact to a human choice: pursue one evidence check or defer. Other practices are independent alternatives. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: contrast SI and ISV growth paths before selecting one', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the growth question, strongest evidence and largest uncertainty. Confirm that the partner has not accepted a plan or target. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring approved dated actuals, ambition, capacity constraints and source references for one partner. Use sanitized samples if permission is unclear. Timebox: 1 minute scope, 2 generate, 2 verify, 2 decide, 1 commit.
facilitatorQuestions: Can another PDM reproduce the baseline? Which assertion is inferred? What evidence would overturn the preferred priority?
listenFor: A dated baseline; incompatible measures flagged rather than summed; an executable capacity test; a named evidence owner.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If an agent is unavailable or exceeds two minutes, use approved supplied excerpts to fill the same output columns manually. Mark unverified claims and decide what evidence to obtain. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector or source-system update is assumed. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which growth fact became an assumption after checking its denominator and source?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could examine a growth assumption against its source and consider what its evidence owner would need to verify; no dated request or planning-discussion evidence is required for the huddle. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized growth assumption corrected after source or denominator checking and whether it changed the priority; partner acceptance may remain pending. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Expose one PBP target-definition conflict
activities.description: Visible conflicting definitions allow a real negotiated choice rather than artificial agreement.
activities.prompt: Create a target-alignment issue card for the partner/objective identified in [Microsoft and partner target views and dated baseline]. Preserve each party's original target, period and metric definition. Identify the single conflict that prevents meaningful comparison, then propose two clearly labeled resolution choices without changing either party's position. Explain the consequence of each choice and the evidence needed for the reviewers to decide. Return the conflict table, one proposed wording for discussion and an acceptance field set to DRAFT - NOT ACCEPTED. If a baseline or definition is missing, do not infer agreement or calculate growth; mark NOT PROVIDED and ask a precise clarification. Do not commit partner resources or approve the integrated PBP.
activities.expectedOutput: One conflict table, two resolution choices and discussion wording with draft status and paired review owners.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM confirms the conflict; partner representative must accept negotiated wording. Stop if a definition is missing or wording implies agreement; preserve both positions and request clarification.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners.
activitySteps: 1. select one objective and both target statements.
2. generate the conflict card.
3. verify neither party's position changed.
4. select the resolution question.
5. record both review owners and date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Visible conflicting definitions allow a real negotiated choice rather than artificial agreement.

activities.name: Turn one PBP objective into a dependency-aware milestone
activities.description: One executable milestone connects planning to evidence without inventing cross-role commitments.
activities.prompt: Draft one integrated PBP milestone for the partner identified in [the objective, dated baseline, dependencies and review date if known]. Include a measurable completion condition, evidence to bring, proposed Microsoft and partner owners, one critical dependency and the decision needed if that dependency is not confirmed. Distinguish proposed ownership from accepted ownership and separate activity completion from business outcome. Return one milestone row and a short acceptance checklist for PDM and partner review. Do not invent dates, target values, capacity or commitments; use NOT PROVIDED and identify who must supply them. Keep the integrated plan DRAFT until PDM and partner explicitly accept it. Do not schedule meetings, assign work in systems or submit a plan.
activities.expectedOutput: One milestone row with completion evidence, paired proposed owners, critical dependency, contingency decision and acceptance checklist.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks feasibility; partner confirms its owner and contribution. Stop if the milestone depends on unaccepted capacity or invented targets; record the dependency and do not mark accepted.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. No prior practice is required.
activitySteps: 1. select one objective and baseline.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Name one partner and unresolved objective. No plan becomes accepted through this exercise: PDM and partner must agree.
keyTalkingPoints: Keep baseline, target, horizon and metric owner together. Separate Microsoft asks from partner commitments. Name cross-role dependencies without assigning unconfirmed capacity. Official guidance informs an accountable decision; it does not establish automatic eligibility.
discussionQuestions: Where do parties use different measures while appearing aligned? Which dependency invalidates the milestone? What evidence allows both parties to accept the row?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Expose one PBP target-definition conflict'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Use the chosen artifact to form one acceptance question. Each Featured practice accepts supplied inputs independently; do not run them as a required sequence. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: tailor a PBP milestone for SI or ISV execution', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the proposed objective and unresolved acceptance condition. Confirm both review owners and label the integrated plan draft. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved draft objective, dated baseline, partner feedback and dependency notes. Preserve conflicting statements where permitted. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; preserve time for human review and commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What has the partner actually accepted? Which target is proposed? Does the artifact identify both the decision and someone who can make it?
listenFor: Preserved disagreement; comparable definitions; reciprocal owner responsibilities; unaccepted dependencies and explicit draft status.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Use approved plan excerpts to fill the same conflict, milestone or guidance table manually if agents are unavailable or exceed two minutes. Missing policy evidence becomes an accountable-owner question. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector is assumed; no plan is submitted. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What disagreement became visible when target, baseline and owner occupied the same row?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a draft PBP row and the question for PDM/partner review. Their response and acceptance must not be assumed; no review or response needs to be secured for the huddle. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized baseline, target or ownership disagreement clarified in PBP review and whether it improved the draft; do not imply partner agreement. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask what one decision the executive or POD must make, not what slides they need. PDM recommends; authorized owners commit resources.
keyTalkingPoints: Participation does not confer approval authority. Separate decider, contributors and people to inform. Preserve no-action consequences and escalation triggers. Funding, discounts, eligibility and commitments require the accountable approver's sign-off.
discussionQuestions: What precisely must the executive decide? Who owns the consequence if the dependency fails? Which proposed commitment exceeds the forum's authority?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft a one-question executive decision brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. After the chosen practice, ask a peer to restate the decision without background material. If they cannot, narrow the ask before committing. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: tailor a POD decision for SI transformation or ISV co-innovation', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the decision, decider and unresolved approval. Confirm nothing has been approved, sent or committed by the agent. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted partner issue, decision-rights notes, two feasible options and dated evidence. Remove unnecessary customer/personal detail. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; preserve time for human review and commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Can the decider answer yes, no or defer? What is evidence rather than advocacy? Which request needs a separate approval route?
listenFor: A decision verb, evidenced trade-off, no-action consequence, accepted human ownership and explicit authority limits.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Use approved notes to complete the same decision/accountability card manually if agents are unavailable or exceed two minutes. Unknown authority remains a governance-owner question. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector, outbound message or assignment is required. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed when decision ownership was separated from participation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore a bounded ask and identify its decision owner. Actual requests beyond that person's authority must be routed correctly; no response or review date is required for this exploration. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized decision-owner boundary clarified and whether it made the executive or POD ask actionable; deferral is valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.requiredContext: Dependency: existing Sales Agent access, MSX authorization and visibility to named records; seek no broader permission. Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps. activitySteps: 1. confirm existing authorization and bind exact identifiers.
2. run read-only prompt for at most three records.

4. select one customer decision for owner review.

activities.name: Reconcile customer-opportunity facts with partner assertions
activities.description: Separate lanes prevent partner assertions or referral assumptions becoming customer opportunity truth.
activities.prompt: Reconcile evidence for the opportunity/cutoff identified in [the dated CRM extract and partner notes] to answer [customer decision/question]. Keep three lanes separate: recorded MSX facts, attributed partner statements and unresolved questions. Identify the single discrepancy most likely to block the customer design or execution decision and propose the right account, delivery or partner owner to clarify it. Return a compact discrepancy table with source, date, effect on the customer decision and verification action. Do not merge conflicting values or infer referral status from CRM stage. Missing or unattributed evidence stays NOT PROVIDED. This is a review draft, not source-system truth; do not update records, certify referrals or claim partner or customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: One source-separated discrepancy table and verification action tied to a specific customer design/execution decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM preserves attribution; account/delivery owner validates facts; authorized partner-system owner separately verifies referral questions. Stop if source identity or permission is unclear; never overwrite disagreement with synthesized status.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. No live connector assumed.
activitySteps: 1. choose one identified opportunity and supplied evidence.
2. generate the three-lane table.
3. trace the key disagreement to both sources.
4. select the clarification that unlocks the decision.
5. record responsible reviewer and date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Reconcile one MBR/QBR variance before explaining it
activities.description: PDM avoids corrections based on inconsistent reporting or unsupported causal stories.
activities.prompt: Create a one-metric variance bridge for the partner/period identified in [the approved plan, dated actuals and issue notes]. First compare periods, units and definitions; calculate a difference only when supplied values are genuinely comparable and show the calculation. Separate observed variance, evidenced contributors and untested causal hypotheses. Return one compact table with planned value, actual value, comparable variance, source, confidence limitation and the first owner question. Do not attribute causation from timing alone or fill absent values with zero. If inputs are incompatible or missing, mark NOT PROVIDED or NOT COMPARABLE and identify the smallest reconciliation step. This is an MBR/QBR review draft, not a forecast submission or an accepted plan revision.
activities.expectedOutput: One source-linked variance table with checked calculation or noncomparability, causal-confidence limit and owner question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM/metric owner verify comparison before correction. Stop causal conclusions when definitions conflict, provenance is missing or observations only correlate; carry a reconciliation question instead.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners.
activitySteps: 1. select one metric and its two sources.
2. generate the variance bridge.
3. check units, period and calculation.
4. choose first reconciliation/cause question.
5. record owner and review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: PDM avoids corrections based on inconsistent reporting or unsupported causal stories.

activities.name: Choose one corrective action with a reversal condition
activities.description: A correction becomes accountable when its trade-off, owner and reversing evidence are explicit.
activities.prompt: Draft a corrective-decision card for the partner/variance identified in [cause evidence, options and confirmed constraints]. Compare no more than two corrections and a wait-for-evidence option. For each state the mechanism, expected observable change, principal downside and dependency. Recommend one reversible choice, with proposed owner, next evidence checkpoint and a condition that would trigger revision or stopping. Do not turn suspected causes into facts or invent impact estimates. Missing ownership, baseline or capacity stays NOT PROVIDED and becomes an evidence request. Keep the recommendation separate from approval: any integrated PBP change remains draft until PDM and partner accept it, and funding, commercial or resource commitments require accountable sign-off.
activities.expectedOutput: One correction comparison with decision, downside, owner, checkpoint, reversal condition and acceptance/approval requirements.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM recommends; partner/resource owners accept changes in their scope. Stop execution if cause is unverified, capacity unaccepted or approval absent; retain the proposal.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. No prerequisite practice.
activitySteps: 1. select one variance and up to two corrections.
2. generate choices including wait-for-evidence.
3. challenge causal proof for the preferred choice.
4. choose correction proposal or evidence request.
5. record owner, checkpoint and reversal condition.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A correction becomes accountable when its trade-off, owner and reversing evidence are explicit.

activities.name: Test an external explanation for one partner performance variance
activities.description: PDM avoids accepting external conditions as an untested excuse for execution variance.
activities.prompt: Test [proposed external explanation] as a possible contributor to the variance identified in [approved sanitized variance brief] as of today, starting with the approved source URLs. Use at most two dated authoritative sources and cite title, publisher, URL, date and the relevant finding. Compare the source's geography, period and population with the partner issue. Return evidence that supports or weakens the explanation, one alternative interpretation and the internal evidence needed to establish causation. Do not equate correlation with cause or infer a quantified partner impact from market data. If sources are missing, inaccessible or mismatched, state the limitation and leave the explanation unverified. End with one question for the operating-review owner, not a recommendation to excuse or conceal the variance.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited explanation note with supporting/weakening evidence, applicability limits, alternative interpretation and internal causation question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks source fit; metric owner supplies internal causal evidence. Stop treating the explanation as fact if sources mismatch or causation is untested; keep variance visible.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for missing inputs.
activitySteps: 1. bound one explanation and source references.
2. run the two-source check.
3. verify period/geography/metric fit.
4. decide plausible or unverified status.
5. record internal evidence question and owner.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: PDM avoids accepting external conditions as an untested excuse for execution variance.

activities.name: Monitor one approved MBR or QBR correction
activities.description: Track evidence for an approved operating-review correction and surface only changes for PDM review.
activities.prompt: Draft, but don’t activate, an MBR/QBR correction watch from [snapshots and dated action baseline/prior report]. Include scope, sources, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval gaps. Establish a first baseline; later, report changed evidence/status, missed dates and access gaps. Missing history means comparison unavailable. Don’t infer causes, accept actions, alter partner plans or notify anyone; status and disposition need owner validation.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated baseline-only or change-only supplied-evidence review draft with source/history/access gaps and an unactivated proposal for the named reviewer; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The action owner validates execution; PDM retains correction and closure decisions.
activities.requiredContext: An approved correction, approved cadence, evidence locations, dated baseline, named action owner, and PDM reviewer. Provide authorized dated snapshots and user-maintained baseline/prior report if available. Source permissions, scope, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and automation approval are explicit proposed fields; missing inputs remain gaps and no tool access/state retention is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one bounded dependency/action and supply authorized dated snapshots; clearly labeled synthetic evidence is rehearsal-only.
2. Check the user-maintained baseline/prior report, comparable definitions and named reviewer; leave missing history, permission or criteria explicit.
3. Compare supplied evidence manually or with one already authorized tool; no schedule, live retrieval or persistent agent memory.
4. Produce a dated baseline-only/comparison draft and unactivated proposal with source, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval fields.
5. Apply the unchanged HumanCheckpoint before interpretation/action; future automation, notifications and system changes require separate explicit authorization.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Change-only monitoring keeps the operating decision current without turning unattended checks into acceptance.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Select one partner review and material variance. Ask what decision the review should produce. Generated causes remain hypotheses until checked.
keyTalkingPoints: Reconcile definitions and periods before judging performance. Separate variance from suspected cause. Tie corrections to owner, evidence and review point. PDM/partner accept plan changes; accountable approvers sign funding and commercial changes.
discussionQuestions: Is the variance real or a measurement mismatch? Which cause has direct evidence? What correction is reversible, and what would stop it?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile one MBR/QBR variance before explaining it'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Use the selected artifact to read one continue, correct or defer decision. Other Featured practices are alternative routes, not required follow-on work. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test an external explanation for one partner performance variance', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm one human correction decision, owner and evidence checkpoint. The integrated plan stays unchanged until required PDM/partner acceptance and separate approvals. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted prior commitment, actual and baseline with dates/definitions/references, plus issue notes and owners. No deck required.
facilitatorQuestions: Is the cause distinguishable from a convenient explanation? What changes for the owner? What evidence belongs in the next review?
listenFor: Comparable planned/actual measures, causal uncertainty, one corrective choice, clear owner and proof, unchanged approval boundaries.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If agents are unavailable or exceed two minutes, fill the same table manually from approved review extracts. Label unsupported causes hypotheses and choose an evidence request. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector or automatic review update is assumed. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: How would your correction change if the suspected cause proved wrong?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a correction or evidence question for MBR/QBR, considering what would make the measure comparable. Obtaining an owner response or bringing a later measure is not required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized variance or cause checked and whether it changed the MBR/QBR correction or evidence request. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Separate a transformation claim from its actual evidence
activities.description: Traceable baselines and visible limits let PDM reuse learning responsibly.
activities.prompt: Build a claim-evidence matrix for the partner/claim identified in [the approved outcome evidence and audience/permission notes]. Compare the baseline and result for period, units, population and measurement method. Separate measured change, plausible contribution and unsupported causal attribution. Return one claim row with source references, substantiation status, limitations, required redactions and the next evidence or permission question. If the baseline or result is absent or incomparable, mark the outcome unsubstantiated rather than manufacturing a benefit. Missing permission is NOT PROVIDED, not implied consent. Suggest cautious internal-review wording only for supported facts. Do not publish, upload, contact anyone or claim that the customer or partner has approved reuse.
activities.expectedOutput: One claim row with baseline/result sources, substantiation status, attribution limits, redactions and next evidence/permission question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM reviews claim; measurement owner validates proof and permission owner validates audience. Stop outcome wording if baseline, attribution or permission is unsupported; retain only a redacted review request. No publication.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. No unapproved sensitive detail.
activitySteps: 1. select one claim and permitted source pack.
2. generate the claim-evidence row.
3. verify comparability and references.
4. choose supported wording or evidence/permission hold.
5. record measurement reviewer and permission owner.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Traceable baselines and visible limits let PDM reuse learning responsibly.

activities.name: Draft one internal transformation case with permission boundaries
activities.description: A bounded case carries verified learning forward without an unauthorized customer success claim.
activities.prompt: Draft a concise internal learning case for the partner alias/outcome identified in [approved sources, limitations and permission status]. Structure it as starting condition, partner action, measured result, contribution limits and one reusable lesson. Preserve the baseline, result, period and evidence reference, and distinguish observed improvement from proof of causation. Remove names, quotations or metrics not permitted for the intended internal audience. If evidence is absent, provide an evidence-request outline instead of a success narrative; mark missing permission NOT PROVIDED and hold that detail. End with evidence-owner and permission-owner review fields and a NOT APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION banner. Do not publish, upload, send or imply customer or partner endorsement.
activities.expectedOutput: One five-section internal case or evidence-request outline with sources, reviewer fields and not-approved-for-publication banner.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM verifies learning; evidence/permission owners validate claims and audience. Stop narrative reuse if baseline proof or permission is missing. Do not publish or send the draft.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. No prerequisite practice.
activitySteps: 1. choose one permitted outcome and internal audience.
2. generate the structured case.
3. verify numeric claims and remove unsupported causation.
4. check redactions; choose draft or evidence outline.
5. record evidence/permission reviewers without sharing.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A bounded case carries verified learning forward without an unauthorized customer success claim.

activities.name: Test where one outcome pattern can and cannot transfer
activities.description: Distinguish reusable lessons from assumptions that another partner will repeat the same result.
activities.prompt: Test the transferability of [outcome pattern and original conditions] to [target context] as of today, starting with the official sources. Use at most two authoritative sources and cite title, publisher, URL and date for relevant guidance or market facts. Identify two enabling conditions, one material mismatch and one boundary where the pattern should not be generalized. Distinguish external evidence about context from the private outcome's substantiation; do not imply that published guidance validates that outcome or guarantees similar results. If sources or context are missing, mark the conclusion uncertain and ask for the minimum evidence. Return an internal research note only, with no customer identifiers, publication, performance promise or inferred permission to reuse the original case.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited internal note with two enablers, one mismatch, one non-generalization boundary and validation question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM tests contextual fit and keeps original proof/permission reviews separate. Stop extrapolated promises or confidential identifiers in external research; no source substitutes for permission.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. sanitize one pattern and select one target context.
2. run the two-source check.
3. verify one cited condition and applicability.
4. choose further investigation or retain the boundary.
5. record validation question and owner.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Distinguish reusable lessons from assumptions that another partner will repeat the same result.

activities.name: Extended: preserve SI and ISV outcome evidence in a reusable pattern
activities.description: Distinct transformation/product proof and reuse limits make future partner planning credible.
activities.prompt: Create contrasting internal reuse cards for the partner alias identified in [the operating-model notes, outcome pack, permission notes and official references]. The SI card must separate CustomerZero proof from broader transformation claims and state delivery-capacity and Majors/ATU conditions needed for reuse. The ISV card must separate product adoption or value evidence from Marketplace motion, co-innovation contribution and unverified MBS or MACC implications. For each include baseline, result, source, attribution limit, reusable mechanism and permission hold; mark the applicable card and the other comparison only. Missing evidence prevents an outcome claim, and missing permission prevents reuse of the detail. Invent no eligibility, program benefits or repeatable results. Produce review drafts only; publish or send nothing.
activities.expectedOutput: One applicable internal reuse card and comparison-only card with baseline/result proof, attribution limits, mechanism, reviewers and permission holds.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM, measurement owner and permission owner review. Stop unsupported CustomerZero scaling, implied Marketplace/MBS/MACC benefits or unauthorized detail. Neither draft is published or treated as approved for reuse.
activities.requiredContext: Available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners.
activitySteps: 1. Select one model and permitted outcome pack.
2. Identify baseline, result and intended audience.
3. Generate cards and mark the applicable one.
4. Check attribution/permission limits with proposed reviewers.
5. Record one learning and one evidence/permission hold.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
