facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask for one outcome rather than a collection of success stories. Distinguish measured change from causal attribution and internal learning from publication.
keyTalkingPoints: Match periods, units and populations. Separate partner/customer contribution and avoid unsupported causation. Review permission for names, quotes, metrics and audience independently. Reusable patterns need boundaries where they do not apply.
discussionQuestions: What changed relative to which baseline? What does evidence not prove? Who can permit the metric or story for this audience?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate a transformation claim from its actual evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Decide whether the selected artifact is ready for internal human review, needs evidence or is held for permission. A draft is not publication approval. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: preserve SI and ISV outcome evidence in a reusable pattern', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read one supported claim, limitation and permission decision. Confirm internal-review draft status and no publication performed. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted source pack with baseline, result, dates, method and limitations. Supply audience and documented permissions; redact where necessary. No publication, upload, email or external sharing.
facilitatorQuestions: Can a reviewer reconstruct the claim? Is causation overstated? Which detail requires permission before reuse?
listenFor: Comparable measures, traceable sources, bounded attribution, redaction, named permission owner and unsupported claims removed or held.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If agents are unavailable or exceed two minutes, fill the same claim/case/transferability template manually from approved excerpts. Missing evidence or permission allows only a redacted evidence-request outline. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector is assumed; nothing is published or sent. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which evidence made the outcome credible, and which detail must remain excluded until permission is established?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an internal reuse candidate and the evidence-owner and permission-owner questions that must be resolved before broader use; no review deadline is created. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized transformation claim qualified or permission condition identified and whether it made reuse defensible; do not publish or bring the case. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.

What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

Where can we find the shared resources and access help?

activities.name: Find corroborated potential signals for up to three recruits
activities.description: Concentrates recruitment attention on traceable potential rather than confident but uncorroborated market claims.
activities.prompt: For up to three candidates identified in [approved non-MPL SDC profiles and criteria/version], use the approved profile excerpts, the supplied qualification criteria/version, and the supplied credible source URLs. Confirm the candidate scope and criteria; mark absent inputs unavailable. Check only decision-relevant market, product, and adoption signals, citing links, dates, and whether each source is independent or recruit-authored. Return a maximum three-row shortlist table with criterion, supporting evidence, contrary evidence, unknowns, and a provisional next question; do not invent weights. Ask the PDM-R owner to verify the decisive source and accept, reject, or investigate each candidate. Stop at the evidence table or earlier if access or criteria are missing. Do not declare program qualification, contact candidates, or share externally.
activities.expectedOutput: Maximum three-candidate evidence shortlist with dated citations, source independence, unknowns, and a next question for each candidate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R checks the decisive citation and owns the shortlist decision. Missing criteria or inaccessible evidence stops ranking; no automated qualification or outreach.
activities.requiredContext: Up to three candidate names; approved profiles; criteria owner/version; two or three credible links; PDM-R decision owner. Authorized research only; protect recruit-specific data from public queries or sharing.
activitySteps: 1. Scope candidates and confirm criteria (1 min).
2. Run bounded cited research (3 min).
3. Inspect decisive and contrary evidence (2 min).
4. PDM-R records disposition or evidence request (2 min); stop before outreach.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concentrates recruitment attention on traceable potential rather than confident but uncorroborated market claims.

activities.name: Apply supplied qualification criteria without inventing scores
activities.description: Makes recruitment prioritization reproducible and exposes where incomplete evidence would otherwise masquerade as low potential.
activities.prompt: Build a recruit decision matrix for the maximum three candidates identified in [the approved recruit evidence packet] and the current qualification criteria with owner/version. Use supplied material only and finish. List the criteria and preserve any supplied scoring rules exactly; otherwise use Supported, Contradicted, or Unknown. Match evidence to each criterion with document/page/date references, distinguishing recruit claims from verified facts. Produce a compact matrix plus a provisional shortlist rationale and one decision-changing gap per candidate; label missing inputs separately from observed lack of progress. Pause for the PDM-R owner to validate evidence and record accept, reject, or investigate. Stop if the criteria are absent or inconsistent. Do not manufacture scores, certify eligibility, update systems, or send the shortlist.
activities.expectedOutput: Criteria-by-candidate matrix with references, separate evidence states, provisional shortlist rationale, and one priority gap per candidate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies the supplied rules and decisive evidence before deciding. Absent or conflicting criteria require clarification, not synthetic scoring or qualification.
activities.requiredContext: One approved evidence packet for up to three candidates; qualification rules with owner/version; any authorized weights; PDM-R reviewer. Cowork access and spending policy confirmed; no assumed PMX connection.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm criteria and packet scope (1 min).
2. Generate the evidence matrix (3 min).
3. Review unknowns and shortlist rationale (2 min).
4. PDM-R records a bounded decision (2 min); stop without system writes.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes recruitment prioritization reproducible and exposes where incomplete evidence would otherwise masquerade as low potential.

activities.name: Resolve one shortlist-changing contradiction
activities.description: Turns a disputed signal into a small, accountable validation task rather than a misleading shortlist decision.
activities.prompt: For the recruit identified in [the two conflicting approved excerpts and qualification criterion], compare the two conflicting approved evidence excerpts against the supplied qualification criterion to prepare one clarification decision. Identify the exact conflicting claim, source owners, dates, and scope; do not assume the newer source is correct. Separate differences in definitions or reporting periods from genuine contradictions, and mark absent evidence as unavailable. Return a one-page contradiction note containing what is known, what cannot be concluded, the shortlist consequence if each account is true, and one precise evidence request to the source owner. Ask the PDM-R owner to choose hold, investigate, or proceed with a documented caveat. Stop before resolving an unsupported fact, changing qualification status, or sending the request; keep all material internal.
activities.expectedOutput: One contradiction note with known/unknown facts, conditional shortlist consequences, and a precise draft evidence request.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R decides whether the contradiction blocks recruitment attention. The source owner must validate disputed facts; AI cannot silently select a winning account.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit; two conflicting approved excerpts with references/dates; the relevant supplied criterion; source owner and PDM-R reviewer. No external discovery or source-system writes.
activitySteps: 1. Select one contradiction and criterion (1 min).
2. Compare definitions, periods, and evidence (3 min).
3. Inspect the conditional shortlist consequence (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects disposition and request owner (2 min); stop before sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.prompt: Assess the adjacent-segment recruit identified in [approved profile and applicable criteria/version], using the approved profile, the supplied criteria/version, and up to three supplied authorized credible sources. Research the recruit's actual buyer and adoption context with dated citations, separating its claims from corroboration. Return a five-row transferability note with evidence, comparator limitations, unknowns, and one next-validation question; absent segment data does not prove weak traction. Ask the PDM-R owner to decide whether to investigate the adjacent segment or retain the existing scope. Stop if relevant evidence or applicable criteria are unavailable. Do not declare qualification or promise recruitment support.
activities.expectedOutput: Five-row transferability note identifying valid comparisons, unsupported assumptions, and one evidence-backed next question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R validates criteria applicability and decides whether to explore. Missing comparable data cannot be converted into a rejection or a new qualification rule.
activities.requiredContext: One adjacent-segment candidate; existing shortlist segment; approved profile and criteria; up to three credible sources; PDM-R owner. Research only within authorized sources and sharing boundaries.
activitySteps: 1. Define one adjacent-segment comparison (1 min).
2. Check relevant cited evidence (3 min).
3. Review comparator limitations (2 min).
4. PDM-R chooses investigate or retain scope (2 min); stop before commitments.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: Which signal would make us invest another recruitment conversation, and can we verify it? Contrast a sourced market signal with an untested recruit claim. Keep this non-MPL recruitment work distinct from managed-partner performance reviews.
keyTalkingPoints: Qualification uses the supplied current criteria and scope; AI does not invent weights or certify eligibility. Cite source dates and separate independent corroboration from the recruit's own statements. A missing export or inaccessible source means input unavailable, not no progress. PDM-R makes the accept, reject, or investigate decision.
discussionQuestions: Which criterion changes our next decision? Where are apparent market traction and actual product evidence being conflated? What is the smallest missing fact that could reverse the shortlist?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Find corroborated potential signals for up to three recruits'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the most decision-relevant uncertainty to one Featured practice. before moving on, compare the proposed disposition with its strongest evidence and weakest assumption. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test an adjacent-segment recruit without borrowing comparators', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Have PDM-R name the candidate decision and cite one fact that supports it. Keep unsupported candidates in an investigation state rather than treating the AI scorecard as qualification. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring up to three candidate names, approved profile excerpts, qualification criteria with owner/version, and two or three credible source links. Confirm research access and sensitivity boundaries; Cowork needs approved access and an applicable spending policy. Redact unnecessary personal/customer data. Choose a single question and keep the exercise ; do not contact recruits or submit program applications.
facilitatorQuestions: What supports each candidate beyond its own marketing? Which criteria are unknown rather than unmet? Can a reviewer trace the decisive claim to a dated source? Who is authorized to decide the shortlist?
listenFor: A small candidate set, explicit criteria, dated citations, distinct claims and evidence, and a reversible human disposition. Challenge numerical scores without supplied weights and any statement that unavailable records prove inactivity.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If tools or evidence are unavailable, annotate the supplied criteria manually for one candidate with Unknown/Input unavailable labels. Produce an evidence request rather than a fabricated ranking; a clearly marked synthetic example may demonstrate format but cannot support a real decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption did we retire, and which could still change the shortlist?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could examine a recruit criterion and candidate evidence, then consider a shortlist disposition. Missing data must not be treated as qualification; no dated validation request is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized recruit criterion checked or unavailable and whether it changed shortlist judgment; no candidate scorecard is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Choose between two evidence-backed value angles
activities.description: Connects recruitment messaging to a real business priority while preserving the boundary between capability evidence and desired outcomes.
activities.prompt: For the recruit/priority identified in [approved recruit notes], compare two Microsoft platform or AI positioning angles using the approved recruit notes and up to three supplied current credible capability sources. Extract the verified priority and list assumptions separately. Check the capability claims with dated citations and applicability limits; do not infer technical readiness or guaranteed ROI. Return a two-row positioning table containing recruit relevance, cited capability, uncertainty, and one discovery question per angle, followed by a provisional recommendation. Ask the PDM-R owner to select the conversation angle and the technical owner to validate any fit-dependent claim. Stop when evidence is insufficient or review is required. Do not contact the recruit, promise funding, or publish the brief.
activities.expectedOutput: Two-row positioning comparison with citations, limits, uncertainty, discovery questions, and a provisional preferred angle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R approves positioning and the technical owner verifies fit-dependent claims. Unavailable evidence remains an open question, not a capability or outcome promise.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit and verified priority; approved notes; up to three current Microsoft capability sources; PDM-R and technical reviewer. No sensitive recruit details in public search queries.
activitySteps: 1. Select one documented recruit priority (1 min).
2. Check cited capability evidence (3 min).
3. Compare two positioning angles (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects an angle and assigns validation (2 min); stop before outreach.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Connects recruitment messaging to a real business priority while preserving the boundary between capability evidence and desired outcomes.

activities.name: Turn a supplied value brief into a recruit agenda
activities.description: Turns verified positioning into a useful recruitment conversation without disguising assumptions as stakeholder knowledge.
activities.prompt: Prepare one internal engagement agenda for the stakeholder/role identified in [the approved recruit profile, cited value brief and meeting objective]. Complete the draft. Identify verified stakeholder priorities and mark unconfirmed interests as hypotheses. Select no more than three relevant points from the supplied brief, preserving evidence references and qualifying technical or commercial assumptions. Return a fifteen-minute meeting agenda with opening question, two discussion blocks, proof points, and one proposed next decision; include a short do-not-claim list for unsupported benefits. Pause for the PDM-R owner to approve personalization and assign validation of any sensitive or fit-dependent statement. Stop before inviting attendees, sending material, or promising commitments. If priority evidence is missing, draft discovery questions instead of invented personalization.
activities.expectedOutput: One fifteen-minute internal agenda, referenced proof points, a do-not-claim list, and one proposed next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R reviews relevance, sensitivity, and personalization; technical/commercial claims need their accountable owners. No invitation, sharing, or commitment is made by the practice.
activities.requiredContext: Approved profile, cited value brief, stakeholder context, meeting objective, and PDM-R reviewer. Cowork access/spending policy confirmed; supplied inputs only; no outreach permission implied.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one stakeholder and objective (1 min).
2. Draft an agenda from supplied evidence (3 min).
3. Inspect personalization and do-not-claim list (2 min).
4. PDM-R approves or requests corrections (2 min); stop before sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Turns verified positioning into a useful recruitment conversation without disguising assumptions as stakeholder knowledge.

activities.name: Pressure-test one competitive or AI objection
activities.description: Builds trust by answering the real objection with evidence rather than unsupported competitive or AI claims.
activities.prompt: Examine the objection identified in [approved recruit objection notes and proposed Microsoft response], and up to three supplied credible Microsoft and competitor sources. Limit the work to one evidence check. Restate the objection neutrally and distinguish the recruit's reported concern from verified facts. Verify only the disputed capabilities or constraints with dated citations; record mismatched versions and missing evidence explicitly. Return a three-part response card: what we can substantiate, what needs technical validation, and one discovery question that tests the recruit's actual requirement. Ask the PDM-R owner to approve the response and PTS or PSA reviewer to validate technical applicability. Stop before claiming superiority, guaranteeing results, or contacting the recruit. If sources conflict, preserve the conflict instead of choosing a convenient claim.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited response card with substantiated statements, unresolved technical questions, and a neutral discovery question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R owns the response; PTS/PSA validates technical applicability. Conflicting versions or missing sources block confident comparative claims, not the discovery conversation.
activities.requiredContext: One objection; approved notes and proposed response; up to three current credible sources representing both sides; named PDM-R and technical reviewer. Authorized sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Scope one objection and response (1 min).
2. Verify disputed claims with sources (3 min).
3. Review the three-part response card (2 min).
4. PDM-R approves wording and routes technical checks (2 min); stop before outreach.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.

activities.prompt: For the recruit identified in [the approved architecture and switching-constraint notes], use the approved architecture summary, the documented switching constraints, and the supplied cited Microsoft value brief to outline a limited discovery experiment, not a migration commitment. Stop before scheduling work, allocating resources, or presenting the experiment as technically approved or commercially funded.

activitySteps: 1. Confirm incumbent constraints and one question (1 min).
2. Draft a bounded discovery experiment (3 min).
3. Inspect exclusions and unknown dependencies (2 min).
4. PDM-R and technical owner review the proposal (2 min); stop before mobilization.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What would this recruit gain that it actually values? Start with one supplied recruit priority and compare an evidence-backed capability statement with an unsupported AI promise.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate verified recruit needs, public claims, and our value hypotheses. Cite current Microsoft capability evidence and equally credible competitor sources. PDM-R approves positioning; technical owners validate fit. Internal preparation is not permission to send, promise support, or make commercial commitments.
discussionQuestions: Which recruit priority can we substantiate? What capability or outcome claim would be unsafe to repeat today? Which question would test whether our preferred angle resonates?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Choose between two evidence-backed value angles'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose the single weakest part of the planned conversation: evidence, personalization, or objection handling. Use its Featured practice, then inspect one claim before accepting the brief. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Position a bounded experiment for an incumbent-platform recruit', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Have PDM-R approve one positioning hypothesis and name its evidence and technical-validation owner. Keep unvalidated claims in the question list, not the talking track. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved recruit profile, current priority notes, two or three capability/competitor sources, and the stakeholder context. Confirm authorized Researcher or Cowork access; Cowork also needs an applicable spending policy. Keep sensitive recruit details in approved work sources, not public searches. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; no automated outreach or public reuse.
facilitatorQuestions: Can we distinguish a capability from a promised outcome? Which positioning angle has the strongest recruit-specific evidence? Who will validate technical relevance before reuse?
listenFor: Concrete recruit priorities, cited capabilities with applicability limits, honest unknowns, and a clear discovery question. Challenge invented ROI, competitive disparagement, and assertions that an architecture is already approved.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without live research, use approved source excerpts and mark freshness unverified. Without a documented recruit priority, draft a discovery question rather than a personalized claim; do not fill missing context with a generic success promise. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which statement became more credible when we replaced a promise with a question?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore a recruit priority or capability claim and adapt an internal conversation agenda. Any actual approval stays with its authorized owner; no recruit conversation or dated owner response is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized positioning promise replaced by evidence or a question and whether it improved credibility or the recruit agenda. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Inspect one authorized MSX opportunity for case evidence
activities.description: Anchors the partnership case in the recorded opportunity without inflating CRM observations into partner commitments or eligibility decisions.
activities.prompt: Inspect MSX opportunity [opportunity ID] read-only for the recruit partnership case. Show available stage, value/currency, dates, owner and relevant notes with dated record references; separate facts, stale/conflicting fields and gaps. Give one opportunity-owner question. Stop on unresolved identity; ask for an extract if access is missing. MSX alone doesn’t establish referral status or MACC eligibility. Don’t update records, submit anything or make commercial/funding decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: One read-only evidence strip with record references, recorded values/dates, freshness caveats, missing inputs, and one owner question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies linkage and the opportunity owner validates recorded facts. Unresolved record identity/access stops inspection; MSX cannot certify partner state or commercial applicability.
activities.requiredContext: One exact authorized MSX opportunity ID; recruit/case linkage; evidence questions; existing CRM security role; PDM-R and opportunity owner. No PMX, Partner Center, or partner-referral access assumed. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Verify one record and permitted scope (1 min).
2. Inspect authorized MSX evidence only (3 min).
3. Review freshness and missing fields (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects case evidence and owner question (2 min); stop without writes.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Anchors the partnership case in the recorded opportunity without inflating CRM observations into partner commitments or eligibility decisions.

activities.name: Assemble a one-recruit SPP/MACC evidence case
activities.description: Makes the partnership rationale reviewable without treating forecast opportunity value or recruit intent as an approved commercial outcome.
activities.prompt: Draft one internal SPP/MACC partnership case for the recruit identified in [the SPP structure, approved opportunity evidence, assumptions and current commercial criteria/owner/version]. Identify the decision requested and label absent source inputs unavailable. Separate evidenced opportunity facts, recruit statements, commercial assumptions, and proposed commitments with source/page/date references. Return a one-page case with value hypothesis, evidence table, MACC applicability questions, risks, accountable validators, and one next-decision recommendation; do not invent financial estimates or criteria. Pause for the PDM-R owner to validate the case and authorized commercial/program owner to validate current applicability. Stop before submission or any commitment, eligibility, discount, or funding decision. Missing rules block the affected conclusion, not the recording of known facts.
activities.expectedOutput: One-page draft case with referenced evidence, assumptions, MACC applicability questions, risks, validators, and a bounded next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R owns case quality; authorized commercial/program owners validate rules and any subsequent decisions. Absent criteria remain unresolved; no inferred eligibility, funding, discounts, or commitments.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit; supplied SPP format; approved opportunity excerpts; partner assumptions; current commercial criteria/owner/version; PDM-R and authorized reviewers. Cowork access/spending policy; supplied sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one case decision and inputs (1 min).
2. Assemble facts, assumptions, and case sections (3 min).
3. Inspect commercial applicability questions (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns authorized reviews (2 min); stop at internal draft.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes the partnership rationale reviewable without treating forecast opportunity value or recruit intent as an approved commercial outcome.

activities.name: Separate reciprocal commitments from proposed asks
activities.description: Prevents a promising recruitment conversation from becoming an unsupported promise of resources, money, or partnership obligations.
activities.prompt: For the recruit/decision identified in [the approved meeting notes and draft case], use the approved meeting notes, the draft case excerpt, and the supplied commitment/approval rules to clarify reciprocal expectations. Extract no more than five commitments or asks, preserving each speaker, date, and source reference. Label each as documented agreement, proposed ask, disputed statement, or input unavailable; do not treat silence or a proposed owner as acceptance. Return a compact decision ledger with Microsoft/recruit action, evidence, accountable confirmer, dependency, and the smallest next clarification question. Separate any commercial or technical approval still required. Ask the PDM-R owner to verify the ledger and named authorized owners to validate their commitments. Stop before sending requests, recording new agreements, allocating support, or making eligibility, funding, or discount decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: Maximum five-item reciprocal decision ledger with acceptance evidence, dependencies, accountable confirmers, and one priority clarification question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies evidence; each authorized owner confirms their actual commitment. Proposed ownership, silence, or draft language cannot be represented as acceptance or approval.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit decision; approved meeting notes and draft case; supplied approval rules; named PDM-R and authorized commitment owners. Supplied sources only; preserve internal sensitivity boundaries.
activitySteps: 1. Select one decision and up to five asks (1 min).
2. Classify commitment evidence (3 min).
3. Inspect acceptance and approval gaps (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns clarification owners (2 min); stop before commitments.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: Which part of this partnership case is evidenced today, and which is still a hypothesis? Distinguish recorded MSX opportunity state from the recruit's commitments and applicable commercial rules.
keyTalkingPoints: Sales Agent may inspect authorized MSX records only. Cowork assembles supplied inputs without assuming PMX or Partner Center connectors. MACC applicability, eligibility, discounts, funding, and terms require current evidence and authorized owner validation. PDM-R owns the case, not every commercial approval.
discussionQuestions: Which assumption could change the partnership decision? What must the recruit confirm directly? Which commitment needs a commercial, program, or technical owner's review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect one authorized MSX opportunity for case evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Select the bottleneck: CRM evidence, case structure, or reciprocal commitments. Run one Featured practice and test whether its final recommendation stays inside the available evidence. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare a partnership hypothesis when opportunity evidence is absent', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R names the next case decision, one unresolved assumption, and its validator. Retain an internal draft status until the necessary commercial and partner evidence is actually reviewed. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit, one authorized MSX opportunity ID or an explicitly missing-record note, supplied SPP structure, relevant current MACC/commercial criteria, and owner information. Confirm CRM permissions and Cowork access/spending policy. Keep source dates and labels. Choose one practice ; neither tool may update records, submit applications, or make commitments.
facilitatorQuestions: Can the reviewer trace each commercial statement to an applicable source? Where does recorded pipeline differ from partnership intent? Is the next action evidence collection, case review, or an authorized decision?
listenFor: Facts and assumptions in separate fields, named validators, commercial caveats, and input-unavailable labels. Challenge eligibility inferred from pipeline, unsupported revenue certainty, and partner referral conclusions derived solely from MSX.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If MSX access or an opportunity ID is unavailable, use supplied approved excerpts in Cowork or draft a missing-evidence note manually. Do not infer that a missing record means no opportunity; if commercial criteria are absent, hold that part of the case for the authorized owner. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which statement moved from an implied commitment to an explicit assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a case assumption or commitment and the evidence an authorized owner would need before a partnership decision. No new evidence request or decision is required for the huddle. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized case assumption checked and whether it clarified the partnership decision or governed hold. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What exact technical decision would help this recruit move toward launch? Separate an intake that is complete enough to review from a solution that is technically ready to build.
keyTalkingPoints: Use supplied current intake and prioritization rules; do not invent regional SLAs or resource entitlements. PDM-R owns intake quality, PTS cross-solution direction, and PSA technical design judgment. Official documentation is evidence, not proof of recruit implementation. Proposed reviewers and milestones are not accepted assignments.
discussionQuestions: Which missing requirement would prevent meaningful technical review? Which dependency is cross-solution versus design-specific? What must the technical owner validate before a build plan can be trusted?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft a one-decision technical intake'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose the bottleneck: incomplete intake, uncertain technical evidence, or an unclear dependency. Run one Featured practice and inspect whether the draft asks for a decision rather than presuming approval. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Triage an existing prototype's cross-solution launch gap', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R confirms what is complete enough to ask; PTS/PSA questions remain explicitly pending. Record the smallest next validation step and who must accept ownership before work is planned. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit opportunity/use case, supplied intake rules, approved requirements and architecture excerpts, known gaps, and relevant official technical sources. Confirm tool access and Cowork spending policy. Exclude secrets and unnecessary customer data. Select one practice; no resource booking, technical approval, deployment, or system changes.
facilitatorQuestions: Is the requested decision small enough for an owner to answer? Can requirements be traced to evidence? Are proposed success checks owner-reviewed rather than invented acceptance thresholds? Who confirms capacity and prioritization?
listenFor: Explicit scope and exclusions, cited requirements, unknown inputs, appropriately separated PDM-R/PTS/PSA responsibilities, and unconfirmed resource requests. Challenge assumed access, technical readiness, or acceptance from a completed template.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or current intake rules are missing, prepare a one-question intake clarification with the known requirements and label rules unverified. Use supplied official excerpts for a manual evidence brief; do not fill technical gaps with a plausible architecture or assume resource availability. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did we remove from the request to make the next technical decision clearer?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could examine an intake gap or dependency and adapt a scoped PTS/PSA question. Review must not be treated as resource approval; no request or response is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized intake dependency clarified and whether it sharpened the PTS/PSA decision without resource approval. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

Confirm offer/referral identifiers, timestamps, and what each source actually represents; mark missing source inputs unavailable. Return a one-page discrepancy note with agreed facts, conflicting claims, source authority still requiring validation, and one precise question for the partner-side/source owner. Ask the PDM-R owner to confirm the needed validation route and the authorized source owner to verify the actual status. Stop before choosing an unsupported status, updating records, contacting partners, certifying eligibility, or submitting co-sell actions.
activities.expectedOutput: One discrepancy note with common facts, conflicts, unresolved source authority, and a precise draft source-owner validation request.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R routes verification to the authorized partner-side/source owner. Microsoft-only CRM cannot settle authoritative referral state; unresolved authority or mismatched IDs stop reconciliation.
activities.requiredContext: One offer/referral discrepancy; approved supplied partner-side evidence and CRM excerpt; current source-ownership guidance; PDM-R and actual source owner. No native Partner Center access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one discrepancy and identifiers (1 min).
2. Compare meanings, dates, and supplied evidence (3 min).
3. Inspect source-authority and missing-input caveats (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects the source-owner validation request (2 min); stop before actions.

activities.description: Recognizes a recruit's existing launch assets while preventing old approvals from being stretched across a materially changed offer.
activities.prompt: For the recruit/listing identified in [approved prior listing evidence and proposed offer/version/geography change], compare the approved prior listing evidence with the proposed offer/version/geography change and the supplied current requirements. Run delta review rather than assuming a first-listing checklist or inherited readiness. Confirm what changed and identify the dated prior evidence that remains relevant. Examine only the changed scope across listing, IPCS, incentives, and co-sell; mark absent current proof unavailable, not automatically failed. Return a four-row delta register with reusable evidence, changed requirement, proof requiring refresh, and proposed validator/date; prior approval does not establish current eligibility. Ask the PDM-R owner and the authorized program/technical owners to validate applicability and the evidence refresh plan. Stop before modifying the listing, certifying readiness, submitting requests, or making incentive/funding decisions.

activities.humanCheckpoint: Authorized program/technical owners validate changed applicability; PDM-R verifies offer scope. Previous listing or eligibility evidence cannot be inherited without current validation.
activities.requiredContext: One existing offer; approved dated prior evidence; proposed version/geography/offer change; supplied current requirements; PDM-R and program/technical owners. Supplied sources only, no portal writes.
activitySteps: 1. Scope one existing-offer change (1 min).
2. Compare prior evidence to current changed requirements (3 min).
3. Inspect reusable versus refresh-needed proof (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns authorized delta validation (2 min); stop before listing actions.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What exactly does our evidence prove about this offer today? Contrast a supplied listing screenshot with proof of current IPCS, incentive, and co-sell requirements; avoid collapsing distinct states into a single readiness label.
keyTalkingPoints: Use current official sources and supplied Partner Center evidence with timestamps and offer identity. Do not assume PMX/Partner Center connectors. Microsoft-only CRM is not authoritative partner referral state. Current eligibility and technical readiness require authorized owner validation; AI cannot certify, submit, or make incentive/funding decisions.
discussionQuestions: Which readiness dimension has the weakest evidence? Does the evidence refer to the same offer/version, geography, and time period? Which missing artifact is merely unavailable rather than proof of failure?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check a bounded slice of current launch requirements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Use the Featured practice that best fits whether the gap is the rule, the proof, or a source conflict. Review the most consequential unknown before moving on and assign its validator. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile one partner-side co-sell status discrepancy', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R names one gap, its exact proof requirement, and its authorized validator. Keep readiness and eligibility decisions pending where current criteria or evidence are incomplete. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit/offer ID, relevant official requirements with dates and applicability scope, and approved supplied listing/Partner Center/co-sell evidence. Confirm research access and Cowork access/spending policy; redact customer details. Identify current program and technical validators. Choose one practice ; no portal writes, eligibility decisions, public sharing, or submissions.
facilitatorQuestions: Can every checklist item point to a current applicable rule? Which status requires partner-side confirmation? Are we assuming incentive eligibility from listing existence? Who can validate a technical or program requirement?
listenFor: Separate readiness dimensions, dated offer-specific artifacts, applicability caveats, actual source owners, and precise evidence requests. Challenge blanket ready/not-ready labels, stale screenshots treated as live state, and eligibility inferred from CRM.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without official-source access, use supplied excerpts and mark currency unverified. Without Partner Center evidence, produce an input request rather than a readiness verdict. Keep conflicting records side by side until the authoritative owner validates them; no portal connection is assumed. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which status had we been treating as proof of a different requirement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore an offer-specific artifact or current rule and what its program, technical or source owner would need to confirm. Actual register updates require human review; no update or dated check is assigned. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized listing, IPCS, incentive or co-sell claim separated from its proof requirement and whether it changed validation. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.

Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Reconcile customer decision, partner status, and monetization proof
activities.description: Protects early-win decisions from source mismatches and from confusing a promising deal narrative with verified monetization.
activities.prompt: Reconcile the case identified in [the approved MSX extract, customer-decision evidence, partner-side artifact and dated monetization evidence]. Use the bracketed inputs only and finish. Match opportunity, offer, customer, currency, and reporting periods where relevant; flag unmatchable or absent inputs. Separate recorded deal facts, actual customer decisions, partner-side claims/records, and realized monetization proof, retaining artifact references. Return a four-row evidence note with what each source proves, what it cannot prove, conflicts, and one highest-priority validation question; Microsoft-only CRM cannot establish authoritative partner referral state. Ask the PDM-R owner and the authorized source owners to confirm the facts before deciding the next action. Stop before declaring a win or revenue, updating systems, submitting actions, or sharing any lighthouse story externally.
activities.expectedOutput: Four-row evidence note separating decision, recorded status, partner-side proof, and monetization, plus one priority validation question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies partner-side facts with authorized source owners; monetization and customer decisions require their actual evidence. Missing artifacts cannot imply no progress or a verified win.
activities.requiredContext: One early-win case; approved MSX, customer-decision, partner-side, and monetization artifacts with dates/identifiers; PDM-R and authorized source owners. Cowork access/spending policy; no portal connectors assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one case and matched identifiers (1 min).
2. Reconcile four distinct evidence dimensions (3 min).
3. Inspect conflicts and limits of proof (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns source-owner validation (2 min); stop before outcome claims.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Protects early-win decisions from source mismatches and from confusing a promising deal narrative with verified monetization.

activities.name: Prepare one evidence-backed lighthouse blocker escalation
activities.description: Turns early-win friction into a small accountable decision rather than a broad, unsupported escalation or commercial promise.
activities.prompt: Prepare an internal escalation brief for the blocker identified in [the approved win-evidence note, actual owner responses and escalation/approval guidance]. State the one decision needed and separate an evidenced blocker from an unavailable input or unverified claim. Trace its impact and dependency to source references without inventing revenue loss, customer commitments, or partner-side status. Return a half-page brief with known facts, disputed facts, two bounded response options, accountable decision owner, and proposed evidence/date for the next check. If a customer decision is involved, cite its actual evidence rather than assigning an assumed stage. Ask the PDM-R owner to verify facts and choose whether to escalate. Stop before sending, changing records, promising remedies, or approving commercial terms, discounts, or funding.
activities.expectedOutput: Half-page internal blocker brief with referenced facts, uncertainty, two response options, decision owner, and proposed follow-up proof/date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies the evidence and decides whether/how to escalate. Authorized owners retain all commercial and technical decisions; the practice cannot send or promise a remedy.
activities.requiredContext: One blocker; approved win-evidence note; actual owner responses; current escalation/approval guidance; PDM-R and decision owner. Customer decision evidence only if genuinely relevant; supplied sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Select one evidenced blocker and decision (1 min).
2. Trace impact and owner responses (3 min).
3. Inspect two bounded response options (2 min).
4. PDM-R chooses escalation or evidence collection (2 min); stop before sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Turns early-win friction into a small accountable decision rather than a broad, unsupported escalation or commercial promise.

activities.name: Check whether a repeat win truly advances early monetization
activities.description: Makes the second win a test of repeatable recruitment outcomes rather than a duplicate success story or inflated monetization total.
activities.prompt: Compare [first-win and subsequent opportunity/transaction evidence] using [monetization definitions]. Match customer/offer IDs, periods and currency; flag possible overlap without assuming fraud or failure. Separate new decisions/transactions from reused narrative and booked/forecast value from realized monetization. Draft a five-row repeatability note with lessons, new proof, attribution/duplication gaps and one source-owner question. Missing evidence isn’t no progress; don’t aggregate unsupported revenue, update systems or publish a win.
activities.expectedOutput: Maximum five-row repeatability note distinguishing reused lessons, new evidence, overlap/attribution unknowns, and a source-owner question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R and the source owner validate what is genuinely new and monetized. Reused narratives, missing evidence, or unverified aggregation cannot establish repeatability or realized value.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit; approved first-win baseline; one subsequent case packet; supplied monetization definitions; identifiers/periods/currency; PDM-R and source owner. No invented financial aggregation or system access.
activitySteps: 1. Scope one subsequent case against first-win evidence (1 min).
2. Check new proof and possible overlap (3 min).
3. Review monetization definitions and unknowns (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects one delta-validation action (2 min); stop before claims or publication.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.description: Practice a blocker conversation while preserving PDM-R, seller, and customer decision boundaries.
activities.prompt: Conduct a rehearsal of a lighthouse customer blocker conversation for the lighthouse case identified in [paste/describe a fictional or approved de-identified blocker brief, objective and participant roles]. Test the blocker statement, missing evidence, escalation boundary, and next decision. Return a labeled rehearsal transcript, critique, and meeting questions. Treat every simulated reaction as role-play, not customer evidence, seller confirmation, partner commitment, win proof, or authorization. PDM-R selects the recruitment action, the seller owns opportunity actions, and the customer owns its decision.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript, critique, and blocker-resolution questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R, seller, and customer decisions remain separate and human-owned; only actual responses count as evidence.
activities.requiredContext: One lighthouse case, approved blocker evidence, conversation objective, participant roles, and PDM-R reviewer.
activitySteps: 1. Open Agent J.ai.
2. Supply these inputs before running the prompt: [Lighthouse Case], [Approved Blocker Evidence], [Conversation Objective], [Participant Roles].
3. Run the prompt within the stated scope and access boundaries.
4. Review the result against the approved evidence and flag unsupported claims.
5. Apply the human checkpoint: PDM-R, seller, and customer decisions remain separate and human-owned; only actual responses count as evidence.
Fallback: If Agent J.ai is unavailable, use a peer or written fictional de-identified rehearsal. Simulated reactions are never customer/partner evidence, consent, acceptance or commitment.
