facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What do we mean by win here, and what evidence supports that meaning? Compare a recorded MSX stage, a customer decision note, partner-side transaction status, and monetization proof; none automatically substitutes for another.
keyTalkingPoints: Sales Agent inspects authorized MSX records only and cannot establish authoritative partner referral state. Cowork reconciles supplied evidence, not live portal truth. PDM-R verifies partner-side facts and determines escalation. This recruit lifecycle huddle has no default MCEM mapping; an actual customer decision must be evidenced before applying a customer-stage lens.
discussionQuestions: Which part of the win story has actual proof? Is the next blocker a customer decision, partner-side action, or missing monetization evidence? What would the source owner need to confirm before we call progress?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect the recorded MSX state of one lighthouse opportunity'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose whether the next decision needs CRM facts, cross-source reconciliation, or a blocker brief. After one Featured practice, ask the owner to state exactly what the evidence permits and what it does not. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile customer decision, partner status, and monetization proof', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R identifies one validated fact, one unresolved claim, and the next human decision. Separate internal evidence review from permission to announce a lighthouse win or make a commercial commitment. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one exact authorized MSX opportunity ID or approved excerpts, supplied customer decision notes, partner-side status evidence, and early monetization artifacts with dates and identifiers. Confirm permissions and Cowork spending policy. Redact unnecessary customer details. Choose one practice; no stage writes, submissions, commercial decisions, commitments, or external win sharing.
facilitatorQuestions: Are we comparing the same opportunity, offer, and reporting period? Does the source prove a decision, transaction, or realized value? Which missing field is unavailable input rather than observed lack of progress? Who validates partner-side truth?
listenFor: Precise win definitions, matched identifiers, recorded versus verified status, separate monetization proof, and a named validation owner. Challenge MSX-derived referral conclusions, forecasts described as revenue, and permissionless lighthouse publicity.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If MSX access fails, work from approved supplied excerpts or a manual evidence strip. If customer or partner-side artifacts are absent, label them unavailable and request them; do not declare no win, no progress, or realized revenue. Keep any escalation a draft until PDM-R reviews. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which success claim required a different source than the one we initially used?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could examine a win, partner-side or monetization claim and consider an escalation or next-action question. Do not infer outcomes from missing inputs; no validation deadline or achieved result is expected. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized lighthouse or monetization claim checked and whether it improved the next human decision; no win material or publication is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Review graduation evidence against supplied current criteria
activities.description: Prevents a polished graduation packet from concealing unverified rules or an unaccepted transfer of recruit ownership.
activities.prompt: Review [recruit graduation packet] against [current criteria/owner/version, transfer conditions and receiving-authority/acceptance evidence]. Draft a source-linked matrix of supported criteria, claims, conflicts, gaps and acceptance scope—not a graduation verdict. Don’t invent thresholds, transfer points or receiving owners. Missing mandatory evidence requires a decision hold, not assumed PDM/BPA acceptance. Leave completeness, authority and acceptance for owner validation; don’t submit nominations, graduate or transfer accountability.
activities.expectedOutput: Criteria-to-evidence matrix with dated references, explicit UNVERIFIED governing inputs, acceptance scope, evidence requests, and a provisional decision-readiness/hold note.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R attests completeness; authorized owners validate current criteria, receiving authority, actual acceptance, and transfer conditions. Missing mandatory evidence blocks the decision; AI cannot graduate or transfer accountability.
activities.requiredContext: One approved recruit packet; current criteria owner/version; transfer conditions; receiving-authority evidence; actual acceptance or explicit missing-input note; PDM-R and authorized decision reviewers. Cowork access/spending policy; supplied inputs only.
activitySteps: 1. Check governing criteria and acceptance inputs (1 min).
2. Map one recruit's evidence to supplied criteria (3 min).

activities.name: Draft a continuity package with explicit acceptance boundaries
activities.description: Keeps the recruit's open obligations owned while the actual receiving authority and acceptance conditions are resolved.
activities.prompt: Draft a continuity handoff package for the recruit identified in [approved assets/decision log, current graduation/transfer criteria, authority evidence and actual acceptance or missing-input note]. Summarize no more than five open obligations with source references, artifact location, next action, and proposed versus accepted owner/date. Return a one-page package plus an acceptance ledger showing exact accepted scope, unresolved conditions, and accountability pending a validated transfer; naming a recipient or sending a package is not acceptance. Ask the PDM-R owner and the authorized receiving/decision owners to validate completeness, current criteria, actual acceptance, and transfer conditions. Stop at the internal draft; do not send, graduate, or transfer ownership.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R validates completeness and continuing ownership; authorized receiving/decision owners validate current criteria and actual scoped acceptance. No assumed recipient role, silent acceptance, automatic graduation, or transfer.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit; approved asset/decision log; current graduation and transfer rules; current/receiving authority evidence; actual scoped acceptance or missing note; PDM-R and authorized reviewers. Supplied sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Verify current/proposed owner authority inputs (1 min).
2. Draft up to five continuity obligations (3 min).
3. Inspect actual acceptance and pending accountability (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns authorized acceptance review (2 min); stop before transfer or sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: If we stopped owning this recruit today, what proves another authorized owner has accepted the right responsibilities? State explicitly that graduation thresholds, receiving owner, evidence standard, and transfer point are UNVERIFIED in the source; a receiving PDM/BPA must not be assumed.
keyTalkingPoints: Use supplied current graduation criteria and transfer conditions; invent no thresholds or receiving role. PDM-R attests package completeness but does not infer acceptance from a named recipient, silence, or a sent document. Actual authorized acceptance is mandatory decision evidence. The Extended Scout variant is optional, access-unverified, and read-only preview only; scheduling needs separate approval.
discussionQuestions: Which criteria and transfer conditions have a current authoritative source? What proves the actual receiving owner is authorized and has accepted the defined scope? What remains owned by PDM-R while a decision is pending?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Review graduation evidence against supplied current criteria'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose the decision bottleneck: evidence against supplied criteria, continuity/acceptance, or missing governing inputs. After one Featured practice, require the PDM-R owner to name the remaining decision gate rather than announce graduation. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Preview a bounded missing-artifact monitor for an incomplete handoff', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R states package completeness and the decision's evidence limits. Record graduation/transfer as pending where mandatory evidence is missing, and name the accountable continuity owner until an authorized human decision confirms otherwise. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit's approved assets, decision log, current graduation criteria with owner/version, transfer conditions, receiving-authority evidence, and actual acceptance or an explicit missing-input note. Confirm Cowork access/spending policy. Scout is optional only after access is validated, with an approved bounded source list; no source-system connector assumed. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; preserve internal labels and perform no graduation, transfer, submission, sharing, or scheduling.
facilitatorQuestions: Can we distinguish package completeness from criteria satisfaction and actual acceptance? Which owner/threshold/transfer claim remains UNVERIFIED? Is unavailable acceptance evidence being mislabeled as rejection? Who retains accountability pending an authorized decision?
listenFor: Current criterion references, explicit unresolved thresholds, actual acceptance tied to scope, verified receiving authority, and a continuity owner pending decision. Challenge automatic graduation, assumed receiving PDM/BPA, or an artifact monitor that changes state or schedules itself.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without current criteria, receiving-authority evidence, transfer conditions, or actual acceptance, produce a decision-hold note and targeted request. Do not invent defaults. If Scout access or source approval is unavailable, review the supplied artifact list manually or in Cowork; no automation is required for this active huddle. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption about thresholds, ownership, or acceptance did this review expose?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a current criterion, receiving authority, acceptance or transfer artifact and identify the human decision still needed. Do not automatically graduate or transfer a recruit; no validation request is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized graduation criterion or continuity-owner assumption checked and whether it improved transfer judgment or justified pending status. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.

Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)
roles.description: Advances Enterprise solution-area opportunities through prospecting, discovery, proof, objection handling, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning, coordinating account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances Enterprise solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and customer decisions.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. Leads customer outcome conversations, coordinates partner-led deals and forecasts, routes work to appropriate scale engines, and plans portfolio renewals and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages SME&C territory coverage, customer outcomes, partner-led deals, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Engages early with the opportunity owner to shape executable commercial constructs across Microsoft and partner transaction routes. Navigates negotiation guardrails, coordinates owner-validated policy and licensing questions, routes approvals and exceptions, and hands off approved terms while addressing renewal commercial risk.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes SME&C commercial terms across transaction routes and coordinates approvals and renewals.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Assesses SME&C handoffs against coverage, sold outcomes, technical decisions, and accepted owners. Supports covered consumption portfolios through milestone readiness, partner and scale-engine handoffs, targeted adoption and technical interventions, attributed value evidence, and expansion hypotheses without assuming blanket customer or partner-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports covered SME&C consumption portfolios with readiness, handoffs, and targeted interventions.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: PDM
roles.description: Leads partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executive stakeholders and governance around growth priorities. Coordinates partner growth and co-sell efforts, drives course correction through business reviews, and brings technical, sales, and marketing owners together while reserving investment and commercial commitments for authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads EPS partner strategy and joint business planning, aligning executives and growth efforts.

roles.name: PDM-R
roles.description: Develops a recruitment portfolio from qualification and partnership development through launch, a first transactable listing, and early wins. Mobilizes technical specialists, coordinates validated readiness, and prepares graduation handoffs accepted by accountable owners, with program approvals and graduation criteria retained by authorized owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Recruits EPS partners from qualification to launch, first transactable listings, and early wins.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: PMM
roles.description: Shapes partner marketing plans and campaigns around market needs, partner maturity, and joint business priorities. Recommends investments, coordinates approved claims, localization, activation, and qualified sales handoffs, and optimizes performance with attribution limits and reusable learning in view, leaving funding approvals with program owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS partner marketing plans, campaigns, approved claims, and qualified sales handoffs.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Manages USPSI account priorities, opportunities, forecasts, renewals, and expansion. Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Manages USPSI accounts and pipeline using certified records and approved, human-verified evidence.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Sales Professional
roles.description: Advances USPSI solution-area prospecting, discovery, proof, and customer decisions. Builds value-based selling plans and competitive positioning using approved evidence and handling information according to organizational requirements. Coordinates account owners, technical teams, partners, and investment preparation; funding decisions remain with authorized approvers.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advances USPSI solution-area sales through discovery, proof, and decisions using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads USPSI commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewal planning by assessing commercial risk and structural exposure. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries through authoritative sources and approved handling, coordinating decision narratives, approvals, and execution without assuming policy, exception, legal, or compliance approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads USPSI commercial strategy and negotiation within authoritative policy and approval boundaries.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Provides USPSI technical advice on production architecture, validation, technical health, and cost optimization using approved evidence and organizational handling requirements. Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates USPSI outcome-based success plans, milestones, and accepted owners using approved health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder evidence. Aligns executives and teams, supports adoption and growth planning, and manages delivery risks within organizational requirements while retaining technical architecture approval owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates USPSI success plans, adoption, milestones, and delivery risks using approved evidence.

roles.name: All ATU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for AE, ATS, and CE roles to explore account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution. Compare account, technical, and commercial perspectives on customer decisions and handoffs while keeping each role's responsibilities clear.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared account team workflows for account strategy, customer planning, and coordinated execution across AE, ATS, and CE roles.

roles.name: All STU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for SSP and SE roles to explore discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs. Compare customer outcomes, technical criteria, and evidence for the next decision, including what sending and receiving roles need from one another.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared solution team workflows for discovery, solution development, and coordinated handoffs across SSP and SE roles.

roles.name: All CSU
roles.description: Shared huddle content for CSAM and CSA roles to explore customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution. Connect customer outcomes with delivery, usage, and technical evidence, and clarify decisions and handoffs across the success team.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shared customer success workflows for customer-success planning, adoption, and coordinated execution across CSAM and CSA roles.

roles.name: Services Account Executive (SAE)
roles.description: Co-architect a Services strategy from customer execution and value gaps, with continuity through delivery and value realization. ATU leads account discovery; SAE customer/commercial strategy does not own project delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Execution/value gaps, Services strategy and commercial continuity.

PLC-EPS-PMM-W01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PLC-EPS-PMM-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-EPS-PMM-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

activities.name: Choose a segment using a three-signal market brief
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes for one segment; an approved prior response is the retrieval fallback.
activities.prompt: Using only the supplied approved segment brief, dated maturity excerpt and two or three market sources, create a three-signal market brief for the named partner, segment and geography. For each signal show the claim, citation, publication date, regional applicability and whether it is fact or inference. Separate market attractiveness from evidence of partner marketing capability. Propose one bounded marketing hypothesis, one disconfirming question and one missing maturity input. Do not invent market size, campaign results or readiness scores. Ask the PMM to choose pursue, narrow or defer. Stop with a draft brief and explicit gaps if citations or applicability cannot be verified; do not publish or initiate outreach.
activities.expectedOutput: Three cited signal rows, one hypothesis, one disconfirming question, one maturity gap and dated PMM decision; unsupported rows stay unknown.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM verifies dates and applicability. Stop/defer on missing critical evidence; no outreach or publication.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies exactly one approved partner/segment/geography/decision-date brief, one dated maturity excerpt and two or three approved market URLs/excerpts with dates. Only accessible supplied sources; no native system access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. confirm segment, region and sources.
2. run the prompt or inspect the approved prior response.
3. challenge one inference and maturity gap.
4. PMM records pursue/narrow/defer; stop at the draft.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Separate a marketing hypothesis from readiness or future-sales claims.

activities.name: Expose the evidence gap in a maturity assessment
activities.description: Featured alternative: three supplied maturity dimensions for one segment.
activities.prompt: Review the supplied three-dimension maturity rubric, dated partner assessment excerpt and approved evidence snippets for one segment. Build an evidence coverage matrix with one row per dimension: rubric definition, observed evidence, source date, supported assessment, unknowns and evidence owner. Apply a rubric rating only when its stated criteria are demonstrated; otherwise write not established. Identify the single evidence request most likely to change our marketing plan and explain why. Do not infer missing capability from market interest or create a numerical score not in the rubric. Ask the PMM to confirm or defer the assessment. Stop at the reviewed matrix and draft request; do not send it or update a system record.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-row maturity matrix and one prioritized draft request with owner, due-date placeholder and decision impact.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM accepts only rubric-supported assessments. Stop on missing definitions or unsupported ratings; do not send.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one approved rubric with three dimensions/definitions, one dated segment assessment and up to three approved evidence snippets with owners. No marketing-system query assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm three rubric definitions.
2. Map snippets to dimensions.
3. Replace unsupported ratings with not established.
4. PMM selects one request and owner; stop before sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Unknown capability needs an evidence request, not an invented score.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Name one partner, segment and region. A strong market signal does not prove partner marketing capability. PMM owns the marketing decision, not customer opportunity progression.
keyTalkingPoints: Use dated applicable citations; unknown maturity is not low maturity. Researcher supports cited contextual research; Cowork supports plans and evidence/decision synthesis. Owners supply authorized extracts: no native PMX, Partner Center, Marketplace or dashboard access. Cowork needs applicable access/spending policy. PMC Pro is partner-facing and eligibility-gated, not employee-native. Direct FY27 RAIN exports were unavailable to the research; Asia-specific evidence must not become a global rule. Detailed practices remain synthesis, not SME approval.
discussionQuestions: Which evidence shows market interest versus capability? What would narrow the segment? Which assertion is region-specific?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Choose a segment using a three-signal market brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from market enthusiasm to one bounded hypothesis; carry the gap into PBP planning. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Expose the evidence gap in a maturity assessment', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Market-segment choices need current regional evidence and a realistic view of partner marketing maturity. A polished brief cannot establish readiness; narrow or defer when the deciding signal is unsupported. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Supply one approved segment brief, dated maturity excerpt and two or three approved sources. Have an approved prior Researcher response if retrieval exceeds the timebox. Handle tool/source caveats within the active practice, not as an upfront launch gate.
facilitatorQuestions: Which dated signal supports this segment hypothesis and which only suggests it? What partner capability remains unverified? How would a peer choose pursue, narrow or defer using the supplied maturity rubric?
listenFor: One segment/region; dates; fact/inference/unknown labels; supplied rubric; no invented market size, pipeline or readiness.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, complete three signal rows with source/date or unknown, one testable segment hypothesis, a disconfirming question, maturity gap and provisional pursue/narrow/defer rationale manually from permitted excerpts. If none are available, use a clearly labeled synthetic campaign to practice the method only; it is not evidence of demand, eligibility, approval, customer intent or outcomes. Preserve unknowns and do not substitute historical funding amounts or invented rules. Annotate approved excerpts manually if access is unavailable. Missing evidence produces a request and deferred decision, never invented demo results.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where did AI overstate readiness or regional applicability?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a segment hypothesis and its partner/PDM input gap, considering pursue, narrow or defer. No dated validation request or recorded disposition is assigned. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized segment or marketing-maturity assumption checked and whether it changed pursue, narrow or defer; the full three-signal brief is unnecessary. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Draft a one-campaign PBP alignment canvas
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes for one plan slice.
activities.prompt: Create a one-page draft campaign alignment canvas using only the approved PBP excerpt, audience brief and dated channel/capacity sheet supplied here. Scope it to one campaign and map up to three actual PBP statements to a marketing action, owner and evidence of contribution; leave absent links blank. Add audience, one message hypothesis, channel, timing constraint, required reviewers and one unresolved assumption. Define one response metric with numerator, denominator and observation window; do not forecast incremental revenue or claim ROI. Preserve PDM ownership of the PBP and PSS ownership of sales progression. Ask the PMM to choose revise or seek review. Stop at the draft: no sending, publication or launch until required approvers and the partner agree.
activities.expectedOutput: One-page canvas, up to three PBP links, one defined metric, reviewers and one owned assumption.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM validates alignment/capacity; PBP owner confirms priority. Stop on missing evidence/agreement; no activation.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies approved PBP excerpt with up to three statements, partner-agreed audience brief and dated channel/capacity sheet with reviewers. Missing links stay blank; no system access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. confirm campaign/PBP priority.
2. generate canvas and sourced links.
3. inspect capacity, metric and assumption.
4. PMM revises/seeks-review; stop at draft.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expose unsupported commitments early.

activities.name: Resolve one ownership collision before plan review
activities.description: Featured alternative: four existing deliverables.
activities.prompt: Use the supplied campaign draft, current owner/approver list and existing review convention to create a four-row decision-rights map for this campaign only. For each supplied deliverable identify the producing owner, required input owner, actual approver, partner agreement point and evidence of review. Preserve existing authority: PMM owns marketing planning, the PBP owner confirms alignment, and PSS owns downstream sales progression. Flag one collision or missing decision right and draft a neutral resolution question for the named owner. Do not invent personnel, grant approval rights or interpret silence as agreement. Ask the PMM which issue to resolve first. Stop at the map and unsent question; do not notify participants, change records or activate the campaign.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM verifies existing authority. Stop if unclear; no new approval rights or notifications.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one approved campaign draft, current partner/PDM owner/approver list and existing review convention. Select four deliverables; missing authority stays unknown.
activitySteps: 1. Select four deliverables and supplied owners.
2. Generate map with authority gaps unknown.
3. Inspect one collision and question.
4. PMM prioritizes; stop before communication.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expose existing decision rights without inventing governance.

Add one data-quality check per measure and one unresolved counting decision. Ask the PMM to accept the definitions or request clarification from the named owner. Stop at the draft contract; do not query systems, create reporting jobs or communicate it automatically.

3. Inspect missing fields and attribution wording.
4. PMM accepts/clarifies; retain draft.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Choose one supplied PBP priority. Ask how one campaign supports it and what marketing can measure. A contribution hypothesis does not promise incremental revenue or authorize launch.
keyTalkingPoints: Preserve PBP ownership and partner commitments. PMM owns marketing; PSS owns sales progression. State metric denominators/windows. Cowork uses supplied extracts, not assumed PBP/PMX/dashboard access. No sending, publication or activation before approvers and partner agree.
discussionQuestions: Which PBP statement supports the action? What lacks alignment? Whose agreement is outstanding?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft a one-campaign PBP alignment canvas'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Carry aligned plan constraints into investment governance. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Tune one campaign plan for xPMM L100 or sPMM L200', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Campaign alignment should show a defensible contribution to the partner business plan without turning correlation into a revenue promise. Draft objectives and owner links need PDM and partner review before agreement. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Supply an approved PBP excerpt, partner-agreed audience brief and dated channel/capacity sheet with reviewers.
facilitatorQuestions: Which campaign action traces to the partner business plan? What denominator, window and capacity assumption could change the plan? How does another PMM resolve an ownership conflict before claiming alignment?
listenFor: One campaign; cited priorities; supplied capacity; no revenue attribution; real reviewers and draft status.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, complete one campaign alignment canvas with PBP citation or unknown, action, measurement denominator/window, capacity dependency, proposed owner and acceptance gap manually from permitted excerpts. If none are available, use a clearly labeled synthetic campaign to practice the method only; it is not evidence of demand, eligibility, approval, customer intent or outcomes. Preserve unknowns and do not substitute historical funding amounts or invented rules. Fill canvas manually if unavailable. Without the PBP, record questions and unverified alignment, never invented priorities.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Did the draft clarify contribution or turn correlation into a revenue promise?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could examine a plan assumption and the question for its owner. The plan must remain draft until approvers and partner agree; no owner response is required for the huddle. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized PBP alignment or attribution assumption checked and whether it improved the campaign draft without promising revenue. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Assemble a one-request investment decision packet
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes for one investment line.
activities.prompt: Assemble a draft decision packet for the single supplied campaign investment request using only the authorized cost line, current requirement excerpts and approver list. Use five fields: purpose/PBP link, amount/currency/cost status, applicable cited requirement and effective date, evidence gaps, and authorized decision owner. Distinguish proposed, approved, committed and actual spend exactly as documented. Recommend hold, revise or seek authorized review, explaining the one gap that could change the recommendation. Do not infer eligibility, promise funding or reimbursement, fabricate approvals or claim ROI from campaign response. Ask the PMM to confirm the recommendation and evidence owner. Stop at the draft packet if a rule, amount or authority is unclear; do not submit requests, commit funds or send communications.
activities.expectedOutput: Five-field packet, one prioritized gap and PMM recommendation separate from funding approval.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM validates recommendation; authorized program/finance approvers decide eligibility/funding. Stop on unclear rules, costs or authority; no commitment/submission.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one authorized request, dated cost line with currency/state, current requirement excerpts with effective dates and actual approver list. No funding-system access assumed; undocumented approval/eligibility stays unknown.
activitySteps: 1. identify request, amount and state.
2. assemble five fields with dated references.
3. inspect gap and authority.
4. PMM chooses hold/revise/seek-review; stop before submission.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Separate evidence readiness from funding authority.

activities.name: Check currency of three requirements for one investment

activities.prompt: Research the three supplied requirement questions for the named investment program, geography, activity and planned date using only the supplied official policy URLs or excerpts. 3. Inspect currency/scope/conflicts without inferring status.
4. PMM prioritizes clarification; stop at unsent check.

activities.name: Reconcile one campaign investment variance without ROI claims
activities.description: Featured alternative: one cost line/window.
activities.prompt: Reconcile the supplied single-campaign budget line and authorized ledger extract for the stated reporting window and currency. Produce a three-state bridge for approved budget, committed spend and actual spend, keeping the supplied definitions and noting whether actual is included in committed. Calculate only comparable differences using supplied numbers and show the arithmetic; do not sum overlapping states or convert currencies without an approved rate. Mark missing values unknown, not zero. Identify one discrepancy, its evidence owner and the decision it could affect. Do not infer overspend from incomparable periods or calculate ROI from response or referral counts. Ask the PMM to accept the reconciliation or request finance clarification. Stop on unresolved definitions; do not change the ledger or commit funds.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-state cost bridge with comparable arithmetic, one discrepancy and PMM accept/clarify status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM checks governance impact; finance validates definitions. Stop on unresolved currencies/windows/overlap; no ledger change, funds commitment or ROI claim.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one authorized campaign/window ledger extract, approved budget line, cost-state definitions, currency and reconciliation date. No rate, ledger access or attribution model assumed; missing values stay unknown.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm campaign, window, currency and definitions.
2. Build three-state bridge from supplied amounts.
3. Check arithmetic, overlap and one discrepancy.
4. PMM accepts/clarifies; stop without ledger edits.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparable cost states support governance without false return attribution.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Choose one investment line and trace amount, purpose, requirement and approver. AI assembles evidence but cannot approve funds or establish eligibility.
keyTalkingPoints: Check rule versions/effective dates and proposed/approved/committed/actual costs. Researcher cites current accessible published requirements; program owners resolve ambiguity. Cowork uses authorized extracts, not PMX/Partner Center/Marketplace/dashboard access. No eligibility, funding, approval or reimbursement promises; no response-based ROI or automatic submissions.
discussionQuestions: Which gap changes the recommendation? What cost state is recorded? Who actually has authority?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Assemble a one-request investment decision packet'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Carry only confirmed investment constraints into localization. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Tailor investment evidence to xPMM L100 or sPMM L200', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Marketing-investment judgment separates requirements, cost state and recommendation from approval or reimbursement. Resolve the material discrepancy with the authorized program or finance owner before any commitment. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Supply one authorized request, dated cost line, current requirements and actual approver list.
facilitatorQuestions: Which current rule, effective date and cost state support this request? Who can decide eligibility or funding? How would another PMM distinguish hold, revise and seek-review without importing historical amounts or implying approval?
listenFor: One request; dated rules; explicit cost state; real authority; unresolved evidence; no invented funding or returns.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, use permitted excerpts to complete one investment packet: request purpose, current rule and effective-date evidence or unknown, cost currency/state, authorized approver or unknown, and a hold, revise or seek-review recommendation. If no excerpts are available, use a labeled synthetic campaign for practice only. Preserve unknowns; do not substitute historical amounts or invented rules. Hold the recommendation for the program owner when current criteria are unverified.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where could a recommendation sound like an approval or reimbursement promise?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore an investment evidence gap and the question for its authorized program/finance owner. Do not submit or commit funds through this practice; no resolved gap or deadline is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized marketing-investment requirement or cost-state mismatch clarified and whether it reduced rework; no packet or funding disclosure is needed. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Choose one approved master and locale. Translation can alter availability, conditions, technical scope or outcome claims. A fluent draft is not activation authorization.
keyTalkingPoints: Verify original claims are current and localized claims faithful. Use qualified native-language and technical/brand reviewers. Researcher checks published current context; Cowork synthesizes supplied material. No platform, PMC Pro, PMX, Partner Center, Marketplace or dashboard access assumed. All campaign artifacts remain draft until approvers and partner agree; no sending, publication, launch or submission.
discussionQuestions: Which claim changed scope? Is the original still current locally? What proves partner agreement rather than an internal draft?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check three original-to-local campaign claims'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from fluent wording to evidenced claims and agreement; carry validated context into the PSS handoff. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Review localized claims at xPMM L100 or sPMM L200 depth', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Localization preserves original claim boundaries, qualifiers and actual availability. Language or technical review supports readiness; it does not authorize campaign activation or partner agreement. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Supply one master excerpt with three claims, current approved claims/availability sheet and one locale/brand brief with reviewers.
facilitatorQuestions: Which original claim changes meaning in the localized version? What applicability or language-review gap prevents approval? How would a peer preserve qualifiers and hold the asset until the qualified reviewer confirms it?
listenFor: One asset/locale; both versions checked; qualifiers preserved; verified availability; actual reviewers/partner status; no strengthened outcome claim.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, complete a three-claim original/local comparison: unchanged qualifier, evidence/applicability gap, translation concern, qualified reviewer and hold reason manually from permitted excerpts. If none are available, use a clearly labeled synthetic campaign to practice the method only; it is not evidence of demand, eligibility, approval, customer intent or outcomes. Preserve unknowns and do not substitute historical funding amounts or invented rules. Annotate original claims and validation gaps manually. Missing language review means hold, never assume translation correctness or invent approval.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Did AI remove a qualifier or broaden availability/outcomes?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an original/local claim or agreement gap and identify a useful reviewer question. Keep the campaign draft until approvers and partner agree; no review date or response is assigned. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized localization qualifier corrected and whether it prevented an unsupported activation claim. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

Create a denominator audit showing unique in-window submitted referrals, explicitly accepted referrals by the cut-off, pending or unknown dispositions, exclusions and duplicates. Show accepted divided by eligible submitted only when the denominator is nonzero and the supplied definition permits it; otherwise report not calculable. Keep pending records visible rather than treating silence as acceptance or rejection. Cite the source row keys for counted records and show any deduplication decision.
