facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A partner-sales plan is useful when a named seller can act on a defensible priority. Focus on one execution choice, using current opportunity evidence and the partner strategy as context.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Use three identified opportunities, not the entire territory. Separate PSS execution priorities from PDM strategy changes. Marketing visibility, accepted referral and customer commitment are different evidence categories. In Asia name the country and covered solution areas; validate cross-solution applicability rather than generalizing.
discussionQuestions: Which priority changes when an undated partner claim is removed? Which issue belongs to PDM strategy rather than PSS execution? Which named seller must confirm the next action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile partner plan claims into a three-opportunity execution slice'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in a reviewed three-opportunity execution slice with dated support, priority rationale, proposed owner/action and an explicit unresolved decision. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'ISV variant: test Marketplace assumptions in a territory execution slice', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: A territory priority becomes executable only when record evidence, partner claims, accountable owners and the next review decision are separated. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring an approved three-opportunity territory slice, exact MSX IDs where available, a short partner-strategy excerpt and dated seller notes. If choosing the one-deal discussion, bring its meeting notes and roster. Label each input with ID, scope, source and date; use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Show one priority and its supporting evidence date. Where did a partner aspiration become a supposed record fact? What would make you hold the execution slice? Who must confirm the proposed seller action?
listenFor: A bounded territory slice; explicit source dates; PSS execution rather than PDM strategy substitution; no inferred agreement; missing access not interpreted as an empty territory.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete three opportunity rows with source/date, partner assertion, customer evidence, conflict, proposed owner/action and review date manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed about your territory choice when you separated record facts from partner claims?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore a territory priority or owner assumption and consider an accept/hold rationale. Your validation does not commit another seller; no dated owner request or return evidence is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized territory assumption checked and whether it changed PSS accept/hold judgment or clarified a separately owned action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.
roles.descriptionSummary: Coordinates Enterprise success plans, adoption, milestones, teams, and delivery risk management.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Plans solution-area sales with pinned SME&C partners, qualifying partner-originated demand using Microsoft-verifiable facts. Reconciles partner pipeline and forecasts, coordinates deal clinics, checks readiness before handoff, connects closed deals to delivery, and reviews performance and expansion opportunities.
roles.descriptionSummary: Plans SME&C sales with pinned partners, qualifies demand, and connects deals to delivery and growth.

roles.name: Sales Manager
roles.description: Guides team account coverage and priorities, coaching with evidence appropriate to each role's accountability. Coordinates accepted handoffs, addresses customer value, renewal, and delivery risks, aligns capacity within the manager's remit, and escalates decisions to accountable owners when needed.
roles.descriptionSummary: Guides Enterprise team coverage and priorities, coaches by role, and coordinates accepted handoffs.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: Partner Solution Sales
roles.description: Drives partner territory sales execution through quality referrals, shared pipeline qualification, and coordinated marketplace sell-through. Coaches partner sellers and inspects renewal and consumption-commitment opportunities, avoiding duplicate pipeline attribution while keeping customer decisions with account teams and partner records and economics with partners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Drives EPS partner territory sales through referrals, shared pipeline, and marketplace sell-through.

roles.name: Leader (M2/M3, OU/Division, or Leadership Team)
roles.description: A leadership audience focused on strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies. Brings attention to issues requiring strategic intervention and communicates decisions and direction, with action and escalation shaped by each participant's applicable authority rather than a shared management remit.
roles.descriptionSummary: A leadership audience for strategic priorities, outcome inspection, and cross-team dependencies.

roles.name: Account Executive

Inspects pipeline using only certified records and minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or user-supplied excerpts, with source, scope, as-of/freshness dates, and human verification; coordinates account teams while retaining technical, policy, and approval owners.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist

roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Check the MSX record linked to one referral without inferring referral state
activities.description: Independent choice: only identified authorized MSX records under existing CRM roles; if unavailable use a supplied-evidence Cowork alternative, not a wider query. Uses record grounding without masquerading as complete partner referral evidence.
activities.prompt: Inspect MSX opportunity [opportunity ID] linked to the referral, read-only. Show dated customer need, partner involvement, owner and next step; separate facts, partner claims, contradictions and gaps. Draft a linked-record evidence table and three referral-source questions. Stop on mismatched linkage or uncertain freshness; ask for an extract if access is missing. Don’t infer Partner Center acceptance/full referral status, accept referrals, change records or decide funding.
activities.expectedOutput: Linked-record table with customer need, partner involvement, next step, source/date, gaps and three source-owner questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS decides use/hold for quality review. Stop on linkage mismatch or unresolved freshness; only the accountable source owner verifies partner-side acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: OPP_ID, REFERRAL_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. OPP_ID is an already known linked authorized MSX record, not a request to search partner referrals. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Uses record grounding without masquerading as complete partner referral evidence.

activities.description: Independent supplied-evidence choice: Cowork uses only the approved inputs and applicable permissions/spending policy. Makes quality inspection explainable and returns weak evidence with a concrete correction.

Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A referral is actionable only when its customer need, evidence and next owner are clear. Focus on one quality or acceptance gap without treating a linked CRM record as proof of partner-side acceptance.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Marketed offer, accepted referral and customer agreement require different evidence. A partner-side acceptance claim is not proven by an MSX reference. If no linked MSX ID is known, use supplied evidence rather than asking Sales Agent to discover all referrals.
discussionQuestions: What makes this referral actionable? Which source can verify acceptance? What missing field would change ready to hold?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the MSX record linked to one referral without inferring referral state'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one quality-review packet with identity link, customer need, evidence gaps, verification owner and a PSS ready/return/hold rationale. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'ISV variant: separate offer marketing from referral acceptance', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Referral quality requires identifiable, dated evidence; marketing visibility and an MSX mention do not prove partner-side acceptance or customer commitment. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved referral packet: ID, partner/customer/solution scope, date, source owner, stated need, next step and explicit acceptance evidence if available. For P1 also bring the exact known linked MSX opportunity ID; otherwise choose P2/P3. Use supplied local quality criteria rather than invented gates. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Show the identity link. Which assertion is still partner-supplied? Does the proposed disposition assume acceptance or customer intent? Who can resolve the first exception?
listenFor: Clear ready/return/hold rationale; marketing/referral/customer evidence separated; exact source-owner question; no automatic acceptance or stage approval.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one referral packet with identity link, customer need, source/date, unknown, verification owner and proposed ready/return/hold rationale manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which apparent referral fact became only a claim when you checked source and date?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could examine a referral field or mismatch and consider ready, return or hold. Actual verification belongs with the named source owner; do not accept a referral or promise customer action for someone else. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized referral-field mismatch checked and whether it improved quality judgment; no referral packet or identifying customer data is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Shared pipeline does not become qualified pipeline by appearing in two systems. Focus on one qualification or duplication question and the evidence needed for the next customer action.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Qualification needs customer need, engagement and next-decision evidence. Referral acceptance is not customer commitment. Repeated shared signals may overlap but similar names do not prove duplication. Do not merge records or change stage through the AI draft.
discussionQuestions: What supports progress rather than verification? What proves two signals refer to the same opportunity? Who owns the next qualification conversation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect three identified MSX opportunities for qualification gaps'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in a reviewed qualification or reconciliation artifact with customer evidence, possible overlap, next owner action and progress/hold question. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'SI variant: untangle partner-seller and AE qualification handoffs', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Qualify the customer opportunity and reconcile shared signals before acceleration; access gaps and similar partner claims do not prove absent pipeline or duplicates. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring three exact MSX IDs for P1, one inbound packet for P2, or supplied rows for three identified opportunities for P3. Include source owners/dates, customer need, engagement, next step and local qualification criteria. For the SI variant bring sending/receiving seller roster and acceptance evidence. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Which fact supports qualification? Is a partner claim being counted as customer engagement? What corroboration resolves possible overlap? Which action still lacks seller confirmation?
listenFor: Evidence-based priority without invented scoring; possible overlap not labeled confirmed duplicate; exact scope/date; PSS prioritization distinct from AE stage authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one qualification row with customer evidence, possible overlap, identity gap, proposed seller action and progress/hold question manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed when partner-reported pipeline was separated from identifiable customer evidence?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore a qualification gap or possible overlap and consider a progress/hold rationale. Any real seller action requires that seller's acceptance; no validation deadline or return evidence is required. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized qualification gap or overlap checked and whether it prevented double counting or premature progress. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Inspect one opportunity for evidence behind the next stage-2/3 decision
activities.description: Independent choice: only identified authorized MSX records under existing CRM roles; if unavailable use a supplied-evidence Cowork alternative, not a wider query. Focuses top-deal inspection on evidence that changes the next decision.
activities.prompt: Review MSX opportunity [opportunity ID] against [next-decision question and MCEM-02/03 criteria], read-only. Show dated customer evidence, stage, risks, owner and next step; separate facts from partner claims. Draft a brief with support, contradiction, decisive gap and one owner question. Don’t invent stage gates. Stop if identity or decisive evidence is unresolved; request an extract if needed. Don’t approve stages, query partner systems, change records or decide funding.
activities.expectedOutput: One-deal brief: record support/date/reference, contradiction, decisive gap, proposed owner question and readiness stop condition.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS chooses coordination action; AE judges readiness and retains stage authority. Stop on unresolved decisive evidence or identity; AI cannot approve or enact progression.
activities.requiredContext: OPP_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE, NEXT_DECISION, MCEM_02_03_CRITERIA. Criteria are supplied authoritative guidance; retrieve only the identified authorized MSX record. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Focuses top-deal inspection on evidence that changes the next decision.

activities.name: Draft a decision brief from one deal's customer and partner evidence
activities.description: Independent supplied-evidence choice: Cowork uses only the approved inputs and applicable permissions/spending policy. Reconciles customer and partner perspectives without treating partner optimism as readiness.
activities.prompt: Use only [paste or attach supplied deal extract, customer evidence, partner notes and MCEM 02 03 criteria] for the deal identified in the supplied extract. Match identity and preserve evidence dates, distinguishing missing access from missing information. Separate customer evidence, record facts and partner claims relevant to the next stage-2/3 decision. Compare proceed-versus-hold considerations against the supplied criteria and identify the single decisive blocker without inventing gates. Draft a one-page next-decision brief with evidence, uncertainty, proposed action, accountable seller and review date; proposals are not commitments. Ask PSS and the AE to choose the next human decision, with each partner seller confirming their action; stop if decisive customer evidence or owner authority is unresolved. No external retrieval, stage approval, messages, writebacks, promises or funding decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: One-page brief with proceed/hold considerations, customer/record/claim distinction, decisive blocker, proposed action, seller and review date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS and AE choose next decisions within their authority; AE retains stage approval. Stop on unresolved customer evidence or owner authority; sellers confirm their actions.
activities.requiredContext: SUPPLIED_DEAL_EXTRACT, CUSTOMER_EVIDENCE, PARTNER_NOTES, MCEM_02_03_CRITERIA, DEAL_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. Each item needs source owner/date; unavailable records stay explicit.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A top deal needs a customer decision, not just a new stage label. Focus on the evidence, blocker and seller conversation that can move one deal forward.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Name one deal and the decision it faces. Top-deal importance does not override missing evidence. Supplied stage guidance is input, not permission for AI to invent gates. Partner sellers own their commitments; you own the opportunity decision.
discussionQuestions: What decision is blocked beyond changing the stage label? What customer evidence changes readiness? Which seller must confirm the next action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect one opportunity for evidence behind the next stage-2/3 decision'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one reviewed next-decision brief identifying decisive evidence, blocker, accountable owner, proposed action and hold condition. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile one deal's meeting actions against the actual blocker', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move the next human deal decision, not the stage label: test evidence, expose the blocker and confirm seller-owned actions. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one exact authorized opportunity ID or supplied deal extract, partner/customer scope/date, applicable stage-2/3 guidance, customer evidence, dated meeting notes, blocker and owner roster. ISV variant requires supplied owner-verified offer/procurement evidence. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Which cited fact supports progression and which is a partner claim? Does the action resolve the actual blocker? What remains for the AE? When must the draft be held?
listenFor: One concrete decision; customer evidence distinct from enthusiasm; supplied rather than invented gates; owners confirming their actions; explicit stop on decisive evidence gaps.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one decision brief with dated evidence, blocker, accountable role, proposed action and hold condition manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: How did replacing advance the deal with a specific decision change the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a deal blocker or evidence gap and adapt a decision brief. Do not approve a stage or commit another seller through the AI draft; no revised brief needs to be brought back. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized deal blocker clarified and whether it improved the seller-owned decision; do not infer acceleration from AI classification. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.description: Official Sales agent overview and example prompts for connected CRM data. Internal sales scenarios and available records can differ.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Inspect the customer next step behind one GTM-linked MSX opportunity
activities.description: Independent choice: only identified authorized MSX records under existing CRM roles; if unavailable use a supplied-evidence Cowork alternative, not a wider query. Grounds GTM follow-through in the customer record without claiming partner transaction-state access.
activities.prompt: Inspect MSX opportunity [opportunity ID] read-only. Draft a sell-through card with dated customer engagement, partner involvement, next step, owner, the customer decision and one seller question. Separate evidence from marketing/partner claims; offer visibility doesn’t prove referral acceptance or commitment. Stop on unresolved identity or decisive evidence and request extracts if needed. Don’t retrieve Marketplace/PMX/Partner Center status, change records, approve eligibility or decide funding.
activities.expectedOutput: One-deal card: dated record references, customer next decision, marketing/partner assertions, evidence gap and seller question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS selects verification action; AE/partner seller confirms their follow-up. Stop on unresolved identity or decisive customer evidence; marketing does not establish commitment.
activities.requiredContext: OPP_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. Known authorized MSX record only; no native partner-system, offer-status or full referral-state retrieval. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Grounds GTM follow-through in the customer record without claiming partner transaction-state access.

activities.description: Confirm a current requirement with authoritative citations and dates while leaving eligibility and approval to accountable owners.
activities.prompt: Verify [Marketplace/GTM requirement question] for the offer type and geography identified in [approved public offer brief or source reference] as of today. Start with the approved starting URLs and use current authoritative first-party material. Return the requirement wording, applicability conditions, publisher, publication or update date, access date, URL, and any conflict or ambiguity. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Marketing activity and offer visibility do not establish a sales outcome. Focus on one deal-to-GTM link or current requirement, with the source owner verifying partner-side facts.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Marketed status, referral acceptance and customer commitment need different evidence. Only accountable owners verify current partner-system status. PSS sales follow-through does not authorize campaign, funding, eligibility or MACC treatment decisions. Permission review precedes outcomes claims and reuse.
discussionQuestions: Which signal is actual customer evidence? Who verifies current offer or referral status? Which action is sales coordination versus PMM marketing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Verify one current Marketplace or GTM requirement'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one reviewed action card or reconciliation packet separating marketing signals, referral status and customer evidence, with verification owner and hold condition. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Turn one GTM handoff into a seller-owned next action', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: A marketed offer is not an accepted referral or customer commitment; translate GTM signals into verified sales decisions and accountable actions. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one deal ID, scope/date, relevant supplied GTM excerpt, dated customer/deal evidence and owner roster. Any Marketplace or referral excerpt needs ID, verifying owner and date. Unknown status remains unknown; marketing activity alone is not a sales outcome. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Does the draft claim sell-through from marketing alone? Is the customer next step dated? Who checks the disputed status at source? Which proposed seller action is still unaccepted?
listenFor: Distinct marketing/referral/customer evidence; bounded one-deal action; named verifying owner/date; PMM/PDM ownership preserved; no eligibility inference or borrowed customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one requirement check with offer/context, official rule/date or unavailable, applicability, source owner and hold question manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which apparent success signal was downgraded after separating promotion, referral acceptance and customer commitment?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore a sell-through assumption and a possible coordination question for the AE/partner seller. Do not promise an offer outcome, funding or another owner's action. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized GTM or Marketplace signal checked and whether it changed the sell-through action; distinguish promotion, referral acceptance and customer commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A renewal plan is credible when timing, risk and the next seller action are evidenced. Focus on one renewal intervention without assuming commercial treatment or partner commitments.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Distinguish renewal intent, record facts, partner expectations and owner-verified commercial facts. Sales Agent here is restricted to identified MSX opportunities, not broader agreement, quote or partner-system retrieval. No AI treatment calculations, eligibility approvals, financial commitments or forecast acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What evidence changes renewal risk? Is timing recorded, partner-expected or customer-confirmed? Who verifies the MACC assertion and who decides whether to use it?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect one identified renewal MSX opportunity for a decision-changing risk'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one renewal-risk card or three-opportunity reconciliation with dated facts, commercial unknowns, intervention owner and accept/hold decision. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'ISV variant: challenge the MACC assumption behind one renewal deal', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Prioritize renewal evidence gaps and accountable interventions; a MACC claim is not verified treatment, committed consumption or approved forecast. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one exact renewal MSX ID or dated supplied evidence for three renewal opportunities, scope/date, source owners, timing/risks and existing review criteria. For the one-deal intervention/ISV variant bring owner roster and explicitly supplied commercial evidence; avoid unnecessary agreement details. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Where is expected renewal treated as committed? Which statement lacks commercial authority? Is missing access being called missing pipeline? What can PSS coordinate without making a forecast or funding decision?
listenFor: Bounded renewal view; facts distinct from claims; exact authorized-owner question; no inferred MACC treatment; seller-confirmed actions; PSS priority distinct from AE forecast authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one renewal-risk card with agreement date or unknown, customer evidence, commercial uncertainty, verifying owner and hold reason manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which commercial assumption changed from usable evidence to a verification request?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore a renewal or MACC claim and consider a risk/hold rationale. Actual commercial verification remains with its authorized owner; do not promise renewal, treatment, funding or another seller's action. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized renewal or MACC assumption checked and whether it changed risk or hold judgment; omit terms and do not imply approved treatment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.

activities.name: Monitor agreed ROB actions
activities.description: Watch agreed sales actions on an approved cadence and report only changes or exceptions for PSS review.
activities.prompt: Draft, but don’t activate, a ROB action watch from [snapshots and dated baseline/prior report]. Include scope, sources, owners, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval gaps. Establish a first baseline of actions, dates and evidence; later, report changed completion evidence, dates/owners, missed actions and access gaps. Missing history means comparison unavailable. Don’t infer intent, score performance, send reminders or close actions; owners validate completion.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated baseline-only or change-only supplied-evidence review draft with source/history/access gaps and an unactivated proposal for the named reviewer; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Action owners validate status; PSS retains coaching and next-review decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Agreed ROB actions, approved cadence, evidence locations, dated baseline, named owners, and PSS reviewer. Provide authorized dated snapshots and user-maintained baseline/prior report if available. Source permissions, scope, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and automation approval are explicit proposed fields; missing inputs remain gaps and no tool access/state retention is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one bounded dependency/action and supply authorized dated snapshots; clearly labeled synthetic evidence is rehearsal-only.
2. Check the user-maintained baseline/prior report, comparable definitions and named reviewer; leave missing history, permission or criteria explicit.
3. Compare supplied evidence manually or with one already authorized tool; no schedule, live retrieval or persistent agent memory.
4. Produce a dated baseline-only/comparison draft and unactivated proposal with source, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval fields.
5. Apply the unchanged HumanCheckpoint before interpretation/action; future automation, notifications and system changes require separate explicit authorization.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Persistent exception monitoring closes the evidence loop without judging seller performance automatically.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Close the ROB loop across three supplied opportunity action histories

agents.name: Scout
agents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Execution coaching starts with observable evidence, not a judgment about a seller. Focus on one accepted action, its follow-through and the question that could improve the next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Observe evidence before judging behavior; an overdue record field does not prove poor performance. Meeting attendance does not prove action acceptance. PSS coaches execution, not PDM strategy or PMM performance. Compare only stated country/solution scope; three opportunities do not describe total partner performance.
discussionQuestions: What behavior can the evidence support and what context is missing? Did the receiving owner accept the action? What evidence at the next ROB shows follow-through rather than another meeting?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect three MSX records for evidence-led ROB coaching questions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one coaching card or three-opportunity ROB exception sheet with evidence, context gaps, owner-confirmed action and next-review test. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare one deal's coaching conversation from observable evidence', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coach one observable execution behavior using dated evidence and a seller-confirmed action; notes and CRM records do not establish full partner context. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring three exact MSX IDs or supplied evidence for three opportunities; use one deal for coaching/relay choices. Include scope/date, prior/current observations, agreed action notes and roster. State country/solution coverage, especially Asia cross-solution context. Permission-review or de-identify evidence. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Which statement is an observation rather than a personal judgment? What proves acceptance/completion? Which missing context should the seller explain? What will the next ROB test?
listenFor: Respectful evidence-led coaching; clear scope/date; no inferred motives or performance scores; proposed/accepted/completed actions distinct; PSS cadence ownership and individual seller accountability.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one coaching card with observable business fact, context gap, proposed/accepted/completed distinction, seller question and next ROB test manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: How did checking missing context change your coaching language or proposed action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore an execution behavior or relay gap and what evidence would help a later review. Confirm only your own actual coordination action; other owners must accept their own actions. If input or access is missing, you could explore a permitted sanitized example or leave the verification question open; do not infer approval, agreement or status. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a de-identified execution question clarified with its seller and whether it improved follow-up; do not assess employee performance. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

roles.name: Account Executive
roles.description: Owns Enterprise account priorities and commercial execution across pipeline, renewals, expansion, and customer conversations. Creates and qualifies opportunities, maintains evidence-backed forecasts, and coordinates the account team; technical, policy, and approval decisions remain with their accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Area Specialist (SSP)

roles.name: Solution Engineer

roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager

Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive

roles.name: Commercial Executive

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist

Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer

roles.name: Digital Cloud Solution Architect

PLC-EPS-PSS-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-EPS-PSS-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-EPS-PSS-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.
