roles.name: Commercial Executive
roles.description: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy and negotiation by assessing structural exposure, commercial risk, and renewal options. Verifies licensing, policy, and approval boundaries against authoritative sources, prepares decision narratives, and coordinates approvals and execution without assuming policy or exception approval authority.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads Enterprise commercial strategy, negotiation, and renewals within policy and approval limits.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Customer Success Account Manager
roles.description: Coordinates Enterprise customer success through outcome-based plans, milestones, and accepted owners. Combines health, usage, support, delivery, and stakeholder signals to align executives, orchestrate teams and partners, support adoption and growth planning, and manage delivery risks without owning technical architecture approval.

roles.name: Digital Account Executive
roles.description: Manages SME&C territory coverage across direct and accepted partner-led routes, identifying uncovered gaps and prioritizing evidence-based prospecting. roles.name: Commercial Executive

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist

PLC-USPSI-SSP-W01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PLC-USPSI-SSP-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-USPSI-SSP-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

secondaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use as a substitute for a specialized agent when the work requires a specific system or workflow, for a multi-step task you would rather hand off and review, which is Cowork, or for work that should keep running on a schedule, which is Scout.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot from the app launcher or copilot.cloud.microsoft and start in Chat.

activities.name: Build a prioritized lead follow-up plan
activities.description: Combine scattered lead, event, account, and interaction signals into a structured SSP follow-up plan. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt: Using only the approved lead/attendee records, account context and email, meeting or public-source excerpts I supply, create a prioritized follow-up plan for the solution area. For each lead include source, account, likely interest, solution relevance, suggested message, owner, and next action. Flag missing evidence and do not send outreach. Use [relevant dated material] only; no search, connectors or actions.
activities.expectedOutput: Prioritized lead follow-up plan with source, fit, message, owner, and next action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The SSP decides whether this lead should be contacted at all. Consent and prior contact are conditions on the approach rather than details of it, and a lead that looks new to the system may not be new to the customer.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Approved lead or attendee lists; account context; solution area; recent interactions.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most of the effort in lead follow-up is assembly. AI can assemble; the SSP decides where to focus.

activities.name: Draft the first contact for the top-priority lead
activities.description: Turn the top-ranked lead into a specific, short first message that connects the signal to a reason for the customer to respond.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Lead and account signals are noisy. Focus on turning them into a focused follow-up plan.
keyTalkingPoints: Qualification is evidence work. Solution relevance, owner, message, consent, and next action must be explicit.
discussionQuestions: Which lead or signal deserves attention first? What evidence makes it real? Who owns the next action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build a prioritized lead follow-up plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from noisy signals to one prioritized follow-up plan. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Close the loop on outreach that never got an answer', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Lead prioritization matters when credible demand leads to appropriate, consent-aware follow-up. Activity or a high AI ranking alone does not establish customer intent. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one lead or account signal, dated qualification evidence and the proposed follow-up owner. Use approved user-supplied evidence with source and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Which lead has the strongest dated evidence of solution relevance, and what is only inferred? Who owns the first follow-up? How does a peer distinguish a buying signal from marketing activity before outreach?
listenFor: Undifferentiated lead lists, vague ownership, weak message fit, and missing consent/context.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a three-lead ranking: dated solution signal, customer relevance, missing context/permission, follow-up owner and next question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal warrants a customer action rather than just a new record, and what evidence would disprove the opportunity?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore whether a priority lead warrants first contact and adapt a possible follow-up. Contact is not a huddle assignment; any outreach still needs appropriate permission and human judgment. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized lead signal and whether the reviewed follow-up clarified interest or avoided a poor contact; no sent message is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorQuestions: What decision and fallback ask should this meeting advance? Which objection would expose a gap in discovery? What did a peer change after rehearsing a similar customer conversation?
listenFor: Meetings framed around content rather than customer decision, objections first discovered live, and unclear ask.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a short customer rehearsal: intended decision, discovery question, likely objection, evidence-qualified reply and fallback ask. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Rehearse with a peer; if alone, write both sides and mark the exchange untested, not a validated customer or coaching response. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence would make this customer conversation credible, and what decision or question still belongs to a person?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could explore the unknown most likely to change your recommendation and adapt a discovery question, without arranging or completing a customer conversation. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized discovery question and what its answer changed, or what remains unknown; note whether the conversation became more focused. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A solution-selling plan is useful only if it changes pursuit execution. Focus on building a plan that can be worked.
keyTalkingPoints: Plan around customer outcome, solution play, stakeholders, proof needs, demo or workshop sequence, and next decision.
discussionQuestions: Which solution pursuit needs a clearer plan? What proof or stakeholder coverage is missing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the solution-selling plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from plan structure to one active pursuit. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Map who actually decides and who is missing', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Solution-selling plans should expose who decides, what proof matters and where engagement is missing. A stakeholder map is a hypothesis until the account team or customer confirms it. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one solution pursuit, the customer outcome, known stakeholders and the proof or decision gap in its current plan. Use approved user-supplied evidence with source and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What next customer decision makes this pursuit worth specialist time? Where does the plan lack a stakeholder, proof path or dated commitment? What planning check from a colleague would expose that gap earlier?
listenFor: Generic solution plans, missing stakeholder coverage, unclear proof path, and no 30-day plan.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or approved context is unavailable, use a sanitized supplied example or a clearly labeled synthetic case. On paper, build one solution-pursuit plan slice: next decision, stakeholder coverage, minimum proof, dependency, owner and dated action. Mark evidence, assumptions and unknowns; proposed ownership, customer status and dates remain unconfirmed until validated. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient. Any later AI run must use project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot and approved supplied inputs.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed your priority or plan, and which assumption needs checking before the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check the decision map for a live pursuit and validate a missing stakeholder or proof requirement with the account owner before outreach. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized decision-maker or proof gap checked and whether it improved the pursuit plan. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The conversation happens before the story is finished. Focus on turning what you heard into a customer-specific narrative the account would recognize.
keyTalkingPoints: The customer defines value. Use sourced evidence, caveats, use cases, and a clear next ask.
discussionQuestions: What customer priority does this solution map to? Which claim is supported, assumed, or missing evidence?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Tailor the solution value narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from what the customer told you to the value logic and the proof it needs. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test the assumptions the value claims depend on', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Customer-specific value depends on defensible assumptions and customer-stated priorities. Removing an unsupported claim can improve trust more than polishing the narrative. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved customer conversation excerpt, the stated priority and sourced value claims with their caveats. Use approved user-supplied evidence with source and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-stated priority anchors the value claim? What source and assumption support it, and what remains unproved? How would a peer challenge the claim before it reaches the customer?
listenFor: Generic value claims, unsupported ROI, customer priorities inferred rather than sourced, and missing caveats.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one value-claim strip: customer-stated priority, proposed benefit, supplied evidence, assumption, caveat and validation owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which outcome can you substantiate for this audience, and what claim or next action still needs validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could test the assumptions behind one value claim, and remove any claim you cannot defend. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized claim qualified, retained or dropped and whether checking it made the value story more credible. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Pursuits stall at handoffs. Focus on making every role, partner, funding dependency, and checkpoint explicit.
keyTalkingPoints: Name the objective, contributors, asks, owners, dates, dependencies, and escalation points.
discussionQuestions: Which handoff is currently assumed rather than owned? Where could partner or funding support change the path?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Bring funding into the pursuit orchestration plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from orchestration principles to one stalled handoff. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Make each ask specific enough to be accepted', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Cross-role orchestration should unblock the customer decision with the smallest necessary accepted contribution. Funding, partner capacity and technical help are not secured merely by requesting them. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one pursuit handoff, current contributors, partner or funding dependencies and the owner or date still unconfirmed. Use approved user-supplied evidence with source and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Which specialist, technical, partner or funding dependency is stalled? What evidence and acceptance does the next owner need? How does a peer make that handoff executable without representing funding as approved?
listenFor: Unnamed owners, handoffs without dates, partner input treated as optional, and funding status overstated.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one specialist/technical/partner/funding handoff row: contribution needed, proposed owner, evidence, acceptance gap and next date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could explore the most consequential stalled handoff and draft a bounded, reviewed ask for its contributor; sending it is not required. Do not request work from every role merely to complete the exercise. Receiving-owner acceptance is required before treating any actual handoff as accepted; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized stalled handoff and whether a bounded ask clarified ownership or exposed a gap; no collection of every role request is needed. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Competitive response should be built on customer context and proof, not generic battlecards.
keyTalkingPoints: Use current approved competitive evidence, win/loss context, differentiators, objections, risks, and review flags.
discussionQuestions: Which competitor or alternative is shaping the decision? What proof is strongest and where is it weak?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the competitive differentiation brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from competitor context to one proof-backed response plan. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test the differentiator against the customer's real decision criteria', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Competitive responses are credible when current approved proof addresses the customer decision criterion. Objection handlers are not permission for unsupported competitor claims. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one competitive pursuit, the customer decision criteria and current approved competitive evidence; label gaps and assumptions. Use approved user-supplied evidence with source and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Which competitive claim changes the customer decision, and which dated source supports it? What would make it inapplicable here? How has a colleague tested differentiation against the customer's actual criteria?
listenFor: Stale battlecard claims, unsupported competitor statements, and differentiators not tied to customer priorities.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one competitive response row: customer criterion, proposed differentiator, dated source or unknown, applicability caveat and validation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which customer criterion does approved competitive proof address, and what claim should you qualify or avoid?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, you could adapt an objection handler tied to approved proof and consider where it might help; using it in a live conversation is not required. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, you could explore a sanitized manual example or leave the gap open; never invent facts. For USPSI, any Microsoft 365 Copilot use must be limited to authorized supplied information; manual exploration is also a choice. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized objection and whether approved proof answered it, required a caveat or showed a need for discovery. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.

What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on selecting the next routing conversation before the opportunity hardens around an ineligible or uneconomic path.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only when external delivery, proof, assessment, deployment, or funding support is needed; partner-led and zero-cost routes should be tested before discretionary ECIF.
Current execution: Use current program guidance and route through DSS/PSS or the named program owner; current submission systems vary by workload and route.
Fallback: If eligibility or system access is unclear, send the routing brief to the authoritative owner and do not promise a program to the customer or partner.
System of record: MSX for the opportunity/customer plan; the route-specific authoritative system only after the responsible owner confirms the route.
Optional AI boundary: ECIF Agent may provide guidance where the DAE has access, but it does not establish eligibility or universally submit requests.
discussionQuestions: What outcome requires outside support?
Which current route is eligible and accepted?
Who must resolve the funding or delivery question before a promise?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Define the support need before choosing a program'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Secure acceptance from the routing owner', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Scale routing needs customer, workload and transaction facts plus accepted ownership. Candidate routes are not eligibility or completed transfers. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one opportunity needing proof/delivery/adoption support, known constraints, applicable current program guidance and the routing owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What support need and customer outcome require a route? Which scalable option fits the current authoritative conditions? How would a peer obtain routing-owner acceptance without promising a program or investment?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one support-routing brief: customer need, scope, scalable candidate, current eligibility question, routing owner and acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which route-fit assumption changed after checking requirements and acceptance?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check a deciding route requirement or input and seek receiving-owner disposition or a documented hold. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized routing assumption checked and whether it reduced misrouting or clarified acceptance. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on preventing late commercial involvement by making the CE trigger and requested decision explicit.
keyTalkingPoints: Use when pricing, agreement route, concessions, funding dependency, renewal, procurement, partner transaction, or approval complexity requires CE judgment.
Current execution: Use the current opportunity, agreement record, approved guidance, and direct request from DAE/opportunity owner.
Fallback: Use a structured engagement brief and named CE acknowledgment if no intake workflow exists.
System of record: MSX for opportunity context; authoritative agreement/licensing and approval sources for commercial facts.
Optional AI boundary: Cowork or Deal Agent may assemble supplied context where available. The CE validates every fact and makes the engagement decision.
discussionQuestions: What commercial decision requires engagement now?
What minimum context lets the owner act?
What would become unsafe if terms were shared before review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Test whether CE engagement is required'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Agree the working boundary', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Early CE engagement follows an actual commercial decision and transaction route, not a general request for help. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one material commercial question, approved opportunity/agreement context, the desired decision and the current engagement owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What trigger makes CE engagement necessary on this deal? What is the exact commercial decision and working boundary? How does a peer establish CE acknowledgment without taking over seller execution?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one CE engagement brief: triggering fact, exact commercial decision, working boundary and acknowledgment needed. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What needs CE involvement, and what can the account owner resolve without it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could clarify a commercial question and ask CE and the customer-path owner whether engagement is needed; evidenced no-engage is valid. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized engagement question clarified and whether it avoided a late surprise or unnecessary handoff. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: Draft a monitoring proposal; don’t activate it. Use only the dated snapshots, baseline and previous report I supply; don’t set up monitoring. activities.bestFitJob: Define what change invalidates or reopens the commercial decision.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.

3. Compare only supplied state; missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no progress.
4. Apply the existing HumanCheckpoint to interpret changes; proposed owners, actions and thresholds are not accepted decisions.
5. Keep an unactivated proposal with approval gaps; do not schedule, retain agent memory, send reports or change records.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on starting only the post-sale work DCSA can accountably carry and expose the rest early.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies only to pinned/eligible accounts or approved material swarms; CASA Stage 2-3 support requires explicit local applicability.
Current execution: Use the accepted technical decision, opportunity/consumption milestone record, coverage rules, and named delivery route.
Fallback: Run a live intake checklist and record the coverage gap/escalation if no integrated handoff exists.
System of record: MSX or current committed-milestone/consumption record; exact role view requires validation.
Optional AI boundary: AI may check completeness of supplied fields; it cannot determine coverage, accept ownership, or invent a baseline.
discussionQuestions: Does confirmed coverage permit this intake?
Which baseline and owner are still missing?
What must be accepted or escalated before post-sale work starts?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Test coverage and materiality'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Confirm delivery ownership and first review', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Intake acceptance needs coverage, outcome and credible baseline, with delivery ownership separate from DCSA coordination. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one proposed post-sale intake, accepted technical decision, current coverage rules, milestone/baseline evidence and the selected delivery route. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What coverage and materiality evidence supports DCSA intake? Is the outcome, baseline and milestone actually accepted? How would a peer return an incomplete handoff rather than silently absorb it?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one consumption intake gate: coverage/materiality, outcome, baseline, milestone evidence and receiver acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which evidence changed accept, reroute or reject after checking coverage?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate the deciding intake gap and seek owner-confirmed accept, reroute, reject or hold; do not assume delivery acceptance. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized intake assumption checked and whether it improved disposition or prevented unsupported ownership. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.description: Align the forecast record to evidence.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the opportunity identified in [paste/attach the approved record and reconciled next-decision evidence], compare the current stage, close date, and risk with recorded next decision, remaining steps, and approval or transaction dependencies. Return a defensible proposed stage, date, and risk update or a reason for no change; separate partner reporting from Microsoft evidence and do not update MSX.
activities.expectedOutput: A defensible stage/date/risk recommendation or documented no-change rationale for DAE review; no MSX update or partner forecast decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE owns the Microsoft forecast call; the partner owns its own forecast.
activities.requiredContext: Next decision, remaining steps, approval/transaction dependencies, and current MSX values. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving one applicable partner-led opportunity without mistaking partner silence for progress or failure.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only when a partner is actively co-selling, transacting, or expected to deliver; use the direct-account route otherwise.
Current execution: Reconcile MSX with current partner-reported status from Partner Center, Partner Timeline, or the named partner seller.
Fallback: If partner-system access is unavailable, obtain a dated partner confirmation and record it as partner-reported rather than Microsoft-verified.
System of record: MSX is the Microsoft opportunity and forecast record; Partner Center/Partner Timeline is the partner-side status source when accessible.
Optional AI boundary: An approved assistant may compare supplied evidence or draft the partner ask; it must not infer partner stage, update MSX, or disclose unapproved account data.
discussionQuestions: Which deal decision is stalled?
What partner status is actually confirmed?
Which next ask can move the deal without guessing stage or intent?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile Microsoft and partner deal evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Correct stage, close date, and risk', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Partner-led progress follows evidenced customer decisions and accepted actions, not unsupported stage or date changes. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one active partner-led opportunity, its MSX record, dated partner-reported status and the blocker or next decision. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which Microsoft and partner facts disagree about this deal? What next customer decision and co-sell ask follow from the verified evidence? How does a peer retain partner-reported status without treating it as Microsoft-verified forecast proof?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one co-sell reconciliation: dated Microsoft/partner facts, partner-reported status, contradiction, next decision and responsible record owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which partner signal failed to support the recorded deal state or next decision?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could inspect deciding deal evidence and ask the seller or record owner to confirm the next action or authorized correction. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized assumption corrected and whether it improved forecast discussion or the partner ask. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Identify changes that alter the plan
activities.description: Compare dated authorized portfolio snapshots to identify movement that may change account priority or intervention needs.
activities.prompt: Draft a monitoring proposal; don’t activate it. Use only the dated snapshots, baseline and previous report I supply; don’t set up monitoring. Without history, report a baseline—not ‘no change’. Include proposed scope, sources, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and change criteria; flag unknowns. Compare the supplied authorized assigned-account, opportunity, activity, usage, and support signals. If two comparable dated snapshots are supplied, return only new movement, materially growing or shrinking risk, resolved items, or changed evidence since the previous report, with source date and confidence. Exclude unchanged background risk and do not decide, assign, or write anything.
activities.expectedOutput: A portfolio-change table or baseline-only view with source dates, comparability limits, changed risks/evidence and questions for DAE; no inferred cause or running monitor.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE decides which movement is material.
activities.requiredContext: Assigned accounts, recent opportunity/activity changes, separately accessible usage/support evidence, and prior review. Supply approved dated snapshots, comparable definitions, user-maintained baseline/prior report if available, reviewer and actual approved change criteria. Missing scope, source permission, cadence, recipients, expiry/review date or future automation approval remains explicit; no persistent state or tool access is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Separate new movement from unchanged background risk.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.
2. Confirm scope, comparable definitions, evidence permission, access gaps and named human reviewer.
3. Compare only supplied state; missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no progress.
4. Apply the existing HumanCheckpoint to interpret changes; proposed owners, actions and thresholds are not accepted decisions.
5. Keep an unactivated proposal with approval gaps; do not schedule, retain agent memory, send reports or change records.
Access/fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied snapshots manually; no recurring job, retained agent memory or notification is required or authorized.
activities.whyThisMatters: Portfolio scale requires exception-based attention, but movement becomes useful only after the DAE assigns meaning and ownership.

agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on acting on the one portfolio change that materially alters the territory plan.
keyTalkingPoints: Use accessible signals only and route by actual coverage; DCSA leads applicable post-sale consumption work and partners may own delivery.
Current execution: Use MSX and separately accessible usage/consumption/support views; do not assume Sales Home provides consolidated current pipeline, renewal, or value realization.
Fallback: Collect a small dated exception list from current role owners when cross-system aggregation is unavailable.
System of record: Each source remains authoritative for its own record; DAE records the resulting account/territory decision in MSX or the current territory plan.
Optional AI boundary: AI may group supplied changes and draft a routing note; it must not score unobservable customer risk or decide technical/commercial ownership.
discussionQuestions: Which portfolio change materially alters the plan?
What source proves the movement?
Which role has actual coverage for the resulting action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify changes that alter the plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Close the loop into growth and forecast', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Portfolio inspection focuses on material change and owned intervention. A new view matters only if it changes coverage, forecast or follow-through. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one dated territory exception, its source records, the current plan assumption and the actual covered or partner owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which portfolio change actually alters the coverage or growth plan? Which accountable role should carry the intervention? How does another DAE close the evidence loop before changing the forecast?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one portfolio exception row: dated change, plan impact, accountable intervention role, evidence gap and next growth/forecast check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which change warranted action rather than another status update?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could inspect a material portfolio change and agree targeted intervention or routing; keep unsupported expansion or forecast effects provisional. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized change and whether action became clearer or a weak hypothesis was rejected. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
