activities.name: State the approval decision and evidence
activities.description: Make explicit what the approver accepts and what happens if declined.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the opportunity identified in the supplied construct and customer-impact evidence, use the requested authority and review the supplied current construct, alternatives, sourced economics, recorded policy rulings, and customer impact. Prepare an approval decision statement showing exactly what the approver is asked to accept, the evidence and assumptions, unresolved gaps, and the consequence of decline. Do not approve, commit, or update the deal. Use the supplied agreement evidence; don’t assume a Deal Agent or Sales Home integration.
activities.expectedOutput: A decision statement with sourced evidence, assumptions, and consequence of decline.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE owns the case and every commercial assertion.
activities.requiredContext: Construct, alternatives, economics with sources, policy rulings, customer impact, and requested authority. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Make explicit what the approver accepts and what happens if declined.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm this specific task: State the approval decision and evidence.
2. Supply authorized dated inputs listed in RequiredContext; use clearly labeled synthetic data if permitted real inputs are unavailable.
3. Produce the stated ExpectedOutput using the prompt; verify claims against supplied sources and expose unknowns.
4. CE owns the case and every commercial assertion.
5. Keep the output as a draft for the stated human checkpoint; no sending, record update, approval or assignment is authorized by this practice.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Read demand in evidence order
activities.description: Combine the available evidence without allowing the loudest or most convenient source to determine priority.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the account identified in [the approved demand evidence], review the available installed-base and approved telemetry, contract or renewal events, direct customer and account-team evidence, partner evidence, and marketing engagement in that order. Return an account-outcome evidence card that labels what each item directly supports, only suggests, or leaves unknown, and identify the customer outcome that may warrant action or state that evidence is insufficient. Do not infer business value from usage or buying intent from engagement.
activities.expectedOutput: An account-outcome evidence card showing direct evidence, proxies, unknowns, timing, and whether action is warranted.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether the combined evidence warrants attention. Telemetry can show activity without value, a contract date can create timing without need, and marketing engagement can show curiosity without intent.
activities.requiredContext: One account; installed-base or telemetry evidence where available; contract or renewal timing; direct customer or team evidence; partner and marketing evidence where applicable. Authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts.
activitySteps: 1. Gather only evidence you are authorized to use.
2. Order it by customer proximity rather than by tool.
3. Separate direct evidence, proxy evidence, and unknowns.
4. Name the customer outcome that may warrant action.
5. Record insufficient evidence rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: A stable hierarchy makes the job solution-neutral while allowing each solution area to supply its own valid telemetry and contract events.

activities.name: Assign the action, owner, and route
activities.description: Turn warranted demand into a time-bound action owned by the DSS, account team, another specialist, or partner.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. From the supplied completed evidence card, coverage model, seller capacity, and timing event, recommend one route: DSS pursues; DSS and account owner pursue together; another solution specialist; partner acceptance; hold for named evidence; or close as not actionable. Return the proposed owner, acceptance requirement, due date, customer-safe next action, and rationale; do not treat routing as accepted until the recipient confirms.
activities.expectedOutput: A recorded action with route, accountable owner, acceptance requirement, due date, and rationale.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns the solution-area routing recommendation but cannot invent another person's capacity or acceptance. Closing or holding is valid only when the evidence and reason are explicit.
activities.requiredContext: A completed evidence card; actual account and partner coverage; seller capacity; relevant timing event.
activitySteps: 1. Check who currently owns the customer path.
2. Decide whether the DSS should lead, join, route, hold, or close.
3. For partner routing, name the acceptance needed.
4. Give the action a date tied to the customer event.
5. Record the reason and owner.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Demand dies when it is analyzed but not owned, or when a partner is named without accepting the work.

activities.name: Open the conversation without exposing internal signals
activities.description: Prepare a customer-safe opening grounded in the likely business situation rather than in how Microsoft detected it.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Draft a customer-safe opening for the account/outcome and recipient identified in [the customer-safe context], for review by the accountable seller. Use only public or customer-provided context from the customer-safe context. Return the opening, open questions, assumptions to avoid, and the answer that would disconfirm active need. Do not expose internal telemetry, engagement tracking, scoring, propensity, or contract surveillance, and do not send or treat the draft as approved until the accountable seller confirms it.
activities.expectedOutput: A customer-safe opening, open questions, assumptions to avoid, and a clear disconfirming answer.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS and accountable seller decide what the customer hears. Internal telemetry and engagement data are not customer messaging, and a polished draft does not authorize outreach.
activities.requiredContext: The account, plausible customer outcome, customer-safe context, intended recipient, and accountable seller.
activitySteps: 1. Start from the recorded customer-safe next action.
2. Remove internal signal details from the input.
3. Turn assumptions into open questions.
4. Check that the opening would not reveal monitoring the customer did not expect.
5. Have the accountable seller approve the outreach.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Using a signal without exposing it preserves trust while still allowing timely discovery.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Demand rarely arrives as one perfect signal. Focus on combining the evidence the DSS can legitimately use and deciding where action is warranted.
keyTalkingPoints: Use an evidence hierarchy rather than a tool hierarchy: installed base and telemetry where available; contract and renewal events; direct customer and account-team evidence; partner evidence; then marketing engagement. No one source proves intent. A DSS decides the customer outcome, owner, and action. Tool availability and signal thresholds vary by solution area and geography.
discussionQuestions: Which evidence has preceded real pipeline in your solution area?
Which contract or usage event is easy to miss?
When is marketing engagement useful corroboration rather than the starting point?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Read demand in evidence order'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from evidence quality to the owner and action the DSS will record. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Open the conversation without exposing internal signals', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Solution-area demand needs credible account-outcome signals and actionable routing; marketing activity is not qualified demand. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one account with at least two forms of demand evidence. Remove customer-sensitive detail that should not be shared in the huddle.
facilitatorQuestions: What changed for the customer, and when?
Which evidence is direct and which is only a proxy?
What outcome and owner make this actionable?
What early signal has a peer used without confusing telemetry or marketing activity with demand?
listenFor: Marketing activity treated as intent, telemetry treated as value, contract events considered too late, local tool outputs treated as universal truth, and accounts prioritized without an owner or action date.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one demand evidence row: customer change/date, direct versus proxy signal, solution relevance, action owner and next validation. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal did you initially overweight, and what changed your judgment?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate a demand signal for a priority account-outcome pair and personally choose an evidenced next action or hold with its owner. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized signal reweighted and whether it improved prioritization or avoided a weak pursuit. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.name: Qualify, merge, route, or close the demand item
activities.description: Make the pipeline decision before creating or updating an opportunity.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the account identified in the supplied demand card, assess the supplied demand evidence card and current qualification criteria against related opportunities already recorded. Return a create, update, merge, route, hold, or close recommendation with supporting evidence, related-record disposition, and the single missing customer fact most likely to change it. Do not treat propensity, engagement, or installed base alone as qualification or write any record.
activities.expectedOutput: A qualification decision with supporting evidence, related-record disposition, and the single fact most likely to change it.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS makes the qualification decision. AI or propensity can organize evidence but cannot choose the stage, create customer commitment, or resolve contradictory account context.
activities.requiredContext: The demand evidence card; current qualification criteria; existing account opportunities; customer and solution context. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Search for related open opportunities.
2. Apply the current solution-area qualification criteria.
3. Separate customer gaps from internal gaps.
4. Decide create, update, merge, route, hold, or close.
5. Record the decisive evidence and missing fact.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Qualification before record creation reduces duplicate, speculative, and wrong-workload pipeline.

activities.name: Route a multi-workload need without fragmenting the customer
activities.description: Identify the lead solution outcome and secure ownership for adjacent solution-area work.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Using the supplied qualified cross-solution customer need, current opportunities, and specialist coverage, identify the lead business outcome, the solution area best placed to lead, and adjacent workloads needing another specialist. Return one customer narrative, proposed owners, and the acceptance required from each; do not fragment the need into separate opportunities solely because multiple products appear.
activities.expectedOutput: A lead solution-area decision, adjacent-workload routing, named owners, acceptance state, and one customer narrative.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS proposes the route but does not assign another specialist without acceptance. Account and solution leaders resolve contested ownership.
activities.requiredContext: A qualified customer need that crosses solution areas; current opportunities; specialist coverage and ownership.
activitySteps: 1. Start from the customer outcome, not product names.
2. Name the lead solution-area owner.
3. Identify adjacent specialist decisions.
4. Request explicit acceptance from each new owner.
5. Preserve one coherent customer narrative and record the routing.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Unowned adjacent workloads stall, while product-by-product routing fragments both the customer conversation and pipeline.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A demand item becomes pipeline only when somebody can execute from the record. This session moves from interest to a qualified and routed opportunity.
keyTalkingPoints: The DSS owns solution-area qualification and progression, not every account or commercial decision. Check for an existing opportunity before creating another. Route cross-solution needs explicitly. Stage and forecast are human judgments supported by evidence; CRM is the system of record even when planning begins elsewhere.
discussionQuestions: What evidence changes an account from target to qualified opportunity?
Where do duplicate or wrong-SKU opportunities begin?
What would another seller need to act from your record without calling you first?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Qualify, merge, route, or close the demand item'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the qualification decision to the exact CRM change and recipient handoff. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Route a multi-workload need without fragmenting the customer', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Qualified pipeline reflects customer evidence and owner-controlled disposition, not a new AI-generated opportunity or stage. If useful, you could revisit this evidence check in recurring work and choose whether to share a safe observation with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one demand item and its current MSX or local CRM record, including any related opportunity.
facilitatorQuestions: Does this warrant a new opportunity, an update, a merge, or a route?
Which solution area should lead?
What evidence supports the stage and forecast treatment?
How would another DSS decide update, merge, route or close without creating a duplicate opportunity?
listenFor: Duplicate opportunities, propensity used as qualification, cross-SKU needs left ownerless, stale next steps, and stage or forecast chosen to satisfy cadence rather than evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one demand disposition row: create/update/merge/route/close hypothesis, duplicate check, evidence, proposed stage and CRM owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Could another seller execute from this opportunity without asking you to translate it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check a qualification gap and recommend advance, merge, route or close; reconcile the record only through an authorized owner. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized disposition and whether it reduced duplication or made the next action executable. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

PLC-SMEC-DSS-W04.roleTopicDescription: Recover what the customer has already heard, frame the solution-area outcome, and agree the criteria and roles that will govern the conversation.
PLC-SMEC-DSS-W04.wiifm: A customer-recognizable position helps you avoid contradictory promises and uncover decisive criteria before a conversation exposes gaps in the account team's understanding.
PLC-SMEC-DSS-W04.name: Discover, Shape, and Validate a Solution
PLC-SMEC-DSS-W04.description: Clarify the customer problem and decision criteria, shape an appropriate technical approach, validate it against evidence and constraints, and communicate what the proof does and does not establish.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Provides USPSI technical advice on production architecture, validation, technical health, and cost optimization using approved evidence and organizational handling requirements. Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

activities.name: Recover commitments before shaping the conversation
activities.description: Find what the customer has already heard and confirm unwritten commitments with the accountable account owner.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the account identified in [approved commitment and interaction evidence], summarize recorded commitments, customer priorities, unresolved objections, partner activity, and prior solution-area messages from the relevant time range. Return a commitment-and-context brief that separates recorded facts from gaps and turns each gap into a question for the accountable account owner or customer; do not infer verbal commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: A confirmed commitment and context brief with unresolved gaps and owners.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides what must be confirmed before the customer conversation. The account record is incomplete, and silence from an account owner is not permission to invent a role split or commitment.
activities.requiredContext: One live customer conversation or decision; CRM history; approved account materials; accountable account owner. Authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts.
activitySteps: 1. Review CRM history and approved account materials.
2. List customer and Microsoft commitments.
3. Separate written evidence from inferred context.
4. Ask the accountable owner about the two gaps most likely to create a contradiction.
5. Update the preparation after confirmation.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Contradicting an earlier promise damages the whole team, not only the specialist message.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Build the customer-recognizable solution narrative
activities.description: Connect the business problem, stakeholders, urgency, solution-area contribution, and customer action in language the customer uses.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. From the supplied confirmed commitments, customer problem, stakeholders, desired outcome, evidence, and coverage model, prepare a one-page customer-recognizable solution narrative. Include the current consequence, urgency, solution-area contribution, next customer decision, stakeholder map, agreed conversation roles, and discovery gaps; preserve unknowns as questions and exclude unsupported product claims.
activities.expectedOutput: A customer-recognizable narrative, stakeholder map, discovery gaps, and agreed conversation roles.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns customer relevance and solution-area framing. The accountable account owner approves the customer path, and technical or commercial claims remain with their qualified owners.
activities.requiredContext: Confirmed commitments; customer problem; stakeholders; intended outcome; current evidence; coverage model.
activitySteps: 1. State the customer problem and consequence in their language.
2. Map stakeholders to the outcome and decision.
3. Explain only the solution-area contribution relevant to that outcome.
4. Preserve unknowns as discovery questions.
5. Agree who leads each part of the conversation under the actual coverage model.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared narrative lets multiple roles add depth without presenting competing versions of the customer problem.

activities.name: Make customer criteria and deliberate concessions explicit
activities.description: Express the position against the customer's criteria and decide which criteria to contest, meet, clarify, or concede.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Using [paste/describe fictional or approved de-identified customer criteria, evidence and unknowns for Microsoft and the alternative], coach me to rehearse which criteria to contest, meet, clarify, or deliberately concede; how to state evidence without overclaiming; likely customer challenges; and evidence-backed responses. Return a criteria map with gaps, proposed concessions, approval owners, and validation questions; do not invent evidence or authorize concessions. Use a fictional or de-identified scenario. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A decision-criteria map with evidence, gaps, deliberate concessions, owners, and validation questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS judges solution relevance; the Commercial Executive or other authorized commercial owner approves commercial concessions, and the accountable account owner approves how the position is carried to the customer.
activities.requiredContext: Customer-stated criteria; current evidence; competitor or alternative information where relevant; accountable commercial and account owners.
activitySteps: 1. Open Agent J.ai and paste the customer criteria, evidence, and unknowns.
2. Rehearse the hardest credible customer challenge, including a criterion where Microsoft is behind.
3. Test whether each response uses customer criteria and supported evidence rather than internal feature priorities.
4. DSS chooses the solution position.
5. Obtain the required commercial and account-owner approval before communicating any concession.
Access/fallback: Agent J.ai is optional. Use a peer or written de-identified rehearsal; simulated reactions are not evidence or accepted commitments.
activities.whyThisMatters: Conceding deliberately can create credibility; conceding without authority or evidence can create commercial and customer risk.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Solution depth is useful only when it connects to the customer's strategy and the decision they are trying to make.
keyTalkingPoints: Recover prior commitments before shaping a new narrative. Use the customer's business outcome and language. Make decision criteria explicit, including criteria Microsoft may not win. Agree the meeting and decision roles according to the actual coverage model; a DAE-led meeting is one variant, not the universal pattern.
discussionQuestions: What has this customer already been promised?
What would the customer say the decision is about?
Which criterion could cause a late loss if it remains implicit?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Recover commitments before shaping the conversation'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the narrative to the decision criteria and the role split required to test them. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Make customer criteria and deliberate concessions explicit', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Customer strategy uses customer criteria and verified commitments, not Microsoft language substituted for their outcome. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live customer conversation, the known commitments, the intended outcome, and any stated decision criteria.
facilitatorQuestions: What has already been said or promised?
What customer outcome connects the stakeholders?
Which criteria will decide, and which might we concede?
Which discovery check has a peer used to expose a criterion Microsoft assumed but the customer did not?
listenFor: Product-first narratives, assumed stakeholders, internal language presented as customer language, criteria invented by Microsoft, and meeting roles based on title rather than coverage reality.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer strategy brief: prior commitment, customer outcome, stakeholder gap, customer-confirmed versus assumed criteria and next question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which part of your original narrative was Microsoft language rather than customer language?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate a deciding customer criterion or commitment with the customer or account owner, then revise the relevant narrative point. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized criterion clarified and whether it made the strategy more recognizable to the customer. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA
roles.description: Translates scoped technical intake into offering architecture, designs, and reusable assets. Develops Customer Zero proofs and validates technical conclusions and offering readiness, coordinating accepted handoffs into commercialization and activation while keeping broader strategy, partner engineering delivery, and commercial approvals with accountable owners.
roles.descriptionSummary: Turns scoped EPS technical intake into offering architecture, reusable assets, and validated proofs.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Shapes USPSI account technical strategy using approved stakeholder, workload, KPI, and risk evidence. Prioritizes AI and cloud workloads, develops executive technical narratives, and aligns technical teams around readiness, impact, and customer decisions within organizational requirements, without default implementation ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes USPSI technical strategy and workload priorities using approved evidence.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions through technical discovery, agreed criteria, architecture options, and grounded responses using approved evidence. Designs demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of concept with success and exit criteria, addressing technical risks within organizational requirements rather than assuming post-sale architecture ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports USPSI opportunity decisions with technical discovery and proofs using approved evidence.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Provides USPSI technical advice on production architecture, validation, technical health, and cost optimization using approved evidence and organizational handling requirements. Diagnoses consumption gaps, recommends targeted interventions, and demonstrates technical progress and customer value without owning every consumption shortfall.
roles.descriptionSummary: Advises on USPSI production architecture, health, and optimization using approved evidence.

activities.name: Name the combined decision and preserve distinct owners
activities.description: Separate solution, technical, commercial, customer, and delivery decisions without pretending they progress independently.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. From the supplied opportunity decision context, criteria map, blockers, and actual coverage, identify the customer decision that would move the opportunity. Return a decision map limited to solution relevance and value, technical validation, commercial construct or concession, customer sponsorship or procurement, and partner or delivery readiness, with accountable humans, acceptance state, and critical path; do not transfer technical, commercial, or relationship ownership.
activities.expectedOutput: A decision map with customer decision, dependencies, accountable owners, acceptance state, and critical path.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns solution-area progression but cannot accept technical risk, make unauthorized concessions, or take over the customer relationship. Each accountable owner confirms their decision.
activities.requiredContext: One opportunity awaiting a customer decision; criteria map; current blockers; actual team and partner coverage.
activitySteps: 1. Start with the customer decision and date.
2. Name only dependencies that can change that decision.
3. Assign DSS, DSE, CE, account owner, partner, or delivery accountability as applicable.
4. Identify the critical dependency.
5. Confirm each owner's acceptance.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Combined progression works only when dependencies are connected and accountability is not blurred.

activities.name: Design proof and conversion together
activities.description: Define the minimum proof and the explicit customer and commercial conditions that turn evaluation into commitment.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Using the supplied customer decision, criteria, baseline, available evidence, owners, and proof context, prepare the minimum sufficient proof-and-conversion plan. Include hypothesis, customer success measure, scope, owner, milestone, evidence source, technical acceptance, decision meeting, commercial conversion condition, and stop condition, or recommend smaller evidence if a trial is unnecessary; preserve customer, technical, and commercial approvals.
activities.expectedOutput: A proof-and-conversion plan with measure, scope, owners, evidence, decision date, conversion condition, and stop condition.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether the proof advances the solution sale. DSE or the qualified technical owner approves technical acceptance; CE or the authorized commercial owner approves commercial conversion; the customer agrees the success measure.
activities.requiredContext: Customer decision; criteria map; baseline; available evidence; technical and commercial owners; trial, PoC, workshop, or proposal context.
activitySteps: 1. State the hypothesis and customer measure.
2. Choose the smallest proof proportionate to the risk.
3. Define technical acceptance with the qualified technical owner.
4. Define the decision meeting and conversion condition.
5. Agree the stop condition and record the plan.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A proof without agreed conversion criteria can succeed technically and still produce no customer decision.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A trial, PoC, workshop, or proposal is useful only if the team knows what decision follows and what evidence is enough.
keyTalkingPoints: DSS owns solution-area progression and customer relevance. DSE owns technical decision quality where engaged. CE owns commercial construct, concessions, and negotiation. The account owner retains the customer path. Define proof and conversion together; do not use technical activity to postpone a sponsorship, budget, or commercial decision.
discussionQuestions: What customer decision is waiting?
What is the minimum evidence proportionate to that decision?
What must be true for a trial or PoC to convert rather than simply end?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Name the combined decision and preserve distinct owners'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the proof plan to the customer commitment and CRM state that close the evaluation loop. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Close the loop from evidence to customer commitment', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Evaluation progress means evidence supports a customer decision and conversion condition, not another completed proof activity. Frontier Accelerator supports experimentation and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Where, if anywhere, could you adapt this judgment in your work?
preparationChecklist: Bring one opportunity in evaluation, trial, PoC, proposal, or negotiation and its current customer next step.
facilitatorQuestions: What exact decision is waiting?
What is the minimum proportionate proof?
Who owns solution, technical, commercial, and customer actions?
What converts the evaluation into commitment?
How has another DSS kept proof, commercial authority and the customer decision date connected?
listenFor: Technical work masking budget or sponsorship issues, PoCs without success or conversion criteria, DSS taking CE or DSE decisions, concessions made without authority, and proof completed without a customer decision date.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one proof-and-conversion card: waiting decision, minimum proof, success/conversion criteria, distinct solution/technical/commercial/customer owners and date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which activity were you treating as progress without knowing what decision it would produce?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check the evidence or owner agreement needed for the next evaluation decision and request clarification; keep unconfirmed commitments open. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized conversion condition checked and whether it focused proof or clarified ownership. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Support is not secured when an email is sent. It is secured when the route is eligible, accepted, owned, and moving through its required states.
keyTalkingPoints: Determine segment, workload, transaction route, MCEM stage, intended outcome, economics, and partner or supplier eligibility before selecting a vehicle. Prefer an appropriate scalable or zero-cost route before discretionary investment. Program rules, approvers, and systems vary; use current local guidance and do not assume ECIF is the default.
discussionQuestions: Which route is appropriate for this outcome and transaction?
Who can accept or approve it?
What state proves that delivery is ready rather than merely requested?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Establish the route and eligibility facts'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from route selection to its current state, next milestone, and escalation owner. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Track eligibility, approval, and delivery state', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Support and co-sell routes have distinct eligibility, acceptance and approval states. Requested help is not secured delivery or investment. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one opportunity needing a partner, program, funding vehicle, technical resource, or delivery service and any eligibility facts already known.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer and transaction facts determine eligibility?
Can a partner-led, assessment, Factory, FastTrack, voucher, incentive, or other approved route satisfy the scope?
What state and owner prove the route is moving?
What acceptance evidence has a peer required before treating a delivery route as moving?
listenFor: ECIF treated as generic deal cash, partner association mistaken for delivery commitment, an email mistaken for acceptance, route selection before eligibility, and work beginning before required approval.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one delivery-route fact base: scope, customer/transaction facts, current rule gap, route candidate, authorized validator and acceptance evidence needed. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where had you confused requesting support with securing it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify the next requirement or acceptance gap on a support route with its owner; record a confirmed next state or reason to hold. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized routing assumption checked and whether it reduced delay or prevented an ineligible route. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.description: Preserve the promised outcome through handoff to the people responsible for deployment, adoption, or consumption.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Compare [the evidenced customer commitment and success measure] with the delivery plan and coverage model. Return an activation plan with outcome, measure, accountable delivery and customer owners, partner role, prerequisites, milestone, evidence source, risk, handoff acceptance state, and DSS follow-through. Mark the handoff accepted only when supplied evidence records the receiving owner's confirmation; otherwise mark it pending and name the required confirmer. Keep technical validation and delivery accountability with their owners.

activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS preserves the solution promise and confirms the handoff. Delivery and technical owners accept their accountabilities; the DSS does not assume post-sale ownership where the coverage model assigns it elsewhere.
activities.requiredContext: Customer commitment; success measure; delivery plan; actual coverage model; partner role; deployment or adoption prerequisites.
activitySteps: 1. Restate the promised customer outcome and measure.
2. Identify the actual delivery and customer owners.
3. Confirm prerequisites, milestone, and evidence source.
4. Obtain handoff acceptance.
5. Record risks and the DSS follow-through point.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.

activities.name: Separate committed, deployed, active, adopted, and evidenced
activities.description: Classify solution state without treating deployment or product usage as proof of customer outcome.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Classify each entry in the supplied bounded set of deployments, approved telemetry, outcome measures, and delivery context as committed, deployed, active use, adopted in the intended process, customer outcome evidenced, or unknown. Return the evidence, gap, owner, and one account ready for outcome validation; treat cross-account patterns as hypotheses, not causation.
activities.expectedOutput: A state-and-evidence view with gaps, owners, and one account ready for outcome validation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides what counts as solution outcome evidence. Usage is not automatically adoption, adoption is not automatically business value, and cross-account correlation does not establish cause.
activities.requiredContext: A bounded set of committed or deployed accounts; approved telemetry; customer outcome measures; delivery and adoption context.
activitySteps: 1. Define the states for the solution area.
2. Review evidence without filling missing states.
3. Separate product telemetry from customer outcome measures.
4. Identify the most consequential gap and owner.
5. Treat cross-account differences as questions to investigate, not causal findings.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Precise state language prevents unsupported success claims and shows where activation work is needed.

5. Do not claim or circulate partner-led outcomes without authorization.

primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

activities.name: Select the same-account next opportunity from evidence
activities.description: Use evidenced outcomes, remaining gaps, and customer priorities to test the next solution-area opportunity.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. For the account identified in the supplied outcome/activation evidence, use supplied evidenced outcomes, activation gaps, stated priorities, installed base, and open opportunities to return at most three next-opportunity hypotheses. For each, show the customer problem, supporting and disconfirming evidence, likely owner, and first validation action; prefer no new opportunity over one based only on usage or seller ambition.
activities.expectedOutput: A bounded next-opportunity hypothesis with customer problem, evidence, disconfirming fact, owner, and validation action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether evidence supports another solution-area conversation. Usage alone does not authorize expansion, and an activation failure should not be relabeled as new pipeline.
activities.requiredContext: Verified customer outcome evidence; activation gaps; stated priorities; installed base; current opportunities; coverage model. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Start with customer evidence and priorities.
2. Distinguish an activation gap from a new opportunity.
3. Check existing opportunities and cross-solution ownership.
4. State a disconfirming fact for each hypothesis.
5. Validate one hypothesis before creating pipeline.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Evidence is most valuable when it improves the same customer's next decision without forcing an upsell.

activities.name: Build the renewal and contract-event action plan
activities.description: Connect contract timing, outcome evidence, risk, and solution-area expansion without taking over commercial renewal ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [dated renewal, contract-event and outcome evidence], draft a renewal/expansion action plan: event date, transaction context, outcome, usage, risks, bounded expansion hypothesis, distinct commercial/account owners, actions and review date. Flag facts needing confirmation; don’t assume CRM/calendar access or persistent memory, or recommend constructs/concessions. Keep any recurring review an unactivated proposal pending separate approval of scope, sources, cadence, recipients, access and expiry.
activities.expectedOutput: A renewal and expansion action plan with timing, evidence, risks, distinct owners, and review date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns the solution-area evidence and expansion recommendation. The Commercial Executive or authorized commercial owner owns commercial construct, concessions, and negotiation; the account owner owns the customer path.
activities.requiredContext: Contract or renewal calendar event; agreement and transaction context; outcome and usage evidence; risks; owners; current opportunities.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the contract or renewal event and owner.
2. Assemble outcome, usage, risk, and open-opportunity evidence.
3. Separate solution expansion from commercial renewal decisions.
4. Assign actions and dates to accepted owners.
5. Set the next evidence review before the customer decision window.

Access/fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Build the same dated action plan manually from supplied evidence; retaining a review date needs no scheduled job, connector or persistent agent memory. No scheduling, messages or record changes occur in this practice.
activities.whyThisMatters: Early calendar-driven action prevents renewal from becoming a late administrative event and keeps solution and commercial accountabilities clear.

activities.name: Reconcile the next opportunity, handoffs, CRM, and forecast
activities.description: Close the loop by making ownership and system state match the validated customer plan.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. Audit the opportunity identified in the supplied validated next-opportunity or renewal plan against its validated next-opportunity or renewal plan. Return discrepancies and evidence-backed proposed changes for duplication, lead solution area, owner acceptance, stage, next customer action and date, partner or delivery handoff, amount or usage basis, renewal dependency, and forecast treatment, naming the authorized human for each; do not resolve or write changes autonomously.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft CRM/forecast reconciliation ledger with supported proposed changes, supplied acceptance status, next customer action, renewal dependency and re-entry signal; no record change.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS is accountable for solution-area pipeline accuracy. Account, commercial, and forecast owners approve their respective decisions; an AI audit may find inconsistencies but cannot resolve them autonomously.
activities.requiredContext: Validated next-opportunity or renewal plan; current CRM and forecast; accepted owner and partner handoffs. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Compare the validated plan with the current record.
2. Propose create, update, merge or close only with supplied evidence; authorized owners decide and no source record changes in this practice.
3. Confirm every handoff was accepted.
4. Reconcile stage and forecast with authorized owners.
5. Record the next review and re-entry signal.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is a preview experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX; no separate installation or opt-in is required. Relevant data varies by role; Germany and Austria await Works Council approval. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. If relevant records are unavailable, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expansion is operational only when owners accept it and CRM and forecast tell the same evidence-backed story.

activities.name: Build an approved proof point after serving the same account
activities.description: Turn one evidenced outcome into a reusable proof point only after the customer's next action and ownership are secure.
activities.prompt: Use supplied material only. From the supplied verified outcome, evidence source, delivery ownership, and permission requirements, draft an anonymized proof point covering situation, action, evidenced measure, time frame, material context, and limits. Remove identifying detail and unsupported causation, list required account-owner, customer, delivery-owner, and partner approvals, and label the draft unapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: An anonymized, bounded proof-point draft with evidence citation, limitations, and approval state.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether the claim is useful and supportable. The customer and relevant delivery or partner owners control permission; anonymization is not permission and correlation is not causation.
activities.requiredContext: Verified customer outcome; evidence source; delivery owner; customer, account-owner, and partner permission requirements.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the outcome and evidence owner.
2. Prioritize the same customer's next action before external reuse.
3. Draft only the evidenced claim and necessary context.
4. Test whether the customer could recognize themselves.
5. Obtain every required approval before reuse.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Reusable evidence builds credibility only when it is accurate, bounded, and authorized by everyone whose work or data it represents.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The strongest evidence should first improve the same customer's next decision. Renewal, expansion, and reusable proof follow from that evidence and the contract calendar.
keyTalkingPoints: Use evidence to test a same-account next opportunity rather than force one. Keep renewal ownership distinct from solution-area expansion and commercial ownership. Reconcile CRM, stage, forecast, next step, and handoffs before closing the loop. External proof requires customer, account-owner, and where applicable partner permission.
discussionQuestions: What next customer problem does the evidence genuinely support?
Which contract event creates urgency?
Which record or handoff would currently surprise the next owner?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Select the same-account next opportunity from evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the expansion or renewal hypothesis to the accepted handoff and reconciled system-of-record state. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the renewal and contract-event action plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Renewal and expansion follow verified outcomes and contract timing, with records, forecast and accepted handoffs reflecting the human plan. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one evidenced outcome or one contract or renewal event within your operating horizon, plus its current opportunity and forecast state.
facilitatorQuestions: What next customer problem does the evidence support?
What contract or renewal event affects timing?
Who owns solution expansion, customer path, commercial renewal, and delivery?
What must change in CRM and forecast?
What evidence has a peer used to decide that same-account expansion is not yet supported?
listenFor: Expansion inferred from usage alone, a reusable case study prioritized before same-account value, renewal ownership blurred, handoffs sent but not accepted, and forecast state inconsistent with the customer action.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one next-opportunity hypothesis: same-account evidence, unsupported assumption, renewal event, accountable role and CRM/forecast reconciliation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Did the evidence support expansion, or were you trying to make it support expansion?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate an expansion or renewal hypothesis and agree the next evidence check; authorized humans control CRM or forecast changes. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized hypothesis revised, retained or rejected and whether it made the plan more realistic. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.
