PLC-SMEC-DSE-W05.roleTopicDescription: Reconcile proof and design evidence against the criteria, obtain an explicit accepted, conditional, or rejected decision, and communicate it in language that survives relay.
PLC-SMEC-DSE-W05.wiifm: Clear technical conclusions let customers and account teams act on what was actually established instead of repeating evaluations or mistaking a qualified result for unconditional success.
PLC-SMEC-DSE-W05.name: Discover, Shape, and Validate a Solution
PLC-SMEC-DSE-W05.description: Clarify the customer problem and decision criteria, shape an appropriate technical approach, validate it against evidence and constraints, and communicate what the proof does and does not establish.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
roles.description: Leads customer-backed technology strategy across relevant solution areas, translating readiness and business priorities into a technical roadmap and consumption plans. Aligns account, solution and customer-success teams around technical decisions and execution without assuming default implementation or commercial approval ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Leads customer technology strategy, readiness, technical roadmaps and consumption planning.

roles.name: Solution Engineer
roles.description: Supports the customer's technical decision through discovery, architecture options, demonstrations and appropriate technical proofs. Makes success criteria, actual findings, unresolved risks and handoff requirements clear, working with specialists and delivery teams without assuming all opportunity, forecast or production-delivery ownership.
roles.descriptionSummary: Supports technical decisions with architecture choices, proof evidence and clear delivery handoffs.

roles.name: Cloud Solution Architect
roles.description: Delivers technical architecture, implementation, adoption and operational-health outcomes within the assigned specialty and engagement. Validates workload blockers, completes agreed technical work and supports measurable customer value, coordinating success-plan inputs and follow-on opportunities without assuming ownership of every forecast, consumption shortfall or customer review.
roles.descriptionSummary: Delivers technical architecture, adoption, health and workload outcomes within assigned scope.

roles.name: Digital Solution Area Specialist
roles.description: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline starting with installed-base telemetry and contract events, supplemented by customer, partner, and marketing evidence. Shapes customer strategy and decision criteria, coordinates multiworkload routing and proof, and connects conversion, delivery, activation, renewal, and expansion.
roles.descriptionSummary: Develops SME&C solution-area pipeline from installed-base evidence through conversion and expansion.

roles.name: Digital Solution Engineer
roles.description: Consolidates existing SME&C discovery from account, specialist, partner, and customer inputs, validating decision criteria and gaps. Shapes viable architecture with delivery owners, runs the smallest useful proof, transfers technical decisions into delivery, reuses assets, and addresses partner technical capability gaps.
roles.descriptionSummary: Validates SME&C discovery, shapes architecture, runs proofs, and transfers decisions into delivery.

roles.name: PTS
roles.description: Shapes cross-solution partner technical direction through multi-horizon roadmaps and Build-to-Consume priorities. Guides offering innovation, establishes technical guardrails, and coordinates handoffs for scoped architecture and execution, inspecting plan progress and applying reusable learning without assuming ownership of partner business strategy or engineering delivery.
roles.descriptionSummary: Shapes EPS cross-solution partner technical strategy, roadmaps, and guardrails for scoped handoffs.

roles.name: PSA

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on converting technical work into a decision rather than another technical conversation.
keyTalkingPoints: Use relayed communication only when direct customer access is unavailable; preserve qualifications and identify the person authorized to accept.
Current execution: Use the technical decision record, customer review, and accepted evidence.
Fallback: Run a live decision review and capture explicit acceptance when no workflow exists.
System of record: The technical decision record is authoritative for the recommendation and acceptance.
Optional AI boundary: An approved assistant may format DSE-authored conclusions; it must not soften qualifications or mark acceptance.
discussionQuestions: Does the evidence meet the agreed criterion?
What qualification must travel with the recommendation?
Who is authorized to accept the technical decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Evaluate every agreed criterion'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Record acceptance and relay-safe summary', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical closure preserves criterion results, alternatives and residual risk. Sign-off exists only after actual authorized acceptance. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one technical criterion, approved proof/architecture results, recommendation qualifications and the accepting customer or delivery owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which agreed criterion is supported, contradicted or still untested? What residual risk limits the recommendation? How would a peer communicate a technical hold without claiming customer acceptance?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical criterion review: agreed criterion, supported/contradicted/untested evidence, residual risk, conditional recommendation and acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which result or residual risk changed proceed, revise or hold?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review a deciding criterion or risk with the technical owner and record their actual proceed, revise or hold; sign-off is not an exercise quota. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized decision clarification and whether it improved confidence or made the hold explicit. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on turning one committed milestone into an executable plan rather than redesign the pre-sale architecture.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies after an accepted technical decision. DCSA re-engages DSE only when a material design assumption changes or a defined trigger is met.
Current execution: Use accepted technical decision, delivery plan, route-specific readiness criteria, and committed milestone record.
Fallback: Run a readiness review with the named implementer and record unclosed prerequisites if no workflow exists.
System of record: Committed-milestone/consumption record for readiness; accepted design repository for technical intent.
Optional AI boundary: AI may check supplied plans for missing dependencies; it cannot redesign, certify partner capability, or declare readiness.
discussionQuestions: Which prerequisite could block the milestone before start?
What has the implementer confirmed?
What design change would require technical re-engagement?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Trace the milestone to accepted technical intent'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Define completion and escalation evidence', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Committed milestones become ready through prerequisite evidence, sequencing and accepted ownership. Labels cannot close dependencies. If a relevant case arises, you could adapt this approach and decide whether to compare what helped or failed with peers.
preparationChecklist: Bring one accepted intake, committed milestone, approved delivery plan, readiness criteria and open prerequisites with their owners. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Can the committed milestone be traced to accepted technical intent? Which prerequisite or owner still prevents delivery readiness? How does another DCSA define completion and escalation evidence before work starts?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one milestone readiness row: accepted technical intent, unclosed prerequisite, implementer, completion evidence and escalation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which prerequisite looked closed until the implementation owner supplied evidence?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check the deciding prerequisite with its owner and agree validation or hold; do not declare full readiness from an AI draft. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized prerequisite confirmed or reopened and whether it made timing more credible. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on turning partner cadence into a deal decision rather than a status meeting.
keyTalkingPoints: Use for a selected material partner deal; routine cadence without a decision remains outside this practice.
Current execution: Use reconciled pipeline evidence, partner input, and named DAE/DSS/DSE/CE/PDM/PSA/program owners as applicable.
Fallback: Run a short live clinic and manually record decision/acceptance if no shared workflow exists.
System of record: MSX for Microsoft opportunity actions; Partner Center/partner record for partner actions; authoritative systems for specialist decisions.
Optional AI boundary: Agent J.ai may help rehearse the partner conversation where available; it cannot identify the true blocker or assign ownership.
discussionQuestions: What decision would unblock this deal?
Which role can actually make it?
What acceptance or next evidence will show the clinic produced more than status?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Select the blocker worth clinic time'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test whether the deal moved', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Deal clinics resolve specific evidenced blockers through reciprocal accepted actions, not broader action-register production. If this fits your work, you could adapt the useful step and choose whether to share a permission-safe lesson; no new habit or report is expected.
preparationChecklist: Bring one stalled partner deal, reconciled pipeline evidence, partner comments, the blocked decision and known specialist/program owners. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which single partner-deal blocker is worth clinic time? Who can decide it and what evidence do they need? How does a peer distinguish an accepted action from a discussion that changed nothing?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one clinic decision card: single blocker, decision evidence, accountable role, proposed action, acceptance gap and next movement check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed when partner and Microsoft actions were made explicit?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could review the deciding partner-deal gap and seek owner acceptance of a bounded action or explicit hold. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized blocker clarified and whether it improved reciprocal follow-through. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: Draft a monitoring proposal; don’t activate it. Use only the dated snapshots, baseline and previous report I supply; don’t set up monitoring. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on preventing partner-assisted closure from becoming an invisible delivery and value gap.
keyTalkingPoints: Use where a partner will transact or deliver. DCSA/PSM/other Microsoft coverage applies only when eligibility and assignment are confirmed.
Current execution: Use MSX, Partner Center, accepted technical/commercial decisions, and the partner's deployment plan.
Fallback: Conduct a live partner handoff and record accepted owners and evidence when no integrated route exists.
System of record: Partner system for partner delivery plan; MSX for Microsoft opportunity/closure and accepted Microsoft handoff.
Optional AI boundary: AI may format supplied handoff material but must not claim partner acceptance or disclose restricted customer information.
discussionQuestions: Who has accepted deployment ownership?
What technical/commercial condition must travel with the deal?
What evidence will reveal a delivery or value gap?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Confirm an executable partner deployment plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Set the post-close evidence loop', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Closed partner deals still need accepted delivery ownership, technical inputs and an evidence checkpoint. Sales closure is not deployment completion. If useful, you could try a small test of better work and choose whether to share a benefit or correction rather than just a draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one partner-assisted committed deal, accepted technical/commercial decisions, the partner deployment plan and named receiving owners. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What makes the post-close partner deployment plan executable? Which route-specific owner has actually accepted it? How does a peer keep transaction closure separate from deployment and outcome evidence?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one post-close deployment handoff: plan prerequisite, route-specific owner, acceptance evidence or unknown and post-close outcome check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which delivery input was not settled by closing the deal?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check a deciding post-close input with the partner delivery owner and seek acceptance or the precise missing condition. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share an anonymized gap clarified and whether it improved continuity or exposed a pending handoff. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on changing partner behavior using evidence and the partner's stated priorities, not invented economics.
keyTalkingPoints: Use for selected partners in PSS scope; do not present PSS as the sole Microsoft route to post-sale outcomes.
Current execution: Use MSX, Partner Center/Timeline, program records, partner-reported outcomes, and current joint plan.
Fallback: Build a dated review from the available sources and label partner-reported versus Microsoft-observed evidence.
System of record: Each system remains authoritative for its own record; accepted actions return to MSX/Partner Center/joint plan as applicable.
Optional AI boundary: Know Your Partner may assemble permitted context. PSS must not invent margin, capacity, or customer outcomes.
discussionQuestions: What partner behavior should change and why?
Which outcome is observed versus partner-reported?
What accepted action supports the stated partner priorities?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile plan, pipeline, program, and delivery evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Agree the next loop and expansion route', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Partner review compares source-attributed outcomes with plan and forecast, then tests expansion rather than equating activity with value. Where, if anywhere, could this fit in recurring work, and what small, safe signal might help you explore its value?
preparationChecklist: Bring one partner review, approved joint-plan priorities, dated pipeline/outcome evidence and the prior accepted actions. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Where do plan, pipeline, program and delivery sources disagree? What partner priority should the review resolve? How does another PSS record the next reciprocal action without inventing agreement or taking the broader partner strategy?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one partner-review exception: plan/pipeline/program/delivery evidence, source conflict, partner priority, reciprocal next action and owner acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which variance changed the partner action or expansion hypothesis?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate a material variance with its source owner and agree your own follow-up plus separately accepted partner action; expansion may stay on hold. If you choose Microsoft 365 Copilot, use it only for permitted drafting or analysis; manual exploration is also a choice. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, you could explore a sanitized example or leave the gap open. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: You may share a sanitized variance checked and whether it improved the review or next action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, you could share a question or gap, or leave it open; no follow-up is required.

activities.prompt: For [Account Name or TPID] or Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], summarize the recorded outcome, priority evidence, owner and next decision for [Customer Plan priority under review]. Name conflicting or missing evidence and one question for the accountable role. Do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance or funding approval, or change records. activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one Customer Plan priority with customer outcome, supporting signal, owner, evidence gap and next decision; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.

activities.prompt: Using only [customer outcome/priority evidence and source references] for [customer/account], draft a Customer Plan priority packet linking each outcome to supporting signals, current priorities, role contributions, recorded owners and the next open decision. Separate customer-confirmed outcomes from assumptions and show missing evidence, owner acceptance and validation questions against known decision criteria. Do not infer agreement from plan entries or change the plan or ownership. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Customer Plan priority packet linking outcomes, priorities, evidence, role contributions, ownership/acceptance gaps and next decisions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Customer/account; customer outcome/priority evidence and source references. Existing Customer Plan context is optional; no new plan is required. Known decision criteria and role/ownership evidence where available.

ATS: Add estate, technical strategy, workload readiness, and risk context. activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one Customer Plan priority with customer outcome, supporting signal, owner, evidence gap and next decision; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public sources to inform customer-plan outcomes, priorities, ownership questions and evidence gaps. Use geographic or time limits only where material to the question. Cite material factual claims with source dates; separate fact, inference and proposed implications, flagging relevant conflicts or stale evidence. Return a focused brief and questions for the plan owner. Public evidence can inform a priority but cannot establish private account plans, accepted owners or commitments. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public research brief informing customer-plan priorities and ownership/evidence questions; it does not establish private plans, accepted owners or commitments.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Own customer outcomes, account priorities, and the actionable Customer Plan. ATS: Add estate, technical strategy, workload readiness, and risk context. Required contribution/role-modeling gap to validate: IA (not currently modeled): Bring business transformation and industry context; role is not represented in the current app. Conditional only where applicable: SAE (Services Sales; active Enterprise pilot role): Add solution-area coverage and execution dependencies; the SAE role is modeled in the workbook under Enterprise > Services Sales for pilot feedback; app availability depends on import.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one Customer Plan priority with customer outcome, supporting signal, owner, evidence gap and next decision; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one Customer Plan priority with customer outcome, supporting signal, owner, evidence gap and next decision. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shorter, decision-led Customer Plan helps the AE focus account effort while making technical and industry disagreements visible before work is assigned. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The team has broad account data but no shared view of the outcomes and work that deserve attention. A shorter, decision-led Customer Plan helps the AE focus account effort while making technical and industry disagreements visible before work is assigned.
keyTalkingPoints: Compare customer outcomes with current account priorities, then challenge one priority rather than polishing the whole plan. AE owns the plan; ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness. Industry expertise may be needed; Services Sales contribution remains conditional.
Use an existing account-team meeting; inspect decisions, not document completeness.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: Which customer outcomes should govern this plan?
Where do business priority and technical readiness disagree?
What will the team stop, start, or escalate?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the account signals to one plan trade-off. Compare peer reasoning, then identify the AE decision, evidence gap, next owner and review point that belong in the one-page plan.

A source Featured starting option is 'Inspect customer-plan outcomes, priorities, owners, and evidence gaps' (atu-w2-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Inputs to Frontier Discovery and named owners in authoritative systems.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Customer planning -> Frontier Transformation/discovery
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move from the account signals to one plan trade-off. Compare peer reasoning, then identify the AE decision, evidence gap, next owner and review point that belong in the one-page plan. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which priority would change if we gave the customer outcome more weight than our current pipeline inventory? Where do industry opportunity and technical readiness pull in different directions?
What does another role or peer notice about one Customer Plan priority with customer outcome, supporting signal, owner, evidence gap and next decision that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Customer outcomes linked to specific choices; evidence versus aspiration; AE ownership; missing industry input; a stop/defer decision rather than a longer list.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without the needed customer or technical context, outline the plan decision and evidence request on paper. Do not invent industry facts or give the manager account-plan ownership. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which peer perspective changed your account priority, and which assumption must be checked before the AE changes the plan?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could choose one outcome/priority decision to check with the AE, or close one named evidence gap; state who reviews it before the authoritative plan is updated. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share a permission-safe verbal account of one priority changed, deferred or retained, its evidence and next review point; an unresolved gap is valid evidence of what remains. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Customer Plan priority looks valuable commercially but has an unresolved technical readiness gap. Compare AE and ATS evidence before changing the proposed next action.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Shared account planning brings AE priorities and ATS readiness evidence together around the next customer decision. AE owns the Customer Plan, ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness, and conditional contributions remain conditional; ATU cannot accept on STU's behalf. Industry expertise and Services Sales input remain conditional; do not assume those contributors are available.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the Customer Plan priority, intended outcome and evidence source in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Peer discussion does not transfer the AE's account-plan ownership to another contributor. Look for a priority challenged by evidence without creating a parallel account plan. Peer participation does not establish a broader manager forecast remit, a new meeting schedule or permission to run automation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: AE plan ownership is not transferred to ATU peers or an unmodeled role. Confirm who can explain the ATU customer-plan and opportunity decisions boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.

activitySteps: 1. activities.name: Structure outcome-led discovery, assumptions, and the candidate use case
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved discovery notes and candidate use-case evidence], draft an outcome-led discovery packet: customer problem/outcome in sourced wording, what is confirmed, candidate use-case assumptions, evidence for/against fit and questions that would settle the next discovery decision. Preserve recorded owners and identify confirmation gaps; use known decision criteria without inventing customer intent or agreement. Do not approve a use case, assign pursuit work or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: Discovery packet with sourced customer problem/outcome, confirmed evidence, candidate assumptions, fit gaps and questions for the next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.

facilitatorQuestions: What did the customer actually confirm, and what are we inferring? Which discovery answer would make us change or abandon the candidate workflow?

You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one statement confirmed, corrected or still open, with the question that changed it; no transcript or customer-sensitive detail is required in the huddle. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.

AE owns the Customer Plan, ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness, and conditional contributions remain conditional; ATU cannot accept on STU's behalf. Industry expertise and Services Sales input remain conditional; do not assume those contributors are available.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand which parts of the discovery statement are confirmed and which remain assumptions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: An internal use-case hypothesis is not customer-confirmed intent. Look for a question that can change the problem or outcome statement. activities.name: Structure use-case impact, readiness, safeguards, and bounded-test criteria
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved candidate use-case impact, readiness and safeguard evidence], draft a bounded-test decision packet. Compare supported impact with evidenced readiness, prerequisites, safeguards and known test/exit criteria; show unknown readiness, capacity, owners and approvals explicitly. Identify the evidence and accountable role needed for the next test decision. Do not turn potential impact into readiness, authorize the test or create commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: Bounded-test decision packet separating supported impact, readiness evidence, safeguards, prerequisites, unknowns and human decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Candidate use case; approved impact/readiness/safeguard evidence; known bounded-test/exit criteria and prerequisite/owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Keep the use case tied to customer outcome and accountable sponsorship. ATS: Assess technical readiness, dependencies, architecture implications, and evidence gaps. Required contribution/role-modeling gap to validate: IA (not currently modeled): Test workflow change, user value, and business readiness; role is not represented in the current app. Conditional only where applicable: SAE (Services Sales; active Enterprise pilot role): Add solution-area feasibility and route-to-specialist context; the SAE role is modeled in the workbook under Enterprise > Services Sales for pilot feedback; app availability depends on import.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one candidate workflow's impact/readiness comparison, safeguards and bounded validation question; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one candidate workflow's impact/readiness comparison, safeguards and bounded validation question. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A use case is only worth routing when its outcome, readiness, owner and safeguards are clear enough to justify the next bounded evidence check. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Prepare the Conversation routing brief and evidence gaps
activities.description: Turn approved ATU working material into a clear handoff request without claiming receiving-owner acceptance.
activities.prompt: Using [the approved ATU discovery/readiness artifacts and receiving criteria], prepare a concise Conversation routing brief with the customer decision to advance, evidence, assumptions, gaps, ATU owners, recommended route, and requested next action. Separate verified evidence from hypotheses and name what the receiving owner must validate. Do not accept the handoff, assign STU ownership, schedule a customer interaction, or make technical, commercial, or system decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: A routing brief ready for receiving-owner review, not an accepted handoff.
activities.humanCheckpoint: ATU role owners approve the brief; the receiving STU owner later accepts, redirects, or returns it.
activities.requiredContext: Approved ATU discovery and readiness artifacts plus known receiving criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Clarify the customer decision, stakeholders, and business outcome. ATS: Package technical context, readiness, and the recommended Conversation route. Required contribution/role-modeling gap to validate: IA (not currently modeled): Preserve the business transformation intent; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Keep this an ATU review request; do not assign STU ownership, schedule the customer interaction or claim acceptance.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A precise routing request lets STU assess the next customer decision without reconstructing discovery, while keeping ATU preparation separate from receiving-owner acceptance. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Inspect sales context supporting the Conversation route
activities.description: Retrieve bounded account and opportunity facts that support the ATU routing discussion.
activities.prompt: For Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], prepare the sales-context strip for [customer decision and Conversation-routing question]: opportunity state, recorded owners, next action and known commitments. Cite records and as-of dates; separate verified facts from missing customer or technical evidence and give the owner-confirmation question. Do not infer technical readiness, choose the Conversation route, assign a receiving owner, accept a handoff or change records. If inaccessible, report the gap.
activities.expectedOutput: A bounded sales-context strip for the ATU routing decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity ID and relevant authorized sales context, or a permitted dated extract identifying that opportunity.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Clarify the customer decision, stakeholders, and business outcome. ATS: Package technical context, readiness, and the recommended Conversation route. Required contribution/role-modeling gap to validate: IA (not currently modeled): Preserve the business transformation intent; role is not represented in the current app. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Retrieve only bounded sales context; ATU humans select the route and the receiving STU owner later decides disposition.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A precise routing request lets STU assess the next customer decision without reconstructing discovery, while keeping ATU preparation separate from receiving-owner acceptance. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

activities.name: Rehearse the ATU routing and handoff conversation
activities.description: Practice explaining the route and evidence gaps without turning simulation into acceptance.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearse an ATU alignment and handoff conversation using [the fictional/de-identified routing brief, receiving role and conversation objective]. Simulate likely questions about the customer decision, evidence gaps, ownership, and next action. Return a rehearsal transcript, critique, and improved questions. Label every simulated response as role-play, not evidence, acceptance, authorization, or commitment. Do not assign the receiving role or claim the handoff has landed.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal and refined handoff questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: An approved routing brief, receiving role, and conversation objective.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Clarify the customer decision, stakeholders, and business outcome. ATS: Package technical context, readiness, and the recommended Conversation route. Required contribution/role-modeling gap to validate: IA (not currently modeled): Preserve the business transformation intent; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Rehearse the handoff explanation without assigning the receiver or claiming that the request has landed.
6. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A precise routing request lets STU assess the next customer decision without reconstructing discovery, while keeping ATU preparation separate from receiving-owner acceptance. A labeled rehearsal can expose unclear questions before a real interaction without masquerading as customer evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Discovery and readiness evidence exist, but the team has not agreed which customer Conversation should happen or who should accept it. A precise routing request lets STU assess the next customer decision without reconstructing discovery, while keeping ATU preparation separate from receiving-owner acceptance.
keyTalkingPoints: Use approved discovery/readiness material to agree the recommended Conversation route. AE supplies business outcome and customer decision; ATS packages technical context; preserve IA transformation intent. This huddle stays within ATU; STU review happens separately.
Keep the huddle within ATU. Validate the receiving criteria asynchronously; do not require STU roles to attend.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What customer decision must the Conversation advance?
Is the evidence sufficient for STU to accept the route?
Who owns preparation and the next customer interaction?
suggestedTransitions: Compare two ways to explain the route, then select the clearest sending-side brief. Confirm what ATU approves and what only the later STU receiving owner can accept, redirect or return.

A source Featured starting option is 'Prepare the Conversation routing brief and evidence gaps' (atu-w5-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: ATU sends the routing brief to the receiving STU owner, who accepts, redirects, or returns it outside this huddle.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Discovery/readiness -> Conversation
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare two ways to explain the route, then select the clearest sending-side brief. Confirm what ATU approves and what only the later STU receiving owner can accept, redirect or return. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What exactly are we asking the receiving STU owner to assess? Which evidence supports the route and which receiving criterion remains unknown?
What does another role or peer notice about one ATU Conversation routing request with decision ask, evidence gaps, sending owners and requested next action that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A clear customer decision, evidence gaps, ATU sending owner and requested next action; an unaccepted receiver being assigned ownership or a rehearsal being called a landed handoff.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: No STU attendance is required. If receiving criteria or owner are not confirmed, label the review request and unknowns; do not invent a receiver, schedule a customer interaction or declare acceptance. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What would a receiver still have to reconstruct from our brief, and what can ATU clarify before sending it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could have the ATU owners review one routing brief or close one evidence gap, then send an explicit review request through the existing handoff route. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share a brief account of what ATU sent, what remained uncertain and any actual STU disposition received later; do not count preparation as acceptance. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: ATU has discovery evidence but its Conversation request does not state the next customer decision. Prepare the ask and keep STU receiving-owner acceptance separate.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Conversation routing makes the customer decision, supporting evidence and sending-side request clear to a possible STU receiver. AE owns the Customer Plan, ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness, and conditional contributions remain conditional; ATU cannot accept on STU's behalf. Industry expertise and Services Sales input remain conditional; do not assume those contributors are available.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the ATU routing brief, decision ask and evidence gap in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: ATU preparation is not STU receiving-owner acceptance. Look for a precise sending-side request with known owners and unresolved context. Peer participation does not establish a broader manager forecast remit, a new meeting schedule or permission to run automation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: ATU preparation is not STU receiving-owner acceptance. Confirm who can explain the ATU customer-plan and opportunity decisions boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Inspect pipeline and forecast exceptions, evidence changes, and owner corrections
activities.description: Ground the team discussion in authorized sales-system context without asking people to paste retrievable records.
activities.prompt: For Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], inspect [pipeline or forecast exception under review]. Show the dated record position, evidence that changed or conflicts, and the supported correction or decision question for the accountable owner. Separate facts from assumptions and unverified customer commitments; cite record references and flag missing access or evidence. Propose only: do not update forecast, stage, value or dates, or approve a correction.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for pipeline and forecast exceptions, evidence changes, and owner corrections, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity ID and relevant authorized sales context, or a permitted dated extract identifying that opportunity.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Own opportunity health, stage evidence, close timing, and forecast position. ATS: Surface technical readiness, account-strategy, and dependency evidence. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one pipeline/forecast exception with changed evidence, defensible correction, rationale and human action owner; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one pipeline/forecast exception with changed evidence, defensible correction, rationale and human action owner. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Inspecting changed evidence helps the AE correct opportunity and forecast records instead of defending dates or stages that no longer reflect the customer situation. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

activities.name: Monitor pipeline and forecast exceptions, evidence changes, and owner corrections
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of pipeline and forecast exceptions, evidence changes, and owner corrections, use [paste/attach the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Confirm recipient access and least privilege. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Own opportunity health, stage evidence, close timing, and forecast position. ATS: Surface technical readiness, account-strategy, and dependency evidence. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one pipeline/forecast exception with changed evidence, defensible correction, rationale and human action owner, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one pipeline/forecast exception with changed evidence, defensible correction, rationale and human action owner. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.

activities.name: Structure pipeline and forecast exceptions, evidence changes, and owner corrections
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved pipeline/forecast exception evidence, prior/current position and source dates], draft an exception packet for the identified account or portfolio. Show changed evidence, recorded position, contradictions, assumptions and the owner correction or further check each exception needs. Use known inspection criteria; preserve recorded versus accepted ownership and proposed correction status. Do not infer progress from record modification, decide forecast commitments or update pipeline/forecast records.
activities.expectedOutput: Pipeline/forecast exception packet with evidence changes, contradictions, proposed owner corrections and required checks; no forecast decision or record update.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Pipeline and forecast records no longer agree with current customer, technical, or seller evidence. Inspecting changed evidence helps the AE correct opportunity and forecast records instead of defending dates or stages that no longer reflect the customer situation.
keyTalkingPoints: Choose one consequential pipeline/forecast exception in the existing rhythm, not a new local report. AE owns opportunity health, stage evidence, close timing and forecast position; ATS contributes readiness and dependency evidence. Managers coach and inspect rather than acquiring a new forecast charter.
Use the existing pipeline or forecast rhythm and discuss exceptions, not a new local report.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What changed in the customer or opportunity evidence?
Which record, stage, date, or risk statement is no longer defensible?
Who owns each correction or follow-up?
suggestedTransitions: Move from exception to supporting evidence, compare peer interpretations, then make a correction list with rationale and named human owners. Only accountable owners update authoritative records.

A source Featured starting option is 'Inspect pipeline and forecast exceptions, evidence changes, and owner corrections' (atu-w6-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Evidence-backed opportunities and risks into commitment decisions.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Qualification and progression -> commitment readiness
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move from exception to supporting evidence, compare peer interpretations, then make a correction list with rationale and named human owners. Only accountable owners update authoritative records. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer or technical fact changed, and which field or risk statement can we no longer defend? Does the source actually establish the correction we propose?
What does another role or peer notice about one pipeline/forecast exception with changed evidence, defensible correction, rationale and human action owner that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Dated changes, source scope, conflict between records and evidence, accountable AE corrections; stale snapshots, unverified causal explanations or automated record writes.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If records are inaccessible or stale, state the evidence gap and owner. Do not estimate the forecast or treat a monitoring draft as a verified current record. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which correction is now defensible, and which still rests on an assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify one exception and ask the accountable owner to make the warranted correction, or request the exact missing evidence before any update. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one checked exception, the owner-validated correction or reason it remained open, and the source/as-of limitation. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A pipeline stage remains unchanged after new evidence undermines the stated next step. Inspect one exception and route a supported correction to the human record owner.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Shared pipeline and forecast review challenges a recorded position with changed evidence while retaining human record ownership. AE owns the Customer Plan, ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness, and conditional contributions remain conditional; ATU cannot accept on STU's behalf. Industry expertise and Services Sales input remain conditional; do not assume those contributors are available.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the exception, changed evidence and record owner in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Inspection cannot let AI set the forecast or assume a correction occurred. Look for a defensible correction question with human ownership and uncertainty visible. Peer participation does not establish a broader manager forecast remit, a new meeting schedule or permission to run automation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: inspection cannot let AI set the forecast or assume a correction occurred. Confirm who can explain the ATU customer-plan and opportunity decisions boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Inspect opportunity evidence and the conditional technical or commercial commitment path
activities.description: Ground the team discussion in authorized sales-system context without asking people to paste retrievable records.
activities.prompt: For Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], summarize sales evidence for [customer commitment decision]: customer outcome, recorded commitments, technical/commercial conditions, owner roles and next action. Cite source/date and distinguish confirmed facts from proposals, missing proof and unverified approval. Name the evidence question for each material condition and its accountable role. Do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance or approval from stage, or make commitments or record changes.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for opportunity evidence and the conditional technical or commercial commitment path, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity ID and relevant authorized sales context, or a permitted dated extract identifying that opportunity.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Own opportunity health, customer decision, and overall commitment path. ATS: Connect technical strategy, readiness, and unresolved risk to the decision. Conditional only where applicable: CE: Join only when commercial structure, policy, negotiation, or approval work is required. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one commitment map linking customer decision, supporting evidence, technical/commercial conditions and authorized decision owners; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one commitment map linking customer decision, supporting evidence, technical/commercial conditions and authorized decision owners. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: An explicit commitment map exposes technical, customer and commercial conditions before they become an unsupported promise. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.
