activities.name: Structure opportunity evidence and the conditional technical or commercial commitment path
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved opportunity evidence and the proposed technical/commercial commitment path], draft a conditional-commitment packet: next customer decision, supporting proof, unmet conditions, dependencies, approval/authority gaps and the recorded owner or role needed to confirm each. Separate selected direction, technical validation, authorized commercial terms and actual customer commitments. Preserve known conditions/dates and mark proposals or acceptance gaps. Do not approve terms, declare a technical win or commit/update the opportunity.
activities.expectedOutput: Conditional-commitment packet distinguishing evidence, technical/commercial conditions, authority, acceptance gaps and next human decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved opportunity evidence; conditional technical/commercial commitment path; known decision criteria, conditions, approval records and owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Own opportunity health, customer decision, and overall commitment path. ATS: Connect technical strategy, readiness, and unresolved risk to the decision. Conditional only where applicable: CE: Join only when commercial structure, policy, negotiation, or approval work is required.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one commitment map linking customer decision, supporting evidence, technical/commercial conditions and authorized decision owners; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one commitment map linking customer decision, supporting evidence, technical/commercial conditions and authorized decision owners. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A customer decision is forming, but opportunity evidence, technical commitment, commercial needs, and approvals are not aligned. An explicit commitment map exposes technical, customer and commercial conditions before they become an unsupported promise.
keyTalkingPoints: Work back from the next customer decision, not a preferred deal structure. AE owns opportunity health and the overall commitment path; ATS exposes technical risk. CE is conditional only when commercial structure, policy, negotiation or approval work is required.
Make CE participation conditional and record why it is needed; avoid a universal role sequence.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What evidence supports the next commitment?
Which technical or commercial condition could block it?
Is CE involvement required now, later, or not at all?
suggestedTransitions: Compare the evidence for the next decision with the conditions that could stop it. Name the human owner for each unresolved condition and keep the technical/commercial path explicitly conditional.

A source Featured starting option is 'Inspect opportunity evidence and the conditional technical or commercial commitment path' (atu-w7-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Executable actions to STU, CE if required, and delivery planning.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Conversation/design -> technical and commercial commitment
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare the evidence for the next decision with the conditions that could stop it. Name the human owner for each unresolved condition and keep the technical/commercial path explicitly conditional. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which condition could block the next commitment? What can AE/ATS resolve, and which commercial or policy question must go to an authorized owner?

What does another role or peer notice about one commitment map linking customer decision, supporting evidence, technical/commercial conditions and authorized decision owners that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Evidence-backed next decision, unresolved technical/commercial dependencies, conditional CE involvement and approval boundaries; a proposed path being treated as approval.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the appropriate commercial or approval owner is absent, capture the question and route it. Do not interpret policy/licensing or promise terms, pricing or commitment dates. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which condition changed the path you would propose, and where did peer input expose an authority boundary?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could resolve one condition with the accountable owner or prepare one decision-ready question; do not commit on behalf of another role. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one condition checked, resulting decision or open approval request, and why CE was or was not needed. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A proposed customer commitment depends on an unresolved technical condition and possible commercial approval. Expose the conditions without authorizing the commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: An opportunity's commitment path depends on customer evidence and unresolved technical or commercial conditions. AE owns the Customer Plan, ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness, and conditional contributions remain conditional; ATU cannot accept on STU's behalf. Industry expertise and Services Sales input remain conditional; do not assume those contributors are available.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the proposed path and its technical and commercial conditions in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A populated opportunity stage does not establish customer commitment. Look for a decision with known evidence, conditions and authorized owners. Peer participation does not establish a broader manager forecast remit, a new meeting schedule or permission to run automation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a populated opportunity stage does not establish customer commitment. Confirm who can explain the ATU customer-plan and opportunity decisions boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Research value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the Customer Plan
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public sources to inform value/health review and possible expansion feedback into the Customer Plan. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material factual claims with source dates; separate facts, inference and proposed implications, flagging relevant conflicts or stale evidence. Return a focused brief and questions for the plan owner. External findings can frame a value or expansion hypothesis, not confirm realized account value, customer health, demand or an agreed plan change. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public evidence brief informing value/health review and possible expansion questions for the Customer Plan; account value, health, demand and plan agreement remain unverified by public research.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Use value and health evidence to update customer outcomes, sponsorship, renewal, and expansion actions. ATS: Connect technical progress and remaining constraints to the account strategy.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Closing the value and health loop changes account decisions rather than adding a separate scorecard or turning optimism into expansion. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

activities.name: Structure value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the Customer Plan
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [approved value/health evidence, expansion hypotheses and current Customer Plan context], draft feedback for the plan: evidenced outcome/health changes, unresolved risks, supported expansion questions and the next decision. Tie each proposed feedback item to its source and customer priority; distinguish analysis from customer-recognized value or agreed expansion. Preserve recorded owners and identify who must validate or accept the feedback. Do not edit the plan, create pipeline or infer customer intent.
activities.expectedOutput: Customer Plan feedback packet with evidenced value/health changes, expansion hypotheses, validation/acceptance gaps and next decisions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved value/health evidence; expansion hypotheses where supported; current Customer Plan and known decision/owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Use value and health evidence to update customer outcomes, sponsorship, renewal, and expansion actions. ATS: Connect technical progress and remaining constraints to the account strategy.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Closing the value and health loop changes account decisions rather than adding a separate scorecard or turning optimism into expansion. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Monitor value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the Customer Plan
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the customer plan, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. AE: Use value and health evidence to update customer outcomes, sponsorship, renewal, and expansion actions. ATS: Connect technical progress and remaining constraints to the account strategy. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Closing the value and health loop changes account decisions rather than adding a separate scorecard or turning optimism into expansion. Governed change review can expose what moved between observations without delegating judgment to unattended work.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Delivery and usage signals exist, but the Customer Plan is not consistently refreshed with health, value, and expansion evidence. Closing the value and health loop changes account decisions rather than adding a separate scorecard or turning optimism into expansion.
keyTalkingPoints: Bring delivery, usage and customer-value evidence back to the Customer Plan. AE owns the plan change; ATS connects technical progress and constraints. Separate customer-recognized value from internal activity, and evidence-backed expansion from a hypothesis.
Close the loop into the Customer Plan rather than adding a separate scorecard.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What value can the customer recognize and verify?
What health or adoption signal changes the plan?
What expansion hypothesis is evidence-backed rather than optimistic?
suggestedTransitions: Compare value claims with the available evidence, then select a plan change, intervention or expansion question. Feed the decision into existing planning/discovery/renewal work rather than a new reporting motion.

A source Featured starting option is 'Research value, health, and evidence-backed expansion feedback into the Customer Plan' (atu-w8-p2); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Feedback to planning, discovery, renewal, and the next team cycle.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Value realization -> health/expansion feedback
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare value claims with the available evidence, then select a plan change, intervention or expansion question. If useful, you could carry this question into existing planning/discovery/renewal work rather than create a new reporting motion. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What changed for the customer, how can they verify it, and which health/adoption signal changes the plan now? What would disprove the expansion hypothesis?
What does another role or peer notice about one value/health evidence statement and the specific Customer Plan change or bounded expansion hypothesis it supports that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Source/baseline limits, customer verification, technical constraints and a specific plan change; activity counts being called value or inferred expansion being forecast.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without baseline, customer validation or usage evidence, mark the claim unresolved. External research and recurring monitoring do not establish account value or expansion readiness. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another role help you distinguish between value evidence and a hopeful interpretation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could validate one value/health claim or take one AE-owned plan-change question forward; keep any expansion proposition conditional on evidence and owner judgment. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one value claim validated or qualified, the resulting plan action and the remaining evidence gap. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A usage or health signal suggests the Customer Plan should change, but its value implication is uncertain. Qualify the evidence and any expansion hypothesis.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Value and health feedback can inform the Customer Plan without turning an expansion possibility into confirmed demand. AE owns the Customer Plan, ATS supplies technical strategy and readiness, and conditional contributions remain conditional; ATU cannot accept on STU's behalf. Industry expertise and Services Sales input remain conditional; do not assume those contributors are available.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the value or health signal and possible Customer Plan change in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: An expansion hypothesis is not earned customer demand. Look for a caveated customer-value claim linked back to AE-owned plan action. Peer participation does not establish a broader manager forecast remit, a new meeting schedule or permission to run automation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: an expansion hypothesis is not earned customer demand. Confirm who can explain the ATU customer-plan and opportunity decisions boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-ORG-ATU-W08.keyTakeaway: Agree the credible value statement and the plan change, intervention, or expansion action it supports.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when an expansion hypothesis is not earned customer demand. Manager support can support the account owner in validating the value claim and deciding whether expansion is justified.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help frame bounded account feedback grounded in customer evidence; keep the plan action and commercial judgment with their owners.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that an expansion hypothesis is not earned customer demand; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support the account owner in validating the value claim and deciding whether expansion is justified? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

PLC-ENT-ORG-ATU-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-ENT-ORG-ATU-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-ENT-ORG-ATU-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-ENT-ORG-ATU-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.

What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?

activities.name: Structure intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [the approved intake packet, receiving criteria and any recorded receiving-owner response], draft an STU intake review packet. Show the customer decision, required evidence present/missing, receiving role, proposed first action and explicit acceptance, conditional acceptance, return or unknown status only where the response supports it. Identify the questions a receiving owner must settle and preserve recorded dates/ownership gaps. Do not accept the intake, assign ownership or update opportunity records.
activities.expectedOutput: STU intake review packet with evidence gaps, sourced acceptance/return status, receiving-role questions and proposed first action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved intake packet; known receiving criteria; recorded receiving-owner response/acceptance evidence and first-action context where available.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own intake acceptance, solution-area fit, value hypothesis, and pursuit path. SE: Assess technical context, evidence gaps, and discovery or validation needs.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own intake acceptance, solution-area fit, value hypothesis, and pursuit path. SE: Assess technical context, evidence gaps, and discovery or validation needs. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

activities.name: Rehearse intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action
activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation about intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own intake acceptance, solution-area fit, value hypothesis, and pursuit path. SE: Assess technical context, evidence gaps, and discovery or validation needs.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: ATU has routed a Conversation or opportunity, but STU must determine whether the intake is actionable. A visible intake disposition prevents silent document transfer from being mistaken for an actionable pursuit.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the ATU packet as supplied context, not a reason to require ATU attendance. SSP owns intake acceptance, fit/value and pursuit path; SE examines technical context and evidence gaps. Accept, redirect or return deliberately.
Make acceptance visible in the existing pipeline rhythm; do not reward silent document transfer.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What customer decision is STU being asked to advance?
What evidence is missing for acceptance?
Who owns the next customer action?
suggestedTransitions: Compare peer assessments of the same intake, then record the explicit receiving-side disposition. A return should specify what is missing rather than simply saying the packet is incomplete.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure intake acceptance, missing evidence, receiving owners, and first action' (stu-w2-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: To customer Conversation preparation or back to ATU with explicit gaps.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Discovery -> Conversation intake
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare peer assessments of the same intake, then record the explicit receiving-side disposition. A return should specify what is missing rather than simply saying the packet is incomplete. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer decision is STU being asked to advance? Which missing item changes the disposition, and who can provide it?
What does another role or peer notice about one intake disposition with customer decision, rationale, evidence gaps, sending/receiving owners and first action that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A single disposition with rationale, sending/receiving owners, first action and next customer interaction; acceptance with no actionable evidence or owner.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If essential intake context is missing, prepare the clarification/return request rather than inferring ATU intent. A simulation cannot accept the intake for SSP/SE. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What made the intake actionable or not, and what would you ask a sender to make clearer next time?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could have the accountable receiving owner confirm one disposition and its first action, or return one precise evidence request to the sender. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one actual intake disposition, its rationale and first action; if blocked, the specific item returned and who must resolve it. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A routed intake contains background material but omits the customer decision and next owner. Compare whether it can be accepted, redirected or returned.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: STU intake makes the customer decision, missing evidence and first receiving action explicit before work is accepted. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the routed intake and open receiving question in the example.

activities.description: Rehearse a consequential interaction and expose unclear evidence, role turns, or decision language.
activities.prompt: Use only a fictional or de-identified scenario. Rehearsal simulation only. Using [the fictional/de-identified rehearsal brief, participant roles and decision criteria], simulate a realistic conversation about customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask. Practice role turns, evidence questions, objections and the decision ask; then offer coaching. Clearly label every simulated reaction. Keep reactions fictional, not evidence of customer agreement.
activities.expectedOutput: A labeled rehearsal transcript and coaching notes for customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Accountable humans verify evidence, conduct the real conversation, and retain every acceptance, approval, judgment, and commitment.
activities.requiredContext: A rehearsal brief, audience profile, and agreed decision criteria.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Own the solution-specific business value, stakeholders, objections, and decision ask. SE: Own technical discovery questions, grounded responses, criteria, and evidence needs.
activitySteps: 1. Use the approved rehearsal brief, audience and decision criteria to rehearse one exchange about one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection; participants can take simulated turns without inviting another org.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.
3. Label every reaction as simulation. Pause on unclear role turns, unsupported facts or the decision ask; capture one coaching correction and an unresolved question.
4. Human owners verify facts and conduct the real interaction before any acceptance, authorization or commitment. Rehearsal is not customer/partner evidence or system input.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A focused Conversation advances a customer decision instead of covering every slide or duplicating role contributions. A labeled rehearsal can expose unclear questions before a real interaction without masquerading as customer evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: STU has accepted the intake and must lead a Conversation that advances a specific customer decision. A focused Conversation advances a customer decision instead of covering every slide or duplicating role contributions.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP owns value, stakeholders, objections and the decision ask; SE owns technical discovery, grounded responses and criteria. Rehearse only the turns needed to expose fit and evidence, not a complete presentation.
Rehearse role contributions briefly; optimize for customer decision, not presentation coverage.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What must the customer decide or agree next?
Which questions and evidence will expose real fit?
How will each role contribute without duplicating the others?
suggestedTransitions: Move from decision ask to one consequential question or objection. Compare peer approaches, rehearse a short exchange, then note what the real customer interaction must establish.

A source Featured starting option is 'Rehearse customer Conversation turns, evidence questions, objections, and decision ask' (stu-w3-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Decision criteria and evidence gaps into solution/value design.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Conversation -> solution definition
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move from decision ask to one consequential question or objection. Compare peer approaches, rehearse a short exchange, then note what the real customer interaction must establish. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which question would expose that the proposed fit is wrong? How does each role's turn advance the same customer decision rather than repeat the other?
What does another role or peer notice about one customer Conversation decision ask with complementary SSP/SE turns, evidence questions and an unresolved objection that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A specific decision ask, distinct SSP/SE turns, honest evidence questions and customer criteria; polished responses concealing unknowns or rehearsal reactions treated as customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: When customer facts or access are missing, rehearse structure with clearly labeled unknowns. Do not claim customer agreement or replace the real Conversation with simulated responses. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another role's question reveal about our decision ask or fit assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could refine one Conversation turn or evidence question, have its role owner review it, and use it in the next authorized customer interaction. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one question or decision criterion clarified in the real interaction, or what remained untested; no sensitive transcript is required. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: SSP and SE plan to cover similar material in a customer Conversation. Rehearse complementary turns around one decision ask and an unresolved objection.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A coordinated customer Conversation gives SSP and SE complementary contributions around a shared decision ask. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.

facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Role-play and internal agreement do not confirm customer intent. Look for a coordinated conversation with a clear evidence question and role boundary. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: role-play and internal agreement do not confirm customer intent. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Research technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public technical sources to inform discovery criteria, evidence gaps and the next technical decision. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Use official product guidance for product requirements; cite material claims with source dates and separate facts from proposed criteria or validation questions. Flag relevant conflicts, staleness and applicability gaps. Return a focused evidence brief and questions for the technical decision owner; public research cannot confirm this customer's estate, criteria or technical acceptance. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated, cited research brief supporting human review of technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Clarify the customer outcome, value question, and business decision the technical work must support. SE: Lead technical discovery and define decision criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Clear technical criteria prevent repeated discovery and oversized proofs that do not resolve the customer's next decision. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

activities.name: Structure technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [the approved technical discovery brief and open technical decision], draft a technical discovery decision packet. Show business outcome, customer-agreed versus proposed criteria, evidence gaps, constraints, highest-consequence unknowns and the next validation question or technical decision. Preserve source and confirmation status; identify recorded accountable roles or ownership gaps. Do not turn hypotheses into agreement, certify a technical win or assign delivery work.
activities.expectedOutput: Technical discovery decision packet with confirmed/proposed criteria, constraints, proof gaps and next technical decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved technical discovery brief; open technical decision and known criteria; constraint/evidence sources and recorded confirmation/owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Clarify the customer outcome, value question, and business decision the technical work must support. SE: Lead technical discovery and define decision criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Clear technical criteria prevent repeated discovery and oversized proofs that do not resolve the customer's next decision. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

activities.name: Inspect technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision
activities.description: Ground the team discussion in authorized sales-system context without asking people to paste retrievable records.
activities.prompt: For [Account Name or TPID] or Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID], summarize the sales evidence for [technical discovery criterion and next decision]. Cite recorded customer needs, known proof references and as-of dates; distinguish facts from assumptions and missing technical evidence. Propose the smallest useful evidence check and the question for the technical owner. Do not infer technical readiness or customer acceptance from sales activity, or change records. State access gaps.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: Permitted access to relevant Sales sources; Account name or TPID, or Opportunity ID for a particular deal; one technical discovery criterion and next decision; available dated customer-need evidence, proof references and known technical-owner context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. SSP: Clarify the customer outcome, value question, and business decision the technical work must support. SE: Lead technical discovery and define decision criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Clear technical criteria prevent repeated discovery and oversized proofs that do not resolve the customer's next decision. Bounded retrieval can expose relevant record evidence; it cannot replace the owner’s decision or fill non-sales evidence gaps.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The Conversation exposed customer questions, but technical criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision remain unresolved. Clear technical criteria prevent repeated discovery and oversized proofs that do not resolve the customer's next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: SSP anchors the business/value question; SE leads technical criteria and discovery. Start with what the Conversation already established and identify the smallest missing evidence instrument, not an automatic PoC.
Do not default to a PoC; choose the smallest evidence instrument that resolves the decision.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What technical decision must the team support?
Which criteria and evidence gaps matter most?
What moves into design or bounded validation?
suggestedTransitions: Compare peers' criteria for the same decision, narrow to the unresolved criterion, then form a design/validation brief with evidence gaps and next technical decision.

A source Featured starting option is 'Research technical discovery criteria, evidence gaps, and the next technical decision' (stu-w4-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Decision criteria into solution design and bounded validation.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Conversation -> technical discovery -> solution definition
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare peers' criteria for the same decision, narrow to the unresolved criterion, then form a design/validation brief with evidence gaps and next technical decision. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which technical decision remains open? What evidence is sufficient to resolve the most consequential criterion, and which already-completed discovery should we not repeat?
What does another role or peer notice about one technical decision criterion with known evidence, remaining gap and smallest useful evidence instrument that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Decision-critical criteria, source gaps and a small next evidence step; feature inventories, repeated discovery or a proof proposed without a decision it resolves.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If technical evidence is inaccessible, map criterion, unknown and responsible verifier. Sales records can supply context but cannot establish technical readiness or substitute for SE judgment. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which criterion changed after peer challenge, and what evidence do you still need before designing a validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify one criterion or evidence gap with the SE and relevant SSP context, or identify the smallest suitable evidence instrument. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one criterion confirmed/revised and the evidence required or checked; state if a proof was unnecessary or not yet authorized. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Conversation raised a technical question without explicit decision criteria. Identify one criterion and the smallest evidence instrument that could resolve its gap.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Technical discovery links a customer criterion to the evidence needed for the next technical decision. SSP and SE make complementary contributions; sending-side preparation, proof execution and receiving-side acceptance are distinct responsibilities. STU records customer commitment; CSU makes a separate receiving-acceptance decision.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the criterion, existing evidence and remaining uncertainty in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A preferred proof instrument is not automatically necessary. Look for a criterion linked to the smallest useful evidence question. Do not assume investment approval, a universal manager cadence or permission to run automation. A partner may execute a justified proof; a no-proof decision is valid when existing evidence suffices.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a preferred proof instrument is not automatically necessary. Confirm who can explain the STU customer decisions and technical evidence boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-ORG-STU-W04.keyTakeaway: Agree the technical decision criteria, evidence gaps, and next technical decision.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a preferred proof instrument is not automatically necessary. Manager support can help the technical owner secure customer clarification before allocating unnecessary proof work.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help focus on the smallest useful evidence question instead of presuming a preferred demo, workshop or proof is needed.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a preferred proof instrument is not automatically necessary; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help the technical owner secure customer clarification before allocating unnecessary proof work? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public technical sources on solution options and the uncertainty a bounded validation would resolve. Consider when existing evidence could support no additional proof as well as a useful validation proposal. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates; separate documented facts, inference and proposals, flagging relevant conflicts, staleness or applicability gaps. Return the evidence brief and questions for the decision owner. Public evidence is not proof of customer-specific acceptance or permission to run a test. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
