Name missing evidence and the question for the accountable receiving role; mark proposed actions or dates unconfirmed. Do not infer technical/delivery readiness, accept the milestone or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for committed-milestone acceptance, evidence gaps, receiving owners, and review date, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity ID and relevant authorized sales context, or a permitted dated extract identifying that opportunity.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Accept orchestration accountability, customer stakeholders, success outcome, and review rhythm. CSA: Accept technical work within the appropriate domain and surface readiness or boundary gaps. activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A receiving-side milestone disposition makes execution responsibility explicit instead of treating an STU customer commitment as automatic CSU acceptance. activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.

activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Accept orchestration accountability, customer stakeholders, success outcome, and review rhythm. CSA: Accept technical work within the appropriate domain and surface readiness or boundary gaps. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Assess engineering execution or acceleration needs; role is not represented in the current app. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. 2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A committed opportunity is moving into execution, but the milestone, evidence, and receiving responsibilities need acceptance. A receiving-side milestone disposition makes execution responsibility explicit instead of treating an STU customer commitment as automatic CSU acceptance.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the supplied STU packet within CSU. CSAM accepts orchestration accountability; CSA assesses domain technical work; engineering acceleration is conditional. Choose accept, conditionally accept or return, with first actions and residual STU obligations.
Keep the huddle within CSU. Use the supplied STU handoff packet and route specific gaps back asynchronously; STU roles do not need to attend.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What exactly is committed and how will success be recognized?
Which receiver owns each first action?
What must return to STU before execution starts?
suggestedTransitions: Compare CSAM/CSA assessments of one milestone, then record the actual receiving-side decision and any conditions. Route precise gaps back asynchronously; STU attendance is unnecessary.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure committed-milestone acceptance, evidence gaps, receiving owners, and review date' (csu-w2-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Into the Customer Success Plan or back to STU with specific gaps.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: STU commitment -> CSU execution
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare CSAM/CSA assessments of one milestone, then distinguish a proposed disposition from any actual receiving-side decision and its conditions. If useful, precise gaps could be taken back through the existing asynchronous route; STU attendance is unnecessary. No acceptance or transfer is required for the huddle. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What exactly is committed and what would completion mean? Which receiving owner can act now, and what must return to STU before execution starts?
What does another role or peer notice about one CSU milestone disposition with receiving-role responsibilities, evidence gaps, conditions and first action that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A documented disposition, rationale, gaps, receiving owners, first action/review point and return conditions; sales commitment or monitoring output being treated as accepted technical completion.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the packet is incomplete, record conditional acceptance only if the responsible owner actually chooses it; otherwise return specific gaps. Do not infer readiness from sales-system context. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which packet gap most affected acceptance, and did the role boundaries make the first action clearer?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could confirm one disposition/condition with the responsible receiving owner or return one precise missing-evidence request to STU. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one actual accept/conditional accept/return record, its first action, review point and any unresolved residual STU obligation. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A customer-committed milestone arrives from STU, but a receiving responsibility or prerequisite remains unclear. Review acceptance, conditional acceptance or return from the CSU perspective.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: CSU intake tests whether a customer-committed milestone has the evidence, prerequisites and receiving ownership needed to act. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the proposed intake, commitment evidence and receiving-role boundaries in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A customer's commitment does not remove CSU's receiving acceptance decision. Look for an accept, condition or return disposition with named owners and first action. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a customer's commitment does not remove CSU's receiving acceptance decision. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a customer's commitment does not remove CSU's receiving acceptance decision. Manager support can help settle receipt conditions and route ambiguity before work is treated as accepted.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help keep acceptance, conditional acceptance and return distinct; a customer's commitment does not settle CSU readiness.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a customer's commitment does not remove CSU's receiving acceptance decision; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to help settle receipt conditions and route ambiguity before work is treated as accepted? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

activities.name: Structure Customer Success Plan outcomes, milestones, owners, risks, and review rhythm
activities.description: Turn supplied working material into a decision-ready packet while preserving role ownership.
activities.prompt: Using only [the current approved Customer Success Plan and milestone evidence], draft a plan execution packet linking customer outcomes to milestones, delivery/adoption dependencies, recorded owners, risks and review rhythm. Separate evidenced progress from record-only changes and unknown status, and accepted commitments from proposed follow-through. Show missing outcome links, dates, mitigation or ownership evidence against known review criteria. Do not change the plan, assign work or infer delivered value from a milestone entry.
activities.expectedOutput: Customer Success Plan execution packet linking outcomes, evidence-backed milestone movement, dependencies, ownership gaps, risks and review rhythm.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Current approved Customer Success Plan; milestone/progress evidence; known customer outcomes, review criteria/rhythm and owner/dependency context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Own the outcome-anchored Customer Success Plan and orchestration rhythm. CSA: Define domain-specific technical milestones, dependencies, adoption actions, and evidence. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Define applicable engineering execution milestones and dependencies; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one accepted milestone's Customer Success Plan link to outcome, technical/adoption work, owners, risks and review decision; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one accepted milestone's Customer Success Plan link to outcome, technical/adoption work, owners, risks and review decision. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: An outcome-anchored Customer Success Plan connects accepted work to executable decisions instead of becoming an inventory of disconnected milestones. A compact structured draft makes gaps and decisions easier for human owners to review.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Accepted milestones exist, but outcomes, delivery work, adoption, owners, and customer governance are not connected. An outcome-anchored Customer Success Plan connects accepted work to executable decisions instead of becoming an inventory of disconnected milestones.
keyTalkingPoints: CSAM owns Customer Success Planning and orchestration; CSA defines domain-specific technical milestones/adoption evidence; FDE engineering input is conditional. Use existing customer/internal rhythms rather than a new universal cadence.
Use the existing customer and internal rhythm; the plan is a decision system, not an inventory.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: Which customer outcome does each milestone serve?
Are owners, dependencies, and review points executable?
What belongs outside this plan?
suggestedTransitions: Compare one milestone's outcome link with a peer, then add the missing owner/dependency/review decision in the existing plan and reference authoritative records.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure Customer Success Plan outcomes, milestones, owners, risks, and review rhythm' (csu-w3-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Plan priorities into health inspection and delivery execution.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Committed milestone -> Customer Success Plan
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare one milestone's outcome link with a peer, then identify any missing owner/dependency/review decision and the authoritative record. You could propose a plan change if useful; actual updates remain with the accountable owner. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer outcome does this milestone serve? Are owner, dependency and review point executable, and what should remain outside this plan?
What does another role or peer notice about one accepted milestone's Customer Success Plan link to outcome, technical/adoption work, owners, risks and review decision that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Accepted milestones linked to outcomes, owners, dependencies and review decisions; implied new ownership, undifferentiated CSA work or CAIP-specific rhythms generalized to every CSU team.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without an accepted milestone or confirmed owner/outcome link, capture the planning gap rather than call the plan executable. No new cadence or FDE attendance is assumed. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did peer input change about the outcome link or the dependency we thought was clear?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could have CSAM and the relevant CSA owner check one plan link or dependency; keep any required record change with its accountable owner. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one milestone-to-outcome link improved, an owner/dependency clarified or an unresolved planning question, using a permission-safe verbal summary. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: An accepted milestone appears in the success plan without a clear customer-outcome link. Connect one technical or adoption action to its owner and unresolved risk.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A Customer Success Plan connects accepted milestones to customer outcomes, technical or adoption actions and accountable owners. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the accepted milestone, outcome link and risk in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: An accepted handoff is not by itself an outcome-led success plan. Look for a milestone connected to customer outcome, owners and the review decision. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: an accepted handoff is not by itself an outcome-led success plan. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

activities.name: Research consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary
activities.description: Add current external evidence with traceable authority, dates, and limitations.
activities.prompt: Research [research question] for [industry/use case] using authoritative public sources on consequential health risks, evidence limits, interventions and escalation considerations. Apply geography or time limits only where material. Cite material claims with source dates; separate facts, possible causes and proposed implications, flagging relevant conflicts or stale evidence. Return a focused brief and questions for the appropriate CSAM/CSA or domain owner. Public research cannot diagnose this customer, verify private telemetry or sentiment, assign an intervention owner or infer health from missing evidence. Additional context: [add a short note or relevant source link]; if this placeholder is unchanged, ignore this field and continue.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated, cited public health-risk/intervention context brief with evidence limits and questions for the appropriate human/domain owner; not a customer diagnosis or ownership assignment.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Role owners verify source relevance and currency and retain all technical, commercial, approval, and commitment decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Research question; relevant industry/use case or public topic; geographic/time scope only where material; any sanitized background needed to bound the question.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Integrate customer, stakeholder, delivery, support, and success-plan signals and own intervention orchestration. CSA: Validate technical health, domain-specific risk, evidence, and feasible intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Add engineering execution risk where applicable; role is not represented in the current app.
activitySteps: 1. Bound one research question that could inform one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point; identify the relevant industry/use case and any geographic or time limit only where material to the research question.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. If the authorized source/tool is available, check citations supporting material findings, source authority and relevant dates/applicability. Flag material conflicts or staleness; separate public facts, inference and unknowns. Public research is not account evidence.
4. The relevant role owner decides relevance and currency before use. A missing source stays a gap; no technical, commercial, commitment or approval decision is delegated to research.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Inspecting one consequential risk deeply helps the team act on the threat to the customer outcome rather than chase every visible signal. Cited research can challenge assumptions; it does not establish this account’s actual state.

Distinguish verified sales facts from inferred health or missing support/delivery evidence. Identify the confirmation question, proposed intervention and review point for the accountable role; cite any established escalation boundary or mark it unverified. Do not infer technical readiness or realized customer outcomes, make commitments or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-led brief for consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary, with gaps, conflicts, owners, and decision questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The accountable seller and role owners validate the evidence, make all judgments and commitments, and perform any system write.
activities.requiredContext: Permitted access to relevant Sales sources; Account name or TPID, or Opportunity ID for a particular-deal question; one customer-health risk under review; available dated risk/commitment evidence, source coverage and known owner, intervention or escalation context.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Integrate customer, stakeholder, delivery, support, and success-plan signals and own intervention orchestration. CSA: Validate technical health, domain-specific risk, evidence, and feasible intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Add engineering execution risk where applicable; role is not represented in the current app. An authorized record owner verifies sales facts; this does not grant sales-system access to other participants or establish post-sales/technical evidence.
activitySteps: 1. Identify the bounded sales-record facts relevant to one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point; use only authorized connected records and permitted identifiers.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Compare returned facts and as-of scope with the actual question. Mark conflicts and missing evidence; do not infer technical readiness, customer acceptance, funding approval or post-sales status from sales context.
4. The accountable record owner verifies the facts and decides any correction or next action; the practice does not write records.

activities.name: Monitor consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary
activities.description: Set up governed recurring exception monitoring with a dated baseline and human validation.
activities.prompt: Use only available permitted evidence. Design only; don’t activate monitoring. For recurring monitoring of consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary, use [the existing approved monitoring specification and dated baseline/current snapshots]; read scope, cadence, permitted sources, recipients, access boundaries, review/expiry, human validator and first/later-run mode from that specification. Require the named human to confirm recipient access and least privilege for each actual run; mark missing access or approval evidence unconfirmed rather than claiming to verify it. For a first run, draft a dated baseline for my validation. For a later run, compare only with the prior approved report I supply and report changes. If that report is missing, stop and ask for it. Flag evidence gaps and unconfirmed acceptance or approvals; don’t change records. Stop at review or expiry unless reapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft monitoring design and dated baseline for human validation, or a draft change-only comparison of supplied snapshots on a later review. If the prior approved report is unavailable, an explicit stop or history gap, not an invented comparison. Actual execution or human validation is claimed only when separately performed and evidenced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: A named human validates every run, approves the baseline and recipients, makes all judgments and writes, and reapproves or stops the work at review or expiry.
activities.requiredContext: Approved monitoring focus, scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access boundaries, review or expiry date, human validator, run type, and prior approved report for later runs.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Integrate customer, stakeholder, delivery, support, and success-plan signals and own intervention orchestration. CSA: Validate technical health, domain-specific risk, evidence, and feasible intervention. Conditional only where applicable: FDE (not currently modeled): Add engineering execution risk where applicable; role is not represented in the current app. A named human validates each run and baseline/recipient/review choices; no automation or schedule is created by this review candidate.
activitySteps: 1. For one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point, check that approved scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients/access, review or expiry, named validator and run type are actually supplied. If not, stop at a design/prerequisite review; do not start monitoring.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. First run: draft a dated baseline only from approved evidence and retain it only after human approval. Later run: require the prior approved report; if missing, stop. Compare against that report and prepare change-only observations.

4. A named human validates every run and recipient access, handles decisions/writes, and reapproves or stops work at review/expiry. Flag stale, conflicting or inaccessible evidence; monitoring never establishes acceptance or approval.
5. Stop if access, appropriate context or the needed human verifier is unavailable. Use a paper workflow discussion and record the gap; do not fill business facts with generated guesses.
activities.whyThisMatters: Inspecting one consequential risk deeply helps the team act on the threat to the customer outcome rather than chase every visible signal. Governed change review can expose what moved between observations without delegating judgment to unattended work.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Usage, support, delivery, sentiment, and technical signals compete for attention, obscuring the risk that matters most. Inspecting one consequential risk deeply helps the team act on the threat to the customer outcome rather than chase every visible signal.
keyTalkingPoints: CSAM integrates stakeholder/support/delivery signals and orchestrates intervention; CSA validates technical risk within domain; FDE engineering input is conditional. Distinguish what tools see from sentiment, causality and facts they cannot establish.
Inspect one consequential risk deeply rather than reviewing every signal.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: Which risk most threatens the customer outcome now?
What can the tools see, and what can they not see?
Who owns the intervention and review point?
suggestedTransitions: Compare candidate risks, select one consequential risk, then test the intervention against the limits of the evidence and the appropriate human/domain authority.

A source Featured starting option is 'Research consequential health risk, evidence, intervention, owner, and escalation boundary' (csu-w4-p3); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Risk actions into delivery/adoption execution and escalations where needed.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Customer Success Plan -> health/risk intervention
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare candidate risks, select one consequential risk, then test the intervention against the limits of the evidence and the appropriate human/domain authority. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which risk most threatens the outcome now? What does available evidence establish, what does it not establish, and what observation would change the intervention?
What does another role or peer notice about one ranked customer-health risk with dated evidence limits, intervention, owner, escalation boundary and review point that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Customer-visible consequence, dated/corroborated evidence, ranked risk, intervention owner and escalation boundary; a tool's silence treated as health or a correlation treated as diagnosis.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If health/telemetry/support evidence is inaccessible, record the visibility gap. Sales context and external research are not a diagnosis; do not invent customer sentiment. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed your risk priority, and what uncertainty must remain visible before the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could verify one risk signal with its proper source/domain owner or take one agreed intervention step with a review point and escalation boundary. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one risk checked, what changed or stayed uncertain, the intervention owner and next review; no sensitive support detail needs to leave approved systems. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Several health signals compete for attention, but one dated risk most threatens the customer outcome. Compare evidence limits before choosing an intervention question.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Customer health prioritization weighs dated evidence and its limits against the outcome a risk could affect. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the consequential signal, dated source and evidence limit in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A health score alone cannot justify a particular intervention. Look for a prioritized risk with a proportionate action and accountable review point. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a health score alone cannot justify a particular intervention. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Microsoft, customer, partner, support, and delivery workstreams are active but dependencies and accountability are fragmented. Connecting dependencies and accountability prevents active workstreams from drifting apart while the next customer outcome stalls.
keyTalkingPoints: CSAM orchestrates customer, partner, delivery, support and program work; CSA owns domain technical guidance and escalation inputs; FDE acceleration is conditional. Use existing meeting sockets/systems, not a new reporting product.
Favor existing meeting sockets and authoritative systems over new reporting.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: Which dependency threatens the next customer outcome?
Who is accountable versus contributing?
Which existing rhythm and system will hold the decision?
suggestedTransitions: Trace one dependency across workstreams, compare peers' assumptions about accountability, then agree the next intervention and review within an existing authoritative rhythm.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure delivery and adoption dependencies, accountability, escalation, and next review' (csu-w5-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Resolved actions into usage milestones; unresolved risk to the right escalation path.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Customer Success Plan -> delivery/adoption execution
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Trace one dependency across workstreams, compare peers' assumptions about accountability, then consider whether an intervention or review would be useful within an existing authoritative rhythm; taking no next action is valid. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which dependency threatens the next outcome? Who is accountable versus contributing, and which existing rhythm will hold the decision?
What does another role or peer notice about one delivery/adoption dependency across workstreams with accountability, intervention/escalation and next integrated review that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: A consequential dependency, explicit accountable/contributing roles, feasible intervention/escalation and integrated review; an unconfirmed partner action or proposed owner treated as agreed.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If partner/delivery/support status is unavailable, mark it unknown and identify the evidence request. Do not infer capacity, assign another org's owner or invent a meeting cadence. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which dependency was more important than its workstream status suggested, and what did peer comparison reveal about accountability?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could confirm or unblock one dependency with the responsible owner, or route one precise escalation through the existing path. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one dependency clarified or resolved, its owner and next review; if blocked, the missing status or unconfirmed responsibility. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Delivery and adoption workstreams are active, but one cross-team dependency stalls the next outcome. Clarify accountability and use an existing review rhythm rather than invent a meeting.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Delivery and adoption orchestration exposes dependencies across workstreams and uses the existing review rhythm. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the delivery or adoption dependency in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Naming a workstream does not assign its owner or accept an escalation. Look for an explicit dependency and intervention with a receiving owner and next integrated review. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: naming a workstream does not assign its owner or accept an escalation. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Deployment or consumption is behind the commitment, and the team needs to distinguish technical, adoption, and nontechnical causes. An intervention is useful when it changes realized usage in service of a customer outcome, not merely a consumption number.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate observed deployment/usage gaps from technical, adoption and nontechnical cause hypotheses. CSAM owns outcome/stakeholder orchestration; the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain and aligns consumption actions; engineering acceleration remains conditional.
Do not flatten CSA variants; name the domain and bring the right specialist.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What explains the gap between commitment and realized usage?
Which intervention changes the trajectory?
How will usage connect to a customer outcome rather than volume alone?
suggestedTransitions: Compare hypotheses for one observed gap, identify discriminating evidence, then let the appropriate human choose an intervention and milestone. Keep the usage plan tied to outcome.

A source Featured starting option is 'Organize observed usage gaps and competing cause hypotheses' (csu-w6-p3); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Usage evidence into value realization and risk feedback.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Deployment -> adoption/consumption -> realized usage
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare hypotheses for one observed gap, identify discriminating evidence, then discuss whether an intervention or milestone change is justified; any actual decision remains with the appropriate human. Keep the usage plan tied to outcome. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: Which part of the gap is observed and which is a cause hypothesis? What evidence could distinguish the competing explanations before choosing an intervention?
What does another role or peer notice about one observed usage/milestone gap with competing cause hypotheses, missing evidence and the human-owned intervention question that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Actual usage/milestone evidence, domain boundaries, competing hypotheses, owner and outcome link; sales records presented as telemetry or Cowork selecting a technical cause/intervention.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If post-sales evidence is unavailable, structure the gap and evidence request only. Sales Agent supplies bounded sales/commitment context, not usage, health, telemetry, support history or causality. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which hypothesis became less credible after peer challenge, and what must a domain owner verify before action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check one discriminating evidence item with the responsible CSA/CSAM owner or test one authorized intervention; retain the causal uncertainty until evidence supports it. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share observed usage change or a still-open evidence gap, intervention owner/milestone and customer-outcome link; do not imply causality from correlation. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Realized usage trails a commitment, with competing technical and adoption explanations. Test one cause hypothesis without making the CSA owner of every shortfall.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Closing a commitment-to-usage gap starts by separating technical, adoption and nontechnical explanations. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the observed usage gap and competing cause hypotheses in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Technical, adoption and nontechnical causes require different owners. Look for a cause hypothesis with missing evidence and the relevant CSA domain identified. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: technical, adoption and nontechnical causes require different owners. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Technical progress and usage exist, but the team has not assembled evidence the customer recognizes as value. A defensible value narrative shows what changed for the customer against a baseline and what still needs their validation.
keyTalkingPoints: CSAM owns the customer-outcome narrative and validation; CSA validates technical progress, usage/cost/optimization evidence and limits; FDE contributes only where applicable. Internal activity, external benchmarks and role-play reactions are not customer-recognized value.
Ask the customer to validate value; internal activity is not itself an outcome.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What changed for the customer and against which baseline?
Which claims are verified, inferred, or still missing?
What customer decision should the evidence enable?
suggestedTransitions: Compare one proposed value claim with its evidence, qualify it where necessary, then prepare a short narrative and explicit customer validation question rather than declare value proved.

A source Featured starting option is 'Structure value evidence, baseline, caveats, and questions for customer validation' (csu-w7-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: Value evidence to ATU planning, renewal, health, and expansion decisions.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Adoption/consumption -> value realization
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare one proposed value claim with its evidence, qualify it where necessary, then prepare a short narrative and explicit customer validation question rather than declare value proved. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What changed against which baseline? Which claims are verified, inferred or missing, and what should the customer validate before the next decision?
What does another role or peer notice about one value claim with baseline, technical/usage evidence, caveats, unresolved assertions and question for customer validation that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Baseline/source/date, caveats, unresolved claims and a customer decision ask; metrics without outcome meaning, external benchmarks treated as account results or rehearsal treated as validation.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without baseline or customer confirmation, retain the claim as unverified. Research can supply methods/benchmarks only; it cannot establish account-specific value. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did peer review make you remove or qualify in the value claim?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could check one value claim with its evidence owner or take one reviewed validation question to the customer through the appropriate owner. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one claim validated, corrected or still unverified; include baseline/caveat and the next ask rather than a sensitive evidence packet. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A value narrative combines observed technical progress with an unverified benefit claim. Compare baseline and caveats and prepare the remaining customer-validation question.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Customer value claims need a baseline, suitable measurement and customer validation beyond deployment or usage alone. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the proposed claim, measurement limits and customer evidence in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Usage or deployment data does not establish every customer outcome. Look for a caveated claim and a specific remaining customer-validation question. The starting prompt or required inputs still need product-owner clarification; do not fill the gap with an invented capability. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.

activities.prompt: Using only [approved renewal-risk/expansion evidence, Customer Plan context and decision criteria], draft plan feedback with value/health proof, risks, expansion hypotheses, owner-confirmation questions and next decision. Keep expansion need hypothetical unless customer evidence supports it. Use the actual work object and commitment status: for milestones fitting an open opportunity's Customer Priority and commercial scope, committed work may remain with its CSU owner and uncommitted work goes to STU review; a new unaligned opportunity goes to ATU discovery. Include SAE for Services renewal/pursuit needs. Preserve recorded ownership but do not infer acceptance, create pipeline, set forecast, promise terms, transfer work or edit the plan.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal/expansion Customer Plan feedback with supported value/health evidence, hypothesis/confirmation status, work-object-specific routing questions and next decisions; no assumed acceptance or record action.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Named role owners validate the packet and make every decision, approval, commitment, system write, and handoff acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: Approved renewal-risk/expansion evidence; Customer Plan and known decision criteria; actual opportunity/Customer Priority/commercial scope and milestone commitment status where available; recorded owner/customer-confirmation evidence.
activities.bestFitJob: Within-org workflow contribution, not a new job role. CSAM: Synthesize success-plan progress, health, usage, value, and stakeholder readiness. Conditional only where applicable: CSA: Validate technical adoption gaps, platform health, and feasible expansion prerequisites.
activitySteps: 1. Select the approved working material needed to organize one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback; do not copy restricted material into a new surface.

2. Keep the live work to one reviewable fragment: one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback. Other Featured choices are alternatives; Extended work is optional follow-up subject to prerequisites.

3. Review the small draft against source records and agreed criteria. Keep facts, assumptions, gaps, role contributions and open decisions distinct; no generated owner assignment or approval is final.
4. The stated role owners verify the draft and decide any commitment, technical/commercial judgment, handoff disposition or record update.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Health, usage, and value evidence must inform renewal and expansion without turning optimism into forecast. Evidence-backed renewal and expansion feedback helps account owners act without turning health optimism into forecast or an unauthorized commercial promise.
keyTalkingPoints: CSAM synthesizes success-plan/health/usage/value readiness; CSA contributes technical adoption/health checks conditionally. AE/CE retain commercial ownership; CE is not a default attendee. Feed the decision into the Customer Plan and next success cycle.
Keep commercial ownership with AE/CE and orchestration evidence with CSU; CE participation is conditional.

AI methods are suggested options, not an approved universal method; use a permitted tool only if useful and available. Evidence review and accountable human decisions remain separate from generated drafts.
discussionQuestions: What evidence supports renewal confidence or risk?
Which expansion is earned by realized value and readiness?
What must feed back into the Customer Plan?
suggestedTransitions: Compare renewal risk with the value/readiness evidence, choose the intervention or hypothesis to route, then name the accountable commercial recipient without assigning acceptance.

A source Featured starting option is 'Rehearse renewal risk or earned expansion evidence and Customer Plan feedback' (csu-w8-p1); select it only if its exact context, access and reviewer are available. Other Featured activities are alternatives, not extra live tasks. Extended work is optional follow-up, never a prerequisite invented for this huddle.
Keep Preparation, Explore and Practice, and Commit together within the existing 15-minute AI-in-Action segment, with no new phase sub-timings; protect the closing.
Source handoff: To ATU and CE when required; feedback also starts the next success cycle.
Source MCEM/lifecycle context: Value/health -> renewal/expansion -> planning feedback
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Compare renewal risk with the value/readiness evidence, choose the intervention or hypothesis to route, then name the accountable commercial recipient without assigning acceptance. Separate what was actually reviewed from what is still a proposal; name the human reviewer and a bounded next step rather than imply completion.
facilitatorQuestions: What evidence supports renewal confidence or risk? Which expansion is earned by realized value/readiness, and what must remain a hypothesis for the account owner?
What does another role or peer notice about one renewal-risk intervention or earned-expansion hypothesis with verified value/health evidence and Customer Plan feedback that changes your approach?
What must the human owner check before using this draft or observation?
listenFor: Verified health/value, a bounded intervention or expansion hypothesis and accountable routing; CSU implying pricing, forecast, terms or customer commitment authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If value/health is unverified or commercial authority is absent, label the hypothesis and prepare a question for AE/CE; do not forecast, promise terms or assume CE attends. If access or an input is unavailable, stop the tool attempt and map the real workflow on paper. Explicitly label unexecuted work and missing evidence. A discussion, partial draft or bounded next question is a valid huddle outcome.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which evidence changed your confidence, and which commercial decision is outside CSU's authority?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If relevant, you could send one reviewed renewal-risk or expansion-evidence question to the accountable account owner, or close one material evidence gap before doing so. If blocked, you could explore a smaller within-authority question or leave the gap open without a report or promise of inaccessible work; tool use remains optional. You may adapt the idea or choose no next action; no follow-up evidence is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you wish, you may share one feedback item routed and any actual owner response, clearly separated from a commercial decision; explain the remaining condition or evidence gap. A brief anonymized verbal summary is enough; restricted detail stays in its approved system. Sharing a blocker or untested question is acceptable. An observation from this huddle or an open question is equally valid; no new record or follow-up is required.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: Renewal confidence rests on a positive health signal while expansion readiness remains uncertain. Frame bounded account feedback without creating a forecast or commercial promise.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Renewal and expansion feedback translates supported value and health evidence into a bounded account conversation. CSAM owns customer-success stakeholder orchestration and the relevant CSA diagnoses within domain; receiving acceptance and partner or engineering work stay explicit. Forward Deployed Engineer involvement remains conditional; technical domains and local capacity differ.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the renewal-risk intervention or expansion hypothesis and its supporting evidence.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Renewal relevance does not establish entitlement, demand or approved commercial terms. Look for an account-feedback question with customer evidence and a known relationship owner. Do not generalize Cloud & AI Platforms capacity or review rhythms to every CSU team, or infer permission to run automation from peer participation.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: renewal relevance does not establish entitlement, demand or approved commercial terms. Confirm who can explain the CSU customer outcomes and delivery orchestration boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. Be ready to support reflection, the continuing team rhythm, and choosing a Week 10 topic. Confirm the supplied Impact Survey link is available without asking for personal responses.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.

roles.name: Account Executive

roles.descriptionSummary: Owns Enterprise account priorities, pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and expansion.

roles.name: Account Technology Strategist
