PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W01.todayObjective: Understand why Frontier Accelerator matters, the roles that make huddles work, and what to expect as the team begins learning through real work.
PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-ENT-ORG-CSU-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.description: Detailed reference for Sales Agent components, capabilities, and example prompts.

resources.title: Use Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot
resources.description: Official Sales agent overview and example prompts for connected CRM data. Internal sales scenarios and available records can differ.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Cowork
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
keyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

resources.title: What to Use When
resources.description: Routes a request to the best-fit Copilot agent and reserves Cowork for longer multi-output work. Useful early in a role path when tool choice is still forming.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.

primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Helps users sharpen messages, rehearse conversations, anticipate objections, and plan next steps.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Customer conversation preparation and role-play, or de-identified rehearsal of a manager coaching conversation about business judgment where access and scenario support are confirmed. Do not use employee or HR data for rehearsal.
keyBenefits: Rehearsal before the real conversation. Sharpens messages, surfaces objections you had not anticipated, and coaches on clarity and next step, grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.

activities.name: Extract outcomes and planning signals
activities.description: Review authorized account context to distinguish stated outcomes and planning signals from assumptions and missing evidence.
activities.prompt: Extract customer-stated outcomes, priorities and Services-relevant execution/value signals for [Account Name or TPID] or Opportunity ID [Opportunity ID]. Cite available records/sources/dates, separate facts from inference and list evidence gaps and owner questions. Do not recommend a service without a supported gap or change records. If data is unavailable, state that and use a clearly synthetic example without requesting pasted customer data. SAE verifies the draft before reuse.
activities.expectedOutput: Fact/inference-separated outcomes/signals, evidence gaps, references and questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: SAE verifies facts, freshness and permissions; removes unsupported inference.
activities.requiredContext: Identify the account or opportunity record type and its matching ID already accessible to you in Sales Agent. Do not paste record contents; rely only on data the agent returns within your existing permissions. If access is unavailable, use a clearly synthetic case.
activitySteps: Open Sales Agent from its link. Use only the authorized record ID in RequiredContext and request read-only retrieval. Verify the source and any date returned; mark missing data unknown. Stop before any update, send, forecast change, or commitment. If access is missing, use the synthetic fallback without pasting record content.
activities.whyThisMatters: Root Services strategy in account planning and verified gaps, not unsupported service pitch.

agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Build a decision-ready plan slice
activities.description: Use reviewed facts to draft a bounded contribution to the shared account plan, keeping open questions and unconfirmed decisions explicit.
activities.prompt: Retrieve only [authorized account-plan/meeting-note source title or M365 link] within my permitted M365 access. In chat, draft a bounded account-plan slice: customer outcome, evidence-backed Services gap, open strategy question, dependencies, recorded owner or owner to confirm and next decision. Identify source title/date when available; preserve unknowns and distinguish proposed contributions from accepted ownership. If the source is unavailable, report that gap; do not replace real account facts with invented content or request restricted pasted material. Chat only: do not create/edit files, update records, send, post or schedule.
activities.expectedOutput: Proposed plan segment with evidence and open items.
activities.humanCheckpoint: SAE/account owner approves wording/owner/placement; no record update or commitment without authorization.
activities.requiredContext: Authorized account-plan/meeting-note source title or M365 link; account/plan scope where not identifiable in the source.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this practice or another Featured option and identify only the named approved M365 source(s) you are authorized to read; do not paste restricted content.
2. Request the chat-only draft and review source title/date, evidence, assumptions, gaps and acceptance status. A missing source permits only conclusions supported by the sources actually available.
3. Do not create/edit files, send, post, schedule or change records. Any later action requires its separate authorized process.

4. If live sources/tool access are unavailable for the huddle, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately; never present rehearsal as real customer facts, policy, eligibility, value or accepted ownership. Missing authoritative guidance leaves the relevant judgment unresolved.
activities.whyThisMatters: Root Services strategy in account planning and verified gaps, not unsupported service pitch.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Connect shared Enterprise account planning with customer outcomes, priorities and evidence-backed execution or value gaps. Keep one account plan rather than a parallel Services-only plan.
keyTalkingPoints: Services Account Executive lens: Connecting Services strategy to the shared account plan helps you focus on evidenced customer gaps rather than an unsupported Services pitch. ATU leads account discovery; SAE co-architects Services strategy. Strategy continuity does not imply ownership of delivery execution or receiving-team acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What execution or value gap is supported by evidence? What is still an assumption? What human decision is needed for account outcomes and Services-relevant execution or value gaps?
suggestedTransitions: Compare the evidence behind account outcomes and Services-relevant execution or value gaps; select one optional practice, inspect its draft, then name the next human checkpoint.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name a useful fragment or explicit evidence gap toward: Reviewed plan slice: outcomes, evidence-backed gap or no-gap, dependencies, owner-confirmed next decision, evidence refs. Not commitment. Do not imply the huddle completed the customer workflow.
facilitatorQuestions: What evidence supports the proposed Services path? SAE checks fidelity; use actual evidence only after review. What remains unresolved before an authorized owner could act?
listenFor: Customer outcomes before an offer; facts separated from inference; role and delivery boundaries; gaps stated rather than invented. Rehearsal is not customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected practice's sources, permission or tool access are missing, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic manual case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately. Real source gaps remain unresolved; rehearsal cannot establish customer facts, authoritative policy, fit/eligibility, capacity, approval, recognized value or receiving-owner acceptance. Do not request restricted pasted content, send/post, update records or schedule work. A chat-only Cowork practice does not create/edit files.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did the Services lens reveal that the broader account or solution view did not? Which assumption still needs checking?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose an optional next check within your authority: Proposed plan segment with evidence and open items. Confirm the appropriate human owner before any action; reflection or deferral is valid.
bringBackEvidence: If useful, bring back a non-sensitive observation, a verified source reference or an honest evidence/access gap. No new report, deadline, customer commitment or performance assessment is created.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Services seller faces uncertainty about account outcomes and Services-relevant execution or value gaps. Compare the available outcome signals with execution/value gaps and identify the next evidence check without asserting an offer, funding, delivery acceptance or customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: A Services strategy contributes to shared account outcomes by identifying Services-relevant execution or value gaps. SAE connects Services opportunities to the shared Enterprise account motion; authoritative Services, delivery, commercial and policy owners retain their decisions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the account-plan signal and Services-relevant execution gap in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A Services lens must not create a competing account plan. Look for an evidence-backed Services contribution aligned to AE-owned account priorities. Services pilot content remains provisional. Check current official guidance for eligibility, routing and commercial questions; missing guidance is a gap, not permission or approval.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a Services lens must not create a competing account plan. Confirm who can explain the Services strategy, fit and execution dependencies boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-SAE-W02.keyTakeaway: Keep one account plan: use evidenced execution or value gaps to shape Services strategy, not a parallel plan or commitment.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a Services lens must not create a competing account plan. Manager support can support the SAE's account-team coordination without inventing Services authority or approval.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help keep the Services contribution aligned with the AE-owned account plan; modeled pilot content does not establish new Services authority.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a Services lens must not create a competing account plan; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer. If the selected practice is chat-only Cowork, retain named-authorized-source access and no-file/action limits; a separate labeled rehearsal does not resolve missing real evidence or imply customer agreement/acceptance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support the SAE's account-team coordination without inventing Services authority or approval? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Compare an evidenced execution or value gap with a possible Services pathway. Test the hypothesis without treating generic product qualification as proof of Services fit or eligibility.
keyTalkingPoints: Services Account Executive lens: Testing pathway hypotheses helps you route a useful Services conversation without confusing an initial signal with fit, eligibility or authorization. ATU leads account discovery; SAE co-architects Services strategy. Strategy continuity does not imply ownership of delivery execution or receiving-team acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What execution or value gap is supported by evidence? What is still an assumption? What human decision is needed for services pathways and fit guardrails?
suggestedTransitions: Compare the evidence behind services pathways and fit guardrails; select one optional practice, inspect its draft, then name the next human checkpoint.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name a useful fragment or explicit evidence gap toward: Gap-to-pathway hypothesis with outcome, evidence, options, dependencies, questions; no approval assertion. Do not imply the huddle completed the customer workflow.
facilitatorQuestions: What evidence supports the proposed Services path? SAE confirms Team Members/ownership; pathway remains hypothesis. What remains unresolved before an authorized owner could act?
listenFor: Customer outcomes before an offer; facts separated from inference; role and delivery boundaries; gaps stated rather than invented. Rehearsal is not customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected practice's sources, permission or tool access are missing, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic manual case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately. Real source gaps remain unresolved; rehearsal cannot establish customer facts, authoritative policy, fit/eligibility, capacity, approval, recognized value or receiving-owner acceptance. Do not request restricted pasted content, send/post, update records or schedule work. A chat-only Cowork practice does not create/edit files.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did the Services lens reveal that the broader account or solution view did not? Which assumption still needs checking?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose an optional next check within your authority: Status note with evidence, open questions and next step. Confirm the appropriate human owner before any action; reflection or deferral is valid.
bringBackEvidence: If useful, bring back a non-sensitive observation, a verified source reference or an honest evidence/access gap. No new report, deadline, customer commitment or performance assessment is created.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Services seller faces uncertainty about services pathways and fit guardrails. Compare the available outcome signals with execution/value gaps and identify the next evidence check without asserting an offer, funding, delivery acceptance or customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Services pathway assessment compares a fit hypothesis with current official guidance and makes missing applicability evidence explicit. SAE connects Services opportunities to the shared Enterprise account motion; authoritative Services, delivery, commercial and policy owners retain their decisions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the Services-fit hypothesis and official reference, or the explicitly missing source, in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Generic product qualification does not establish Services eligibility or fit. Look for a qualified pathway question with its source and applicability gap. Services pilot content remains provisional. Check current official guidance for eligibility, routing and commercial questions; missing guidance is a gap, not permission or approval.

Confirm who can explain the Services strategy, fit and execution dependencies boundary if challenged. activities.description: Define and exercise a reusable read-only check for changes to approved scope assumptions, prerequisites and dependencies; distinguish first-run baseline from observed changes.
activities.prompt: Using Scout’s already-enabled M365 connection, check [scope-guidance source and dependency list] read-only. activities.requiredContext: Scout M365 access already enabled and approved; exact named SharePoint/OneDrive source allowlist, fields and scope/dependency evidence. activities.bestFitJob: Check scope dependencies against a dated baseline
activitySteps: 1. Name the approved M365 source allowlist and scope/dependency fields; confirm Scout M365 access and human review before running.

4. If live sources/tool access are unavailable for the huddle, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately; never present rehearsal as real customer facts, policy, eligibility, value or accepted ownership. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Bring delivery expertise in early to test outcomes, feasibility, assumptions and dependencies, including whether a bounded proof would help. Distinguish delivery feasibility from generic solution architecture.
keyTalkingPoints: Services Account Executive lens: Engaging delivery expertise early helps you surface feasibility risks before assumptions become promises. Approval rights, staffing gates, proof criteria and acceptance still require verification. ATU leads account discovery; SAE co-architects Services strategy. Strategy continuity does not imply ownership of delivery execution or receiving-team acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What execution or value gap is supported by evidence? What is still an assumption? What human decision is needed for delivery co-solutioning and feasibility?
suggestedTransitions: Compare the evidence behind delivery co-solutioning and feasibility; select one optional practice, inspect its draft, then name the next human checkpoint.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name a useful fragment or explicit evidence gap toward: Preliminary outcome/scope hypothesis with assumptions, dependencies, feasibility questions and reviewers; not SOW, plan, acceptance or promise. Do not imply the huddle completed the customer workflow.
facilitatorQuestions: What evidence supports the proposed Services path? SAE validates criteria with customer and authorized owners; rehearsal is not approval. What remains unresolved before an authorized owner could act?
listenFor: Customer outcomes before an offer; facts separated from inference; role and delivery boundaries; gaps stated rather than invented. Rehearsal is not customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected practice's sources, permission or tool access are missing, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic manual case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately. Real source gaps remain unresolved; rehearsal cannot establish customer facts, authoritative policy, fit/eligibility, capacity, approval, recognized value or receiving-owner acceptance. Do not request restricted pasted content, send/post, update records or schedule work. A chat-only Cowork practice does not create/edit files.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did the Services lens reveal that the broader account or solution view did not? Which assumption still needs checking?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose an optional next check within your authority: Decision log/open scope; not SOW or design. Confirm the appropriate human owner before any action; reflection or deferral is valid.
bringBackEvidence: If useful, bring back a non-sensitive observation, a verified source reference or an honest evidence/access gap. No new report, deadline, customer commitment or performance assessment is created.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Services seller faces uncertainty about delivery co-solutioning and feasibility. Compare the available outcome signals with execution/value gaps and identify the next evidence check without asserting an offer, funding, delivery acceptance or customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Services co-solutioning tests delivery assumptions and dependencies, not only whether a solution architecture is plausible. SAE connects Services opportunities to the shared Enterprise account motion; authoritative Services, delivery, commercial and policy owners retain their decisions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the draft feasibility hypothesis and current guidance in the example.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A solution architecture alone does not settle Services delivery feasibility. Look for a bounded question about execution assumptions, dependencies or a justified proof. Services pilot content remains provisional. Check current official guidance for eligibility, routing and commercial questions; missing guidance is a gap, not permission or approval.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a solution architecture alone does not settle Services delivery feasibility. Confirm who can explain the Services strategy, fit and execution dependencies boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a solution architecture alone does not settle Services delivery feasibility. Manager support can help involve delivery expertise early without inventing delivery capacity or a funded route.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help the facilitator surface the delivery question an accountable owner needs to answer; do not treat a draft scope as accepted or a proof as executed.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Review the commercial conversation alongside account and renewal context. Reuse pipeline inspection discipline while checking Services-specific forecast, renewal, portfolio and approval guidance before treating it as policy.
keyTalkingPoints: Services Account Executive lens: Separating commercial evidence from assumptions helps you focus risk discussions and source follow-up. Services forecast, unified renewal and portfolio details remain provisional until supported by current guidance. ATU leads account discovery; SAE co-architects Services strategy. Strategy continuity does not imply ownership of delivery execution or receiving-team acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What execution or value gap is supported by evidence? What is still an assumption? What human decision is needed for services commercial progression and renewal risk?
suggestedTransitions: Compare the evidence behind services commercial progression and renewal risk; select one optional practice, inspect its draft, then name the next human checkpoint.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name a useful fragment or explicit evidence gap toward: Reviewed status of verified decisions and risks; unverified commercial details for follow-up. No invented stage, probability, value or approval. Do not imply the huddle completed the customer workflow.
facilitatorQuestions: What evidence supports the proposed Services path? SAE validates with commercial owner; no forecast update or terms from AI draft. What remains unresolved before an authorized owner could act?
listenFor: Customer outcomes before an offer; facts separated from inference; role and delivery boundaries; gaps stated rather than invented. Rehearsal is not customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected practice's sources, permission or tool access are missing, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic manual case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately. Real source gaps remain unresolved; rehearsal cannot establish customer facts, authoritative policy, fit/eligibility, capacity, approval, recognized value or receiving-owner acceptance. Do not request restricted pasted content, send/post, update records or schedule work. A chat-only Cowork practice does not create/edit files.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did the Services lens reveal that the broader account or solution view did not? Which assumption still needs checking?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose an optional next check within your authority: Evidence-backed note with pending validation. Confirm the appropriate human owner before any action; reflection or deferral is valid.
bringBackEvidence: If useful, bring back a non-sensitive observation, a verified source reference or an honest evidence/access gap. No new report, deadline, customer commitment or performance assessment is created.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Services seller faces uncertainty about services commercial progression and renewal risk. Compare the available outcome signals with execution/value gaps and identify the next evidence check without asserting an offer, funding, delivery acceptance or customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Services commercial progression separates permitted agreement or opportunity facts from assumptions about terms and renewal outcomes. SAE connects Services opportunities to the shared Enterprise account motion; authoritative Services, delivery, commercial and policy owners retain their decisions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the example's authorized agreement or opportunity scope and commercial question.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A retrieved commercial fact does not approve a Services term or confirm a renewal result. Look for a verified progression question and a named commercial decision owner. Services pilot content remains provisional. Check current official guidance for eligibility, routing and commercial questions; missing guidance is a gap, not permission or approval.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a retrieved commercial fact does not approve a Services term or confirm a renewal result. Confirm who can explain the Services strategy, fit and execution dependencies boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-SAE-W06.keyTakeaway: Separate verified commercial decisions from assumptions about Services forecast, renewal, portfolio detail, and approval.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a retrieved commercial fact does not approve a Services term or confirm a renewal result. Manager support can support the SAE's commercial or renewal coordination while retaining approval boundaries.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Help keep retrieved facts separate from approved terms, forecast or renewal action; retain the commercial decision with its authorized owner.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a retrieved commercial fact does not approve a Services term or confirm a renewal result; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer. If the selected practice is chat-only Cowork, retain named-authorized-source access and no-file/action limits; a separate labeled rehearsal does not resolve missing real evidence or imply customer agreement/acceptance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support the SAE's commercial or renewal coordination while retaining approval boundaries? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.description: Detailed reference for Sales Agent components, capabilities, and example prompts.

resources.description: Always-available hub for role guidance and enablement.

resources.description: Official Sales agent overview and example prompts for connected CRM data. Internal sales scenarios and available records can differ.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Organize outcome evidence and limitations
activities.description: Review approved outcome measures for trends, missing baselines and attribution limits without making unsupported value claims.
activities.prompt: Read only [approved M365 outcome-report title or link] within my permitted access. In chat, extract stated measures, periods, baselines, definitions and limitations, then summarize source-supported trends. Distinguish observation from attribution; mark missing baselines or uncertain comparisons, and do not infer causation or customer-recognized value. Report unavailable evidence without substituting invented data or requesting restricted pasted material. Do not create/edit files, share, send, post, schedule or change records.
activities.expectedOutput: Descriptive analysis, method and evidence gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: SAE/metric owner verify definitions/access/interpretation before claims.
activities.requiredContext: Authorized M365 outcome-report title or link; intended outcome/period if not identifiable in the report.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this practice or another Featured option and identify only the named approved M365 source(s) you are authorized to read; do not paste restricted content.
2. Request the chat-only draft and review source title/date, evidence, assumptions, gaps and acceptance status. A missing source permits only conclusions supported by the sources actually available.
3. Do not create/edit files, send, post, schedule or change records. Any later action requires its separate authorized process.

4. If live sources/tool access are unavailable for the huddle, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately; never present rehearsal as real customer facts, policy, eligibility, value or accepted ownership. Missing authoritative guidance leaves the relevant judgment unresolved.
activities.whyThisMatters: Services measurement, value realization, lifecycle ownership and renewal rules are not verified.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Review outcome evidence and customer feedback to inform whether the account team should sustain, expand, renew or stop. Use the Enterprise renewal foundation while verifying Services-specific measurement and lifecycle guidance.
keyTalkingPoints: Services Account Executive lens: Reviewing evidence and feedback helps you frame a balanced next decision. Services measurement, lifecycle ownership and renewal rules still require verification. ATU leads account discovery; SAE co-architects Services strategy. Strategy continuity does not imply ownership of delivery execution or receiving-team acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What execution or value gap is supported by evidence? What is still an assumption? What human decision is needed for evidence, value realization and next opportunity?
suggestedTransitions: Compare the evidence behind evidence, value realization and next opportunity; select one optional practice, inspect its draft, then name the next human checkpoint.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name a useful fragment or explicit evidence gap toward: Outcome brief: intended outcome, evidence/limits, customer feedback, remaining gap and next decision. No guarantee or verdict. Do not imply the huddle completed the customer workflow.
facilitatorQuestions: What evidence supports the proposed Services path? SAE validates attribution and leads discussion; no expansion recommendation before review. What remains unresolved before an authorized owner could act?
listenFor: Customer outcomes before an offer; facts separated from inference; role and delivery boundaries; gaps stated rather than invented. Rehearsal is not customer evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected practice's sources, permission or tool access are missing, use a clearly labeled sanitized/synthetic manual case or paper discussion to rehearse the method separately. Real source gaps remain unresolved; rehearsal cannot establish customer facts, authoritative policy, fit/eligibility, capacity, approval, recognized value or receiving-owner acceptance. Do not request restricted pasted content, send/post, update records or schedule work. A chat-only Cowork practice does not create/edit files.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did the Services lens reveal that the broader account or solution view did not? Which assumption still needs checking?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose an optional next check within your authority: Options and next human decision with gaps. Confirm the appropriate human owner before any action; reflection or deferral is valid.
bringBackEvidence: If useful, bring back a non-sensitive observation, a verified source reference or an honest evidence/access gap. No new report, deadline, customer commitment or performance assessment is created.
facilitatorGuide.exampleScenario: Illustrative scenario: A Services seller faces uncertainty about evidence, value realization and next opportunity. Compare the available outcome signals with execution/value gaps and identify the next evidence check without asserting an offer, funding, delivery acceptance or customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Services outcome review connects minimized data and measurement limits to a possible sustain, renew, expand or stop decision. SAE connects Services opportunities to the shared Enterprise account motion; authoritative Services, delivery, commercial and policy owners retain their decisions.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Understand the example data definitions, period and baseline before discussing a claim.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: A calculated measure does not establish all customer value or justify automatic expansion. Look for an evidence-qualified sustain, renew, expand or stop question with an explicit measurement gap. Services pilot content remains provisional. Check current official guidance for eligibility, routing and commercial questions; missing guidance is a gap, not permission or approval.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to surface the distinction: a calculated measure does not establish all customer value or justify automatic expansion. Confirm who can explain the Services strategy, fit and execution dependencies boundary if challenged. Keep confidential context minimized and the example facilitator-arranged; attendance must not depend on a new Team Member artifact.

PLC-ENT-SAE-W08.keyTakeaway: Use outcome evidence and customer feedback to inform the next decision; neither makes renewal or expansion automatic.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: This topic matters when a calculated measure does not establish all customer value or justify automatic expansion. Manager support can support customer-value validation and the account decision without inferring unsupported metrics.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Encourage an evidence-qualified next question without implying a value verdict, automatic expansion or a customer commitment.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Invite different interpretations of the evidence without scoring individuals. Reinforce that a calculated measure does not establish all customer value or justify automatic expansion; keep the consequential judgment with its accountable human owner. Ask for the uncertainty rather than pressure for a confident answer. If the selected practice is chat-only Cowork, retain named-authorized-source access and no-file/action limits; a separate labeled rehearsal does not resolve missing real evidence or imply customer agreement/acceptance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions: In the next existing 1:1 or account/team review, what changed in our ability to support customer-value validation and the account decision without inferring unsupported metrics? What remains blocked, who owns that decision, and what manager support is still useful? Treat an untested action as untested rather than demand a success story.

PLC-ENT-SAE-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on the team’s progress over the past eight weeks, identify the AI habits to keep building, and agree how to continue learning through team huddles.
PLC-ENT-SAE-W09.whyItMatters: Huddles make AI part of everyday work through shared learning, not a one-time push. Team-owned priorities keep the motion relevant as work changes.
PLC-ENT-SAE-W09.desiredOutcome: A shared understanding of what has changed, the habits worth continuing, how the team will keep learning together, and an agreed topic for Week 10.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Use the two-minute Overview to reconnect to why the motion matters: to take customers to the Frontier, we go first.
2. Frame the transition from guided Activation into team-owned Sustain, not the end of huddles; do not assume everyone completed every earlier week.
3. Preview the 30-minute agenda: Overview 2, Share Your Experience 8, Recap & What's Next 15, Close & Survey 5. These are coordinated components, not four alternative practices.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Use eight minutes to share what you tried with AI since the last huddle: a permitted task, prompt, workflow or moment.
2. Discuss what worked, what did not, and what you learned; no success story is required.
3. Name useful approaches, dead ends and process, data, tool, access or confidence blockers without ranking participants.
4. Carry observations into Recap & What's Next; the deeper eight-week recap and team prioritization share that following 15-minute block.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: Recap & What's Next: choose team priorities
activities.description: Reflect on moments that mattered and friction from the first eight weeks, then choose two or three workflow priorities and agree how team-owned huddles will continue.
activities.expectedOutput: Two or three team priorities for manager and facilitator planning, an agreed continuing huddle structure, and a next topic or custom-draft starting point where available.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the 15-minute Recap & What's Next block to name a real moment that changed work, a habit to keep and friction or session improvements. Do not assume all participants completed all weeks.
2. Explore where AI could change repeated work, not just speed up a task. Agree two or three useful or urgent team priorities that manager and facilitator can use in planning.
3. Agree the structure for continuing huddles and who coordinates the next planning step; do not turn all priorities into simultaneous individual commitments.

4. If useful and available, browse All Topics for a relevant existing huddle using the filters actually offered and tools permitted for the team. If no topic fits, consider Huddle in a Box: download the approved HTML, open it in a browser, build or edit with approved AI, and review before running it. This is a future-content route, not a requirement to finish a custom huddle live or to import it through the app's current HTML import option.

5. Confirm the priorities and structure before the final five-minute Close & Survey. If the app, filters, button or download is unavailable, record the priorities manually and locate approved content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: Participant-owned impact feedback opportunity with five minutes protected in-session; an access gap is recorded for follow-up if needed, without collecting individual responses.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Reserve the final five-minute Close & Survey block for participants to complete their own Impact Survey through the approved link. Priorities and the continuing structure should already be agreed in Recap & What's Next.
2. Briefly reinforce that feedback helps understand change over time and shape what comes next; do not claim usage or survey completion proves impact.
3. Let participants answer privately. Do not collect individual responses or proof of completion, and never generate answers for them.

4. If the survey link or access fails, record the access gap and follow up through the approved process without extending the session or inventing a substitute survey. Continue team-owned Sustain; this is not the final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Look back on experience from the first eight weeks without assuming everyone completed every huddle. This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion: keep sharing, explore workflows that matter, and build on what works.
keyTalkingPoints: Use the shared Transition HTML, not the ordinary AI-in-Action practice format. Share recent experience and journey-wide reflection; the facilitator or manager briefly explains why practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue. Then agree the ongoing huddle rhythm and a Week 10 topic, and close with feedback. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
discussionQuestions: Since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well or did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?

Looking back across the journey: Moments that mattered—what changed in how you think about or use AI, and what are you doing differently? Habits worth continuing—which habits and peer learning should we keep building? Make it our own—what has worked about our huddles, what would we change, and what should ongoing huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep a team-owned rhythm, and which topic will we use for Week 10?
suggestedTransitions: Open with the purpose (2 minutes). Use Share Your Experience (15 minutes) for both the since-last-huddle check-in and the journey-wide reflection. The facilitator or manager then presents Sustain (3 minutes): practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Move to What’s Next (8 minutes) to agree the ongoing rhythm and a Week 10 topic using All Topics or Huddle in a Box as appropriate. Close & Feedback (2 minutes) welcomes questions and points to the Impact Survey only if not already completed.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the habits worth continuing, the team's ongoing huddle rhythm, and the agreed Week 10 topic. Use Close & Feedback for questions and the Team Member Impact Survey invitation. Participants who already completed the survey do not need to repeat it; this is the beginning of Sustain, not the end of the motion.
facilitatorQuestions: Share Your Experience—since the last huddle: What did you try with AI? What worked well, and what did not? What did you learn, and where did you run into friction?
Looking back across the journey:
Moments that mattered: What experience changed how you think about or use AI? What are you doing differently today that you were not doing at the beginning?
Habits worth continuing: Which AI habits are becoming part of everyday work? What have you learned from one another that you want to keep building?
Make it our own: What has worked about our huddles, and what would we change? What should our ongoing team huddles look like?
What’s Next: How will we keep learning together, and which topic will we choose for Week 10?
Close & Feedback: What questions, comments, or ideas would you like to share before we close?
listenFor: Listen for concrete changes, honest uncertainty, habits worth continuing, peer learning, and support needs. Include people with mixed experience or access gaps without assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Seek a shared Week 10 topic, not a tool quota or a ranking of participants.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If app, topic-library, customization, or survey links are unavailable, continue the team discussion and agree a Week 10 topic without a live build or download. Raise the access gap through the approved support route. Do not invent personal impact evidence or generate survey answers.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What has changed in how we think about and use AI, which habits should continue, and where would more practice or support help?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Agree how the team will keep learning through huddles and choose a Week 10 topic. Existing All Topics content or Huddle in a Box are options described in the supplied HTML, not required live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; each person supplies their own feedback.
bringBackEvidence: Keep bringing useful experiences, questions, and friction into the existing team rhythm. No new individual report, artifact, or survey-completion proof is required. Distinguish an observed benefit from an untested idea and keep human judgment explicit.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Help the team move from guided Activation to team-owned Sustain. Reflect on the first eight weeks, identify useful habits and remaining support needs, agree how huddles will continue, and choose a topic for Week 10. This is a shared team review, not account planning or technical strategy.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the shared Transition HTML and its five-part agenda. With the manager, agree who opens the session, facilitates reflection, presents the brief Sustain explanation, and guides the Week 10 planning. Locate the All Topics, Huddle in a Box, and Impact Survey links before the huddle.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Follow the shared 30-minute agenda: Overview 2; Share Your Experience 15; Sustain 3; What’s Next 8; Close & Feedback 2. Sustain is a short facilitator/manager explanation of why ongoing practice, peer learning, and Customer Zero continue—not another open discussion or AI-practice block. Do not require a success story, a new artifact, or live tool use. Invite the Impact Survey only if not already completed; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree how to draw out experiences and friction, reinforce why huddles continue, and help the team choose its Week 10 topic and continuing rhythm. Keep the same shared Team Review content across audiences; do not substitute a role-specific planning exercise.

PLC-ENT-SAE-W09.keyTakeaway: This is the start of Sustain, not the end of the motion. Keep sharing, explore workflows that matter to the team, and build on what works.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Help the team own its transition from guided Activation to Sustain: recognize learning, keep useful habits, agree how huddles continue, and choose a Week 10 topic. This shared review is not an account-priority or technical-strategy session.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Week 9 Team Review HTML and agree light handoffs with the facilitator before meeting. Be ready to support reflection, the continuing team rhythm, and choosing a Week 10 topic. Confirm the supplied Impact Survey link is available without asking for personal responses.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Make space for wins, dead ends, and friction without rating people or assuming everyone completed every earlier huddle. Agree who will present the brief Sustain explanation: practice builds habits and confidence, peers learn together, and Customer Zero starts with us. Help the team agree its continuing rhythm and a Week 10 topic. Follow the shared five-part agenda rather than adding a live tool exercise.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
What habits and support needs should we carry into our existing team rhythm?
Have we agreed how huddles will continue and which topic we will use in Week 10?
If the Impact Survey is still outstanding, do people know where to find it without repeating an already completed response?
