PLC-ENT-SAE-W01.whyItMatters: Firsthand experience helps us bring real insights to customers. A consistent huddle rhythm builds confidence and helps teams learn from one another as AI becomes part of everyday work.
PLC-ENT-SAE-W01.desiredOutcome: Understand the huddle motion, the connected roles, where to find shared resources, and what to expect when workflow huddles begin in Week 2.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the shared Frontier Accelerator Orientation. Understand why we go first as Customer Zero, how the huddle motion works, and how to participate. The Huddle Experience previews the repeatable weekly format from Week 2 onward.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the Customer Zero purpose, the five connected roles, and the weekly rhythm of real work and peer learning. Distinguish today’s Orientation from the future weekly-format examples. Point to the HTML’s readiness checklist and shared resources; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2.
discussionQuestions: What questions do we have about the huddle motion and how to participate?
Where can we find the shared resources and access help?
What would help us feel ready for the first workflow huddle in Week 2?
suggestedTransitions: Move through the Orientation story, then use Huddle Experience to preview the familiar weekly structure. Explain that sharing prior experience and hands-on workflow practice start with the role-specific huddles, not as extra Orientation tasks. Close with readiness questions and the next huddle.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Confirm the team understands the motion, where to find the shared resources, and what to expect in Week 2. Point to existing Top 5 Agents readiness guidance in the learner HTML without adding a separate assignment. Make clear that the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional and the weekly pulse starts in Week 2.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the huddle motion for, and how will we learn from one another?
What will feel different when the role-specific huddles begin in Week 2?
What questions do we have about participation, the shared resources, or getting help?
listenFor: Listen for clarity about the weekly rhythm, the five connected roles, safe experimentation, and learning from wins and friction. Separate questions about future practice from Orientation participation; no expert knowledge, completed tool trial, or polished artifact is needed today.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If a link or tool is unavailable, explain the motion from the supplied HTML and name the access blocker for support. Do not bypass permissions or invent a completed demonstration. Discussion and questions remain useful; never supply an AI-generated survey response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What is clearer about how huddles work, and what question would help you feel ready to participate?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Confirm the shared next step into the first role-specific huddle. Use the learner HTML's existing readiness guidance as needed; the recurring-work discovery prompt remains optional. Do not require a tool trial or a new deliverable from every participant.
bringBackEvidence: Invite questions or learning to share at the next huddle. No new artifact, access screenshot, completed prompt, or proof of participation is required by this host guidance. Keep sensitive details in approved systems.
facilitatorGuide.roleWorkflowContext: Introduce the shared huddle motion: why we go first as Customer Zero, how peer learning builds confidence, and what to expect from Orientation, role-specific Weeks 2–8, and team-owned Sustain. This is Orientation for everyone, not a role-specific work exercise.
facilitatorGuide.facilitatorPreparation: Review the supplied Orientation HTML, including its Orientation and Huddle Experience tabs. Confirm the HTML and baseline-survey link are available; identify where to find the Top 5 Agents overview and access help. Agree the opening and handoffs with the manager before meeting.
facilitatorGuide.facilitationWatchouts: Distinguish today’s Orientation from the weekly-format preview that begins in Week 2. There is no prior huddle experience to share today. Do not turn the preview into a required live tool exercise. Use the HTML for readiness guidance; the recurring-work discovery go-do is optional, not a required deliverable. The weekly usefulness pulse begins in Week 2; participants provide their own feedback.
facilitatorGuide.managerFacilitatorAlignment: Agree who introduces the why, who guides the Orientation and weekly-experience preview, and how questions or access blockers will be supported. Use the same shared content for every audience; local examples can add flavor without creating a maintained role-specific Orientation.

topicResources.title: What we've learned from Microsoft's own AI transformation
topicResources.description: Microsoft Customer Zero evidence for outcome-first transformation, end-to-end workflow redesign, employee-centered change, Capability Add measurement, and continuous human-AI learning. Metrics are bounded to the cited samples and periods.

topicResources.title: Becoming a Frontier Firm: Microsoft Frontier Playbook
topicResources.description: Practical Microsoft guide to Persona Acceleration, AI-Powered Process Redesign, and AI-First Possibility, grounded in Customer Zero transformation lessons.

PLC-ENT-SAE-W01.keyTakeaway: We go first as Customer Zero. Huddles build confidence and useful AI habits through real work, peer learning, and sharing what worked and what did not.

managerGuide.managerTeamRelevance: Explain why the shared huddle motion matters: we go first as Customer Zero, learn from peers, and build confidence through real work. Orientation establishes the motion for everyone; role-specific practice begins in Week 2.
managerGuide.managerPreparationGuidance: Review the Orientation HTML and agree a brief opening and handoffs with the facilitator. Locate the baseline survey, readiness checklist, shared Top 5 Agents resources, and access help so questions can be supported.
managerGuide.managerDuringHuddleGuidance: Introduce the why, reinforce the weekly rhythm, and welcome questions. Help distinguish the future weekly-experience preview from today's Orientation. Support readiness and access questions without inspecting individual tool usage, survey answers, or performance.
managerGuide.managerFollowThroughQuestions:
Does the team understand the motion and what to expect in the first role-specific huddle in Week 2?
What readiness question or access blocker needs support through our existing channels?

agents.Name: Sales Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.
agents.KeyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.Name: ECIF Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Through Sales Agent, ECIF Agent brings program guidance, guided workscope drafts, guided creation/submission of supported investment requests, request-draft editing and delivery-health signals together with account and opportunity context. The full end-to-end conversational investment lifecycle is still evolving.
agents.WhatItIs: Investment guidance and supported workflows surfaced through Sales Agent.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Discover programs and prior investments/yield; search suppliers; create guided AI workscope drafts; create and submit supported investment requests, edit request drafts, link workscopes and select consumption plans; review milestones, delivery health and risk. Compliance hold/release is role-permitted; eligibility, supplier selection and approval remain governed decisions.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Discovering programs or suppliers for an evidenced investment need; preparing guided workscope drafts; creating/submitting supported investment requests or editing request drafts; reviewing available milestones and delivery risk. Confirm request-type coverage and role permissions; this does not imply saved-workscope editing or full Agent MCR.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat the agent as the final authority for policy, eligibility, compliance, funding approval, or supplier selection. Review generated content and required evidence before submission, and use governed ECIF channels for exceptions or approvals.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Sales Agent and ask for ECIF, process or program help in the chat. The current capability guide can help distinguish supported steps from in-progress features. Use reviewed text and analysis in the huddle; any request or record change needs a separate authorized action.
agents.KeyBenefits: Simplifies investment preparation and progression by bringing program guidance, supplier search, guided workscope drafts and supported guided request creation, draft editing and submission into one conversation; helps teams review milestone and delivery-risk evidence. Generated drafts and signals still need human verification.

agents.Name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
agents.ShortDescription: AI assistant across Microsoft 365 apps and work data.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Draft, summarize, analyze, prepare, and create within familiar Microsoft 365 experiences.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Everyday work grounded in emails, meetings, chats, files and app content, in the app you are already working in. Ask and get: you want the answer or the draft now.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as a substitute for a specialized agent when the work requires a specific system or workflow, for a multi-step task you would rather hand off and review, which is Cowork, or for work that should keep running on a schedule, which is Scout.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot from the app launcher or copilot.cloud.microsoft and start in Chat.
agents.KeyBenefits: Reduces time spent drafting, summarizing, and preparing work; uses permitted Microsoft 365 context to keep work grounded.

agents.Name: Cowork
agents.ShortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.
agents.KeyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

agents.Name: Scout
agents.ShortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.
agents.KeyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

agents.Name: Researcher
agents.ShortDescription: Deep research agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that produces structured, source-cited reports.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Combines work content and web research across multiple steps.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Customer, market, competitor, industry, and strategic research requiring citations. Researcher is also reachable inside Sales Agent, which uses it to answer research questions; call Researcher directly when you want the full sourced report rather than an answer inside a sales conversation.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid for quick summaries or lightweight drafting.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Researcher agent, then state the research question and sources.
agents.KeyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

agents.Name: Analyst
agents.ShortDescription: Data-analysis agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot for statistics, trends, outliers, charts, and reports.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Analyzes supplied data and produces understandable findings and visuals.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Multi-file quantitative analysis, trend analysis, and executive-ready data insights.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid when authoritative operational reporting must come directly from a certified business system.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Analyst agent, then attach the data you want analyzed.
agents.KeyBenefits: Turns supplied data into findings and visuals a non-analyst can act on, including trends, outliers, and executive-ready charts, without building the analysis by hand.

agents.Name: MSXI Assist V2
agents.ShortDescription: MSXI assistance for report discovery, published KPI definitions and report-context insights where the relevant Copilot experience is available.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Find the right MSXI report, understand KPI definitions and investigate pipeline, performance or consumption questions using report metrics.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you need a report or metric that fits your business question, or want to inspect a pipeline, performance or consumption signal before deciding what to do next.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use report metrics alone to diagnose technical causes, infer customer intent or authorize record, forecast or commercial changes. Subscriptions and delivery require separately confirmed Proactive Insights support.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open MSXI and start in the available Copilot Pane with your goal or metric; you do not need to know the report name. For analysis, check the report/view, scope, period and relevant visual, then ask a concise question using its terms. Role starters and book prompts are optional; Copilot availability varies by report.
agents.KeyBenefits: A clearer path from the business question to the relevant report and evidence, with KPI meaning and source limits visible before you make a decision.

agents.Name: Agent J.ai
agents.ShortDescription: Text-based coaching experience grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Helps users sharpen messages, rehearse conversations, anticipate objections, and plan next steps.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Customer conversation preparation and role-play, or de-identified rehearsal of a manager coaching conversation about business judgment where access and scenario support are confirmed. Do not use employee or HR data for rehearsal.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as the authoritative source for CRM or commercial data.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Agent J.ai in Microsoft 365 Copilot, then describe the conversation you want to rehearse and who you will be speaking to. For manager coaching rehearsal, use a de-identified scenario and review the suggested questions yourself. Related Manager Empowerment guidance: https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/MCAPSAcademy/SitePages/MCAPS-Manager-Empowerment.aspx
agents.KeyBenefits: Rehearsal before the real conversation. Sharpens messages, surfaces objections you had not anticipated, and coaches on clarity and next step, grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.

agents.Name: Auto-Fix Pipeline Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Agent in MSX intended to resolve supported pipeline hygiene issues.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supports targeted pipeline cleanup inside MSX.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When a Practice explicitly addresses supported pipeline hygiene correction.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not generalize beyond supported issues.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens MSX. Auto-Fix has no standalone URL. Inside MSX, open the Pipeline Hygiene workspace and select Auto-Fixes, then choose which automated fixes to enable and review, accept or revert each change after it is applied.
agents.KeyBenefits: One-click cleanup for supported pipeline hygiene violations, with review and revert available so the seller stays in control of what changes.

agents.Name: MSXI Copilot
agents.ShortDescription: Copilot help for interpreting MSXI business metrics and trends, with report discovery and KPI explanations.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Understand MSXI business metrics and trends in their report context, locate a relevant report and clarify the KPI behind a planning or inspection question.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When a business question needs the right report or KPI definition, or when you want to explore the metrics and trends in an MSXI report.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not replace human interpretation of measure scope, filters or customer context, or treat report variation as proof of a cause, commitment or approval. Proactive Insights subscriptions and notifications need separately confirmed support.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open MSXI and use the Copilot Pane where available. Start with your goal or metric to find a report, or open the relevant report directly. For analysis, check its view, filters, period and visual, then ask a concise question using report terms. Optional role starters or book prompts can help; availability varies by report.
agents.KeyBenefits: Connect report metrics to the business question, clarify what the KPI means and make evidence gaps visible before choosing a next action.

agents.Name: Customer Success Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Teams-based customer success experience referenced in Customer Health Success Program dispatch guidance.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supports Success Program dispatch and customer-success workflow steps where available.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Customer Health Success Program dispatch or customer-success process steps that are explicitly supported.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as authority for policy, delivery commitments or customer-facing claims.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens the Customer Success Agent app details page in Teams. Install the app once and it stays in your Teams rail, then follow the supported Customer Health Success Program dispatch workflow.
agents.KeyBenefits: Connects Customer Health Success Program execution to CSAM workflow steps in Teams, so dispatch and follow-through happen where the team already works.

agents.Name: MSX Deal Assistance
agents.ShortDescription: The investment request front door inside MSX. Consolidates ECIF, ACO, Azure Access, and Solution Assessment requests that were previously spread across separate tools.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Create, submit, and track investment requests against an opportunity, with ROI calculation and opportunity data prepopulated rather than retyped.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When an investment request needs to be created or submitted, or when you need the current status of one you already submitted.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for building the workscope itself, which happens in ECIF Central, and not for policy or eligibility judgments, which stay with the accountable owner.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open an MSX opportunity, go to the Deal Assistance tab, select New Request, then choose the request type such as ECIF, ACO, or Azure Access.
agents.KeyBenefits: One front door instead of several legacy request tools. Opportunity data and ROI calculation carry over, so the request starts mostly complete.

agents.Name: ECIF Central
agents.ShortDescription: Where the workscope is built and where delivery actually runs, including supplier collaboration, milestones, and change requests.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Create a workscope against an opportunity, add suppliers and scope detail, calculate the spend plan, and track execution and milestones once funding is approved.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you need to build or revise a workscope, onboard or work with a supplier, or check delivery progress and milestones.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not the submission point. The completed workscope is submitted through MSX Deal Assistance.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open ECIF Central, create a workscope using the MSX Opportunity ID, add suppliers and scope detail, calculate the spend plan, then generate the completed workscope for submission. Suppliers collaborate through partner.ecifcentral.microsoft.com.
agents.KeyBenefits: Keeps workscope, supplier collaboration, and delivery tracking in one place instead of email threads and spreadsheets.

agents.Name: Investment Tracker
agents.ShortDescription: The status view inside MSX Deal Assistance showing where a request sits, who holds it, and what is blocking it. Sometimes called the Pizza Tracker.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: See request stage, current owner, blockers, and recommended next steps without asking someone for a status update.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When a submitted request has gone quiet and you need to know where it is and who holds it.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not a substitute for contacting the owner when a request is genuinely stuck. It shows status, not urgency.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens MSX Deal Assistance. The Investment Tracker is a view inside it rather than a separate site: open your submitted request and read the tracker view for stage, ownership and blockers. FY27 material describes proactive at-risk alerts; confirm current availability with the ECIF program team.
agents.KeyBenefits: Replaces the status-chasing email with a view. Makes ownership visible so the next action has a name attached.

agents.Name: Azure Offer Navigator
agents.ShortDescription: The front door for Azure investment offers, including Azure Accelerate, with eligibility guidance and nomination support.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Find which Azure offers an opportunity is eligible for, choose the right one, submit the nomination, and track its status.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When the investment is Azure-specific and you need to identify and request the right offer.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for non-Azure ECIF requests, which go through MSX Deal Assistance.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open the Navigator, enter the MSX Opportunity ID, review the eligible offers it returns, select the appropriate one, and submit through the Navigator workflow.
agents.KeyBenefits: One place to see what an opportunity actually qualifies for, with recommendations and next-best-action guidance rather than reading offer documentation.

agents.Name: MCAPS Help for ECIF
agents.ShortDescription: Support, guidance, and ticketing for ECIF and investment process questions.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Get help when a request is blocked, access is missing, or the process itself is unclear, and raise a case when self-help does not resolve it.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you are blocked on process, access, or tooling rather than on a business decision.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for eligibility, policy, or funding decisions, which belong to the accountable owners rather than support.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open MCAPS Help for ECIF, search the guidance first, and raise a case if the answer is not there. Have the opportunity ID and request ID ready.
agents.KeyBenefits: A defined path for process and access problems, so a blocked request does not sit waiting on an informal ask.

agents.Name: Consumption Manager
agents.ShortDescription: Consumption plan information used inside Global ECIF and ACO request flows.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supply and review the consumption plan detail that a Global ECIF or ACO request requires.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When submitting a Global ECIF or ACO request that needs consumption plan information.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not a standalone consumption reporting tool. For consumption trends and ACR, use Sales Agent or MSXI.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens ECIF Central. Consumption Manager is not opened directly - it is reached from inside the Global ECIF and ACO request flow as part of a submission. Confirm current behavior with the ECIF program team.
agents.KeyBenefits: Keeps consumption planning attached to the investment request rather than tracked separately.

agents.Name: Sales Home
agents.ShortDescription: The seller landing experience within Sales Agent for SME&C individual contributors using MSX. It brings relevant alerts, prospecting signals and pipeline context together. Preview is opened across SME&C without separate installation or opt-in; useful data depends on role and assigned records. Managers use separate reporting. Germany and Austria await Works Council approval.
agents.WhatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. For SME&C individual contributors using MSX, preview does not require separate installation or opt-in. Relevant data is currently concentrated in AE, Specialist and CASA workflows involving Sales Accelerator signals or owned opportunities; do not infer that every role has useful records or that CASA means DCSA. If relevant signal data is absent, use Sales Accelerator or the source system that assigned the queue. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Sales Home is only for SME&C individual contributors using MSX, not non-SME&C audiences or managers; managers use separate reporting. Germany and Austria are fast-follow pending Works Council approval. Do not assume useful data for every SME&C role or map CASA to a role without confirmation. Renewal, Campaign, Planning, Realization and Deal Agent integration are roadmap, not available today, so do not build an activity that depends on them.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens Sales Agent. Sales Home is the seller surface inside it - My View for alerts and quota attainment, Prospecting for signals, account research, contacts and outreach, and Pipeline for opportunities, forecast comments, close plans and deal risks. It is not a separate product and has no separate link. No separate installation, opt-in or user enablement is required for the SME&C preview. Use relevant records only; an empty view is not proof of missing provisioning. Germany and Austria await Works Council approval; managers use separate reporting.
agents.KeyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.
agents.AccessLinkLabel: Open Sales Agent, use Sales Home

agents.Name: Know Your Partner
agents.ShortDescription: SME&C partner briefing agent. Assembles partner performance from Partner IAP (ACR, CSP, Copilot seats, net new revenue) and program utilization from Activities Utilization ROB (Azure, Copilot and Security Accelerate), then adds web-sourced partner news and situational fluency. Type a partner name or PartnerOne ID; name several to compare. States placeholders rather than inventing missing data.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Prepare or compare partner briefings using permitted partner-performance and program-utilization data, with partner news kept distinct from operational evidence.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Before a partner planning conversation, deal clinic, readiness discussion, or performance review when permitted partner context is needed. Enter a partner name or PartnerOne ID; compare named partners only where access and comparable data support it.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat a briefing as proof of current staffing, delivery capacity, customer intent, partner economics, eligibility, or approval. Verify dates, scope, and source differences; retain missing-data placeholders rather than inventing facts. Do not bypass partner-data sharing or role-access rules.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens the Know Your Partner app details page in Teams via the owner-maintained alias. Install the app once and it stays in your Teams rail.
agents.KeyBenefits: Reduces partner-context gathering for a preparation or review conversation, making available performance and program signals easier to compare while preserving evidence gaps for human follow-up.

agents.Name: GitHub Copilot
agents.ShortDescription: AI coding assistant available in an IDE, GitHub Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. Repository or working-folder context supports code and configuration work rather than acting as a CRM source of record.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Write, explain, refactor and test code; scaffold infrastructure-as-code and deployment artifacts; build the smallest spike that proves or disproves an architecture assumption; generate sample data and validation scripts; and reproduce a reported failure so you can see it rather than describe it.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When the next step is to build something rather than to plan or describe it. Validating an architecture assumption with a spike, standing up a demo or workshop environment, iterating a proof of concept, reproducing a deployment or integration failure, or packaging a reusable asset with tests and setup steps.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for customer, market or account research; that is Researcher. Do not use it to assemble a customer-facing document or deck; that is Cowork. Do not point it at production without the review your team already requires, and do not paste customer data into it. It works on code and configuration, not on the CRM record.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Choose the Copilot extension in your IDE, GitHub Copilot CLI for terminal work, or the GitHub Copilot app for coordinating agent-driven development. Open or select the relevant repository or working folder so the task has context. Start with: Explain what this deployment does, then write the smallest test that would prove the assumption I am least sure about. Review proposed commands and edits, run the relevant tests, and follow your approved environment and data-handling rules.
agents.KeyBenefits: Creates reviewable code and test evidence to validate an architecture assumption or reproduce a failure, giving technical and account teams a more concrete basis for the next decision. Human review and testing remain required.

agents.Name: Deal Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Deal Agent is surfaced through Sales Agent. It is not a standalone agent to install or select; it triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Discover agreements and EA/EAS enrollments, generate and reuse renewal Deal Books, explore growth scenarios, and support EA quotes, proposals, amendments and pre-approvals through Sales Agent. Provides integrated MCA-E policy/process/licensing guidance and tools for MCA-E proposal creation or revision, including BYOD and MACC configuration where applicable. Validate returned deal data and recommendations; tool capability does not grant commercial, legal, funding or customer approval.
agents.WhenToUseIt: For an enterprise EA/EAS renewal, start with an account name, TPID, PCN or Master Agreement when the enrollment is unknown; review returned enrollment details before selecting the intended enrollment. Known agreement/enrollment identifiers remain valid for their specific tasks. For applicable MCA-E work, ask sourced policy/process/licensing questions or use proposal creation and revision tools within your authority. Inspect recorded MACC and growth scenarios where they help the renewal decision; treat recommendations as hypotheses.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Verify complex-deal responses against current data. For general decks, emails or documents beyond deal-making artifacts, use Cowork instead. Review exact proposed record changes and obtain the accountable owner's decision before any creation, edit, claim or submission in an authorized workflow. A confirmation card or tap is not pricing, funding, legal or customer approval.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and use the agent picker to select Sales. Start a new chat with a renewal or deal question, such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically; there is nothing separate to install or select. Lead with a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number, keep one chat thread per deal, and review returned facts and proposed actions before using them.
agents.KeyBenefits: Brings deal facts, renewal context, Deal Books, and proposal work into the Sales Agent conversation instead of gathering them across separate portals. Keeps the capability visible while retaining one entry point and human review of commercial decisions.
